The Phoenician Resort and Spa · Scottsdale, AZ

tripadvisor · 2025-07-02 · 4/5view source
disappoint / activitieslack of / activities

A Beautiful Stay with Room for Improvement The Phoenician Resort is undeniably stunning, from the breathtaking mountain views near our hotel room to the beautifully landscaped grounds, multiple pool options, and towering palm trees that truly make the resort feel like a desert oasis. However, while the scenery impressed us, several aspects of our stay fell short, especially when compared to other top resorts in the Phoenix area. Dining & Amenities: One major concern was the limited dining hours. Most on-site restaurants closed by 5:00 PM, with The Tavern being the only option open until 8:00 PM. As out-of-town guests, this left us with little choice in the evenings aside from room service or ordering out. We expected more flexibility and variety in a luxury resort. Shops & Pool Experience: All shops on the property also closed early at 5:00 PM, and pool amenities, including the water slide, music, bar, and even the water fountains, were shut down around the same time. This was disappointing, as the pool is typically a hub of activity and relaxation, especially in the summer. Children's Activities: We were especially let down by the Funicians Kids Club, which was never open during our stay. This was a major reason we selected the Phoenician, and our children were incredibly disappointed by its unavailability. Summer Activities: We appreciated the advertised “Legendary Summers” theme, but there were no events scheduled during the weekdays only on the weekends. Other Phoenix-area resorts we’ve visited provide daily family-friendly activities all summer long, so the lack of weekday activities was a letdown. Overall, while the resort is visually impressive and offers a serene setting, we felt the guest experience didn’t fully match the high rating and reputation. With a few key improvements especially around extended hours, family activities, and consistent activites the Phoenician could offer a truly legendary experience to match its branding.

google · 2024-11-19 · 2/5view source
disappoint / showlimited / activities

I recently stayed at The Phoenician in Scottsdale with my wife and kids, and after reading all the glowing reviews, I just don’t understand the hype. It was fine, but I wouldn’t call it luxury by any means, nor exceptional, especially considering the price or the points required for a stay here. As a Gold Elite member with years of travel experience, I’ve come to recognize top-notch service and value, but this resort falls short in nearly every category. First impressions matter, and our check-in experience wasn’t great. We didn’t feel welcomed or even like we were at a luxury resort. The staff member who checked us in barely explained anything about the property—just handed me a map and a booklet and sent us on our way. The main pool area was closed for maintenance, and the kids' splash park wasn’t working when we tried to use it—not once, but twice. The only other pool available for kids was cold! Honestly, no one else was in it because it felt unheated, and after talking to a few guests, they agreed it was too cold. We also didn’t see any pool attendants around to ask about life jackets or pool toys, or anything that might make the experience better if the pool was heated. The kids' club or play area was also closed on Monday, so there was literally nothing for our kids to do for the first couple of days of our stay. Fortunately, we had a larger unit with a hot tub and a golf cart to get around, which helped salvage the experience—without that, there wouldn’t have been much to do. Speaking of the hot tub, not good. After using it on Sunday, the next day all of us had rashes or skin breakouts. We suspect it was from the excessive chlorine, as there was an unusually thick layer of foam and bubbles in the tub. Our 5-year-old, 1.5-year-old, and both adults all had reactions. Room 7704 itself was disappointing, especially for the price and points required. It’s showing its age—there were missing pieces of flooring near the dining table (my wife actually hurt her toe), cracks and dents in the walls, and the doors don’t close properly. The whole place just felt a bit run-down. I certainly wouldn’t pay thousands to stay here. The wifi also didn’t work for our entire stay which wasn’t ideal at all. I had a couple of meetings Monday and no wifi. Costing me money to use data. We called down to have someone come up and check it out Sunday but nobody came for almost 2 hours. Called back to inform them nobody came by, kids had to go to sleep. They were going to update the ticket and have someone come by Monday. Nobody came, no follow up, nothing. Just terrible service. We also ordered food from the Tavern one night, and it was mediocre at best—not worth the price at all. Save your money and eat elsewhere. As a Gold Elite member, I expected better treatment, especially with pools being closed and limited activities for kids on certain days of the week. We were hoping for an upgrade to a unit with a pool, which is supposed to happen as a gold elite member (enhanced room upgrade benefit) but despite some of the other residences being vacant both nights, they didn’t offer us anything. They were more focused on charging extra for upgrades than making sure we had a better experience, even though we were loyal members with kids and limited options at the resort. Honestly, I regret spending 240,000 points to stay here. This resort was a major disappointment overall, and I’ll definitely be looking elsewhere next time. It was a huge waste of both time and points. I encourage others looking to spend their hard earned dollars or points to look elsewhere. For those of you who love this place, glad you enjoyed it and had a better experience. I know it’s hard to please everyone and it’ll rarely happen but we felt overall, it simply underwhelming and not worth it.

tripadvisor · 2013-04-16 · 5/5view source
disappoint / at nightlack of / at night

Attention to Detail A wonderful place to stay with friends especially if someone in your group has food allergies. This property boasts a dedicated allergen-free kitchen where dishes from all food service outlets can be made and then served. The options for gluten-free are plentiful and pretty much limitless. If it's not on the menu, just ask. The servers throughout the food outlets are knwoledgeable and attentive. Sometimes to a fault, they tend to enjoy your company a little too much and don't want to bring you the check to leave, but alas, there could be worse things. The rooms are spacious and feature a his & hers closet as well as double sinks in the bathroom. If at anytime your remote control stops functioning, simply drop it on the floor and it will resume operations (not sure why this method is so effective). The beds are also extremely comfortable. However, there are few poweroutlets by the nightstands making it rather challenging to charge anything than an iPhone for which the alarm clock has an adapter for. They claim to have 9 pools, but I'd say it was closer to 7 as 3 of them are actually just one pool with some land bridges. Just saying. The hot tub tends to be really hot during the day, but I'm sure its more than enjoyable at night. I was slightly disappointed with the lack of swim-up bar, but the lounge chairs service more than made up for it. Also if you plan on outdoor dining off of the lobby at the firepits, claim your spot early as they fill up and folks are reluctant to leave. Moreover, the hotel does NOT provide s'more kits, so bring your own. It's not condoned, but allowed. There are also 27 holes of golf as well as putting green and a driving range. The driving range prices are extremely affordable considering everything else on property. Sadly, I did not make it to the gym, but the cactus walk was a nice touch. Finally, don't get roped into the $29/day valet parking when the self-parking option is free and easily accessible from the elevators in the lobby.

No stay is without issues but based on overall experience, I decided to give this resort a 4 ⭐️ PROS: Room was clean and big. Beautiful property with great service, nice pools, high quality food and service. High Tea experience: Good experience but overpriced ($100 per person for 3 course after gratuity and tax) Mowry and Cotton restaurant: We went to M and C during our stay to eat breakfast and dinner and feel that it’s of high quality in terms of food and service with nice views of the pool. Especially at night the blue light reflecting the pool was amazing. Thirsty Camel bar: Great bar with nice outside seating area and 🔥 pits. Great drinks and service and live music. CONS: -CheckIn experience was not great, things were not explained clearly, for e.g I opted for self parking but no one explained that I could use my room key for in and out from the Self parking. I was paying every time using credit card every time I went in and out. Once I talked to the front desk, they were kind to waive the $23 per day charge they were going to charge me. -On-site activities: Very few activities for kids or Christmas related events. We visited and attended the Fairmont Princess (a different resort in Scottsdale not associated with Marriott) Resort Christmas lights and ride experience ($72 for 4 with self parking included) and were blown away by the light and kids rides etc. Wish this resort had some nice Christmas lights and more activities for kids. If I had to book around Christmas, I would have booked Fairmont Princess resort just to have access to the Christmas light experience. -Gym: Far from the property; have to use a golf cart to go there for bike rentals and use. -Spa: We couldn’t get appointment because it was booked so can’t share the experience however feel it was overpriced

tripadvisor · 2024-12-01 · 2/5view source
lack of / show

Not Worth The Money This was one of the most disappointing resorts we have ever visited. My husband had planned a big surprise for my 60th b-day going to a warm sunny place in November to enjoy the beautiful pools this hotel offered. Upon arrival we encountered very persistent valet attendants. Without checking in they insisted on taking our suitcases from our car and holding them until we checked in. After standing in a very long line to check in because there was only one attendant available and the line was out the door, I took a walk only find that the entire main pool was under major construction. Something that was not mentioned prior to reservation made or at check in. After check-in we were told about the two pools available, however, the lower pool was off limits due to a convention. So, we really only had use to the smallest pool on the grounds. We then had to wait for our car to load it back up to head to the other end where the casitas are located. We reserved a casita, a little more exclusive and private. Once we got settled in, we realized right outside our door they were setting up for the convention dinner, no privacy at all. The casitas are very outdated, not very clean, mattress needs to be replaced and the tiny shower was covered in mold (see photos). We headed to the hot tubs that we were told would be available. Currently it is a maze of construction to get through only to find one of the hot-tub is off limits and the other had warm water with no jets. The next morning, we requested a room change, we were moved to the main building. The rooms are much more spacious and updated and all though it has a large bathroom the shower is still very small. We had a very nice balcony that would normally oversee the main pool. If you like quiet, this is not the spot. They have their private events there every night. At the time we were there you either could hear the party and music or the construction noise. We asked what options they could offer us as the front desk was also not aware about their hot tubs off limits. We were offered a one- day pass to the spa for the next day. We decided to give the spa a try. Apparently, something they don’t normally offer. Upon arrival, the spa manager was already aware we were coming and was very gracious as he proceeds to let us know there was an electrical problem on the men’s side and the steam room was not working. The spaces are separated for men and women so we would not be able to spend our time together. We skipped the spa. On this second day when returned from being out all day to a room that had not been serviced all day. We called to get it cleaned and were told they would send someone. The evening housekeeper that does the turndown showed up, was very apologetic for the morning staff but could only get trash and send someone else. After waiting for 45 minutes a lady showed up with towels and a lack of desire to clean anything. If you are a golfer, the course is beautiful and the gym was very nice surrounded by glass with views of the grounds. Overall, this hotel was very disappointing and for the cost I would choose something newer and with better service.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-14 · 2/5view source
disappoint / music

Please, 5-star? Who are you kidding? The Phoenician is a lovely property, but take a bundle of cash for ANY extra charge you can imagine and be prepared for surprises. A regular cup of carry-out coffee is more than $4.00, oatmeal is $9, you are charged for "porterage" even if you never see a porter and wheel in your own bag, and despite the high-end rack rate, you are charged on top of that for housekeeping, which, for us, one day did not happen at all and another day we had to request it since past 2 PM, it did not look like it was going to happen for the second day in a row. Then to add to our comedy of errors, we received three phone calls over the course of two nights AFTER we had gone to sleep, all between midnight and 2:30 AM with no one on the other end of the line, just music. I feel badly I had to explain my disappointment to such a nice young lady at the desk, but though this place is indeed beautiful, it needs a lot of work behind the scenes.

tripadvisor · 2009-06-02 · 3/5view source
boring / activities

The bloom has fallen off the rose.... I really should have listened to the negative comments on this site about The Phoenician. The grounds of the hotel are amazingly well cared for, standing in stark contrast to the guest rooms. The guest rooms were spacious, however, they were in need of a serious renovation. The carpets had stains on them and were generally on the thread bare side. The bed was large and nice, however, the sheets had a few small holes in them. The crown modeling and the walls looked slightly worn. The bathroom was large, but needed an overhaul. Everything needed updating/replacing. You could tell that perhaps ten or fifteen years ago this resort was beautiful, but they had done very little, if anything, to upgrade and modernize the facility. The first room I was assigned was at the end of a hallway in the main building that smelled like feet. There was a large pile of trash in front of the door of an adjacent room that sat there for hours before it was removed. The room itself was dark and the patio doors opened to a patio that was almost completely blocked by a wall and shrubbery. Only a sliver of light reached the inside of the room, making it feel cave like (or jail like) and confining. I promptly asked for another room and was assigned a casita near the spa. This room was equally as worn, however, it had a lovely view of the koi fish pond and the pool. The pools are plentiful (nine of them, to be exact) and nice, however, they seem to have a duck problem. Flocks of ducks swim in both the koi pond and the pools themselves, leaving duck poop around the entrances to the pool. On one occasion, a duck had left a gift right at the entryway to the pool, and when one of the cabana boys was alerted to its presence by one of the guests, he said he would "tell his manager" and did absolutely nothing about it. Neither he or manager did anything about that poop pile or any of other poop piles left by the duck during my four day stay. Safety might be an issue at this hotel as well. While I was sitting in my room, a gentleman opened my door with a keycard that the front desk had given him. I think we scared the living daylights out of one another. He told me that he had been assigned the room I was in, and I told him there must be some mistake. After he left, someone from the front desk called, not to apologize, but to ask me what I was doing in the room because according to the hotel's records, I was supposed to transfer rooms again on that very day. I informed her that I had no desire to move and if I had to move again it would be to another room at another hotel. The resort food is expensive, however, that wasn't my biggest problem with it. The resort has a problem with ever aggressive birds that swoop down and grab the very expensive food straight from the plates of the patrons. As people would leave their tables to retrieve food from the breakfast buffet ($25 + tip), the birds would swoop in and take a nip from people's water and juice glasses. If someone left the table with food on it, forget about it. The crow-like birds would carry everything off in an instant. The operated in packs. At one point during breakfast on Saturday, a bird flew down and pecked a woman eating breakfast. She wasn't hurt, and the restaurant staff was extremely apologetic, but they could do nothing to abate the chronic bird situation. The resort was particularly boring as well. No real activities to speak of and the pool bars, which were hopping during the day, closed at 6pm sharp, leaving most folks looking for things to do off of the resort property during the evening. Good thing self-parking was plentiful, because you could come and go as you pleased in order to find entertainment off property. The spa is sufficient, however, it's ridiculous that the only way you can use the only gym in the resort without paying an additional daily fee, is to purchase a spa treatment. If you purchase a spa treatment, access to the smallish gym is complimentary for the day of your spa treatment, however, if you don't, you have to pay $20 a day to use the gym. Final note: If you go to this resort, make sure you have mapquest directions or a GPS before you come to Phoenix. On three different occasions, I called the resort for directions and got different and wrong directions every single time. What should have taken about twenty minutes to get to the resort from the airport, ended up taking me more than an hour. I eventually just ran across it with absolutely no help from the resort staff. p.s. -- On my last morning at the resort, I made my way to one of the pools and guess what saw on the lawn? I pair of dirty mens underwear. Lovely.

tripadvisor · 2024-04-08 · 4/5view source
limited / activities

Four out of five stars Stayed here for 5 nights with family (including kids 10 and 6 yrs) in 2 rooms. Overall a 4 out of 5 – many highs about this resort but not currently operating at 5 star resort level. Cons: • Housekeeping was inconsistent. Sometimes beds straightened, sometimes not. Sometimes chocolates, sometimes not. They seem to always clean the rooms while leaving the door open, which for our rooms (where the door opened to outside hallway) allowed bugs in every day. This should be a change to their standard practices. • Service in some areas is good; other areas not. The concierge team was fantastic. Servers at Mowry & Cotton seemed overwhelmed and service was objectively bad (at dinner, I went to get water refills for the table and in search of additional menus). Pool wait staff was also overwhelmed at times, and service was mixed (over 1 hour to get a sandwich on one of the more busy days). • Limited view rooms are really limited/no view. Our rooms overlooked the roof of the convention center. There are a large number of rooms similarly situated. I have not seen a ‘luxury’ hotel with so many rooms that have objectively bad views. This is especially odd given on the other side of the rooms is the beautiful cactus garden/camelback. No clue why the hotel did not build the rooms facing something you’d actually want to look at. At least the hotel could spruce up the roof with planter boxes of plants. I was prepared for limited/no view but still surprised at how bad it was. • Kids club activities were mixed. Some of them were good, others were cheap and a waste of time and money. • Annoying fees. A $75 per night connecting room charge so my kids and I could be in rooms next to one another? Pros: • Great location at the base of Camelback. We hiked it on multiple days. You can just walk from the hotel to the Cholla trail entrance. • Overall resort build is very high quality and nice. The hotel lobby bar is great. Attention to detail in the hotel in various areas e.g. fresh flowers, falconer, is high and shows. The grounds are beautiful and well kept. The cactus garden was great. • Pool deck areas are expansive and very nice. On some days we found seating to not be an issue but on other days all chairs were claimed by early morning. Our kids loved playing in the various pools and all ages thoroughly enjoyed the water slide. • Variety of restaurant options that kept everyone happy with food options. • Amenities very good (golf, fitness club) Overall I’d be very upset paying rack rate prices with the cons above. If you can get a deal and go in eyes open to some potential flaws, it’s very good. Hopefully some of the issues above can be fixed with better training or additional staff hiring.

google · 2025-04-04 · 4/5view source

J&G Steakhouse at the Phoenician – Elevated Dining with a Minor Letdown We recently dined at J&G Steakhouse at the Phoenician, and the experience was overall very good, with standout food, excellent service, and just one disappointing detail worth noting. To start, we shared the French onion soup. The kitchen thoughtfully split it for us, which was a nice touch and set the tone for the night. The soup was warm, flavorful, and satisfying — not the best I’ve had, but definitely a solid and comforting way to begin the meal. Following that, we had the black truffle cheese fritters — six in total. These were outstanding. Rich, hot, and savory with plenty of truffle flavor, they were a highlight. That said, you do need to enjoy truffle to fully appreciate them, but for us, they were a hit. For the main course, we both ordered the 19-ounce bone-in ribeye, cooked medium-rare. Haley’s steak came out perfect — beautifully seared and full of aged flavor. Unfortunately, mine arrived very overdone, more of a medium-well. While the staff promptly took it back and corrected it, the recook took about 15–20 minutes. While I appreciate that they got it right the second time, I was a little surprised that nothing was offered — no comped dessert or gesture — for the extended wait and initial miss, especially at a restaurant of this caliber. We finished the night by sharing the carrot cake, and I have to say, it was a pleasant surprise. I’m not usually a carrot cake person, but this one was moist, well-balanced, and absolutely delicious — a great way to end the meal. Final Thoughts: Service was excellent throughout — attentive and professional. The food was mostly outstanding, and the atmosphere was what you’d expect from a fine dining spot at the Phoenician. While the mishap with my steak did dampen the flow of the evening, it was handled well, and overall, I’d still recommend J&G for a high-quality steakhouse experience. Just a little more attention to recovery would’ve made it flawless.

I recently revisited Mowry & Cotton after having a great experience there for brunch a few years ago. Unfortunately, this time around, it was a disappointing visit that didn’t live up to my prior expectations. The most noticeable difference was in the food quality, which seemed to have dropped significantly while the prices have surged. For three people, we ordered three drinks, three mains, and one appetizer, and the bill came out to a steep $200. For the price, we expected much more in terms of both flavor and presentation. For the appetizer, we tried the tomato flatbread, which was forgettable and lacked any real punch. As for the mains, we had the tacos, croque madame, and ahi tuna bowl. The barbacoa in the tacos was the only highlight—tender and flavorful—but the rest of the dish, like the other mains, felt bland and uninspired. The service didn’t redeem the experience either. Our server was distant and somewhat curt, making the overall atmosphere less enjoyable. While not outright rude, their standoffishness added to the sense that the restaurant has lost the charm it once had. In the end, Mowry & Cotton felt like an overpriced and underwhelming dining experience. With a bill that high, I was hoping for something memorable, but instead, it felt like a letdown. I give it a 4/10 and probably won’t be returning anytime soon.

I had the pleasure of dining at The Phoenician Tavern on Sunday, March 16, after church services with a friend and colleague. From the moment I entered the resort, I was captivated by the beautifully maintained grounds, the scenic drive past the golf course, and the inviting atmosphere of the tavern itself. The food was outstanding—absolutely 5-star worthy! The tavern burger was hands down the best burger I’ve had in a long time. The service was just as impressive, with a special shout-out to Daniel for his exceptional hospitality. The ambiance was lively and enjoyable, especially with the indoor-outdoor bar patio offering stunning views of the golf course. While the atmosphere was great, I’m giving it 4 stars simply because I expected a bit more of a refined resort feel. That said, I was pleasantly surprised by the unique offerings, including the St. Patrick’s Day menu, craft beer sampling, dueling pianos every Saturday, and bourbon tastings (reservations required). The Phoenician Tavern is a fantastic place to unwind, whether you’re knocking back a local craft beer, enjoying pub-style fare, or just soaking in the beautiful setting. It’s a hidden gem within a luxury resort that doesn’t feel overly formal—perfect for a laid-back yet elevated experience. I’ll definitely be back! ⭐ Food: 5/5 ⭐ Service: 5/5 (Thank you, Daniel!) ⭐ Atmosphere: 4/5

google · 2026-05-14 · 5/5view source

We had the pleasure of staying at the The Phoenician last month and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The resort itself is aesthetically beautiful, with an impressive range of activities and spaces for both families and adults. Multiple pools, several restaurants, recreational options, and quiet nooks throughout the property make it a destination where nearly everyone can find a place to relax. What stood out most, however, was the service, particularly at check-in. Christian noticed that we shared a somewhat uncommon last name and took a few extra moments to genuinely get to know us. He made the arrival process effortless, but what happened later truly surprised us. When we returned to our room that evening, we found a heartfelt handwritten welcome note along with special snacks and a thoughtfully prepared margarita cocktail ensemble. That level of personalization is increasingly rare today, especially in an era where staffing shortages often leave guests feeling rushed through transactional interactions. Experiences like this are a reminder that service is personal and meaningful, and that organizations capable of delivering it consistently likely invest well in their people and culture. The rooms were well-appointed, the beds comfortable, and the bathrooms spacious and functional. As someone who admittedly notices details like water pressure, I can report that it was more than adequate. The on-site restaurants offered a nice variety of options, and the servers throughout the resort clearly understood what genuine hospitality looks like. The Tavern in particular was lively and enjoyable, with good live music and excellent service. A couple of practical notes for future guests: reservations are highly recommended for the restaurants. The seating process can feel a bit cumbersome, with multiple hand-offs even during slower periods. Additionally, poolside service could be more attentive at times, as we occasionally needed to flag staff down. That said, those issues were minor compared to the overall experience. While five stars may feel slightly generous given the price point and a few operational inefficiencies, on a 1–10 scale this resort is a very solid 9/10 and absolutely worthy of consideration for anyone visiting Scottsdale.

Nothing about this hotel is luxury. 4 star at best. We arrived to our interconnecting rooms and walked straight back out. In what can only be compared to a motel block, the carpet was taped down with black masking tape, stains over furniture, general signs of years of wear and tear were hugely obvious. Even our balcony had some sort of juice stain that hadn’t been cleaned from the previous guests. We went back to reception to tell them we were changing hotels when they suddenly found us interconnecting rooms in the main hotel (previously unavailable). Whilst still a far stretch from what we would consider luxury - especially for close to $1000 per night per room - these were better than our previous option. Douglas agreed to modify the rate too - thank goodness because we’d have been sick paying what we’d originally committed to. However the disappointment didn’t end there. Discarded glasses and rubbish decorate communal areas. Staircases and outdoor areas haven’t had a thorough sweep or wipe down for what looks like months. Pool loungers are very uncomfortable with thin basic towels. There is a queue for breakfast everyday and you’re unable to make reservations. Free coffee machines and milk canisters are often found empty. Asked for an ice coffee at the pool but apparently this isn’t on offer and I have to go into one of the restaurants to see if they might serve it - this would be totally acceptable for a hotel that doesn’t claim to be 5 star luxury. Staff are friendly enough, but most don’t go over and above. I can only assume lacking a manager who is experienced in what 5 star luxury actually means. It appears other recent reviews emulate our experience and I only wish we had studied these before making our reservation. Kids were happy enough with tennis and pool areas. But unless this hotel has a huge overhaul, its increasingly negative reputation will get the better of it.

tripadvisor · 2025-11-02 · 5/5view source

Wonderful anniversary weekend! My wife and I spent two nights at the Phoenician in October celebrating our 28th wedding anniversary. Since I am Hilton Diamond member, we usually only stay at Hilton properties but this time we wanted to stay at the Phoenician (Marriott) since we have heard so much about the hotel over the years. While we have no membership status at Marriott, from the time we booked our reservation, my wife and I felt welcomed as a top Marriott Bonvoy member. We received an email right away from the concierge asking if we needed any assistance on our stay. When we checked in, the front desk congratulated my wife and me on our anniversary and they gave us a $50 food and beverage credit for our stay which was very nice and unexpected. The hotel also delivered a bottle of champagne and chocolates to our room our first night which again was such a nice surprise. While the Phoenician is a large hotel, it is beautiful and it is well maintained. All of the staff members were professional and courteous. We had paid for a pool view and that was worth it for the view. Due to some rainy days during our stay, we were unable to use some of the facilities like the tennis courts but we did use the work out facility which was beautiful with plenty of modern fitness equipment. We also had some really good meals at two of the restaurants. One day we had lunch at the Phoenician Tavern which is located by the golf pro shop and a short walk from the hotel. It is casual with a nice atmosphere with golf course views and good food. We celebrated our anniversary dinner at the J&G Steakhouse which was fabulous! The service was spectacular and the steaks were incredible. We would definitely recommend both restaurants and not just because of the convenience/location. Overall, we had a fabulous couple of days at the Phoenician and would highly recommend it to all. Whether it is for a couples trip or family trip with children, the hotel has something for everybody.

Where do I even start?! From the moment we arrived, The Phoenician delivered an unforgettable experience of luxury, ease, and pure indulgence. google · 2025-07-02 · 4/5view source

A Beautiful Stay with Room for Improvement The Phoenician Resort is undeniably stunning, from the breathtaking mountain views near our hotel room to the beautifully landscaped grounds, multiple pool options, and towering palm trees that truly make the resort feel like a desert oasis. However, while the scenery impressed us, several aspects of our stay fell short, especially when compared to other top resorts in the Phoenix area. Dining & Amenities: One major concern was the limited dining hours. Most on-site restaurants closed by 5:00 PM, with The Tavern being the only option open until 8:00 PM. As out-of-town guests, this left us with little choice in the evenings aside from room service or ordering out. We expected more flexibility and variety in a luxury resort. Shops & Pool Experience: All shops on the property also closed early at 5:00 PM, and pool amenities, including the water slide, music, bar, and even the water fountains, were shut down around the same time. This was disappointing, as the pool is typically a hub of activity and relaxation, especially in the summer. Children's Activities: We were especially let down by the Funicians Kids Club, which was never open during our stay. This was a major reason we selected the Phoenician, and our children were incredibly disappointed by its unavailability. Summer Activities: We appreciated the advertised “Legendary Summers” theme, but there were no events scheduled during the weekdays only on the weekends. Other Phoenix-area resorts we’ve visited provide daily family-friendly activities all summer long, so the lack of weekday activities was a letdown. Overall, while the resort is visually impressive and offers a serene setting, we felt the guest experience didn’t fully match the high rating and reputation. With a few key improvements especially around extended hours, family activities, and consistent activites the Phoenician could offer a truly legendary experience to match its branding.

Date: 06/14/25 Title: “The Best of the Best” Pros: * Guarded checkpoint at the main entrance * a luxurious resort entrance with Camelback Mountain in the backdrop. * Several accommodation options on site including under ground parking. With a fully functional parking garage. * I was very surprised how they were able to bring the classic luxury experience into 2025. * Valet is always available to assist you at the main entrance with all of your transportation needs day or night. * The main lobby entrance is very grand and opulent with people catering to your every need and fountains I mean the whole nine yards. * This location offers a true resort experience almost as if you’re away in another country. * It’s located in one of the best locations in Scottsdale across from Old Town Scottsdale and adjacent to Paradise Valley. * They have several eating options on site. Such as The Markerplace adjacent to the main lobby which is like a cafe bistro. Across from that is an actual convenience store like shop within the hotel. They have Mowry & Cotton which has a great everyday food menu with class. They also have The Tavern which is like a pub with excellent food options but more casual. They have a restaurant at the pool named Kalio. You can get food also at Thirsty Camel which is the lobby bar that has excellent food options. The crown jewel is J&G steakhouse with excellent service and views of Camelback Mountain. And lastly they have 24/7 room service. * onsite there are several activities and venues such as the Athletic Center, Tennis Courts, Game Room, Golf Center, Several Pools with a slide, The Phoenician Spa and even a kids center called Funicians Club. * There are 645 total accommodations: 577 guest rooms and 68 suites. Guest rooms span 600 square feet; suites are twice that size with one or two bedrooms. I stayed in a Grand Deluxe King w/ pool view this trip which was lovely like a mini suite. In the past I have stayed in the large suites which is just as lovely with more space. The rooms have a very classic feel but are still very modern and updated. * They have the Canyon Suites on-site which is a separate hotel within a hotel. I will review that one at a later date. Although it’s supposed to have a more personalized luxury experience. * $100 incidental per night and a $50 resort fee per night * Romantic/Nature Inspired Cactus Garden across from the main lobby entrance. Cons: * no house car anymore for everyone except VIP and people staying at the canyon suites. To be honest I’m mentioning this because it was an experience when they did have it. But of course Ubers are readily available. * there was no trash bin in my bathroom. Just overall there should have been more small trash bins in the room I had. * The property is very large. There are so many things available to do and see. Although they do provide you with a guide at check in. It would be nice to have property tours if they don’t already have this. * There were so many shops/food options available on-site that I had no idea about until I literally toured the whole property. Summary: This is the place that you stay when you have finally made it in life. Anything you want or need is here on site or close by including the stunning views of Camelback Mountain. If you’re looking for a true resort experience this place provides that and more. I believe my title for this place says it all. Thumbs Up Or Down: Thumbs Up Key People: Devin - Front Desk (a true GEM for the property with his knowledge and skillset with the charisma to match) Javier - Front Desk (another star I encountered on site. He checked me in and was able to determine exactly the experience I was looking for and he nailed it) Chad - Bell desk (exceptional service, remembered my name, and made me feel special and valued each time I encountered him) Dino - Bartender (he may be the best mixologist in Phoenix) Sydney - Hostess (The Tavern) - very knowledgeable and helpful when explaining the menu and the property.

5 Star Expectations But Mainstream Experience This place is a campus. The grounds and location present a “wow” factor and the Old World glamorous rep of this place proceeds itself so one has an expectation that it’s going to be special experience. Sadly, it is not. The resort is owned by Marriott and so it is mainstream or standard in many ways. I’d say The Spa, Fitness, golf and tennis facilities are extensive and the multiple pool options are as well providing a lot of sport variety. The resort is located at the base of Camelback Mountain so if one wants to hike the iconic mountain and tackle their challenging trails it is easy to access and there is a guided hike offered by the resort as part of resort off site activities. Where the resort falls short of 5 stars is on service - it’s a disappointment. For starters, our room was never made up. My husband and I were out at 7:15am and I came back at 5:10pm to find the room never made up. I was shocked. When I tried to call housekeeping and the front desk it rang and I sat on hold for several minutes. So I have yet to make contact with a manager. I must say the staff at the Spa is very attentive and accommodating and the menu there is lovely. Not Worth The Money This was one of the most disappointing resorts we have ever visited. My husband had planned a big surprise for my 60th b-day going to a warm sunny place in November to enjoy the beautiful pools this hotel offered. Upon arrival we encountered very persistent valet attendants. Without checking in they insisted on taking our suitcases from our car and holding them until we checked in. After standing in a very long line to check in because there was only one attendant available and the line was out the door, I took a walk only find that the entire main pool was under major construction. Something that was not mentioned prior to reservation made or at check in. After check-in we were told about the two pools available, however, the lower pool was off limits due to a convention. So, we really only had use to the smallest pool on the grounds. We then had to wait for our car to load it back up to head to the other end where the casitas are located. We reserved a casita, a little more exclusive and private. Once we got settled in, we realized right outside our door they were setting up for the convention dinner, no privacy at all. The casitas are very outdated, not very clean, mattress needs to be replaced and the tiny shower was covered in mold (see photos). We headed to the hot tubs that we were told would be available. Currently it is a maze of construction to get through only to find one of the hot-tub is off limits and the other had warm water with no jets. The next morning, we requested a room change, we were moved to the main building. The rooms are much more spacious and updated and all though it has a large bathroom the shower is still very small. We had a very nice balcony that would normally oversee the main pool. If you like quiet, this is not the spot. They have their private events there every night. At the time we were there you either could hear the party and music or the construction noise. We asked what options they could offer us as the front desk was also not aware about their hot tubs off limits. We were offered a one- day pass to the spa for the next day. We decided to give the spa a try. Apparently, something they don’t normally offer. Upon arrival, the spa manager was already aware we were coming and was very gracious as he proceeds to let us know there was an electrical problem on the men’s side and the steam room was not working. The spaces are separated for men and women so we would not be able to spend our time together. We skipped the spa. On this second day when returned from being out all day to a room that had not been serviced all day. We called to get it cleaned and were told they would send someone. The evening housekeeper that does the turndown showed up, was very apologetic for the morning staff but could only get trash and send someone else. After waiting for 45 minutes a lady showed up with towels and a lack of desire to clean anything. If you are a golfer, the course is beautiful and the gym was very nice surrounded by glass with views of the grounds. Overall, this hotel was very disappointing and for the cost I would choose something newer and with better service.

I recently stayed at The Phoenician in Scottsdale with my wife and kids, and after reading all the glowing reviews, I just don’t understand the hype. It was fine, but I wouldn’t call it luxury by any means, nor exceptional, especially considering the price or the points required for a stay here. As a Gold Elite member with years of travel experience, I’ve come to recognize top-notch service and value, but this resort falls short in nearly every category. First impressions matter, and our check-in experience wasn’t great. We didn’t feel welcomed or even like we were at a luxury resort. The staff member who checked us in barely explained anything about the property—just handed me a map and a booklet and sent us on our way. The main pool area was closed for maintenance, and the kids' splash park wasn’t working when we tried to use it—not once, but twice. The only other pool available for kids was cold! Honestly, no one else was in it because it felt unheated, and after talking to a few guests, they agreed it was too cold. We also didn’t see any pool attendants around to ask about life jackets or pool toys, or anything that might make the experience better if the pool was heated. The kids' club or play area was also closed on Monday, so there was literally nothing for our kids to do for the first couple of days of our stay. Fortunately, we had a larger unit with a hot tub and a golf cart to get around, which helped salvage the experience—without that, there wouldn’t have been much to do. Speaking of the hot tub, not good. After using it on Sunday, the next day all of us had rashes or skin breakouts. We suspect it was from the excessive chlorine, as there was an unusually thick layer of foam and bubbles in the tub. Our 5-year-old, 1.5-year-old, and both adults all had reactions. Room 7704 itself was disappointing, especially for the price and points required. It’s showing its age—there were missing pieces of flooring near the dining table (my wife actually hurt her toe), cracks and dents in the walls, and the doors don’t close properly. The whole place just felt a bit run-down. I certainly wouldn’t pay thousands to stay here. The wifi also didn’t work for our entire stay which wasn’t ideal at all. I had a couple of meetings Monday and no wifi. Costing me money to use data. We called down to have someone come up and check it out Sunday but nobody came for almost 2 hours. Called back to inform them nobody came by, kids had to go to sleep. They were going to update the ticket and have someone come by Monday. Nobody came, no follow up, nothing. Just terrible service. We also ordered food from the Tavern one night, and it was mediocre at best—not worth the price at all. Save your money and eat elsewhere. As a Gold Elite member, I expected better treatment, especially with pools being closed and limited activities for kids on certain days of the week. We were hoping for an upgrade to a unit with a pool, which is supposed to happen as a gold elite member (enhanced room upgrade benefit) but despite some of the other residences being vacant both nights, they didn’t offer us anything. They were more focused on charging extra for upgrades than making sure we had a better experience, even though we were loyal members with kids and limited options at the resort. Honestly, I regret spending 240,000 points to stay here. This resort was a major disappointment overall, and I’ll definitely be looking elsewhere next time. It was a huge waste of both time and points. I encourage others looking to spend their hard earned dollars or points to look elsewhere. For those of you who love this place, glad you enjoyed it and had a better experience. I know it’s hard to please everyone and it’ll rarely happen but we felt overall, it simply underwhelming and not worth it.

My husband and I just enjoyed 4 nights at the resort. Service was amazing. Javier at guest registration was very kind and accommodating. His service set the tone. We rented cabana’s at the adult only pool which was awesome. They included the cabana with seating within, 4 lounge chairs by the pool, as well as a patio table with seating for 4. The rental could comfortably accommodate 6-8 people as long as everyone doesn’t need to be on a lounge at the same time. there were lots of other perks like snacks, several treats throughout the day, sunscreen, etc. Christine and Raymond were our attendants and both were superb, really excellent service and nice people. He was very professional and had a strong yet not unpleasant technique to tackle the knots in my back. After our services we spent the day at the private spa rooftop pool. High-class eats, low-class sleeps My wife and I stayed here in room 6054 (a "1 King Bed, Superior Guest Room") for two nights in September 2024. Rating: 8/10 Positives: • Spectacular Dining: The dining options here were truly outstanding. From steaks under the city lights at J & G Steakhouse, to chimichurri breakfast potatoes at Mowry & Cotton, afternoon tea at Thirsty Camel, and pub grub at The Phoenician Tavern, this hotel boasts an impressive array of culinary experiences. I rated each of these restaurants a solid five stars. • Inviting Pool Areas: The resort offers several inviting pools and outdoor lounge areas, all complemented by excellent poolside service and equally impressive cocktails. • Reasonable Room Rates: Although room rates at this resort can sometimes be steep, we enjoyed very reasonable prices for a hotel of this caliber during our September stay. Of course, this did come with triple-digit heat at the pool, but it was a fair trade-off! • On-Site Convenience: The variety of on-site stores for treats, coffee, and sundries meant that we had everything we needed without ever having to leave the resort. This added to the sense of luxury and convenience throughout our stay. Negatives: • Uncomfortable Sleep: Unfortunately, we didn’t sleep well. The bed was worn, uneven, and quite uncomfortable. To make matters worse, the front desk confirmed that the hotel uses motion sensors to throttle the air conditioning when it detects no movement in the room. The real-world implication is that the air conditioning shuts off at night while guests are asleep—precisely when it’s most needed. It’s baffling that a 5-star resort would use such a flawed system that disrupts guest sleep. For me, no amount of dazzling amenities can make up for a bad night’s rest. • Chromecast Issues: On our first night, we struggled for half an hour to get the TV’s advertised Chromecast feature to work, only to give up and resort to streaming on our own iPad propped up on the bed. The next day, the front desk informed us that Chromecast was currently non-operational across the entire resort and offered a $100 credit for the inconvenience. While the gesture was appreciated, this level of technical oversight was frustrating. • Inconvenient Late Checkout Process: As a Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite member, I was granted a much-appreciated 2pm late checkout. However, I was told that our existing keys would stop working at 11am, requiring me to visit the front desk for new keys. When I went to do so, I had to wait in line for 20 minutes with people checking in, just to get access to my own room. This inefficient process overshadowed the benefit of the late checkout and left a negative impression. • Bland Room Décor: The room’s gray decor felt bland and uninviting, lacking the warmth and luxury you would expect from a 5-star resort. A design refresh would go a long way in making the rooms feel more comfortable and welcoming.

tripadvisor · 2024-06-24 · 5/5view source

Great location, top notch service Had a conference in AZ (different resort) and decided to have my wife fly out and go ot the Phoenician for a couple of nights. A few friends had recommended it and I am so glad they did. We really enjoyed our stay and the entire property. The property, while architecturally a little dated, has been updated so well. On top of that everyone on the staff we interacted with was so fantastic and helpful and really seemed to want to make our stay something memorable. Room: We did not stay in the main building, but booked one of the casitas, which are out buildings below the pool area neat the spa and golf course. inside they are standard hotel rooms but from the outside they have the feel that maybe they were originally intended to be apartments/ condos. We wanted to go for this set up since we had plans at the golf course, spa, and ‘Mother of Pearl’ pool which is closest to the casitas. We were very happy with this decision as we were very close to those things and felt like we had more privacy. Point of clarification: There are two types of casitas. The regular casitas are along the back row of casitas and face towards either a parking lot, the golf club house, or a parking deck. We booked the Deluxe Casita which is guaranteed to face toward the pools and Camelback Mountain. We had a regular king room, but I believe they have some large casitas with fire pits outside and even fireplaces inside if you are there in winter months. Food: While it si resort food so not cheap, there wasn’t a single thing we ordered and ate that we regretted. It was all delicious and you could tell it was prepared with care. We ended up having food from basically every restaurant option at the resort and you can’t go wrong with any. The pool side restaurant and service is perfect for eating outside pool side. Cotton and Mowry is great variety , and J&G has some incredible views. MY wife’s favorite was actually the Tavern which is above the golf pro shop. Each place had fantastic service,so props to the place for the training of the staff. Pool: We were there in June which is not the busiest, but it didn’t bother us. The pools at The PHoenician are great. I surprised my wife with a cabana rental at the Mother of Pearl pool for our full day there and it really elevated the experience. The cabanas have ceiling fans and TVs in them and we really didn’t need to go anywhere all day. There are plenty of chairs and umbrellas even without the caban rental of course and we noticed the staff always being very attentive to all guests in moving umbrellas to t keep their things in the shade. Rich was the assigned staff for our cabana and he was the best. There are several other pools as well at the resort, including a kids splash zone and a water slide. Golf: The golf course at The Phoenician is run and managed by Troon Golf, so you can expect great conditions and good service. It delivered on that for sure. As for the course itself, I will say that if you are looking for classic desert golf, this won’t be your course. Conditions are great, but the front nine feels like playing a residential muni or country club. Lots of houses all around and you even ahve to drive through as construction site at one point. The back nine is where it is at on this course. The front and back are far from one another, but once yo get to th back, it’s a different course. You are on the slopes of Camelback Mountain and the views are outstanding on each and every hole. Spa: While I was golfing my wife was at the spa. She loved everything inside. She spent some time on the rooftop pool and said it was enjoyable, but to know there are no views at that pool like there are at the regular resort pools. Fitness Center: I have to call this out. The gym at The Phoenician is without a doubt the best hotel/ resort gym I have ever used and it is not even close. It is a little bit of a walk from the buildings and over by the tennis courts, but once your are up there you see why they put it where they did. Tennis/ Pickleball: Several courts dedicated for both. We didn’t play tennis, but saw others using the courts. We did play some pickleball using paddles and balls provided by the resort which was super easy. The courts did seem like they were not being used much or needed a good cleaning, but were in perfectly good shape. Shops: There are retail shops everywhere. The golf shop, below the gym near the tennis courts is the tennis shop, then there are a set up shops attached to the main building. They all have variations of things depending onto e activity they pertain to. They are all well appointed and serviced well. My wife found a hat she liked at the tennis shop and I found one I liked at the golf shop. The other shops were great for buying things for our kids. We do wish they had more T shirt options specifically featuring the phoenician logo. Other Activities: We did not do any of the organized activities, but there were plenty offered. We did walk through the cactus garden on the back side of the property and enjoyed that being from a very different part of the country. Overall I would recommend a stay at the Phoenician to anyone. Could work for couples but also families. Beautiful setting and fantastic service all around.

We were upgraded to a poolside room upon arrival, the room was very large (huge bathroom), with great linens and comfortable beds. tripadvisor · 2024-04-08 · 4/5view source

Four out of five stars Stayed here for 5 nights with family (including kids 10 and 6 yrs) in 2 rooms. Overall a 4 out of 5 – many highs about this resort but not currently operating at 5 star resort level. Cons: • Housekeeping was inconsistent. Sometimes beds straightened, sometimes not. Sometimes chocolates, sometimes not. They seem to always clean the rooms while leaving the door open, which for our rooms (where the door opened to outside hallway) allowed bugs in every day. This should be a change to their standard practices. • Service in some areas is good; other areas not. The concierge team was fantastic. Servers at Mowry & Cotton seemed overwhelmed and service was objectively bad (at dinner, I went to get water refills for the table and in search of additional menus). Pool wait staff was also overwhelmed at times, and service was mixed (over 1 hour to get a sandwich on one of the more busy days). • Limited view rooms are really limited/no view. Our rooms overlooked the roof of the convention center. There are a large number of rooms similarly situated. I have not seen a ‘luxury’ hotel with so many rooms that have objectively bad views. This is especially odd given on the other side of the rooms is the beautiful cactus garden/camelback. No clue why the hotel did not build the rooms facing something you’d actually want to look at. At least the hotel could spruce up the roof with planter boxes of plants. I was prepared for limited/no view but still surprised at how bad it was. • Kids club activities were mixed. Some of them were good, others were cheap and a waste of time and money. • Annoying fees. A $75 per night connecting room charge so my kids and I could be in rooms next to one another? Pros: • Great location at the base of Camelback. We hiked it on multiple days. You can just walk from the hotel to the Cholla trail entrance. • Overall resort build is very high quality and nice. The hotel lobby bar is great. Attention to detail in the hotel in various areas e.g. fresh flowers, falconer, is high and shows. The grounds are beautiful and well kept. The cactus garden was great. • Pool deck areas are expansive and very nice. On some days we found seating to not be an issue but on other days all chairs were claimed by early morning. Our kids loved playing in the various pools and all ages thoroughly enjoyed the water slide. • Variety of restaurant options that kept everyone happy with food options. • Amenities very good (golf, fitness club) Overall I’d be very upset paying rack rate prices with the cons above. If you can get a deal and go in eyes open to some potential flaws, it’s very good. Hopefully some of the issues above can be fixed with better training or additional staff hiring.

tripadvisor · 2023-12-20 · 3/5view source

Taking away more and more from loyal customers I had just seen U2 in Vegas and wanted to extend my vaca someplace a little warmer, so my friends and I decided to spend 5 days in Phoenix. The Phoenician is a beautiful property in Scottsdale and it's also pretty close to a lot of great shopping and restaurants. I'm a Platinum Elite member of Bonvoy so I get special perks from Marriott properties. I've been to tons of Marriott properties and when you check they offer either 1,000 points or breakfast for 2 for the stay. It always seemed like an odd choice, I mean unless you don't eat breakfast? We took the breakfast. Another perk is being offered an upgrade (if available). No upgrade was available. We checked into our room. We got in after midnight, so bedtime was fairly immediate. Breakfast is served at a nice restaurant at the main hotel, Mowry & Cotton. The menu has a nice selection of choices. The first day I had their French Toast. It was exceptional. When we got back to the room, I finally opened the curtains and there was a huge surprise. There was a wall very close to the balcony. Maybe a couple feet and it was as high to block pretty much everything. I really couldn't believe my eyes. I really had no idea what was going on? How could a hotel be built like this? Excepting this wall was for real and not some kind of prank I thought this is the kind of room you would give to your worst customer. And yet here I was, a Plat Elite staring at a wall? A made a call and low and behold another room was available and we eventually moved over to the new room and the vaca could continue. Unfortunately for myself the next day I got some kind of sinus infection which would slow me down for the rest of the trip, but my 2 friends enjoyed their time at the pools. The pools are very nice. 3 big pools, 2 Jacuzzis, hundreds of lounge chairs, although Marriott has started a new policy where the best chairs are roped off and you have to pay more money to sit there. Status means nothing for these chairs. On the day we were checking out I received an email with the final bill. When checking it I noticed the breakfast charges were a bit high, considering we were supposed to get credit for 2 breakfasts each day. Btw, this restaurant includes the tip. I thought that was odd. I missed it on the first day, so they got a nice big tip that day. I called about and the front desk couldn't explain it. A manager from the restaurant called me a told me the free breakfast was only 1 choice on the menu. Mostly everything on the breakfast menu was over $22, but the last breakfast on the menu, the Continental was around $15. I think it was yogurt and a croissant. He asked if anyone, the front desk, any waiter or waitress, had explained this and I told him no, no one has said anything about it. He told me he would make some adjustments, and I said fine. The bill I received was $399. btw, valet parking was $38 and self was $28. We went with the valet. So nobody got back to me so I stopped by the front desk to ask for a final bill. The woman printed it out, but something still didn't add up. She said she would review it and call me. She called later after we left the hotel and said she was going to take off $120 and I said that was great. Later I received a new email and the grand total now was over $600. That's right, the bill actually went up. Once again, beyond belief. I called and asked if a manager could contact me. Not feeling well the last 4 days I was at the hotel made this exiting experience even worse. $399 (old bill) - $120 = $279 $612 (new bill) - $279 = $333, so since I contacted the front desk about charges for breakfast I am now paying $213 more than that bill. I know that was hard to follow, but it's because there are more than 1 moving parts. I'm home now, and no one has contacted me. A very nice resort, but as you can see, the hotel has some issues, and it all rubs the wrong was for Marriott and its guests. I really hate writing negative reviews, but I gave this hotel several chances to explain themselves, but I feel I'm being ignored. A wall.

At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, “I am sorry mam, there is nothing we can do.” Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items. We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $1,500 at Neiman Marcus just down the street so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, “Things get stolen from the pool all the time” - If that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority. Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant (>$500) but not catastrophic. The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can’t list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property. Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, “I am sorry, we can’t track that.” How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff “If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately.” With today’s tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests. Moral of the Story: Don’t take anything valuable to the pool and Don’t rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do. (11/15 Follow up to Mr. Fredricks response) With all due respect Ben, I find it a bit disingenuous to be told I am getting a “response from the business owner” when in reality it is a room operations manager who has been in the workforce for just over six years. I don’t mean to slight you directly Ben, you could be highly proficient at your role and I know this lack of attention to our case is not orchestrated by you. The frustration is with your bosses who are merely applying damage control. It is a strategy as old as time, deflect and neglect. Placate the upset client with feckless apologies in hopes they just go away. You allude to hints of action, “steps are being taken“ . . . Please feel free to contact us with what exactly these are. We accept your “sincere apologies” but six weeks later, we are awaiting to see what these might be.

I was invited to a private cocktail hour by the sponsor of the conference I am attending. I am a black woman and I arrived with my colleagues who are black and Hispanic. We arrived to the happy hour and spoke to the host. We mingled and said hello to a few attendees. One we sat down and looked over the menu, a waitress came over to take our order. She asked me for my card to start a tab. I thought this was odd because it was a private cocktail event and the host was paying for everything. I gave her my card. I checked in with another attendee and asked if we were paying for our drinks and food. They told me no. When the waitress returned I told her that I was a part of the private event and she said "Oh, someone told me that you all snuck into the back of this event and you're not with them." She politely returned my card, however, that doesn't change the racial bias that I experienced at the hands of this hotel. Before taking our initial order she could've asked if we were a part of private event. She could've asked the host. Yet, instead she chose to believe something the "someone" told her. These are microagressions. There was a lack of respect for me because if it was a private event and I want not meant to be in that area, she could've asked me to move. This is how racism persists because two black people and a Hispanic person look like they don't belong at an upscale event at a luxury hotel. My night was soured and my experience at this hotel event as an invited guest was ruined.

tripadvisor · 2022-08-20 · 5/5view source

Best Resort in the Valley of the Sun! I thought it apropos to review of an establishment visited very, very often for both day visits and staycations, special events, and culminating in some incredible memories – our absolute fave combined resort, spa and restos in the Valley. Having the opportunity to regularly stay over many accommodations across and occasionally outside the country, not a professional hotel reviewer by any means, and not a regular business traveler - but as a primarily pleasure and needs wanderer, I have developed as what I believe is my concise method for scoring the worthiness of each hotel visited. A little exception for this establishment is necessary though, since my wife and I enjoy staycating here very often and find the amenities, eateries and then some, very satisfying and enjoyable. The Phoenician spa lives up to its hoopla from massages to aromatherapy. For swimming and lounging in the sun the Phoenician has its main pools, lazy river or the Spa Pools. For contemplating a valley view while imbibing some of the best The Valley can offer The Thirsty Camel Bar has its cool, modern and relaxing inside, or the outside patio with live music and firepits. Or you can select being more recluse in the Phoenician Tavern! If you want an upscale yet casual dinner there’s Mowry & Cotton, which has been our only disenchantment to date at the Phoenician. They have gift shops with above average quality items, for adults and children alike. The poolside Kalio Kabobery Mediterranean offers an above average menu. Get your morning coffee and then some at the Marketplace Coffee House. If you your into Hi-Tea or Afternoon Tea you can’t go wrong with our fave Valley Tea, Afternoon Tea & Champagne offering in the English tradition, with tasty selections of Finger Sandwiches, Fresh Baked Scones, not to mention the pastries, along with some incredible tea selections. Love it! Combining the aforementioned with my criteria are as follows and the results are: 1) ease of access to and from public or private ground transportation [Score:4.5]; 2) convenient and safe parking [Score:5.0]; 3) access, accuracy and convenience of check in and check out [Score:5.0]; 4) atmosphere, ambience, public facilities, lounging areas and access to an office center and Wi-Fi access [Score:5.0]; 5) overall customer service - including but not limited to Hospitality, Support Services, Concierge knowledge, communication, attitude and demeanor of staff [Score:5.0]; 6) quality, cleanliness, value, convenience, amenities (i.e., ironing board, iron, TV, charging access, phone, et.al.) and comfort of rooms, beds, room safe and/or valet services [Score:5.0]; Taking all the aforementioned categories in a scale of 1 star to 5 stars with 1 being the worst and 5 being the best a hotel can be! This hotel rates a: 4.9. If you have an opportunity to experience the Grifin Club you will most definitely appreciate the upcharge, and being a Member of Marriott’s Bonvoy goes a long, long way! Great work staff and management, kudos and congrats for work well done. We’ll just keep coming back!

tripadvisor · 2022-06-24 · 5/5view source

Birthday Staycation I was looking for something low-key, relaxing, and fun for my family and I to do for my birthday. We live in Queen Creek so we were looking for a good spot for a staycation. I never liked the idea of staycation, why spend your money where you live? It’s not really a wise investment considering you’re not having a new adventure? However, the way things have been going for me recently, that’s all I wanted. I wanted to pack up the family, but not have to worry about the anxiety of going to an airport, flight delays, “flightmares,” etc. We decided upon the Phoenician as I am a Marriott ambassador and it is part of the luxury collection of Marriott. I used my points for a two night stay with my husband and one year old. They upgraded us to a beautiful room on the ground floor called the Casita. It had a beautiful garden and fire pit outside but the room itself was very small. Typically we have much larger rooms. As an ambassador I get a certain amount of suite nights where I can put in a request to get upgraded to a suite. Anytime I’ve ever used that it’s always been accepted, but this time around it wasn’t. Too bad because I’ve had a horrible year and I really wanted that for my stay here. It’s also difficult with my one-year-old because he sleeps much better with his own space and when we have a suite he will have his own room. What was cool is that we didn’t have to park in any parking lot. We had our own parks parking spot right there outside of our room. It also only cost about $14 a night which isn’t bad for a resort. You do have to pay resort fees which I believe are $49 a night and include the regular resort fee type things like activities, etc. We took advantage of one of the activities because they had a play time out on the splash pad for kids. They had some toys for my son to play with. The concierge was absolutely lovely. They have a whole team of people and we checked in with them often to make reservations, ask questions, etc. We ate at Cotton & Mowry the first night we were there and that was delicious. I will do a separate review on the restaurants. I actually enjoyed that restaurant more for breakfast than anything. I thought they would have a buffet breakfast, but they only had a sit down. It was delicious. The service there is great as well. They were very accommodating to my one year-old. The second night we dined at J&G Steakhouse. That’s not open on Mondays and Tuesdays. It was very fancy and very fun to celebrate my birthday dinner there. A separate review on that as well, great food, great service. I took advantage of the spa which I will try to do a separate review on as well. I made myself a massage appointment for the first day we got there. I was so happy I did that. It was one of the best spa experiences I’ve ever had and I already cannot wait to go back. The massage itself was amazing, my massage therapist is named Zach. He was great. What I really loved about this experience was the amenities. I felt so relaxed. It was the first time in a long time I’ve gone to the spa with a really amazing amenities. They had a steam room, a sauna, a large hot tub. A gigantic and beautiful quiet room, a locker room, showers, everything you would want and more. They serve tea, snacks, different flavored waters, it was so relaxing and so fun. My only regret is that I didn’t have more time there. They also have a rooftop pool. You can chill there, order off the menu, they have a bar and they also have fun nonalcoholic drinks. You can also rent a cabana while you’re there. I only had about an hour to enjoy all the amenities before my service, and I was able to enjoy everything within that hour, but if you wanted to spend more time relaxing, maybe fall asleep in a quiet room or at the pool, you definitely want to maybe make a day of it. You do not need to be a hotel guest in order to use the spa. Although, you do need to book a service in order to use the amenities, meaning they don’t let you pay just to use the amenities. I kind of like that, actually because it made the spa not busy at all. At one point, I swear I was the only person there. They also have a great gift shop on your way out if you’re looking to spend some extra money as everything is very expensive. Skin care, hair products, workout clothes, yoga wear, candles, & aromatherapy, etc. On the day of my birthday we rented a cabana for $325. We were at a very quiet pool and there were only a few people who rented a cabana and they all had families as well so it was very kid friendly. It was great to have a private spot to keep us out of the sun, however it was still very hot there. They don’t have any kind of cooling system or misters in there. Just the shade. They have a TV, they give you a choice of a complimentary champagne or a food item as well as a fully stocked refrigerator with water, Gatorade, etc. You get your own personal server who comes in and wait on you. I thought the price of the cabana was pretty high in comparison to what we actually got, but it definitely made the day more fun and more private. There are three pools there on site. There’s a big splash pad for the kids, there is a pool restaurant, and of course the opportunity to rent cabanas. The food was really good at the pool. We ordered fish tacos, and as our complimentary item we got chips and salsa with guacamole, we also ordered the hummus tray. The drinks were just OK. Honestly, my son‘s banana smoothie was probably the most delicious thing. I ordered a beer and a vodka drink and my husband ordered a beer and a margarita but the liquor drinks were very weak. The same person who waits on you also makes the drinks. It was a nice day. Honestly, I was a little bit disappointed about the room, although it was nice to sit outside after we put the baby to bed and enjoy our wine by the fire pit and watch the sun go down. Being from Queen Creek it definitely felt cooler with the mountains blocking some of that sun, and I think the big take away was the pool day and the spa experience. The restaurants were great as well. I thought the service was good. Normally at Marriotts when they know you are celebrating a birthday, they send something, a letter, card, food tray, or wine to the room, they really didn’t do anything like that. I thought in terms of hospitality, that was lacking. Otherwise, I definitely recommend staying here. It’s a beautiful resort. They also have an athletic club and a golf course that I did not take advantage of but that looked beautiful.
