tripadvisor · 2022-01-04 · 4/5view source

Exceeded Expectations The Phoenician is a large resort - my expectations were not high and I have to say we really enjoyed our time here. The rooms are not “new” or stylish, but I had nothing to complain about in terms of cleanliness or “worn out” furniture. We did have a very large room (Executive Suite) and I did not feel like there was enough furniture to fill the room up adequately but the bed was comfortable and there was so much space for my family (2 adults, 2 kids). Our room did not have a great view - looked out onto a concrete structure - we were trying to decide if we wanted to ask for a better view but looking at the layout of the hotel, it seems like many of the rooms do NOT have a view. I can see how this could be very disappointing to some people and while it would have been really nice, ultimately it didn’t affect our overall enjoyment. One additional quirk was there was a cricket stuck between the walls (we spied an antenna) who was pretty loud at night. We did not get the staff to do anything about it because we didn’t want them to spray chemicals near where our kids were sleeping. We were there at a busy time of year - the biggest issue with that was that every morning when we tried to get breakfast at the main restaurant, Mowry and Cotton, there was a very long wait. And the restaurant staff definitely seemed a bit overwhelmed. One of the best things about the resort was the pool scene. Plenty of chairs such that I didn’t feel the need to ever fight for a spot. More importantly, the staff at the pool was the best. Our favorite was Gennaro (I am so sorry but I probably have his name wrong - it starts with a G though. He was really great and memorable but it’s been over a month since we stayed and I am not good with names!). Literally as soon as you sit down they bring you a pitcher of ice water and replenish throughout the day. Additionally I think the pool menu is much better and more inventive than the usual pool menu at other resorts. I read some people complain about the music by the pool but I liked it. I would be the first to complain if it was too loud but I never found that to be the case and I liked the soundtrack. We also loved utilizing the pickleball/basketball/tennis courts. Easy to get court reservations even at this busy time of year and easy to borrow equipment. It’s a great amenity. Finally, we had dinner one night at J&G and enjoyed it immensely - the views are spectacular and the food was so good. (We hadn’t planned ahead and didn’t know anything about the restaurant beforehand - the concierge booked the table for us on our first day of our stay). Overall, we had a really nice experience here - I am surprised to say that we want to go back already!

Amazing!!! We had a perfect stay for the last 5 days! We travel often and enjoy high end accommodations and experiences and I cannot say enough great things about this resort. It is beautiful and well maintained. We stayed in a king room on the 4th floor and we had an amazing view of the property. The room was huge, with two closets, an enormous bathroom with a big tub (wish there were bath salts to use in the tub!), step in glass shower, separate toilet, a long counter and full wall of mirrors. The bed was very comfortable. The room and entire resort were immaculate and very well cleaned. The front desk staff was professional and attentive and always available (in person at the desk, calling them from the room isn’t helpful as the phone just rings and rings). The valet team…amazing! Always there to assist, offer bottled waters, etc. The pools were wonderful. Plenty of chairs because there are so many pools! The pool attendants are constantly refreshing pitchers of ice water for you and the pool servers are always around offering drinks and food if you’d like. The pool service is fast! The spa is the best we have ever been too…and I am a spa person. The epitome of relaxation, the spa, the staff, music, services, amenities and treatment cannot be beat! We had our treatments first thing in the morning and then got to spend the day at the spa enjoying the sauna, steam room, relaxation areas, whirlpool and our favorite…the rooftop pool. It’s quiet and wonderful. The Thirsty Camel is a great bar in the lobby that has a beautiful outdoor area with fire pits at night and a good menu for small bites. We loved the restaurant Cotton and Mowry for two of our breakfasts. Good selection and ambiance. Excellent service and the food came quickly…and tasted amazing. tripadvisor · 2021-05-28 · 3/5view source

Gorgeous views, fabulous food, but not worth the expense of staying on site General: The food is excellent, but you'd be better off staying literally anywhere else and just visiting the restaurants. It's exorbitantly expensive, and they still charge you for something every time you turn around, and provide you the absolute bare minimum for a hotel stay (of any tier). The service would probably be great if they didn't overwork their employees and had more staff to take care of their guests. Oh, and don't think you can get in anywhere to eat or relax during your stay unless you've made reservations several days ahead of time. I have provided more detailed pros/cons below. You have been warned! Negative: -Room- My mother and I flew to AZ to aid in a family health issue, and because it was going to be a long and stressful visit, I thought I would treat my mother and myself to a stay at this luxurious resort (it was Mother's Day as well, after all). Because we would be spending all of our downtime during these 10 days at the resort, I wanted to make sure we had an absolutely spectacular view, as shown in the pictures on their website. Upon booking I emphasized this factor, and the concierge helped guide my room selection appropriately, although they recommended a follow up call before I flew out to verify the room selection. I called twice before arriving to verify, and each time was assured of the beautiful garden views we'd get to enjoy during our 10-day extended stay. I traveled for 16 hours to get there, and at the end of a long day, I arrived late in the evening for check in. Before even going to the room to get settled for the night, I again verified the room requirements with the concierge. He said he was unsure of the view of that room, but if we were unsatisfied with the space once we got there, he would happily move us. (This is laughable in retrospect). It took several minutes to get to our room, as it was the very last one at the end of the hotel, past many utility spaces and conference rooms. It was probably a storage space that was later converted to a room. The room was spacious, but seemed unfinished (some items in the room were still extremely dirty (spilled makeup, and a few unknown substances), there was a garbage bag still in the room, and the beds looked as though they'd merely been made, not newly cleaned). I was so exhausted after traveling so long that I was willing to let these issues go so I could get to sleep. But then we opened the draperies to assess our "beautiful view" that we'd be gazing at for the next 10 days: it was the gravel rooftop, huge metal exhaust vents for the hotel, and their loading dock where utility vehicles and delivery men frequented! It was so ludacris it seemed to be a cruel joke. The bellhop asked about where to put our luggage, and I felt awful making him wait, but the concierge insisted we call if there were any issues with the view, and this was too much to overlook. However, after being on hold for almost 10 minutes, I finally got through to the concierge, only to find out that moving us to another room would be IMPOSSIBLE as they had every. single. room. booked out for the next several days. And this was not at limited capacity due to Covid restrictions, this was every single room being taken up on the entire property! About halfway through our stay they'd have a room open up elsewhere on the property, but until then we were stuck. When we moved, we were glad to at least have a better view, but the second room was so cramped that you couldn't leave the room if either of the closets or the bathroom doors were open! Surely this is a fire hazard?! We also had an alarming cleanliness issue in the new room (the second day of our stay there we discovered someone had spilled popcorn in our room in the middle of the floor while we'd been out! There isn't even a microwave in the room, and this happened while we were gone during the day, so it was very alarming to find). The first day of our stay I bought a full sized Lysol container at the store and cleaned the room myself each day, wary of what happens when we are out of the space. I spent almost $10,000 on this trip for my mother (who'd I not been able to see in two years) and there were an alarming number of disappointments for a hotel of this caliber. -I realized upon hiking the grounds that the lovely views they show on the website of the gorgeous flowering trees, hillsides, or even the lovely cactus garden are not from the hotel at all, but rather small private houses they have on the grounds that you can rent. That would have been nice to know ahead of time when booking! -A severe lack of service (people not returning with what they were sent to obtain, delivery office closed, finding out about the calendar of activities AFTER it was too late to do any of them) -Reservations are a necessity (this would have been nice to know ahead of time). Don't expect a meal or a spa appointment whatsoever unless you've called several days ahead of time! We were "lucky" that we were staying so long (10 days) that we were able to make a couple appointments at the end of our visit. I heard many disappointed guests in line for the concierge who were only staying over the weekend and couldn't even get into the restaurant or get so much as their nails painted! -Spa costs vs. poor quality massage. I have held memberships at multiple spas, and this one was not only the most expensive massage I'd ever received, but also of the poorest quality. Multiple times I had to ask for firmer pressure (not once was I asked if the pressure was okay), and several techniques were just silly or unproductive. Even the most novice massage therapists know to not rub someone's spinal column! Gah. It was an uncomfortable and awful experience that I anxiously awaited to end (which thankfully was brief, as your 1-hour massage includes a 10 minutes consultation on your areas to focus on (all my comments were ignored), 10 minutes of you "changing" even though you are merely in a robe at this point, and 10 minutes at the end of you changing back to your robe). So it was $200+ per person plus tip for about 30 minutes of an uncomfortable massage. If it wasn't for the other amenities (private rooftop pool access, steam rooms, hot tubs) and the absolutely exceptional service by the locker room attendants (WOW! They are incredible, detail-oriented, and they know what you need before you know you need it!) then it wouldn't even be worth going at all. -There were no perks or benefits to extended stay guests. People with short stays (one, two days) seemed to be treated extra well. -Toiletry and room amenities on par with a motel. Here you got the standard "Shampoo/Conditioner/Body Wash/Lotion" but that was it! Hotels of similar quality provide their guests with everything from mouthwash to showercaps to lip balm and shoe buffing kits. Oh, and one bar of soap to last your entire stay, no matter how many people are in the room or how long you're staying, is just not acceptable. And we actually had to ask for more TP on more than one occasion (there was only the single roll in the room, and it was not replaced each day or an extra placed elsewhere. They only replaced it once it was literally gone). -Fees for EVERYTHING. You pay $33 a day for valet (plus tip), on top of already being charged an additional $40 per day for "self parking" access. So even without going anywhere or even using your vehicle onsite, you are spending $73 dollars a day!!! Also, even though you pay a $40 Resort Fee per day because you are staying at a resort with a variety of amenities, you still also have to PAY for many of those amenities (rental fee in golf putting green, spa, equipment rentals, etc.). Also, they don't even have enough of items to allow their guests to utilize them. For example, when we were there, ever single room was sold out in the hotel, meaning that at capacity they had 1,200 guests, yet they only had 8 total bikes available for guests to utilize (and 2 of those are for children, and 2 have been broken for some time, so really ONLY 4 bikes available for their 1,200 guests to utilize). Ridiculous. -Service. Their main issue here seemed to be that several areas were understaffed. For example, it took more than an hour to get our drinks poolside (but the server was amazingly positive under the stress of trying to cover the entire adult pool deck by herself during peak hours on weekend with hundreds of guests to satisfy! I believe her name was Aspen and she was wonderful, though very taxed). Our group ended up going to the kitchen area ourselves to get drinks and food. And when our group first sat down at the pool, some nice women next to us gave us a couple of their seats because every seat at the pool was taken and they were just waiting on their bill. It took an hour and a half for them to just get their receipt so they could leave! However, they were told *afterwards* that if they had just gotten up and left their bill would have been closed out and there would have been an automatic 20% gratuity added. That would have been good to know ahead of time! -At their nicest restaurant I experienced the most passive aggressive restaurant service I've ever received. This was at P&G Steakhouse, the restaurant one "absolutely MUST visit while in Scottsdale" and yet during my 10-day stay I could only get into one possible night (and had to reschedule my Grand Canyon visit to do so). The food was incredible (we each ordered the 5 course tasting menu), but our server made snarky or outright rude comments at every interaction. He also completely ignored us when we asked for something as he walked past, or on one occasion, he got so frustrated/irritated that we asked him to repeat something (that was difficult to understand through the muffling of a face mask) that he stormed to the balcony outside where we watched him stare into the darkness for a few minutes to cool down. I don't know if this gentleman was going through anger management and needed to count to 10 or something, or was just having an especially difficult day, but we were more than pleasant and cheerful in all our interactions with him, which he met with sarcasm and criticism toward us. He was incredulous that we would put any items in "to go" boxes, and scolded us for ordering the tasting menu if we didn't think we were able to eat it all. I explained that I was treating my mom for Mother's Day, and that the tasting menu was the nicest item on the menu, so that it was meant to be a special occasion treat, even if we required To Go boxes. Then, when he sarcastically commented on packing up our desserts immediately rather than plating them, I uncomfortably laughed it off and informed him that the dessert was what we most looked forward to in the meal, and that we'd be eating it on-site. He seemed outraged that we "would eat dessert but take a steak To Go" and spoke angrily to himself as he went to retrieve the dessert course. It was an exhaustive, uncomfortable, and awkward exchange with him all evening, on what was to be the culmination of our visit. Positive: -The valet team was excellent and prompt in all interactions, no matter how early or late in the day. -Exceptional service from much of the staff, with special shout-outs to concierge staff Kevin and Sarah, Tony the young bellhop, Aspen the pool attendant, the young ladies of the tennis gift shop, the entire reservations team, and all the spa front desk, gift shop, and locker room staff! Thank you for all that you do! -The landscaping around the grounds was incredibly gorgeous. -The food was absolutely outstanding! We made it a point to eat at every restaurant on the premises at some point, and were never disappointed. From J&G Steakhouse for more upscale fare, to The Tavern for delectable pub style meals, to fabulous meals at Mowery & Cotton, to exotic poolside iced drinks with quesadillas, to fancy coffee beverages at The Marketplace in the shopping area, the chefs of these areas took great care in presentation, flavor, and accompaniments. I could eat at all these locations for the rest of my life and be happy!

tripadvisor · 2021-04-26 · 4/5view source

The Phoenician Scottsdale Great but not Fabulous My husband and I vacationed here April 21-25, 2021. We had previously stayed here on vacation before several years ago and we were looking forward to returning. Check-in: we were able to check in early at 11:30 AM. The negative of the experience was having the registration person question our rate with our discount code since my husband is a lifetime elite platinum rewards member with Marriott. We had to go back the next day and correct the rate, which they had adjusted back up to the standard rack rate because he didn’t have his business cards with him since they were on the bag tags with the valet. That was an epic fail. The room: So, the rooms in the main buildings are better from a location perspective. However, the view from the fifth floor 5064 room was of a concrete roof and certainly not what we had in mind and why we stay with Marriott on business and pleasure. Epic fail # 2. Dining: breakfast and lunch at Mowry & Cotton were better than average. They need to fix the weird break between breakfast and lunch where they “close” for 30 minutes. We said seat us now, we will order something and then wait the 30 minutes to order again. Reminded us of the stupid checkin fail. Thank goodness we don’t always comply with their plan and manage around a really stupid hour issue. Epic fail number 3. J&G Steakhouse: This deserves a special section because it is still one of the best restaurants in all of Phoenix. Food, service, ambience, wine list and especially drinks from Abby at the bar were all amazing. My husband takes clients there regularly and is never disappointed. Our server Austin and the manager Patrick were consistently wonderful. Simply cannot say enough good things about this venue. Only suggestion would be to open up the bar at 4:30 PM for first seatings at 5 PM. We ate there three times on this trip. Golf: The course was wonderful and this was our first time playing there. Front nine is much more wide-open and manicured than the back which is a bit crammed into the mountain side, but still very pretty. The rental clubs we had were great Callaway current top of the line clubs. Including my women’s left-hand set, which is tough to find. Food at the 19th hole Grill was very good and they did open at 6 AM with breakfast sandwiches. Staff at the course were exceptional and very accommodating and helpful. We went back to the practice range and putting three more times during our stay. Pool area: One of the reasons we chose this property is they had one of the most spectacular swim up pool bars in the nation. That is until they tore it out a few years ago. They have three large pools to choose from with plenty of lounge chairs but it does get harder to find spots for four or more on on Saturday. Pool staff were attentive and helpful. However, they do need more servers and bar staff on the weekends. That said we simply got our drinks from the bar and enjoyed the very nice pools and had a great time with friends there. Lobby bar area: The central gathering spot for the hotel is the lobby bar area which opens at 2 PM. They really need to change this to high noon. People are ready to drink at resorts starting at noon waiting to 2 o’clock when you’re on eastern time is very disappointing. Not a big ask, but would be a big plus for the resort. Very nice live entertainment on Thursday thru Saturday night. Overall: they are obviously restarting up operations and have some customer service training to do. Especially for lifetime members of their rewards programs. Pay attention. That was the worst room we’ve had at a Marriott in the last 10 years. We have always been upgraded to really wonderful rooms and this was a huge disappointment.

tripadvisor · 2021-01-23 · 4/5view source

Weekend Getaway During COVID-19 Stayed here in mid-January 2021 (sadly during COVID times) for two days during the weekend. Check-in (4/5): We were able to check in early (around 1pm) and able to check in with little wait. We had booked a deluxe room in the main building and, as Marriot Gold, we were "upgraded" to a room with a garden view on the fourth floor. It wasn't much of an upgrade, but we still pleased with our check-in experience. Parking (5/5): It was very easy to find a parking spot in the covered self-parking garage underneath the hotel. There is also valet parking, but it really isn't necessary as the garage entrance has an elevator that delivers you right into the lobby. Room (5/5): The room was pristine. Television allowed us to stream music and was nicely sized (probably about 50''). Bed extremely comfortable. Nice balcony area overlooking Camelback Mountain with a table to enjoy a nice meal/room service at sunset. The room was exactly what I expected from a "luxury collection" hotel. COVID-19 Protocols (3/5): Plenty of hand sanitizer adjacent to high-touch areas (elevators, etc). Most guests adhered to CDC guidelines (wearing a mask, 6 ft social distancing). Temperature check before entering the gym. Guests were less compliant in pool areas, but I think everyone was doing their best. Fitness Center (5/5): The fitness center was incredible. Two peloton bikes and plenty of weight lifting equipment. Nice view overlooking Scottsdale. Also, there was bike and tennis racket rental. Wasn't too busy on a Saturday afternoon and the large space of the center made it easier to socially distance. Pools (5/5): This is where the Phoenician really shined. There are 3-4 pools, a Jacuzzi (which was closed due to the pandemic), and a waterslide for the kids. The pools were nicely heated, open 24 HOURS and at night, had differently colored lights. We have stayed at several hotels in Phoenix/Scottsdale, but the Phoenician was in a class of its own. Will return when we are back in the area.

Several times we tried to use the fitness center but this was also closed when we went. We tried to use the bicycles one evening but these were also locked up. The nearby trailhead to Camelback is also closed There is no place at all in the evening to get a quick snack or dessert. We ended up ordering one dish of ice cream from room service which cost over $20 with the delivery fee. If you are coming here with children I would keep this in mind and bring some games to entertain them. Most of the rooms in the evening had on the TV which seems a shame in such a nice resort. An outdoor activity like a small mini golf course would’ve been nice. We used the hotel contracted car service in the beginning which was expensive and slow but the local Uber drivers were very reliable.

tripadvisor · 2020-02-21 · 4/5view source

Expansive luxury. Lackluster service. Walking the immense, perfectly manicured grounds, admiring the desert-influenced, contemporary architecture, and soaking-in the sumptuous, modern lobby, you’d never guess this beautiful property is now three-decades old. Clearly, the owners have invested in keeping it best-of-class in Scottsdale. The newish, stand-alone spa and fitness center is nothing less than amazing. Resort amenities abound at every turn, from the vast, multi-tiered pool levels, to nature highlights, to top-notch dining and entertainment. The rooms, particularly if you have a view (take note, many do not), are an oasis in the desert — large, well-appointed and sumptuously comfortable. Outstanding food and service is found in many onsite dining outlets, especially at JG on the top hotel floor (don’t miss the signature tater tots at their golf club bistro). Unfortunately, however, as too many other recent reviews have noted, the juxtaposition to an otherwise flawless hard product is in the service. Upon a weekday afternoon arrival, only one front desk agent is working, struggling with three non-functioning keycard machines, resulting in a 20-minute wait to check in... with only one person in line. When a supervisor does finally appear to reluctantly help, instead of apologizing for and expediting the guest experience, instead she then wants to argue with a repeat guest about a minuscule corporate discount on a $600/night room. An overnight shoeshine service is offered, but the receptionist says only if you have ‘black shoes.’ Housekeeping is hit or miss, but the exquisite, Le Belge dark chocolate and sea salt turndown amenity almost makes up for it. I’ve stayed at this hotel a dozen or so times over the years, despite what seem to be nagging service issues, but the service was such a turnoff this past trip it may merit exploring other options next time around. Hopefully management takes note of the service issues feedback being shared repeatedly here on TripAdvisor, since no post-stay survey is sent. The hotel itself is a jewel in the desert, but this Phoenician will rise much higher with a little more focus on delivering a service level that matches the otherwise wonderful surroundings.

Great Return Visit! I have stayed at the Phoenician previously (December 2017) and had a bad experience since the property was under renovations/construction. I was greeted by the valet by name (from the tag placed on my windshield by the security gate) and directed toward check in. Check-in was efficient although I had to ask about my American Express Fine Hotel and Resorts benefits. I always book through American Express Platinum travel for the great benefits during my stay ($100 resort food and beverage credit, free premium internet and $80 per day breakfast credit). I had room 4061 a nicely decorated King Deluxe Guest Room with a Mountain View. The view off the balcony was really nice and most of all very quiet. However, it was way too hot to enjoy the balcony with its very nice furnishing. I found the room to be too quiet and I called for a fan for white noise which arrived in five minutes. The bathroom was huge and the Le Chemin bath products are quite nice. I checked out the Thirsty Camel (lobby bar) and started putting my $100 food and beverage credit to good use. I found the service to be top notch and the selection of wines very good. After a great night’s sleep, I enjoyed my free breakfast at Mowry and Cotton – since I had a credit to burn, I splurged and had several breakfast items with juice and coffee. While enjoying breakfast I got to meet the Falconer and his buddy Calvin. Calvin’s presence keeps the other birds and crows away from the outdoor breakfast venue. The lack of birds was a great improvement over my previous stay in 2017. The Phoenician grounds are gorgeous, and the pools are awesome. I enjoyed the pool early morning (around 9am) and pretty much had it to myself. I was greeted at my lounger with a pitcher of ice water and fresh towels. My ice water never ran out! I also really loved to sound system at the pool. The music was quite relaxing, and the sound system made it sound almost live. Bottom Line: The Phoenician is a gorgeous property! I will definitely book The Phoenician again!

tripadvisor · 2019-04-09 · 5/5view source

Amazing guest-first attitude, caring and friendly staff! We’d always wanted to stay at The Phoenician and finally got our chance! Overall, the resort caters to conference attendees & guests of special functions (very spacious conference and ballroom areas). Our room was located very close to a series of these rooms in the main building and while it was in a quiet area of the hotel, it was very odd to walk through the conference/meeting room areas and staff setting up to get to and from our room each day. Seeing all those tables of food for conference attendees was very tempting!! We felt so cared for by the friendly customer service throughout the entire resort…from check in with the front desk to the gentlemen setting up the conference areas (on the way to our room, of course!), we were always greeted with a hello and a smile. This presence goes a long ways and is definitely noticed by guests—to know that we’re not in your way and respected as patrons of the hotel. Special recognition and a thank you to Ms. Snodgrass in the Funician Kids’ Club. While we don’t have kids ourselves (hey, we ARE the kids stuck in an adult body!), she was very friendly and kind to us when we went to check out the club…and even presented me with my own bunny Phoe Phoe! Thank you! Facilities Amazing property and as a personal trainer, I was BLOWN AWAY by the exceptional state-of-the-art and spacious fitness center at The Phoenician. Can I move in now??! The resort features 9 pools and it’s nice there is a specific-adults only pool area. We were very grateful for this especially as we were at the Phoenician during baseball Spring Training and the place was crawling with rugrats! Time was limited for us otherwise I'd have done it...but did you know that you can learn how to fly like a trapeze performer at The Phoenician? Yup, they offer classes! Lots of fun resort activities offered daily. Rooms Spacious, modern and stylish with many extra amenities (we loved the roomy counter space, as well as his and hers sinks in the bathroom). My favorite was the live aloe vera plant in the bathroom, which added a nice touch. How often do you get a hotel room that features a live plant? Unfortunately our room, while in a quiet area, did not have a view (see photo). The patio “furniture” looked a bit old. Perhaps because we were in a general population run-of-the-mill room, there also wasn’t a desk in the room, which seemed ironic for a conference oriented hotel. We did like the convenient bedside chargers and haven’t seen anything ever like it in our travels! As one of my pet peeves, there also wasn’t a recycling bin in the hotel room. Service Again, exceptional guest services and as Marriott Gold members, the evening turn-down service and chocolates were a fun treat! Overall, a great place to stay and The Phoenician lives up to its hype as a luxury resort. Just be prepared for an overdose of kids, especially during Spring Training and Spring Break (do these kids know how lucky they are to be staying in such an amazing resort?!). We already miss the place and definitely look to returning. "I'll be back!"

Nice Resort, Yes, But Luxury May Be Too Strong a Word I stay in a lot of hotels for work and often for vacations and I have an issue with that word "luxury". It's like "awesome." Awesome used to mean truly unbelievable and god-like. It now means "Really good!" The Phoenician hotel is very nice, it's not quite luxury. Luxury is Solage in Calistoga. Luxury is Resort Pedregal in Cabo San Lucas. Luxury is often a Four Seasons. Still the Phoenician is a very good hotel and very comfortable. The grounds of the Phoenician are very well- maintained. It's clean and spread out, there are pretty waterfalls, super green grass, new tennis courts and a curated golf course. The spa was modern and huge, and the gym was modern and inviting. We had very good service throughout our stay, and our room was big with 2 queens (for our family of 3) with sofa and desk, and a view of the pool. Nicely comfortable and a big bathroom-similar size bathrooms to those in nice Las Vegas strip hotels like Palazzo and the Wynn. I liked the overall architecture of the buildings as well - sorta 70's sorta not. Some things worth mentioning: - The food was very good. Not run of the mill hotel food. Kebabs and hummus by the pool felt homemade. The restaurant food was strong. - Lots of amenities for little kids that my older kids wouldn't take advantage of, like kids activities, a mini water park and water slide. - We were there when it was very busy - Spring Break - and if we didn't get to the pool before noon, we couldn't find 3 pool chairs together. Overall, we were pleased with our stay. We would potentially stay here again when in the area.

tripadvisor · 2019-03-19 · 5/5view source

Exceptional Service at an Exceptional Resort! OVERVIEW: It is rare that the staff makes such a difference for a stay, but the staff at the Phoenician truly enhanced our vacation. From the front desk to the housekeeping and the restaurant staff to the managers, the service was excellent and friendly. From moment we arrived we could feel the difference. The Phoenician Resort is a five star, luxury resort. It has been recently redone and it appears no expense was spared in making the resort a quality destination with a wonderful ambiance. The property is spread out and has excellent restaurants, bars and facilities. It is at the base of Camelback Mountain and has some excellent views. Although the resort is relatively large (over 600 rooms), it is spacious and doesn’t feel crowded or busy. There are plenty of areas where you can “get away from it all” and relax. ROOMS: The resort has a variety of room types – all with a balcony or patio. We stayed in a casita. It was an excellent room with spacious layout and a nice patio slightly away from the main building. The room had a mini-bar and a separate mini-fridge. The décor was modern and comfortable. The room was clean and the staff who serviced the rooms were excellent. Tip: Some casitas have a fire-table which would be nice in cooler weather. RESTAURANT, BAR & FACILITIES: The resort has several restaurants and bars ranging from the Tavern, a causal restaurant and bar overlooking the golf course, to the J&G Steakhouse with a great view of the property. We typically had breakfast at Mowry & Cotton where there is a good selection of breakfast entrees and a nice buffet. Tip: For a casual light dinner we enjoyed the newly opened Tavern Restaurant at the golf clubhouse. The resort has multiple pools (both adult and family) and a special area for children with a water slide and splash pad. Other facilities include a luxurious adult spa, a well-equipped fitness and activity center including tennis and pickle ball courts, and several golf courses. On the grounds there are quiet spaces for relaxing with a cup of coffee or a cold drink. We particularly enjoyed our walk through the resort’s cactus garden. BOTTOM LINE: We had a wonderful time at the resort. The staff and the service were exceptional. The resort ambiance and facilities were excellent. Our room was perfect for our needs.

At the top of the list My husband and I had never been to Arizona before so we decided to spend our 5 year anniversary there this past November. Growing up in the midwest, our vacations almost always centered around Florida or South Carolina. I was a bit nervous venturing to the desert for fear it would be boring and not tropical feeling. Scottsdale surely did not disappoint and neither did The Phoenician. The dry desert heat is phenomenal compared to the humid south, and we loved the amazing restaurants in Scottsdale, hiking Camelback Mountain and the service at this beautiful resort. Apparently we came at an opportune time because it was the very start of peak season (first week of November) so the resort was not crowded and the temperature was at a perfect 80 degrees. The grounds of the Phoenician are massive and expertly groomed, and while we were staying there there were at least 2 large conventions going on but luckily the place is so big that those large groups never "took over" any of the pools/restaurants/bars, etc. Our room was also gorgeous with a view of Camelback mountain and the cactus garden. The one drawback was that the room was a bit of a hike from the lobby, pools, etc. but we were never really in a hurry so it didn't matter. We loved getting lattes every morning from The Marketplace, and having a delicious breakfast at Mowry and Cotton. The service and ambiance at Mowry and Cotton was great and the breakfast was delicious. The highlight in terms of service and experience was at the spa and spa pool. We booked spa treatments one day and spent the rest of the day relaxing at the private spa pool. The service at the spa pool there from our waiter, Gennaro, was literally the best service we've experienced at any spa or resort. Gennaro was friendly, fun to talk to, and went out of his way to make sure our experience was relaxing and memorable. The following day we decided to pay the premium to get the spa privileges despite not having treatments so that we could relax by that pool again before our flight back home. Needless to say, we cannot wait to plan another trip back to Scottsdale and when we do we will definitely be staying at The Phoenician.

Wonderful Experience We needed to be in Phoenix for the Cheez-It Bowl, so I looked long and hard where to stay in Scottsdale/Phoenix. Ultimately, I ignored the mixed reviews and booked at the Phoenician and we are glad we did. The resort is majestic, the people are friendly and, overall, the service was excellent. Our rooms were a nice size, well appointed and clean; what we would expect for this price range. Registration was friendly and welcoming. The concierge staff, who we consulted daily, was receptive and helpful. We thoroughly enjoyed a magnificent sunset dinner at J&G Steakhouse. My family loves to dine and our standards are very high. The dinner exceeded our expectations in every way. The ambiance is superb, the service was attentive and the food was delicious. Appropriate live music was the cherry on top. This restaurant feels so much more than a hotel restaurant. The golf course was in tip top shape (and hostess on the beverage cart was charming and timely!), the Spa lived up to its billing, and the Athletic Center is the best we’ve seen at a hotel. Our only disappointment was at Mowry & Cotton, where we ate breakfast two mornings. The place is very nice, the breakfast buffet was more than ample and the food was good, but the service left much to be desired. Both times, we were greeted, escorted to our table and presented with a waiter/waitress who would attend to us. But, after the initial introduction, they were AWOL. We were pretty much on our own or had to get up and hunt down a wait staff for attention. The cost of breakfast was very high, and we’ve had better service at Denny’s. Fortunately, we stayed here on the American Express Platinum program, and the benefits include a daily credit of $80 for breakfast, so the pain of poor service was somewhat mitigated. Overall, however, our family was very pleased with our stay here. We recommend it highly to others and intend to return as often as we can.

tripadvisor · 2018-11-18 · 5/5view source

Royal Treatment Absolutely superior stay at this desert Oasis nestles in the shadow of Camelback Mountain. From our first warm greeting at reception to our final, personal goodbye, we felt like royalty. It was our 30th wedding anniversary and every person we met greeted us by name and wished us Happy Anniversary. There was champagne and a card in our room; we were treated to free dessert and more champagne at Mowry and Cotton restaurant, and a card and more delights at J&G Steakhouse. Inventive food at both restaurants, top-notch service and ambiance. The Spa is unrivaled in its offerings and its serenity. It has a private rooftop pool and lunch service. The pools overall are massive - yet offer private cabanas and little meandering paths and cozy corners. The loungers are comfortable and there are plenty of umbrellas for shade. (There are handicapped lifts at every pool which is a courteous, embracing gesture.) The tennis center is new and crisp and has a stadium court. We didn't golf, but the links were green and glorious. The lobby bar - both in and out - has a view of the resort and beyond, with creative cocktails and excellent service. The general feel and flow is desert chic, yet relaxed everywhere you go. AND THE GUESTROOMS!!! Our room was huge, with a deck so large that we had an outdoor sitting area, a dining area AND two lounge chairs. We could have had a party of 75 people - all with a sunrise view. The marble bathrooms are loaded with thick, fluffy high-quality towels and beautiful smelling amenities. Separate shower, bathtub and personal commode. Clean, clean, clean and I am fussy. Concierge services included mailing postcards at no charge. I don't know why, but this simple offering made a difference to me. Sure, we were paying 5star prices, but most places charge you, and The Phoenician doesn't nickel and dime you there. Very nice. Service was the best we have had nearly anywhere. Wonderful people and a well-run resort on every level. HIGHLY recommend. People of note: Ryan Sudden, Daniel Uhlry, in the front of the house. Rebecca at the bar and TWO Davids in the restaurants. Cher, Amanda and Jennifer in the Spa. Ivan in Tennis. All of you made a difference to us in person. Michelle in chef service and Patrick at J&G sent us cards. THANK YOU ONE AND ALL!!!!!! We are in LOVE.

Top Notch Service We stayed here for a combination of business and personal for 4 nights. The resort is quite large and in excellent condition. Even though there were a number of conferences underway, it was quiet for sleeping. They rise to the commitment of superior service. EVERYONE was friendly and acknowledge each guest. We requested a complimentary upgrade and received the King Deluxe room. There are a few enhancements from the regular King room: a love seat vs a chair, a larger table, higher end water to purchase, and a couple of additional bath amenities. Otherwise, the rooms are the same so if deciding to pay for the upgrade, perhaps save your money. We had both rooms during our stay and enjoyed the privacy of the regular King that looked out into Camelback Mountain vs the driveway. The rooms are large and well appointed with very comfortable beds. The balconies have tables and chairs. Room service was great, offering help with anything else we needed. Everyone was so very helpful. There are a number of food options and a few shops, though they are quite expensive. The best good value is the gelato - double scoop for $5 at the cafe, yum. They have grab and go food items as well. The food at the conference was excellent as was the table service. There was no waiting - they were VERY efficient. At the end of the conference there was a buffet lunch before travelling and they offered take-away boxes if you could t stay - awesome. There is a Happy Hour each day at The Thirsty Camel with $5 beers and $2 off local wine. The pools are lovely and there are adult-only sections. The loungers are high quality and there are lots of umbrellas. We enjoyed a stroll through the Cactus Garden, but passed on the lawn bowling due to the heat. There is an air conditioned games room for teens or young at heart. Overall, this resort was fabulous and does live up to being part of “a luxury collection” especially because of the service. So pleased to have had the opportunity to stay here.

24 Hour Staycation with Girlfriends! I booked this hotel during the busy Mother's Day weekend to celebrate two of my closest friends Birthday's and as a "Thank You" for being my "older-sisters/substitute-mothers" (my mama passed a few years ago). We were unable to participate in the High Tea service on Saturday afternoon as it was fully booked (3 weeks in advance!). However, I was able to secure tickets to Paint-Nite for Friday evening and High Tea Service (Saturday) about a mile away. Was pleasantly surprised that we were upgraded to a deluxe room with a view of the pools, a nice seating area with a couch and a lovely balcony. The room was very welcoming and large enough for three women. We loved the upcycled bathrobes, comfy beds, pillows, and staff. The room was quiet and we slept very well. When we checked in, at 1pm, we were able to get access to the room right away. We had lunch at Mowry & Cotton, which was delish! Dinner was sent to our Paint Nite setting from the steakhouse. Be warned, medium rare is more like rare, just go for well done. The package I purchased included a room-service breakfast for two ($65), which was fantastic. When we checked out we are gifted the difference for the additional food ordered for the third person, a nice surprise. Speaking of checking out, we requested a late checkout of 2pm, no problem. We were able to sleep in and lounge around all we wanted. This is a hotel that is currently going through a transition of redecorating and re-establishing its profile, service, and amenities. It appears that it is on its way.

Frustration with Spa and Renovation I was so disappointed with the spa as it was highly recommended to me. I just couldn't wait to get there. I made an appointment for Friday, February 23 for the Crowning Touch and Desert Serenity Scrub Wrap massage. I was referred to the spa by my friend who said it was amazing - excellent salt baths, etc. I knew the spa was going through some renovations, however I had no idea that the Spa on 4th was just another hotel hallway. The website lists that there are limited amenities. The truth is that there are no amenities- the waiting area is a regular hotel room with a few chairs and lemon water. I had my service in another hotel room which was quite awkward. There were kids running around the hall during my treatment and the lady told me the other side of the hall is actually occupied with guests. My spa gal, Dawn, was amazing and was trying to do the best she could with what she was given, but this is not a "spa experience" as described on the website. I've been to many spas-some full and some during upgrades. I was very disappointed and tried to talk to someone at the spa. I couldn't reach someone directly and they kept butchering my name even after I pronounced and spelled it. After several phone calls back and forth, I was told that the price reflected the renovation of the spa. That is simply not true - I paid $358 for almost 2 hours of service and nothing else. Now if I had never been to another spa, then maybe I would have understood. However, I've been very lucky to go to many spas and the price I paid at the The Phoenician was actually more than other spas where you can spend all day in the sauna, spa, pool, baths, etc. There was no option at this time. I have paid less than $200 at other spas and have received much more and also spent the entire day at the spa which is worth the money. I was very disappointed with the lack of regard for my concerns and the high price of a "spa experience" that happened in a hotel room. I do understand the idea of the renovation but it is not communicated clearly about what services they actually offer during the renovation. This was not a spa - it was a service in a room. I paid way too much money for that and do not recommend it. This is not a great place to be during construction. tripadvisor · 2018-01-28 · 4/5view source

Big and Splashy We decided to stay here primarily to check out this newly renovated legendary property. Overall we were impressed with what we saw. Of course the room is an important part of a stay and we really liked the new room look. It is easy to say it is straight out of a Restoration Hardware catalog and for us that is a good thing. The room was very spacious and included a large couch with a lounger section. There was also a nice desk area and plenty of drawer space and good lighting. The color palette was soft grays and blues. The bathroom was very stylish with double sinks, separate shower, tub, and water closet. The shower was nice but a little tight. The only thing we did not like about the room was that the entry area was a little busy with two closet doors, and the bathroom door all converging on top of each other along with the entry door. The spaciousness of the room flows out through a wide sliding door to a private terrace with a small cushioned couch and a table and two chairs. A great indoor outdoor setup can be enjoyed as long as you have a good view. A big deal at this hotel is the three level pool area. While big and fun, it is a little too much and I did not like that two of the pools were strange shapes that created a clunky arrangement around them. The bottom level is where you will find the famed mother of pearl pool which has a more traditional and refined look to it with cabanas around it on one side. As noted in reviews, the spa is not open yet and seems to have a ways to go. It is going to be near the pools so construction noise can be a factor at times. The hotel is also operating with a temporary gym located in the tennis center. About half of the gym space is in a covered open air patio. If you workout in the morning or evening this space can be very cool. Regardless, there is enough equipment to pretty much obtain a full workout. The rest of the hotel carries out the RH look to a stylish and somewhat glamourous effect. The exception is Mowry & Cotton which has a more relaxed modern country feel. We wanted to have breakfast here but the menu was limited with no basic fair such as pancakes or waffles. Relish Burger Bistro has a classic golf club look but that might be changing. One of the best advantages of this hotel is its location close to downtown Scottsdale making it easy for off-site adventures. While we enjoyed our stay at this hotel it is not one we would most likely return to primarily because of its size. It is just a little too big, at over 600 rooms plus large event space areas. And as attractive as the interior renovation is and the grounds pretty, the hulking exterior is very hard looking and dated in appearance. But if size is not an issue, the posh space, convenient location, and ample on site activities will make you a happy guest.

The trick here is to avoid your room It would be tempting to just sit in a bathtub and lounge in the bed and admire the mountain view’s from your balcony. No one would blame you if you ordered steaks from room service and binged “Fixer Upper” (especially if you’re a cord-cutter). But NO - go wander the little path running behind the hotel along the mountain and see a gecko or two. Wend your way across the property toward the golf course and at least watch putting practice. When you drive up to the lobby, resist the tempatation to turn left toward the elevators. Instead, amble down into the bar and hang out. People on vacation in Arizona are exceedingly laid back and chatty. When they’re watching birds eat patio-dining guests’ food RIGHT OFF THEIR PLATES, their conversation is downright exciting. It’s a superb location - right where Arcadia abuts Scottsdale and within a short drive to Chandler and Tempe. Use The Phoenician for beauty and abatement - not just lodging. I’ve stayed there 5 times over 7 years. The place isn’t brand new, but it is classic and the people who work for Starwood take pride in it and in caring for guests’ experiences at a high level. I like it better than the North Scottsdale Westin.

tripadvisor · 2017-12-04 · 4/5view source

Not my best visit to The Phoenician The Phoenician is beautiful, classy, and a hands down 5 star resort. This was my third stay there and I have to say it was my least favorite. One of the greatest features of this resort is their elaborate pool area... 3 levels of pools set to the backdrop of Camelback mountain. The huge amount of construction however, completely took away from the entire experience. The top pool had a restaurant being built all day... loud non stop drills and circular saws right next to where people are sitting in lounge chairs. Not at all relaxing. Then I moved all our things to the bottom pool for some peace and it turns out an entire building is being constructed next to it as well so you have the luxury of listening and watching cement mixers driving by, and beep beep beep as they are backing up, etc. I'm amazed they kept the place open during such a renovation. The middle pool is for adults only and probably the best bet, but I had my 3 year old daughter with me. It was very disappointing because the pool was the reason we came. Also, after receiving a sour mix filled $12 margarita, I asked the woman if she could have the bartender make it more like the one from the lobby bar instead of full of mixer. She came back and said the skinny margarita is what I was looking for and charged me the extra $ for that without even asking. Bad form for a hotel of this caliber. Relish is a nice hang out and good bet for food. It's right on the golf course and more laid back. Mowry & Cotton had great service but that's about it. Expensive mediocre food and Il Terazzo, the restaurant that was previously in this spot, was much better. The outdoor patio on the main level of the hotel is amazing...excellent service and a very relaxing environment to enjoy some drinks. The renovations are actually done in that part of the hotel and the results are stunning. If you are traveling with children, there are a few options for you especially if they are a little older. The splash pads could be for younger kids but that was closed for renovations. The water slide would probably be for 5 and above. I'm not sure how the kids club works but I believe it's extra. Kids under 5 need to be accompanied by an adult and when we stopped in to check it out the woman behind the couldn't have been less interested so my daughter and I looked around quietly and left. I think it's a good space though. There is also a nice sized playground near the tennis courts that is shaded. While I was disappointed in this recent trip to Phoenician, it doesn't take away from how beautiful and amazing it is and I look forward to going back when the renovations are finished

tripadvisor · 2017-11-11 · 1/5view source

Forget relaxing by the pools and they charge for Wi-Fi We arrived in the evening having flown in from the UK. When we checked in it was dark but first impressions were good. Prestigious and well appointed lobby with an inviting bar area. The guy who checked us in said we had been upgraded. I should have trusted my instincts and made specific enquiries about our booked room and it’s location and the “upgraded” casita. The casita was away from the main hotel below the pool complex. The room itself was fine and again well appointed. Ridiculously in 2017 this hotel still clearly thinks it makes commercial sense to charge guests for Wi-Fi. It cost $12.50 to use the slower of the two options. This is the US of A for crying out loud, it’s supposed to be a leading developed economy and this hotel still thinks it’s right to charge for Wi-Fi. Go to Hoi-An in Vietnam and there is free high speed wi-Fi in the hotels and in the taxis! We were woken up at 7am by an angle grinder /drill right outside our balcony. Two workmen had started working on a water feature alongside our casita block. It got worse because across the lawn there was a full blown construction site with workmen, saws, grinders, plant etc. Working on the construction of a new gym complex. At that point we thought we’d ring reception and look to change our room (3 hours later and they had still not returned our enquiry and yet the website was showing vacancies for that night). Whilst waiting (as it turned out in vain) to hear about the room change we went up for breakfast just above the pool area. We were then met by yet more builders and workmen who were working on a children’s play area and a new pool bar restaurant. The time was now 7:45am. At breakfast at times you couldn’t even hear the background music because the sound of drills and circular saws drowned it out. So far that was 4 construction areas near our room: the gym, the water feature, the children’s play area and the new pool bar/restaurant. Things weren’t looking good for a relaxing day by the pool but there was a lower pool area that we had yet to look at. After the breakfast shared with 20 workmen and their tools, we took a walk to look over the rest of the hotel. Lo and behold there was yet another huge construction project complete with an operating JCB digger 30 yards from the adults only lower pool. We went backed to the room and checked straight out. No one from the front desk or management was in the slightest bit apologetic for our experience. Their website fails to disclose that there are significant construction works with attendant noise in progress. The gym construction has only just started and the building by the lower pool has at least another two to three months to go. Awful experience and inexcusable failure by the hotel to disclose the ongoing construction.

tripadvisor · 2017-03-22 · 3/5view source

looks luxurious, feels inhospitable The Phoenician looks like a luxury property and it has lots of luxury details --our rooms were large, the beds comfortable, nice toiletries, fancy pools and grounds. But the whole place feels incredibly corporate and nothing about it seems intended to make guests feel valued as opposed to sucking every last cent out of their pockets. The staff has clearly been coached to mouth welcoming phrases, but bottom line is there are polices in place and nothing will be changed for individual guests. As an example, when I was checking in, I was asked if the employee could indicate a check out time for me in their system. Which sounds like, when do you want to check out, we can be flexible. It's not. I asked if it could be a bit later than noon and they said no, so basically this question is designed to look like it is individualizing your experience while getting them information about which rooms they can clean early (helping them, not the guest). There is nothing wrong with adhering to a set check out time, but it’s silly to try to dress it up this way. They charge extra for connecting rooms, which just makes me feel like a profit center to be exploited. If you have connecting rooms available give them to me, if you don't, don't. It is not more expensive to you to do that. The pools are beautiful but the shapes and sizes are such that you can't really swim much, and they were, in 60 degree February weather, heated only to 82 degrees. That feels cold (by contrast, earlier in the week we stayed at the Arizona Biltmore which heats pools to 86. that’s a big difference). In the bathrooms, the floor had a drain but was not sloped toward it, so you just have a drain surrounded by puddles, and for some reason the hook for robes is placed in the one part of the wall that means hanging anything makes the light switch inaccessible. None of these are horrible but at the prices they charge, shouldn’t happen. The minibar, which is an extra cost, is very easy to get to. The coffeemaker, which is free? Its stuck inside a cabinet at floor level so you have to sit on the floor or squat down to use it. Even the business center – which is free to use in many hotels – is subcontracted out to Kinko’s/FedEx and charges for anything but printing boarding passes -- which is especially annoying when you already have to pay for WiFi. I would single out the pool attendants as a good thing, very nice people who set up lounges with big soft towels (and enough of them) and drinks.

A "Funician" club for kids (note: somewhat pricey at $95/day and only for kids 5 or 6 and up). A trapeze class with a complete trapeze set up (yes you read that right, TRAPEZE!) Tennis courts Complimentary bikes/helmets/locks A children's play structure/park (covered so your tots don't get burned) Pools, Pools and more Pools A water slide A kids splash pad/play area Hot tub Golf Hiking trails/popular mountain hike right behind the hotel Yoga and other fitness classes Fitness center SPA - Ahhhhh! Shops inside the hotel luxury car rentals (or you can get a Rav4) Bocce ball Nature trails around the hotel that are beautifully landscaped Several restaurants Coffee shop the list goes on, and on, and ON! I was here for several days while my husband was on business and I found it to be so great that I didn't even have to leave the hotel to keep myself busy! The rooms: We had a room with a mountain view or should I say mountain touch, it felt like we could reach out and touch the mountain from our balcony it was so cool. The room was VERY spacious and well appointed. I have stayed at some nice places and I always like it when there are little things that they provide, this place provided something I have never seen before - lip balm - among all of the other things one needs. Nice touch! I spent a lot of time in the room since I wanted to relax while my husband worked, so I can honestly say that I got to know the room pretty well and I really enjoyed it. Very calm and relaxing space. The bathroom was huge, separate shower, tub, private toilet area, and double vanity, all in warm, neutral desert tones that felt very serene. I did indulge in room service and found it to only be so so as it was $40 for 2 coffees and some pastries that were pretty bland. I would suggest walking down to the coffee shop and getting lattes there which were great and their pastries much better! The staff - I felt like the staff here were particularly excellent. We were staying with my husbands company who rented out about 80% of the hotel. Every staff I encountered was friendly, knowledgeable and seemed genuinely interested in making sure guests were comfortable. The Spa/Fitness center: I also indulged in a massage. The spa itself is really nothing special, again, I frequent spas and found this one to be average. The SERVICE is a different story. I got a massage from Gene and he was AMAZING. My only regret about the spa was not doing a longer service. Definitely request Gene! I also took a yoga class and wasn't sure what to expect, I do a lot of Yoga in a pretty earthy crunchy yoga town so I was worried it might be superficial or watered down. Wow, I was wrong. Rhonda literally made me feel like I had known her for years and made me feel welcomed and comfortable in a class where most of the people seemed to know each other well and must attend regularly. Her style and her philosophy was intense and deep and really made you contemplate. She has a gift. I am usually not so impressed by services or classes at hotels, the Phoenician hires excellent, knowledgeable staff. Location: Excellent. I don't know the area too well but we were a 5 minute uber from old town Scottsdale which has great shops and restaurants. Also less than 2 miles from what looked like a really nice mall. I can definitely say I plan to go back at some point and would stay here again! Also, worth noting, I took a walk up to the canyon suites just because I love checking out everything at a hotel, that area was super private and even more luxurious. They had a morning spread set out that looked incredible. It might be worth staying up there if you are looking for something more private, it had its own private pool also. Overall: Impressed!

tripadvisor · 2016-12-18 · 5/5view source

Thanksgiving - 3 generations Ok, so here goes. My 70-something mom and I have frequently visited the Canyon Ranch / Miraval spa complex many times. However, for this Thanksgiving, we decided to do a three generation reunion in Phoenix to try to please everyone while being able to visit my nephew's new graduate school layout. I insisted on The Phoenician in Scottsdale as a good compromise and was wholeheartedly pleased. Look, you can never please everyone all the time, but The Phoenician did everything they could to please, satisfy, entertain and host my various family members through our long holiday stay as best possible. A couple of features: my mom recently had hip replacement, and the hotel offered a complementary wheelchair for her use the entire time we were there (NB, wheelchairs are first-come-first-served, which was no problem upon our arrival, however, I suggest the hotel do an actual reservation system, so we would have arranged for a rental had it been needed). The Thanksgiving buffet was a very interesting affair with excellent breakfast / bunch / sushi options - something for everyone with no one going away hungry. We wanted to go to the Grand Canyon, and my 80-something dad was thinking he needed to exert his patriarchal duties in renting a van / driving the trip, (which I kaboshed). The concierge recommended David Joachim at My Arizona Guide for a full-day Grand Canyon Tour, which was a tremendous / superlative choice. David met us at 7 AM with his large accommodating van, and we stopped in Sedona, saw a couple of prehistoric sites we never would have seen on our own, had lunch in the turn-of-the-20th century period El Tovar restaurant (breathtaking original period murals). During the weekend, we had dinner in the formal steak restaurant, which was excellent, mom, me and sister-in-law did a spa afternoon while the guys went on a hike on Camelback Mountain, had cocktails and high tea, and in short, it was a wonderful weekend for an eclectic family with divergent interests, which I highly recommend.

tripadvisor · 2016-11-18 · 5/5view source

Luxury in a beautiful setting The Phoenician has a bit of a sordid past, created by Charles Keating out of money he stole from depositors in the S&L scandals. Today, it's a Starwood "Luxury Collection" hotel. Located at the base of Camelback Mountain, the hotel has great views of the mountain, a wonderful several acre cactus garden with paved walking trails (walk attentively though; posted sign warns of rattlesnakes, although that is true anywhere in the Arizona deserts). The staff are very polite and attentive, offering free bottled water while waiting for check-in or getting into a taxi, asking if you need help anytime you seem lost in the sprawling hotel and spacious grounds, turn-down service with slippers and chocolates. Beautiful pool area with several pools and attentive staff to bring out towels for the comfortable, cushioned lounge chairs--nice little touch, they bring a free pitcher of ice water to your chair; servers check regularly but not intrusively to see if you want food and drink and they return promptly with your order. Rooms are spacious, quiet and well-appointed. Nice cocktail bar with outdoor heated patio. I only had breakfast in one of the hotel's restaurants, service and food were good, and we were entertained by a staff person who had a trained falcon. The only minor complaint I have is that there was a line of about 10 people when I checked in and no separate line for Starwood Gold/Marriott Gold status (you can link your points to have reciprocal elite status, e.g my Marriott Gold status qualified me for linked SPG Gold status). Most hotels especially luxury ones have a dedicated and shorter check-in line for Elite status customers. The Phoenician should do the same. The hotel is only 10 minutes from downtown Scottsdale/Old Town via Uber, Lyft, taxi or hired town car, or your own wheels.

Exceptional Resort We expected an upscale, family friendly resort and we got a new favorite vacation spot. The desert resort setting was exceptionally beautiful. The design of the hotel and amenities was incredibly well thought out. There was extensive desert wildlife to be seen on the not to be missed golf cart safari. The shady cactus garden was phenomenal for a short meander and photo opportunities. The hotel brought in a bird of prey to keep the nuisance birds from the outdoor seating at breakfast and lunch. My 10 year old loved the water slide, splash pad, ping pong, tennis courts, playground and the opportunity to feed the koi poolside every morning. The main hotel was undergoing extensive renovation, but it was remarkably quiet and did not disturb us. We stayed in a newly renovated room that was lovely. Room service the first night was the best room service experience I've seen- like performance art. What made this hotel was their staff. From the groundskeepers at the golf course to the front desk, servers and housekeeping staff, everyone we met working at this hotel was genuine, friendly, helpful and true hospitality professionals. It made every moment we spent there a pleasure. Note for those unfamiliar with Arizona- it is extremely hot from May-Nov plan most outdoor activities in the shade or before sunrise- it is too hot to run outside during the heat of the day.

An exceptional Starwood property The Phoenician is probably the best overall Starwood property I've ever stayed at. Rachel, the front desk supervisor, is a star. Very nice property I had been here twice before this last stay for business meetings and really did not have the time to explore or take in the property. Two important things happened, first a smile from manger regarding safety; if you looked around, and you knew what to look for, it was clear that security was present, Second, I said that we would move and that I understood that Mr. V was an important guest, manager looked at me and said "you are an important guest"; wow. Next thing I know three staff members are moving chairs to a location specifically where I can see kids; problem solved. Beds are really comfortable, and rooms are large, grounds and pools are off the charts; the only thing this place needs to be heaven is the Carribean Ocean. Two negatives: First, only one bartender at pool bar, and this person was serving all of the servers, I just walked away. Second, room service portions are really small, and pool food is average, except fries which are really good. Definitely would stay again. Check your Amex card, there are perks. Also, kid friendly, separate area for kids; small water park and slide. Night time activities include smores and games. Ask if there is a big conference when you are going to be there, this place has huge conference facilities, and a conference could make pool a little crowded.

tripadvisor · 2016-03-28 · 2/5view source

A disappointing stay. My husband and I just returned from a 4-night stay at The Phoenician. We planned this short trip as a "babymoon" of sorts (with Zika killing our initial dreams of Caribbean/Mexico) and were hoping for a luxurious, relaxing little vacation at a resort with excellent service. We knew we were traveling during spring break (an unavoidable reality given our own schedules), but since the hotel's website boasted an "adults only" swimming pool, we thought we could still have a relaxing environment despite a busy family travel season. First, the good things -- the service at the pool and in the restaurants was excellent. A really amazing pool attendant named Brian helped us find a chair each day. Had it not been for Brian and the other attendants, our trip would have been abysmal. All we wanted was to lay by a pool with drinks in our hands (mine virgin, of course) and in that sense -- once we were able to get a chair -- The Phoenician did not disappoint. (Excellent virgin cocktails by the way!) The servers at the restaurants were also very friendly, and the grounds are well maintained. It is a beautiful place to stay. The bad -- we arrived at the hotel Wednesday night around 8 (10pm our time). We were extremely disappointed that our Casita room -- what we thought would be a nice upgrade from a standard room -- was located offsite from the main building and overlooked a parking lot. It did not justify the inflated price. We spoke to the front desk about a different room, and they were able to move us to a more private room overlooking the cactus garden (very lovely). They told us they would move our bags to the new room, but when we arrived at the new room after dinner, our bags were not there. Mistakes happen -- we understand that. But this introduction to The Phoenician troubled us for several reasons: (1) it took over an hour for the staff to admit to us the bags were even lost -- until then, they were blatantly lying to us by repeating that the bags were "in transit"; (2) the staff didn't listen to us the first time when we said we believed the bags were in another room (when my husband called to move the bags, not knowing our new room number, guest services told him they were going to another room) -- it was not until we had been calling at regular intervals for over an hour that they bothered to look at the most natural location; (3) had we not called repeatedly, suggested where to look for the bags, and asked if they were lost, I am quite confident we would not have received our bags that night at all; and (4) we essentially had to ask the staff for an apology over this incident -- no one contacted us the next day to apologize or see how they could make our stay any better. I am happy we eventually received our bags that night (at 12:15am local time), but for a facility that prides itself on being a luxury resort, we were incredibly disappointed with how this situation was handled. Maybe if this happened in the middle of the day, or maybe if I wasn't 6 months pregnant and had been traveling all day, we would feel differently... but it was an extremely stressful, frustrating start to what was supposed to be a relaxing vacation. We tried to make the best of the rest our stay. Ultimately, the place was not for us. To get a chair by one of the three pool areas, you needed to be there by 8am, or earlier. We learned this the hard way the first day. Since relaxing by the pool was our main goal, we felt like we had to compromise on other things, like not setting an alarm or doing a morning activity like hiking or other exercise. And the pool areas itself were disappointing because the promise of an "adults only" pool area -- a main reason I justified this hotel selection -- did not exist. It did, in theory, but it was not enforced at all. So every pool area was full of children (it was spring break after all), and there was nothing relaxing about the pool environment. In the end, while The Phoenician certainly has beautiful grounds and many nice amenities, it did not provide us with the luxurious, relaxing vacation we have enjoyed in other locations and were hoping to have for this vacation. Given the way our experience from our first night was handled, the "blood sport" competition to get a pool chair each day, and the failed promise of an adults-only pool area, we would not return. They clearly put a lot of effort into making this a family-oriented place, and I respect that. But I certainly do not feel like they catered at all to couples. Even when we do vacation with our children in the years to come, I can't see myself coming to a place that has little semblance of relaxation.

No Longer a Five Star Property 1. The Phoenician eliminated the weekend falcon program at sunset with NO NOTIFICATION to past guests with current reservations. As late as yesterday, March 10, 2016, there was information on The Phoenician's website about the sunset falcon program on Friday and Saturday nights. Our son looks forward to the falcon program every visit and we were shocked to learn that it had been discontinued when we inquired upon arrival about the start time for this evening. Anyone who has stayed at the Phoenician understands that this is an essential part of the experience and that part of the charm is lost without the birds. 2. While the guest policies clearly state "All guest rooms and public spaces are 100% non-smoking," what the policy doesn't make clear is that the hotel defines public spaces as interior spaces only, which means that chain smoking of cigarettes on the patio lounge area is actively encouraged through the provision of ash trays. 3. Lifetime Platinum SPG members, and other SPG members booking with points (regardless of the thousands of dollars in food, beverage and incidentals spent on property) are treated like second rate citizens. Year after year, we are given the worst rooms and face multiple issues with the rooms we have booked. My suggestion to SPG members is to spend your points elsewhere - for example, the Parker Palm Springs is a comparable property that welcomes SPG members using points and always pre-blocks repeat guests into upgraded rooms. 4. While Starwood's Luxury Collection tries to compete with properties such as the Four Seasons, the Phoenician falls short in the area of service expectations. I don't think it's too much to ask for the check-in agent to provide accurate information about the assigned room or for housekeeping to promptly provide a rollaway bed upon request, but these are common issues at The Phoenician that require multiple follow-up visits to the front desk and via phone to correct.
