Luxury and excellent customer service This review is long overdue but I wanted to share how much my mom and I thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Phoenician in Scottsdale Arizona over Labor Day weekend. We were impressed by the beauty of the resort. You would never know it was 27 years old since it maintained so well and we were even more impressed with the service. Everywhere we went, we were offered water and a smile. The grounds are beautiful. There are plenty of pools and plenty of seating. The cushions are so thick they are like little mattresses. As soon as you pick a spot, attendants cover your chair, provide extra towels and a pitcher of ice water that is continually replenished as long as you remain by the pool. There is a cactus garden on site that you can get a tour of. It was amazing to see how many different types of cactus there are. The beds in the room are super comfortable. The bathroom is luxurious with a double sink, tub and rain shower. What stood out most was the excellent staff. The best example of the staff at its finest was in the Bellman Joe. He went above and beyond typical customer service to assist us and make our stay a wonderful one. The dining in the resort was excellent as well. The burgers at Relish are delicious as we discovered on the first day. The manager at the Thirsty Camel was incredibly accommodating. Relish closed early one another evening and we felt like turkey burgers. He made the effort to go get burgers from Relish for us, cook them up and his kitchen and have I served at the lounge. The breakfast at Il Terrazzo was delicious. J&G steakhouse is as fantastic as you would expect a restaurant of the renowned Jean George to be. If you are visiting Arizona and want to be pampered, this is the place to be.

tripadvisor · 2016-02-14 · 3/5view source

Small details let this hotel down When arriving The Phoenician looks like a great resort, with everything you need for an amazing stay - pools, bars, restaurants, golf courses, stunning views and even a cactus garden! However there are a number of small (but cumulative) issues with attention to detail that let it down. I'll start with the good: 1. Beautiful grounds, diverse restaurant options, huge pool area, cactus garden is lovely 2. Location - within walking distance to Scottsdale Fashion Mall (has Macy's, Barney's, Marcus & Neiman and Dillard's plus all the usual major clothing brands). Great view of Camelback Mountain and easy access to hiking. 3. Rooms are large, good for sharing with friends/colleagues as there are two basins, large room, two wardrobes etc. Nice balcony with lounge and chairs to relax in sunshine. The rooms aren't amazing/new but nice enough with great natural lighting 4. Wifi is good - strong and does not have a cap (I believe this is normally paid but was included in my business rate). There is free wifi in the lobby, also very strong. 5. The bathroom is huge, luxurious and had a separate bath and shower It would have been a great stay if not for some minor issues that cumulatively let this hotel down: 1. Housekeeping are friendly however my room was across the hall from a housekeeping depot, where between 7:30am and 8am they would all congregate, sing, laugh and talk before a procession of no less than 5000 (Ok maybe a slight exaggeration) trolleys would be trundled past making it absolutely IMPOSSIBLE to sleep. This is particularly irksome when it's a Sunday morning and you have flown in from Australia the previous day, trying to get over jetlag prior to a conference. Not impressed. 2. My shower gel was never replenished until I called housekeeping to specifically ask for it. 3. I am a gold member but you would never have known it outside the obligatory welcome 'gift'. Given a terrible room (outside housekeeping) and when I requested late checkout I was told this was not available, yet found out later that some colleagues (who asked after me) were given an additional 2 hours despite having no status 4. The shower was really terrible, no pressure at all and it was also annoying that you had to be blasted by cold water when you turned it on. Perhaps that was specific to my room (the water pressure) but it was particularly annoying when trying to wash shampoo out of your hair. 5. The concierge, while friendly enough told me it was not safe to walk to the mall, which was just very strange when it was completely safe! I find it odd that they try to discourage people from walking there and wonder if it is a ploy to get $ from hotel car service (that is what he tried to get me to do). 6. One night stood at the bar for over 10 minutes and wasn't served. It was like the barman was deliberately ignoring our group (I promise we were not being rude/drunk!). They clearly needed more staff working and a lesson in customer service. 7. Lamps in the room are old and very difficult to switch on/off. I couldn't even get the bedside lamp to turn off so had to unplug it from the wall! Tips: 1. Walk to the mall! It's a lovely 15 minute walk and you can go via Chaparell and 68th street (residential) to avoid busy Camelback Way. 2. In 'N' Out burger is 15 minutes away (car) and 5 Guys is at the Mall (5 minutes) if you like a good burger. Personally I preferred 5 Guys :) 3. Bring your hiking shoes and go for a hike up the mountain! 4. At dusk the cactus garden has rabbits and hummingbirds - very tranquil. I would stay there again because of the location and because it is overall a nice hotel, but I do hope management places more focus on improving the finer details, which are letting them down currently.

tripadvisor · 2015-12-29 · 4/5view source

Great Experience for a Christmas Getaway We checked into the Phoenician late on the night of the 23rd and were promptly greeted at the front desk by a lovely bubbly girl. We were given directions to our room, which was 4167 on the back of the hotel facing the cactus garden. After winding through the large wings of the building we arrived at our room, which was large, clean, a little worn, and certainly dated. The 1980's decor is certainly obvious, but when the place is clean and service is as good as it was, a little bit of separating wall coverings and cracked marble in the bathrooms can be overlooked. The one spot that was a little on the "eww" factor was the tiled walk-in shower had black mold around the drain which could have been better addressed. The resort is easy walking distance to the Cholla Trail to the top of Camelback, which was a great way to start the trip. We had excellent coffees and two pastries in the shops before heading out. The two coffees and pastries were $26, so about a 35% push over what we would spend at Starbucks, but the coffees were good and the pastries were very good, and unless I am mistaken, were baked locally so they were worth the spend. We hiked the mountain and then spent some time hanging around the property. The grounds are outstanding. We went back to the shops and had an awesome turkey and havarti sandwich which we easily split, and was on great bread. The sandwich with the chips and bottle of Diet Coke was $14, and again, well worth it. We then returned to the room, had a nice hot shower and went for Christmas drinks at the Thirsty Camel ahead of our dinner at the J&G Steakhouse. Holy smokes! Anthony the bartender was absolutely fantastic. Great personality, talked with us about our plans, kept us filled on bar snacks and we had some awesome drinks. The hubs loved they had blue cheese stuffed olives for his martini. Dinner at J&G was phenomenal. The GM was there, we recognized him from commercials on the hotel channel on the floor, and was helping the servers keep up with the crush of guests. How many restaurant GMs can actually participate in all aspects of the business AND step out to check on all the guests?? Again, phenomenal service, great management, great food with a great view of the sunset. Christmas dinner was at Il Terrazo, which was a set menu, very industrial- think cruise line food. At $300 for two people with wine, it was disappointing, and I would advise that restaurant be skipped. Again, great service, just industrial cruiseship type food. On the third day, after another long day of hiking, we hit up the Thirsty Camel and the amazing Anthony again. That night we ate at Relish Burger Bistro. Wow. Just WOW. We had a beer at Happy Hour, which was 3:00-6:00, then sat down for some shared onion rings, chicken wings and a burger while we watched football and hockey on a multitude of screens. The onion rings and wings were fantastic as was the burger. Total bill- $56!!! And the food was awesome as was the service. So all in all, yes, the lady is showing her age a bit, but with the cleanliness and the service, that is quickly overlooked. I highly recommend this resort.

great 5 star experience I just spent 6 days at the Phoenician on a business trip. The resort is beautiful! Every area is clean and perfectly manicured. tripadvisor · 2015-11-24 · 4/5view source

Great Conference and Family Resort This resort is beautiful. We attended a conference here and our family were able to hang out at the pool and on the property (two small children) and be completely occupied while we were in meetings. The service provided by Alex and Arliss at the breakfast restaurant on the ground level was A+. There was a great nightlfe vibe in this hotel as well. The lounge on the 3rd floor and the upstairs steakhouse were great. My only complaint, is that the hotel Shuttle Service (Infinity SUV) came across as dishonest at times. The drivers were super nice and friendly but were not consistent in how much it cost to drive us to Old Scottsdale. Jeff originally quoted $30 to take us to Old Scottsdale, cash only. My group discussed (in front of Jeff) that we only had $20 cash so we would cab. We asked if we could use our Visas and he said no. Then, he said he would take $20. So we agreed. He told us to call him when we were ready to leave. We called for a pick up back to the hotel and Jeff had left for the night (only 2 hours later) but someone else came to get us. He said the price was $15 to Old Scottsdale and $15 back, doesn't matter the time of day. I asked why Jeff originally quoted us $30 then took $20, and he said he didn't know. The next day, we went back to Old Scottsdale and it was $15 both ways, and we used the service for a ride to the airport for a quoted price of $57 but was charged $60...and each time they DID take Visa. So, my recommendation is that they tighten up on the amounts they charge and how they accept payment. Perhaps have a sign outside that lists the prices so it isn't up to the drivers to disclose? It just confused us all and made us uneasy. It very well could have just been miscommunication but that shouldn't happen at a nice resort like this.

tripadvisor · 2015-11-03 · 4/5view source

Relaxing stay during "off season" My wife and I and another couple recently spent a few nights at the Phoenician. Each couple had a Casita and the rooms were very nice. The bath room was luxurious. There seem to be a number of activities for children including a kids club, a water slide (which I could not resist) and daily koi feeding. Our new favorite! The Phoenician is our new favorite resort! Such a peaceful, relaxing, and tranquil place. I loved the layout that just blends into the surroundings. Pure luxury! We stayed here for two nights rest and relaxation after nearly 3 weeks touring the national parks. We wanted a luxury resort and were not disappointed. tripadvisor · 2015-09-01 · 5/5view source

A fabulous 10 days Firstly, I have to say that I scratched my head in puzzlement reading some of the negative reviews of this place as they don't match our experience at all. We (husband, 8-year-old son, myself) just arrived back from a 10-day stay at the Phoenician and had a wonderful time! We stayed in a grand deluxe room with two king size beds, a table and two lounge chairs with foot stool, a work station with desk, chair, plenty of plug sockets etc, and a good sized patio with table, chairs and sun lounger. Bathroom was huge, with separate shower and toilet, and there was a sunken bath. Plenty of towels, robes, slippers and excellent housekeeping and turn down service (complimentary water, chocolates etc). Housekeeping arranged our toiletries bags so everything was accessible. Well-stocked minibar. Coffee machine. Huge TV, two telephones. Mini-tablet device on desk with info about the resort, weather, news etc. Good wi-fi. Our room was absolutely perfect for the three of us - no tired furnishings, bugs etc. Far from it, it was immaculate. Sure, we encountered a bit of bird poop on the balcony but guess what? Birds fly around and poop as and when they fancy, and no hotel in the world could keep on top of that. Didn't bother us one bit. If we saw a poop, we just cleaned it away ourselves. And in any case, the staff at the Phoenician are so professional and attentive to detail, if we'd told them there was a poop on our balcony/patio, they'd send someone immediately to clear it up! The poolside staff in particular made every effort to shoo birds away from the sun loungers and any mess (minimal in my opinion) was promptly cleaned up. Communal areas of the hotel are lovely. The lobby is elegant, cool and well furnished. Plenty of restrooms, house phones and information points. We saw a number of groups dressed up to the nines enjoying afternoon tea. Lovely to watch! Thirsty Camel piano player and guitarists / singers were brilliant. The pool areas were clean, tidy and very well attended by staff. There are several pools - one adults only. The main pool is big, separated into three sections with noodles, balls, volleyball, basketball hoop etc. Great for both kids and adults. Splash pad and water slide for kids are brilliant! The water slide is staffed and has CCTV so kids are totally safe. Jugs of iced water were handed out to guests regularly which was fantastic in 105 degree heat! Poolside bar service offered from 10.30, including alcohol and food. Cactus garden is shaded and provides a nice way to spend 30-mins or so. Flight of the Phoenix show on the lobby patio was great! Saturday night movie night by the pool with glow-sticks was something else - everyone was having so much fun! I've given separate reviews of the restaurants at the Phoenician and I can categorically state that the food and service in all the restaurants we visited (J&G, Il Terrazzo, Oasis, Surge, Relish) were top notch. At the end of our 10-day stay our food/beverage bill (including a few extras such as a couple of purchases at Grain & Grape and in-room films) was just over $3,000. Not cheap but on par with similar resorts we've been to all over the world. We loved all our dining experiences from a bowl of granola in Il Terrazzo to filet mignon at J&G. No complaints whatsoever. Great food, service and staff. The staff at the Phoenician are a true asset. We didn't encounter a single soul who wasn't friendly, efficient or extremely helpful. Staff said hello all the time and if we were out walking, we'd always get a friendly wave from staff riding around the resort in golf carts. A few times they actually pulled over to ask us if we wanted water or to tell us where to go to get the best views etc. From front desk to concierge to housekeeping to poolside to restaurant servers, the Phoenician offered some of the best staff we've ever met. Even the groundsmen sweeping up leaves and doing odd jobs always stopped what they were doing to say hello as we passed. We really appreciated those kind gestures. What was really nice was that most members of staff knew/remembered our names. In a resort with many rooms/guests, that is impressive. Ordering taxis? No problem. Getting luggage stored? No problem. Late checkout? No problem. Fully itemised bill? No problem. During our entire stay, nothing was a problem for any member of staff. In fact, on one day I got bothered by bees around my sun lounger and a poolside attendant, Jake, kindly picked up all our towels, bags, water, glasses etc and relocated us somewhere else. On arrival, our son was given a soft toy and an information pack about the resort. Room service was, without doubt, the swiftest I have experienced. My husband had to work for 4 days in Phoenix during our stay and the TransStyle drivers who serve the Phoenician were fantastic. A couple of times my young son and I went into town by ourselves and we simply called the driver who dropped us off and he came to collect us. No hassle, no fuss, drivers chatty and good for local advice, tips, restaurants, places to go etc. Faultless service. All in all, this place is excellent. There were a number of stand-out staff for us including Brian (poolside - so friendly!), Jeremy (blond), Jeremy (brown hair), Kris, Jacque, Robert (concierge), Jake... this list isn't exhaustive; ALL the staff at the Phoenician were unbelievably amazing. Thank you all so much for an absolutely amazing stay. We met several well-travelled families during our visit (from both the UK and the US) who stay at the Phoenician for several weeks every year simply because it is so good. That, for me, is a clear indicator of the Phoenician's excellence. We will be back! xxx

Beautiful resort This is probably the most beautiful place you can stay in Scottsdale. I accompanied my partner to a conference here in late April. The scenery is spectacular -- the mountain, the three golf courses, the cactus and flower gardens, the pools, the waterfall and the koi fish pond. The resort is only a 5-minute cab ride to Fashion Square mall, fun restaurants (Salty Senorita, Morning Squeeze) and a vibrant club district. The hotel itself is pretty spectacular as well. The staff are great. Our room had everything we could want and the bathrooms are very spacious. Great hotel - wish we could have stayed longer We stayed a single night at the Phoenician and it was great for our quick stay. We booked two connecting rooms (2 adults + 2 kids), and although initially they had lost our connection booking, they were able to find us two adjoining rooms with a limited delay. The kids thoroughly enjoyed the hotel pools, especially the water slide (although I wished the slide were located in an area where you could easily see it from the deck chairs). Their only complaint was that ducks repeatedly landed in one of the pools they were swimming in, which scared my 5-year-old (although other kids seemed to think it was an added bonus). My daughter rated the chicken fingers served poolside as "the best ever." The pool area was packed and it was hard to get chairs together, so would advise going earlier than we did. Our rooms had no view to speak of (booked on points, so not surprising), but they were very spacious. We ate at the Italian restaurant above the pool area, dining outside in near perfect weather. The kids enjoyed running around on the lawn, chasing real bunnies which appeared. They were also showing a movie on an inflatable screen in the pool area, which was great. We got the sense that there were a number of activities at the hotel (we just missed some sort of birding show), which if we had stayed longer I'm sure we would have been able to take more advantage of. The cactus garden located behind the hotel was a nice little area to explore. All in all, a very nice resort, very family-friendly, and we would happily stay there again.

tripadvisor · 2015-03-20 · 3/5view source

Disappointing. 5 star resort; 2 star room. Our family stayed at the Phoenician's Canyon Suites last June and my review was entitled "Wow!". It was deservedly the best review I'd ever written. For March break we decided to stay at the Phoenician.The 2 properties share the resort; but that is about all they share. First, some pros: The resort property is beautiful. The lawns and gardens are amongst the best we've seen. The main lobby is large and grand. The burger bistro Relish was our favourite on site restaurant with delicious food, excellent service and casual but classy ambiance. There are numerous pools that are kept at a nice temperature. Some general cons: pool was woefully understaffed for March break time. Towels were piled up and often not available. The bathrooms ran out of paper towels with garbage cans overflowing and filthy floors. Food service was slow and spotty. Newspaper delivery didn't happen, and when I'd go to lobby to get one (before 9 am) they were usually "all gone". As for our specific experience: We stayed in a casita room in order to have our car handy and be close to the pools. It was very clear there are different classes of rooms here, regardless of the room category. The casitas that are closer to the pool are bright and open up onto the lawn and a fountain looking at the resort and camelback mountain. The casitas south of these border the entrance ways (and roads) and golf course. Our first room was on the first floor in the "O" building and without a doubt had a notation: "do not rent out ... unless it is March break"! Worst room we have ever stayed in, 5 star or otherwise. Dark, dingy, stained carpets, bubbling and peeling wall paper, unusable walk-out deck. The safe wasn't working (low battery signal) and wooden hangers in closet had an inch of dust (clearly the room hadn't been rented in a long time ...). How does Starwood reconcile a 5 star resort with advertised AAA and 5 diamond service and quality and let out rooms in this condition? "Fully booked" is how. After 2 nights I went to desk at 9 am to at least voice my displeasure assuming nothing could happen as the hotel was fully occupied. Kaitlin was the supervisor and apologized profusely. No argument from her on state of room. She said we could move that day and it would be ready in the early afternoon but without question by 4 pm. I was very grateful. Phew. We packed after lunch and room wasn't ready until 4:30. We were moved to building H which was still a casita in the "second tier" of buildings on the roadway. But it is on the second floor with a view of golf course so at least brighter and the drive-by car noise not as loud. Arrived after dinner at 8:30 pm and the room was really warm despite the AC set to 68 so we called the front desk. Tony the engineer (great guy) came to check it out. He was up on the roof for 20 minutes and advised that the compressor was shot so no air conditioning for the night ... My husband went to the front desk and had a tete a tete with the on duty manager. The foregoing issues were explained along with our frustration. She said they would do something for us and move us again if air didn't work the next day. We left the room at 8 am to let Tony and crew fix the AC; it just started working when we arrived back at 2 pm. Ultimately, after a feeble offer of a meal (no drinks) at Relish as an apology to us, the hotel comped us 2 nights of our 6. This was the right thing to do and was appreciated, but it doesn't take away from the incredibly negative experience we had. If you have the $ to stay at Canyon Suites, by all means, jump at the chance. But unless there are some major renovations to the rooms at the Phoenician (we were told by more than 1 staff member that major renovations for the casistas are planned for the Fall!), and given the array of luxury 5 star resorts in Scottsdale (Four Seasons, Biltmore, Fairmont, JW Marriott etc), the risk of a bad room (less than 5 stars!) given the cost of the stay is not worth it. We will return to Scottsdale but doubtfully stay again at the Phoenecian.

Great relaxation Hotel, service, ambiance, golf course, & spa under the control of the Phoenician were top notch. Only negative was that I booked via Southwest Vacations who used Expedia as their hotel packager. I thought the package route for Air & hotel would be more convenient. Unfortunately, I believe the % of the room fee paid by SWA/ Expedia reduced the hotel's yield that the available room was very distant from the lobby and the pools, etc. The room quality was very nice - just a long walk away. Prior to booking via SWA vacations, I checked the hotel web site and verified that the per day room cost was comparable. My conclusion is that there are two extra commissions when using SWA vacations so that the hotel's yield is much lower - they fill distant comparable rooms with SWA/Expedia bookers. I will stay at the Phoenician again. I just will take the extra step and book directly online.

Service is excellent, property is beautiful, beds not so good.. The property is beautiful, the service is excellent and the rooms are very clean and good size. The pools are very nice, but it’s hard to find a chair on a crowded day. You may end up on a less comfortable lounge set off in the grass away from the pool. Not great if you are watching kids. The restaurants on property are just OK and definitely overpriced. Another issue, due to security, cabs can’t get on property, so unless you happen to catch one that is dropping off a guest or willing to wait 30 to 40 minutes for the hotel to call one for you, you are stuck using the onsite car service. While very nice, they are expensive and you can find yourself paying $25 + tip for a 12 minute drive.. This issue makes the location bad, unless you have a car.

Camelback wrap-around Was here for a business meeting and, although our room 5084 was large with a king bed, desk, lounge chairs, double closets, fridge/coffee maker and big bathroom, it had a stunning view of the roof of the conference center and the room balconies opposite. Their golf course wraps around Camelback Mountain and consists of 27 holes (three integrated 9-hole courses) with desert and lake features. At the rear of the hotel is a cactus garden with over 200 varieties displayed along a pathway which is illuminated in the evening. Rental bicycles are available or you can hike to the top of Camelback if your heart can take it. Sculptures and paintings by local artists are on display in the lobbies. There are a number of swimming pools and a water slide Did not use the spa. Saw many families with children and there is the “Funicians” activities club for kids. There is a concierge desk where you can arrange day tours to Sedona, Tombstone, Navajo Nation or Grand Canyon. Had a relaxing dinner outside on the Terrazzo restaurant. Menu was soups, salads, salmon, chicken and beef on an Italian theme. Service was attentive but not cloying. Picked up breakfast sandwiches and coffee at the Café and Ice Cream Parlor near the shopping arcade and main lobby which is brown and beige and has a fountain in the middle. Hotel staff were pleasant and efficient. The hotel taxi service took us to the Camelback entrance of Fashion Square Mall for $15; got a Scottsdale cab back for $10. But you do need a car if you stay here and we will rent one the next time.

Great place for families I stayed here with my family of 4 and our friend's family of 4 over Thanksgiving break. tripadvisor · 2014-12-27 · 5/5view source

Excelent Luxury Resort The Phoenician is a hidden gem nestled on the base of Camelback Mountain. As soon as we arrived, the attentive bell staff were at our car opening the doors, and taking our luggage out of the trunk. The lobby is magnificent, the clean, shiny marble floors really adds the classic yet elegant lobby. The front desk staff were exceptionally nice, they gave us a "desert view" room overlooking the front of the hotel, which we were not happy about. So we went back down to the front desk and explained that we would like a different room. They were apologetic, and they quickly moved us to a new, beautiful "city view" room. Our room overlooked the pool, but in the morning and at night the sunrise/sunset was beautiful over the city's horizon. The room was extremely comfortable. The hotel provided 2 plush bathrobes and an array of toiletries. The room also had a porch, with a lounge chair and a table with chairs. Off of the lobby by the convention center escalators there is an area of shops, and a business center. The grounds of the resort were beautiful, the waterfall, cactus garden, and the amazing views of Camelback Mountain were definitely one of my favorite parts of my stay. The golf courses were amazing, also the restaurant above the golf shop "Relish Burger Bistro" is a must stop! The pools were very nice, and refreshing. The resort's restaurants Il Terrazzo,J&G Steakhouse, and Relish Burger Bistro were all superb. The Thirsty Camel Lounge, was a great place to go for a quick drink or snack. The patio off of the lobby was simply amazing, the view of the sun rising and setting over the Phoenix skyline was pristine. When you want to leave the resort to go somewhere, the bell staff would have your car waiting for you in minutes, with bottle(s) of water for you in the cup holders. When you arrived back at the Phoenician they would open your doors and valet your car. The bell staff would also give you a lift on a golf cart to any area on the resort. Overall I would definitely stay at the Phoenician next time I am in Arizona.

I come for the High Tea! If you want to experience something new,cespecially if you have little girls, then go to the High Tea at the Phoenician. It is served daily in the Lobby tea court. tripadvisor · 2014-11-13 · 5/5view source

Room Elves Last week my husband and I (in our late 50 early 60's) had the pleasure to stay for 6 nights in a Grand deluxe room. Although prior reviews state the facility needs to be updated I find the marble and decore part of the Phoenician charm. When we arrived we were greated by Andrea at the front desk- we found her to be so friendly & sweet- in fact all the staff at the hotel would always great us with smiles. It was so nice to see those smiles that for once it appeared they really loved their jobs. We were in a room on the 3rd floor which is the hotel lobby floor facing the pool. Loved this room as no elevator to take only to the parking garage, steps down one flight to the pool area. Our room overlooked the pool and lawn which every day we got to see the bunnies come out to play/eat from. The room was big- double doors to the bathroom, the extras - lip balm, shower caps, loofah sponge to the wonderful hair products, lotions & bath salts. We had a king bed with a sofa, coffee table 2 chairs and a work desk. Double closets and a wet bar. Every time we left the room we came back and it was re made- all fresh towels, turn down service was also so nice- they put out slippers by the bed and leave chocolates and fill the ice container- and turn on soft music. I would have loved to catch them but they were like elves- never saw them. I almost thought we were on a cruise ship as we have only had that kind of service on one- never before a hotel. This trip was a belated 30th anniversary trip and the staff made sure to make our stay special- Thank you Andrea for the bottle of Champange and chocolates- they were wonderful and allowing us to have a late check out for our flight home. We did the self park, only one night we had to park at the far end, you park and then its a short walk to the inside lobby elevator - we found all the elevators to be fast. The 1st day we spent at the top pool area- water was a bit cold, after that we spent the rest of our pool time at the grand pool where the cabanas are located- water there seemed to be warmer and pool also a little more cleaner. Kudos to Mario and the pool staff - Jeff , Rich and Roven for also making our stay there so special and fun. We loved the cabana and all the little treats that came with it. Next time we will rent it for the whole week! If you have a family splurge and rent one as it is a great place to hang out for the day and you have your own private wait staff who on our trip far exceeded any other hotel cabanas we have rented from. They have a water slide we used several times- lots of fun! Make sure to check out the cactus garden (located accross from the lobby)- we almost forgot and so glad we did not as so many different types to see- wished we had went sooner as they have lights on them and would have loved to see them at night as well. We ate at the Relish burger place(see seperate review) and our last day had the buffet breakfast. Once again the staff in both restaurants were so nice and made sure we were taken care of. The new manager in the breakfast area was so sweet- she made us feel like we were family - I wish I could remember her name- her's is a very different beautiful name so I am sure someone there will know who we mean. We went by the Tea Service several times -next time I would like to make reservations as it looked wonderful and fun. If you need to print boarding passes allow plenty of time as we tried and tried and could never get them done- we gave up after 30 minutes -I am sure if we went to the front desk they would have helped. We had a wonderful stay and cannot wait to return. Besides it being a 5 star hotel it is located not far from a mall, old town Scottsdale and lots of restaurants (within 3 miles) which gave us more pool time instead of driving a long way for dining. You cannot go wrong by booking a room here.

Good service My family of four (kids 11 and 8) stayed here for 3 nights. The staff was excellent. Our room was in a good, central location, on the same floor of the lobby overlooking the pool. The hallways looked a bit worn with stained carpet and peeling ceiling paint. We were disappointed to find out our only choice for our room was one king bed or two double beds. I didn't know hotels still used double beds! The room was large as was the bathroom with a nice patio with a table, chairs and lounge chair. The kids activity center was quite a hike from our room and when we got there (after a full day at the pool), there was no one to help with getting the video game system to work, much to the disappointment of my son. There was a ping pong table, foosball table, and some board games to play. I wish there were more organized activities for older kids. They do offer a golf cart ride to/from the activity center if the bellman is not busy. The pools were nice and plenty of towels and pool noodles to go around with attentive staff. The food and drinks of course were very expensive as at any other resort, but $17 for a bowl of chips and salsa seemed ridiculous to me. We got breakfast sandwiches from the ice cream café in the morning rather then spend a fortune for a full breakfast. The internet was very slow and our room door did not close all the way automatically. It was actually left open after housekeeping left one day. When mentioned all of this to the front desk at checkout they removed the resort fee from our bill, which was nice. It is a nice resort, but don't think I'd stay there again.

Pretentious overrated Dump!!! Never have I been this negative about any place I have stayed. I take in the culture, setting and truly try to find joy wherever I visit. tripadvisor · 2014-08-22 · 5/5view source

Pretty unbeatable luxury 5 star resort in beautiful surroundings I should preface this review with the fact that when you get to the level of 5 star resorts like the Phoenician, they're all pretty good , amazing in fact, so the only differences often come down to things like the proximity of the property to nightlife , landscaping of the garden areas , bars, restaurants and pools .. Which I realise is quite subjective .. This place caters for everyone's needs ! The decor in public areas is an opulent explosion of Italian travertine ,marble and water, fountains , crystal chandeliers ..it's like a palace ,but on the right side of tacky , not the wrong Vegas side! It's got some class .. Great valets help you get wherever you need to go on check in, we were here a week so had both rooms upgraded to beautiful Necklace Lake view rooms which were as big as suites and were very well appointed .. Great housekeeping, fresh towels and room clean ups TWICE a day, and everything clean and beautiful . Lots of food option restaurants on site from burgers to upscale steak ,catering for every whim and budget . I think for Scottsdale, this place is unbeatable , and bear in mind we checked in from the Four Seasons and are massive fans of that luxury brand which never disappoints . Although we don't play golf, this is a golfers dream too, there's a perfectly manicured golf course surrounding the entire estate and the backdrop of the imposing Camelback mountain adds drama to every tourists photo of the resort. Koi carp in the lake, 9 luxurious pools with cabanas means there's a lounger and space for every guest ..everything you think it's going to be from reading the website ..it is ! in a word it's unbeatable ..try it ..

tripadvisor · 2014-08-10 · 4/5view source

Wonderful Hotel We just returned from a five night stay at this hotel. Overall, the service is superior. We have stayed at many top hotels and the Phoenician wins the service award hands down. As an example, we always received a call to make sure that we were okay with the job housekeeping did on a daily basis. In August, Phoenix is hot so it's their slow season. However, we have stayed at the Kierland Westin a few times now and their pool is so crowded in the summer it's crazy. Not at the Phoenician. It did pick up by the weekend, but it was not bad at all. During the week, there were not many guests around. No problem getting pool chairs and the service around the pool was great (something the Westin has always needed help with in the past). Love how they just leave nice towels rolled up on each pool recliner and refurbish them during the day. The hotel terrace is a great spot at night for a cocktail. We also decided to do the Royal Tea which was fun and the food was great. You must have a reservation for the tea. Parking can be a challenge at this hotel if it's busy and you want to "self park". The spots are quite small so when big trucks or SUVs decide to park, it's very tough to get around them. However, the parking is below the hotel. so the cars stay cool. We did see a large roach on the first morning we were there. It ran across the room and freaked me out. We called the front desk and within minutes someone was there to spray the room. We never saw another bug in the room. We stayed in the hotel portion with a pool view. We were given the casita option but chose to be in the hotel itself and be higher up. We were glad that we went this route. We had the Grand Deluxe Room so we were on the top floor and the room was quite large for a normal hotel room. The one thing that I have noticed being mentioned is that the hotel needs to be refurbished. While the room was still better than most, at the prices they charge during the high season, a guest would expect top notch furnishings. We were told that the entire hotel will be going through a renovation next year. Overall, the location was great with easy access to numerous restaurants, the terrific Scottsdale Fashion Square Mall, Old Town Scottsdale and more. People have mentioned the Activity Center. I have no idea where this was located and wish I had known about it. I didn't see it on the map, but it might have been there. I think the hotel might want to have a better description of it in the rooms so guests know it's available. The only other negative I could mention is that one night a company was having a dinner at the pool area so the hotel took away several rows of pool recliners beginning at 4pm to make room for the dinner/reception. Normally wouldn't be a big deal but since it's so hot, a lot of people don't go to the pool until later in the day and the pool recliners that were removed were at the largest of the pools. Kind of a bummer but I'm sure this kind of thing happens at all of the big hotels. I would rate this hotel with 5 stars except for the roach incident (so gross!) and the furnishings just looking a little tired.

tripadvisor · 2014-08-03 · 5/5view source

Heaven in Scottsdale What an amazing stay, from start to finish! It was a three night stay for my wife's birthday, and we were greeted by the parking attendant with "I understand that someone is celebrating a birthday!" What a way to feel special. The rooms are large, and we are glad we chose a casita. It is nice to have more of a garden feel rather than being in the main hotel, and it is great to park right in front. The grounds are beautiful and well manicured. You would never know you are three minutes from Nordstrom. Great extras for the kids, like Surge, a splash pad that is so well maintained. S'mores night, which was yummy. Half priced meals for the kids at all restaurants, encouraged us to eat on property. Duck and koi feeding daily, the kids loved the interaction. The activity center was a great place for the kids to escape the heat with a parent. Movies to be projected, pool, ping pong, and board games. The only bummer is both the wiki and Xbox weren't working. Three different employees tried to figure it out, but really needed someone that knew what they were doing. A for attitude, they just weren't trained in the equipment, and neither are we. The pools were amazing. Clean, quiet, great service, and amazing quality food. What a great touch to have a pitcher of ice water brought over to us without asking. They even refreshed the ice as it melted. Whenever we walked throughout the resort, employees from maintenance to bellmen always engaged in conversation and asked about our stay. You do not feel like a number at this resort. The breakfast buffet was great. Hot omelet bar cooking eggs made to order, fresh fruit and pastries, and just request waffles or pancakes and they will bring them out fresh. It may be hot as blazes in Scottsdale during the summer, but so were the hotel rates. A great deal that will get us back again.

tripadvisor · 2014-07-17 · 5/5view source

Beautiful resort Just finished our second stay at The Phoenician, and can't wait to return. Ideally located just a very short drive from restaurants and shops, the resort is very peaceful. We come for the location, and the on-site golf. Rooms are tastefully decorated, ours had a massive marble bathroom, large shower and bath. There's art and sculpture everywhere, in the grounds and corridors. If you want to eat in the hotel there's options available, with daily happy hour specials at Relish. Prices do reflect the resort's status! We used the buffet breakfast once on our first day, preferring to venture into the town to sample cheaper and equally as good alternatives. Summer desert golf is quite a challenge, rates drop if you can tough it out after 11am. We did, and enjoyed 3 rounds across Desert and Canyon each day, Oasis was being worked on (9 holes each part, joined to make your 18. Staff are very welcoming and helpful across the resort. Have tried other locations across the years, this is our favourite.

tripadvisor · 2014-07-13 · 5/5view source

Beautiful hotel I've recently had a 3 night stay at The Phoenician following a 5 night stay a couple of months ago. There is little I can say about this property that hasn't already been said other than how amazingly we were treated while on holiday there. As you drive up to the hotel you have to stop at a security post, where they give you a card for your car and take some details, they even wished me a happy birthday, which was the reason for our visit. Then as you arrive at the hotel itself an array of staff start opening doors, welcoming you and taking your luggage. A 5 star welcome. There is a valet option but as self parking is free, we decided to self park but the valet staff took care of our car while we checked in. The lobby is gorgeous with chandeliers and marble everywhere. There was a short wait to check in and upon check in we were upgraded from a Superior, to a Deluxe room based on my SPG Gold status. While checking in, another member of staff handed us a water bottle each, very welcome on a hot day. The rooms are large and well appointed and the bathrooms huge. Each room has its own balcony and coffee and tea making machine. It was interesting to note that during our stay in May, the room had more modern furnishings. We actually preferred the classic style rooms. Not sure if they are actually updating them all or keeping a selection of both. We loved the turndown service which greeted us after dinner or drinks every evening. We'd come "home" to the bed turned down and all the bed decorations removed, tomorrow's weather forecast, some chocolates on the bed, the TV cabinet opened, slippers by the bed and all our toiletries attentively laid out in the bathroom. The pools here are numerous and one of our nights here fell on American Independence Day so the pools as expected were busy. The Phoenician did their best to help with wrist bands for registered guests, lots of staff and extra chairs. The service at the pools was fast and efficient, water was provided without even asking and food and drinks arrived promptly after ordering. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant every morning. There was great choice and the food tasty if a little pricy. There was a buffet available on two of the days, then on the Monday, it was a la carte. The hotel definitely has a feel if refined luxury about it but there are a couple of areas that could do with a little TLC, nothing that takes away from the great experience, but the lifts (called elevators in the US I believe) could do with being replaced. We were trapped in elevator 13 for some time and spoke to the hotel engineer via the lift phone but this was quite a scary experience. No one contacted us from the hotel to find out if we were OK afterwards but this didn't really detract from the whole experience. I will DEFINITELY be returning to The Phoenician.

tripadvisor · 2014-07-11 · 5/5view source

BEAUTIFUL OASIS We ended a two week vacation at The Phoenician. The Hotel- WOW - gorgous! From the moment you enter you are greeted by luxury. We had booked a grand deluxe room. We were offered an upgrade to the casita (but we loved the feel of the Hotel). We did look at the Casita but it seemed older and not as bright and pretty. We had an amazing view (4th floor facing the pool) outstanding view of the pools!! Very spacious room. Very clean. Large bathroom. We had a king bed and our younger children shared the pull out bed. The ladies at the front desk were super sweet. The Pools- We had a wonderful time at the pools which were not crowded. And being from NJ- we did not find it too hot. We had plenty of shade under the umbrellas and stayed cool in the pools. I Highly suggest - buy the $11 Surge cup and use it all week to refill your drink (ice tea or soda). Well worth the price as one ice tea would be $4. Loved the poolside service- especially on the kids menu the grilled chicken tacos...grilled chicken, lettuce on a soft tortilla, with a side of salsa and guacomole and tortilla chips. Everyone in our family loved these. The Mother of Pearl pool was gorgous!! We were disappointed that the "surge" splash area was closed...but the manager was so kind- she sent us up some snacks and a voucher for a free in room movie. The kids LOVED this!!! Thanks Jen!!!! The only downside to the hotel were the bee's. There was a lot of bees around the pool area. We stayed in the pool most of the day - only out to go to the bathroom and eat. I told everyone to watch where they walked so they didn't step on any. The birds could be annoying too but I was more worried about someone getting stung. My kids loved the pool side Chocolate and Vanilla Smoothies! DINING: We enjoyed all of the restaurants. El Torazo- breakfast Buffet --- omlets/eggs, delicious muffins (blueberry were the best we have ever had).... Terrific service. Dinners at Relish (Casual- amazing Chicken Sandwich)....we wish they had a side traditional salad as an option to the tater tots.....we would have gone back if they had. J&G Steakhouse- dined there twice. OMG the shrimp cocktail were some of the best we ever had. The Lobster cocktail was fair- we expected it to be different that what it was.... The Filet Mignon was the BEST... we also had Ribeye (we all enjoyed that but the Filet Mignon was the best). The asparagus was delicious. Everyone was very kind...Even thought J&G is very upscale, they could not have been more friendly and accommodating, they allowed our kids to walk in from the ice cream shop with their ice cream in hand (we allowed them ice cream before dinner!)- it is vacation. Cactus Walk - Highly recommend this tour- the hotel had it- it was on property and the kids enjoyed the walk as did we. No charge, but we did tip the man as it was a fun experience. Oldtown Scottsdale- For $30 roundtrip the hotel will take you about 2 miles away. The kids enjoyed purchasing trinkets for soulveneers. I had wished they were open later so we could go at night but most of the stores are open from 10am-5pm. So we went early 10am so that we could spend the rest of the day at the pool. Highly Recommend Olive and Ivy Restaurant-Fantastic!!! WE had flatbread pizza, bruschetta, Caesar Salad...EXCELLENT food and service.... The stores were just ok. The kids were happy with their little gifts. The Spa at Phoencian- We had visited a few other spa's in Arizona and we felt the spa needed updating. There should be a much better area for men/women to relax together. For Example in Sedona Mi Amo Spa has a co-ed indoor/outdoor pool area for guests... would have been great to have an hot tub (co-ed) and a much nicer relaxation room. The lazy boy leather chairs were kind of cheesy-- we did like the running water feature. Everyone at the spa was super nice. Jean gave an AMAZING massage. Highly recommend him. We got vouchers from TravelZoo- pre-paid discounted massage. The spa charged $28 for gratuity which was more than fair! Concierge- was super friendly and helpful. Thank you Michelle!!! Overall- My husband said this was his favorite hotel of the three we had stayed in. He enjoyed the live music in the lobby at night (piano). He enjoyed the luxury feel. Everyone was very nice. Very clean and pretty property. We would recommend this to our friends. If you go during busy season rent a cabana at the Mother Of Pearl Pool- well worth it - you get reserved seats in the cabana as well as outside of the cabana in the sun. Last thought- they said they are trying to make it more of a family place... would suggest more activities at the pool for the kids (games every few hours run by the kids club).... and maybe an covered outdoor play area like at the Westin Keirland - Outdoor Huge Chess set, fooseball, ping pong etc).... Thank you for a wonderful end to our vacation!!

tripadvisor · 2014-07-11 · 4/5view source

Just shy of perfect ! We quickly changed our destination from Naples Fla (Impending Tropical storm / hurricane) to Scottsdale to ensure great weather (sun & Heat). With less than 1 week to plan we found the Phoenician and surprisingly they had availability for the busy 4th of July weekend and following days. We were offered a " summer Special" which gave us spectacular savings incentive so we booked. As part of the special the $29 daily room fee ( internet) was waived and wifi was free to use while we stayed. When we checked in we had to call the desk to get the free wifi use we were promised when booking as part of the summer deal. Every single person at the resort that we encountered was friendly, professional and most of all the were beyond accommodating. The entire staff smiles at you and greets you as you enter / exit / walk thru . We noticed genuine hospitality and definite desire to ensure that you as the guest are satisfied. The customer service was excellent, and nothing like I had ever experienced in the U.S. ever before. I had asked the front desk the morning of our second day If it were possible to have some " Firm" pillows brought up to our suite. The receptionist said " absolutely, and I am so sorry if you didn't get your routine sleep requirements. I will have them brought up. What is your room number and your last name?" I told her and she then smiled and said, " Mrs. Burger I will have those pillows up to your room. I hope that tonight you will be as comfortable as you are at home." Again Sincere and a can do professionalism, and that is just the initial request. My husband I made our way to the bakery in the lobby and by the time we finished our breakfast, and returned to our room, the pillows had arrived. We headed out for the day and when we returned, we noticed that the receptionist had left a message on the phone " wanting to make sure that the requested firm pillows arrived and were to our satisfaction". Amazing follow up and polite ?? Not so common but Awesome ! The rooms are very spacious. We stayed in a Mountain view King. The rooms are clean and well maintained. The décor is up to date and the beds are comfortable. The bathroom is spacious as well. The rooms and the resort are very clean and well maintained. Our room had a great balcony with some furniture and a fantastic view of the " camelback" mountain. My husband raved about the Golf course. He rented clubs at the course and said they were so great he may buy new clubs to match the set he rented. The pools (9) are very nice a bit too much chlorine I think, but there are many children and wildlife around that appearently also like the pool. There were plenty of chairs during the week, but the weekends can be more challenging to find chairs. There is an adult only pool which we truly appreciated. The hotel has many activities for kids and is very kid friendly, however we are not. There are Water yoga and water aerobic classes offered as well. There is a poolside menu of food and drinks which we did have one day, but it is a bit pricey for what you are actually getting. The Iced tea and soda's are $3.50 and they do not offer free refills. We spent $50 for lunch ( no alcoholic beverages) The wait staff are very friendly and they do bring free ice water and cups to everyone quite frequently. There are a lot of Bees around the pool area, be careful. The hotel also has a very nice Fitness room that was very busy but too busy that you had to wait for a machine. They have ellipiticals, treadmills, free weights and machines Cycling machines. There are towels and water available as well. They even offer daily fitness classes. My only reasons for not giving this hotel the best rating of " Excellent" are described below. These reasons are minimal in the entire scheme of things. But I do think they could be easily improved upon and should be. The rooms' privacy or " do not disturb" sign is a black leather door hanger. The word " Privacy" is etched into the hanger and is not obvious at all. In fact I didn't know the room had a privacy sign and as I was in the shower, the mini bar agent had come in after knocking (loudly). I asked if someone was there and he quickly replied : Just checking the mini bar, " he exited quickly and I was never exposed as bathroom doors were closed. Very awkward for Me and for him but He was totally professional and I was not informed of / did not notice the door hanger until well into our 3rd day there, shortly after this incident. I would suggest that the " Privacy" hanger stand out . Additionally, the room lights are mostly lamps, the lights are controlled by switches on the lamps not the walls. Different but not terrible. We checked out and my husband noticed that our bill had the $29 daily fee for all days we were there on the charges, however as part of the " summer Special" this daily fee did not apply.So he again had to call to get these removed as promised when we booked. Also we Had incurred some various mini bar charges, but we did not have anything from mini bar, we just used the refrigerator for our own water bottles and iced tea. We are still working on getting to the bottom of these charges, as we are not certain what they are. There is a nightly turn down service and they bring chocolates and water to the bedside, we thought this was free but as it turns out it may have been part of those mini bar charges, although we are not sure and still are trying to figure it out.

tripadvisor · 2014-07-10 · 5/5view source

Fireworks Galore We were visiting relatives in Phoenix and they suggested driving over to The Phoenician on July 5 to see the fireworks. What a beautiful hotel! We were greeted warmly at the gate and told where to park. A short walk through the well-manicured grounds and we found a wonderful old-fashioned Independence Day party in the works. There was a live band, children happily running around; lemon water if we were thirsty. The staff offered a mat if we wanted to sit on the ground (which we were given to take home!) or a chair. Later they brought everyone glow-sticks for more fun. The fireworks show was fantastic; early because of a threatening storm - but no one seemed to mind. Kudos to the hard-working staff - everything was so well planned and executed. If this is any indication of the hotel's overall service, we'll be back as guests!

tripadvisor · 2014-07-09 · 5/5view source

Great 4th of July Staycation My family enjoyed our stay at the Phoenician for the 4th of July weekend. First of all, I must state how surprised I was that this resort was very family friendly. For the holiday weekend, they had many activities for the kids ranging from t-shirt painting to their own indoor carnival. I was truly impressed! The resort grounds are kept in good shape. Our room was very spacious and clean. We had turndown service every night. The restaurants on site were good but if you are staying a few nights you may get tired of the same food fairly quickly. Don't worry, they are quite a few restaurants from the resort within 5 miles if you need variety. This resort had alot to offer...numerous swimming pools, splash pad for kids, activity center(includes a small movie room,xbox games, board games, etc.), golf course, hiking trail, tennis courts,etc. I was going to give this resort 4 stars. But I am going to give them 5 stars instead due to the excellent service I experienced from the time I pulled up to the door to the day we checked out. I can't wait to see what festivities they have planned for next year!

tripadvisor · 2014-07-06 · 4/5view source

4th of July weekend I probably would have enjoyed this stay more if I didn't have the expectations of a 5 star hotel. I would not call this a 5 star hotel. The room we had was outdated and had an odd smell. It looked out over an ugly roof and had no view unless you leaned way out and looked to the right and you could see a little sky. The first night we had turn down service. None the second. The housecleaning crew came while I was still in the room the first morning and I asked them to come later. They never returned and so our room was never cleaned over the two nights and three days. The resort fee was pretty outrageous. I get a little bitter when every little thing is added as fees. Drink at the bar was undrinkable. We threw it away and it was $15. I asked for a taxi to downtown, was offered a shuttle service. I wasn't told it would be $15 to go 2.4 miles. The pool was very nice but very crowded. We couldn't get chairs for both of us so we shared. The service by the pool was good. They had a lot of activities all weekend. Probably best for families with kids. I was interested in a cocktail mixology class and called the number listed to reserve a spot three times. No one ever answered. The highlight was fireworks last night on the patio. They were beautiful and we enjoyed the live music too. Service on the patio was good, although the smoking bothered me. I appreciated the underground parking to keep the car cool. Overall, decent room, nice resort, okay service, not what I would call 5 star based on my experience at other 5 star hotels.

The best customer service ever! What a resort/hotel! We have just come back from 5 nights at the fabulous Phoenician and really did not want to leave. Great hotel! Although the weather was about 109 degrees, we totally enjoyed our stay at the Phoenician. The grounds are huge and lovely. Breakfast which was included for us was delicious! Oasis My wife and I spent the weekend at this resort. We arrived in the evening and decided to use their fitness center. They have an amazing center and the walk to it is pretty nice. tripadvisor · 2014-06-10 · 5/5view source

Lovely and met expectations I was recently there with three friends to celebrate a milestone birthday. The hotel is about 20 minutes from the airport. We were greeted by professional and friendly front desk staff, who accommodated our request for adjoining rooms. The rooms are spacious, and very clean. There is a small Keurig with coffee and supplies. There was complimentary Starbucks brewed coffee in the Italian restaurant on the first floor every morning. The bathroom has two sinks, separate water closet and the shower is separate from the tub. There were plenty of clean, fluffy towels and washcloths. A hook for your towel would be helpful near the shower. The shower door is not frosted, so if someone is showering, the bathroom is not really available, which would be a problem if you aren't with a significant other. There is a decent hairdryer provided, as well as the usual toiletries. There are many different pools, all of which were clean, with plenty of lounge chairs, umbrellas and clean towels. Someone was always bringing a pitcher of cold water. There were child friendly and family friendly pools as well as adult only pools. The spa was lovely and professional, and clean. Four of us each had 2-3 spa treatments over two days, and all but one were excellent. The one that wasn't excellent was just an ok massage. The concierge was helpful with a private tour guide arrangement to Sedona, and also sent us champagne to celebrate our birthdays. The restaurant, Relish, was terrific, serving specialty burgers. We also ate at the Italian restaurant, and it was lovely. We all agreed that it was overall a fantastic experience, and we would return, maybe even with our husbands and children. Top notch.

tripadvisor · 2014-06-07 · 5/5view source

Perfect Getaway This resort is top notch all around. Excellent for golf or tennis enthusiasts, couples, families, or babymooners. My wife and I stayed at The Phoenician for 5 nights for a final warm weather getaway before our baby arrives. It exceeded our expectations. The hotel right is next to beautiful Camelback Mountain. There are plenty of activities (golf, tennis, several pools, several wonderful restaurants, hiking trails, bike rentals, etc) available, but if you're looking to simply relax, you can catch some sun near the pool and enjoy a cocktail or 2. In my wife's case, the staff toyed around with several non-alcoholic "mocktails" which was really appreciated. While there is plenty to do on The Phoenician grounds, if you're looking to get away, Old Town Scottsdale is just about a mile or 2 away. There are several bars, restaurants, and an upscale mall as well. When we ventured offsite for dinner, we tried Chelsea's Kitchen (southwestern), The Henry (a little of everything), and The Mission (mod Mex). All three were wonderful, as were all three of the restaurants on The Phoenician property. I highly suggest a burger from Relish and/or a steak from J&G. Now onto the staff/service... One day we rented bikes, and on the way back, my wife got a flat when we were still about 5 miles away. The hotel had a driver pick us up and return us. Belinda at the tennis shop/bike rental office was so kind to send Phoenician hats to our room later that evening as an unnecessary apology. Just one example of the staff going above and beyond. Every night, there were chocolates by our bedside and turndown service several times a day as well. Last but not least, a special shout out to Sam at the pool bar. She was very accommodating, making different "mocktails" for my wife, engaging us in friendly conversation, and providing candid feedback on things to do/places to see around the area. While we came to the resort primarily to relax, I used the gym several times, and the facilities are well above average from what you'd see at other resorts. My wife had a tennis lesson and was thoroughly impressed as well. Not a negative, but one note for potential visitors: There is a daily "resort fee" which covers in-room wifi, tennis, bike rentals, etc. Overall, a truly relaxing getaway with top notch service, plenty to do, and large, above average rooms most of which have beautiful views and balconies. I would highly recommend this resort to anyone looking to travel to the PHX/Scottsdale area. We plan to return at some point in the future.

tripadvisor · 2014-06-01 · 4/5view source

Pampering in the desert A great resort for golf or R&R. We stayed a week recently for a company event and were impressed. Set right up against (Camelback?) mountain – many of the guest room patios allow a lovely view straight up the vista. Other guest rooms look over the resort’s expansive golf course or manicured desert scape. All guest buildings were serene and quiet according to the friends and coworkers travelling with us. We were on the mountain side and enjoyed watching the iguana and quail each morning. The facilities themselves were very good. Although the age of the resort shows through occasionally (like the shiny silver and brass fixtures in our bathroom) – the resort is all about high end, up to date finishes. Our guestroom was huge, well-equipped and clearly renovated recently (only exception being those faucets and handles – why!?) Of course with all the resort amenities you’d expect – bathrobes, slippers, etc. We tried most of the on-site restaurants and liked J&G Steakhouse and the Thirsty Camel Lounge the best. The Camel has gorgeous views and entertainment after dark – really enjoyed that spot. My husband golfed and raved about the course. Neither of us got to the spa but we did enjoy the resort pool – or actually pools. There’s lots of pool/sun decks to choose from – which is a really good thing when it 110° in the desert. Plentiful umbrellas and tree shade – keep the pool very comfortable even in the middle of the afternoon. Food and beverage service outside is quick and fairly priced. Our only criticism would be about the chair cushions. Most were stained and dirty from ducks and birds. We were really taken aback to see such a thing at such a highly ranked resort. Put extra towels down! The resort is also just a short drive from old town Scottsdale, as well as a very high end mall and more. Suffice to say that there is lots nearby to keep you busy should you run out of things to do at the Phoenician – but you probably won’t! We hope to visit again.

tripadvisor · 2014-05-31 · 1/5view source

Left a sour taste One bad apple can truly spoil the barrel. I know I am being hypercritical and The Phoenician probably deserves 3 stars but I can only give it one. For the most part it is a nice resort showing it’s age. The toilet seat cover fell off when opened, wallpaper was pealing and the ice tongs were sticky (all unacceptable for a first-class resort). But my biggest complaint comes from the service or lack thereof at the pool. I was visiting on business but had an hour to spare at the pool and to eat lunch. I had one of the guys working at the pool set me up with a lounge chair. I told him I wanted to order lunch and could he please get me a waiter. 20 minutes passed and no service. I approached Orlando, who worked at the pool but could not take food orders, and asked if he could please get me a waiter. Another 20 minutes passed and still no service. I was fed up and approached Orlando and this time asked to see a manager. 10 minutes later Jeff, the pool manager, approached. I expressed my dissatisfaction and he offered to take my order. By then I was out of time. He took my name and room number and thanked me for my input. The entire event left an extremely sour taste in my mouth. Someone should have called my room or at the very least left an apology note for when I checked out. Needless to say there are numerous resorts in Phoenix and Scottsdale who want my business and will provide the 5 star service I expected.

Fantastic Hotel and Amazing Staff I loved this resort:I travelled alone on business. I checked in at 3pm but my room was only ready around 4:30pm after a 11 hours of travelling. tripadvisor · 2014-05-13 · 5/5view source

Why would ANYONE give this place a negative review?? If I could give the Phoenician more than 5 stars I would!! Let me start by saying we are SPG Gold members. At check in they offered to upgrade us to a suite but since we arrived at 11am, and the suite wouldn't be ready until 4:00, AND we were only there for one night, we opted for a standard room which was ready for us right away. By standard, I mean there was no view (if you call the gorgeous palm trees "no view"). The room (in the main building) was lovely, large and with a huge terrace with a comfy chair and lounge. The king sized bed was SUPER comfortable and the pillows among the best at any hotel I've ever been too. The bathroom is large with a lovely sunken tub, separate shower stall and a separate room for the toilet. I can't for the life of me understand the people who gave the rooms bad reviews. Now for the service. Impeccable! They couldn't do enough for us!! The bartender (Steve) at the pool bar (one of the several pool bars) made me the best Prickly pear Margarita, and then didn't charge me for it! He only charged my husband for his. And it's not like we'd been there for hours or days..it was our first (and it turned out only) drink at that bar! The young man in the ice cream parlor/snack shop was not only incredibly polite, when I went in to buy just a banana, he told me "No worries, just take it". Who does that? And then there are the attendants at the pool. Ok yes, the pool area is BUSY. It's Scottsdale and it's 100 degrees out. If you couldn't get a lounge, get there earlier! Don't blame the hotel or the attendants! We explored the hotel and waited until 3:00 because it was so busy and then found a couple of chairs together. Right away we were brought towels and a pitcher of ice water and two glasses. The ice water was refilled for us about 45 minutes later. We had dinner at the "Thirsty Camel" because the other casual restaurant was filled. Two fabulous personal pizza's out on the terrace with drinks (two free drinks as our Gold welcome gift from the hotel), a guitarist playing and the gorgeous Scottsdale sunset....I can't gush enough. Oh yes, and because I had mentioned on our reservation that it was our anniversary, they sent up a bottle of champagne and some chocolates! And by the way, we didn't even PAY for the room, as we did this particular night on starpoints. We will most DEFINITELY be back.

Stunning Paradise with a couple small quirks Listen this place is the real deal and truly exceptional - beautiful grounds, stunning pools, very good overall service, comfortable rooms and best of all is the weather - I really wanted to give this hotel 5 stars as it's worthy of the designation but there were enough small things that I wanted to take the time to share for cure visitors The Good - pools are just fabulous - my wife and I have 4 kid and love kids and this is a great place with kids or without...some adult only areas and great kids areas too with basketball net in pool and tons of fun - plenty of chairs - awesome tennis program and head pro Jason was likely the best teacher we have ever had - can't say enough good things about this guy - I could go on and on but really this place has it all What could be improved upon - let me start by saying there is not much but a few things that were just plain frustrating; - rooms are getting tired but are still very nice but if you are expecting 5 star rooms this is not your place but rooms are beautiful circa 1995 Reno but kept up very well - pool gets busy and I feel bad for hotel because when hotel is at 98 percent capacity which it was when we were there they need to add a dozen more staff around the pool....staff are tremendous but clearly not enough of them to go around - breakfast is so funny and frustrating...again u can't help but feel bad for hostesses because every person complains...there are dozens of empty tables and 20-35 min waits for outside...similar to pool situations for staff serving lunch and getting drinks there is simply not enough staff to keep up with demand...it's a simple operational issue for hotel where if they came and watched the few bottlenecks it could be easily addressed as it's solely human backlog A few interesting facts that I could not find in advance that I think folks will be interested in - price for cabana rental by the pool ($300 during the week and $350 on weekend per day - I could not make a reservation at a popular restaurant myself but Beverly the concierge worked magic for us and made a reso at a place that does even take reservations which is very cool - I found out last day I waited for no reason for breakfast every morning when u could make a reservation so don't do what everyone else did and gets upset waiting for 20-25 min when u simply can make a reso for breakfast...I didn't know but now you do - they sell bottles of water at store and in rooms but there is free bottles at tennis courts and workout room so really no need to waste your money there - we stayed in a casita room overlooking the pool in building F on 2nd floor and it's wonderful to hear the fountains and it's central to everything - you can order lunch by the pool from any of the on site restaurants which is not obvious as they only brig a menu from the pool side bar and grill and I totally recommend Relish Burger Bistro - wonderful option - just leave an hour from time u order to delivery To conclude - would we stay again...absolutely without a doubt - management needs to watch the couple frustrating bottlenecks I described above as they are easily fixable - rooms are getting a little tired but way better than others ha said online it's truly not a problem to me but does need a refresh soon - love the tennis, thirsty camel lounge, grounds, pools, ice cream shop and much more - excellent service overall If you pick The Phoenician you won't be disappointed but hopefully this review helps and ads some additional feedback not found in others

tripadvisor · 2014-01-09 · 5/5view source

Your Best Starwood Option in Scottsdale – The Phoenician If you are trying to decide on whether to stay at The Canyon Suites or The Phoenician Hotel, I hope this review helps in your decision. Fortunately, we have had the opportunity to stay at both properties. I must first say they are BOTH excellent properties and truly some of the best that Starwood has to offer. Comparing platinum recognition, price, convenience, guest room, and service, The Phoenician is definitely the winner. Let me explain why. Platinum Recognition –The upgrade and recognition we received at the Phoenician was much better than the Canyon Suites. The Phoenician provided us with a suite upgrade, local gift, and waived the resort fee. We did not receive any of these upgrades at the Canyon Suites. You changes of getting an upgrade are better at The Phoenician since they have many more suites. Price/Hotel Category – The Phoenician was much more affordable and requires less Starwood Points. The Phoenician is a category 5 hotel and The Canyon Suites is a category 6. There is truly not that much different to spring for the higher prices or points. The Phoenician also offers cash and point more often. Convenience – Most of what you will want to do at the resort will be located closer to the Phoenician’s property. This include tennis, gym, spa, & golf. We loved parking in front of our Casita at getting into our car quickly for short trips to the mall, store, or dinner. At the Canyon Suites, they offer free car valet service, but it takes a while to get your car. They also have a free car service; however, it is rarely available. You should note that staying at the Canyon Suites will have you feeling a bit “removed” from the center of all shared resort activities. Guest Rooms – I actually preferred the rooms at the Phoenician. The Casita we stayed in was spectacular. The kitchen, fireplace, dining room table, and three balconies were new and picture perfect. The Canyon Suites rooms are a bit dated with 70’s décor. Customer Service – Both locations have outstanding service. Everything from check-in to property maintenance was perfect. Everyone was friendly and helpful. Helpful Hints – Pay extra to stay in a one or two bedroom Casita. They are spectacular. Make sure to take a hike up Camelback Mountain. Access to the trail is just a short walk from the tennis courts. Try the Happy Hour at Relish. It is fun and there are great deals. Have a drink and/or dinner at J&G on the property. Go before sunset to enjoy it. The views are beautiful. Play a game of tennis, which is included in your resort fees. The hotel will provide complimentary rackets and balls. The grass court costs $35 per person and a great splurge if you are a tennis nut. Breakfast at Il Terrazzo is very good. As Platinum members, you get an $18 credit for two ($36 total) towards your breakfast bill. If you prefer, your breakfast will be completely complimentary if you opt for the continental buffet breakfast. If you are looking for the best Starwood value in Scottsdale and want to be close to that action, you will definitely want to stay at the Phoenician. It is one of the best Starwood Resorts in the country.

Great for relaxation and golf My wife and I booked a 4 day stay on SPG points to get away from the cold Northeast, and play some golf just after Christmas, 2013. The hotel itself is on beautiful grounds, well kept, and great scenery all around. As I am a Gold SPG member, we received a base room but with a gorgeous view of Phoenix and the surrounding area. The service was impeccable, and I cannot praise the staff for always looking to go 'above and beyond' It is exactly what a Luxury Collection hotel should be, plus more. Unfortunately, the only restaurant we ate within the resort grounds was Relish, a bistro burger bar. I am a man who enjoys food, and even though the burgers were priced at $16.99, you did get a lot of burger. In addition, we did spend some time at the hotel lounge/bar area, and the wait staff was on point. If you enjoy golf, the resort has 3 9-hole golf courses onsite, and I was only able to experience Desert, and half of Canyon, due to Twilight play. The course/fairways are well kept, the greens are gorgeous, and the course is challenging. For a novice golfer such as myself, I was able to keep the ball in play for the most part, but some of the holes can be quite narrow, with sand traps and rocky areas, aplenty. The golf staff was really courteous and professional. The pro shop had plenty of clothes to purchase, however, I didn't see many ball sleeves. I could have missed these altogether, but just in case, make sure you bring a few extra sleeves of balls if you have a tendency to lose them. This will help you in the long run. Overall, the resort was a bit pricey, BUT you do get what you pay for. Professional service levels, well kept grounds, and a great experience all around. Although this was my wife's and I first trip to the Scottsdale area, we will make sure to return someday and make The Phoenician our resort of preference.
