tripadvisor · 2013-12-21 · 4/5view source

Casita Rooms Are Convenient for Golf, Spa & Parking We had two rooms at The Phoenician for a two-night stay in December. Both rooms were given SPG Platinum upgrades to Casita Rooms. These rooms are roughly the same size as the rooms in the main building but are located in a separate area. Staying in these rooms means you're closer to the golf course, spa and mother of pearl pool. You'll also have a bit more privacy and you'll park your car for free right in front of your room. The downside is that you'll have quite a walk to the main building for access to the free SPG Platinum continental breakfast (if you select that option) or other food & beverage offerings. The golf club house does have a restaurant as well, but will not have as much to offer as the main building. An alternative is to take your car up to the main building when you're dining. The valets were very accommodating and would leave our car right out front without charging us any fees. The room worked well for us since we had golf plans. The main pools were closed during our stay for renovations so we didn't utilize them. The SPG Platinum breakfast is a good option if you're eating on a weekend when they have the buffet, however it's not offered during the week so you'll order from a menu. The service was good overall. Standouts were the omelette chef and server at Il Terrazo. I'd recommend trying drinks and small plates at the Thirsty Camel lobby lounge during sunset. SPG members should note that golf charges do not accrue SPG points.

Luxury Resort. Great Spa, great golf, fine dining and entertainment. Loud jackhammers. For me back for the first time in over ten years, the Phoenician Resort has been a recurring meeting place for my wife's business. But for this weekend, it a fun getaway weekend for the both of us. My wife loves the health spa, I love the Scottsdale golf scene and we both were looking forward to hiking the desert trails. Overall, things turned out great, but we were initially very disappointed with the loud jack-hammering going on with the pool rehab project. What I thought would be a show stopper is now a faded distant memory; so many other good things figuratively muffled-out the noise. By the time we were leaving, we were already making plans to come back. The Phoenician is located at the foothills of the Camelback Mountains in Scottsdale. The resort is a very luxurious hotel, a main building with normal hotel rooms, conference meeting areas, luxury shopping, multiple tiers of swimming pools, and a perimeter of smaller 2 story cottage like building with semi-private rooms, called Casida Guestrooms -- we stayed at one right next to the golf course and Centre for Well-Being spa -- which my wife loved!! Room. Our Casida Guestroom had a beautiful view of Camelback mountain and the swimming pool complex. The room had a nice king sized bed, huge master bathroom with big shower, jacuzzi-style bathtub, two sinks, and walk-in closet. The room had a normal flatscreen TV, Internet (included with the room) with both wired and wireless connections, and for a nice touch the turn-down service set the clock radio to some really nice mood music. We didn't use the room mini-bar. Golf. Our room was across the access lane from the Phoenician golf course. I played a couple of rounds there first day on the Desert, the second day on the Canyon course. The courses were in excellent condition, even though the morning tee times were delayed by frost. The course runs along the foothills of the mountain, making for some really nice low-to-high and high-to-low golf shots; overall, I consider the courses mid-difficulty, not that hard. The course edges up to the desert and we saw beautiful desert plants, roadrunners, and quail. The pro-shop and starter staff did a great job. I was thrilled when they recognized my 10 year old bag tag from my prior Phoenician visit. Poolside. While the weather was cool (low 50s) and we weren't planning on much swimming, we were disappointed that half of the pools were being rehabbed. Loud jackhammers spoiled the poolside atmosphere. But on Saturday, the workers took a break and we spent the late afternoon by the mother of pearl pool. My wife even swam in it; (yes, it was a heated pool); I covered myself in beach towels. A separate time, we sat by the fire on the outdoor patio. While cool, the sky was clear with very little wind. Very refreshing -- and much better conditions that the snow and ice falling over the rest of the country. Both times, the Phoenician staff did a great job taking care of us. Food and Drink. The lobby level has a piano bar -- a very nice place to relax and have drinks; we heard 3 different live performances. On Saturday night we had dinner at the J&G Steakhouse; there, we had a really fine dinner, a great view of the Phoenix sunset, and yet another excellent live band. The J&G was packed; it was a lively hopping place!! While we saw a couple of families, the resort seemed to cater more to business functions and conferences. We were thrilled when the golf starter called out for the St Louis Rams group to tee off. If you are still reading this far down, you need to understand that this is a really nice luxury resort -- these are code words for: It's expensive! We knew this coming here, and overall, it is competitive with other luxury places we've stayed over the last couple of years. Hiking. New for me, we went hiking. My wife's business meetings usually included some kind of activity in the desert. She took us to the McDowell Sonoran Preserve. Here, the desert trails run along the foothills of the McDowell Mountain Range about 30 minutes North East from our hotel. We hiked the Lost Dog Wash Trail, the Bajada Nature Trail, and the Gateway Loop Trail. This was beautiful. We saw big beautiful Saguaro cactus as well as barrel and cholla cactus. Much more lush than I ever thought a desert would be. Basketball Game. We went to the Phoenix Suns vs Toronto Raptors basketball game at the US Airways Center in downtown Phoenix. We went straight from the hiking trails to the game. The game was fun, very good play from both teams; we sat near some visitors from Canada. The courtside announcer was full of energy; the dance crew, the gorilla, and the contests between the basketball timeouts were fun. The stadium was new and the facilities were really nice. We were able to park close and cheap.

Beautiful hotel with beautiful gardens in very nice location We stayed here for birthday celebration for two nights and this was a very pleasant experience. tripadvisor · 2013-11-28 · 4/5view source

Sprawling resort, excellent service If you like big, sprawling resort properties ( 9 swimming pools, 3 -9 hole golf courses ), this is for you. The property, while it shows some signs of age and need for refurbishment, is flawlessly maintained. The staff have obviously been well-trained, as the standard of service is not only high, it is very consistent. Reflecting its size, there is a wide range of accommodation types available, from conventional hotel rooms with no view, to golf course villas to casitas. Food is pricy ( fish sandwich, salad and a beer poolside $ 48.00 ). Although there are 9 pools, one of which is described as " the relaxation " pool, with children banned, you cannot get away from the piped-in music. if you want a quiet time by the pool, you can't do it here. The onsite J&G Steakhouse ( which turns out to be a Jean Georges restaurant ) is excellent. Be advised that there is presently construction underway at the both the extreme east and west ends of the property, so that if you are located at either end, on weekdays you will hear heavy equipment, jackhammers, etc.

tripadvisor · 2013-11-22 · 4/5view source

Very attentive staff I stayed here for 2 nights following a trip to the Grand Canyon. I am Gold, and they upgraded me (I had booked a standard casita) at checkin to a 'lagoon view.' However, this casita seemed like a stepcousin to the casitas facing the pool - it was remote, dark, and also overlooked construction. I went back to the front desk, and the check-in agent was great in finding me a similar room in a better location. I was very satisfied with the service in general, from the bartender (Sean) at the Camel Lounge to the servers at Relish Bistro. I thought the room furnishings were a bit dated, and couldn't believe they still had the old-fashioned thermometers (round, with a dial) in the rooms. One disappointment (first world problems, but hey I'm paying an astronomical resort fee) is that I didn't get any turn-down service the first night, and the second night, someone came by at 10:00 p.m., which in my opinion is way too late. Perhaps it was because I was in a casita and not in the main hotel, but they need to step that up. One great thing, if you are a fitness buff, you can walk to Camelback and hike there and back while everyone else needs to find street parking. Very convenient. Was it the best hotel experience I've ever had? no. It was perfectly servicable, which isn't the best for a Luxury Collection. If I had gone in peak season, and paid a lot more, I would have been much more disappointed. But, the weather was good, I slept well, I ate and drank well, and I would recommend it to others.

tripadvisor · 2013-11-17 · 4/5view source

Service, service, service We recently spent 4 nights at The Phoenician while my husband was on a conference. The stand out of our time spent there was the calibre of the service which we received. This was across the board and included the concierge (who were just so incredibly friendly, helpful and informative), the dining staff in both the restaurant and the conference dining area (who were so obliging in assisting with foods to accommodate my food allergies),the maintenance guy and others too. Whilst we were there we had delicious Mexican Wedding Cakes and when we got home I emailed the hotel asking if it were possible to get the recipe and it arrived in my inbox within the hour!! So thumbs up for excellent service :) The pool area is lovely with plenty of shade if required, which is a pleasure. The room was very nice and spacious but nothing ooh aah. I guess one could say it is a typical Sheraton room of it's time - not suggesting at all that it needs renovating. It was in very good nick and I enjoyed the balcony with lounger. The food in the restaurant was very nice. We ordered 6 meals all up there and they were all great. The food served at the conference was a bit disappointing. Certainly nothing to rave about. It would have been nice to be able to get toast at breakfast. Perhaps this has to do with the choices of the conference organisers.Not sure. All up a great stay at the Phoenician and I can recommend it

tripadvisor · 2013-11-03 · 4/5view source

Great Lobby and Grounds... Hotel appears to be recently renovated with ample parking / valet, spectacular grounds and nice rooms. Service was good, check-in quick, and lobby very nice. Only complaint, was the large party happening outside our window at the pool. Wasn't objectionable to us as it came with some good music to listen to off our balcony. tripadvisor · 2013-10-28 · 5/5view source

Spectacular Resort and Spectacular Staff The Phoenician is a luxury resort, to say the least. From the luxurious rooms, awesome pools, or the spectacular staff. Everything at the resort has the "Phoenician" branding from the water bottles to the towels with the hotel's logo to the bags with a hotel's logo. I don't even know where to start! When you pull into the lobby, bellman open your doors, take your luggage, and even give you Phoenician branded water with the hotel's logo! We arrived at around 1:00 p.m. and they were able to rush the room and get it by around 2:30 to 3:00ish. In the meantime, we went to Relish Burger Bistro, which was fantastic by the way (our family of 4 only needed 2 burgers we realized afterwards), where we were waited on by the awesome and helpful Rachel. She helped us a lot to kind of get to know the area! It is helpful to know that the resort does provide golf carts to shuttle guests around the property since it is so huge-- we had one take us to Relish from the lobby. We had a guest casita room, which was incredible. The spacious bathroom included a huge marble shower, a large soaking tub, double vanity, and a water closet with a toilet and bade. However, we were disappointed that our room wasn't conveniently facing the pool, rather, it was facing the golf course, which was ok too. The large outdoor patio included a chaise lounge as well as a set of table and chairs. We all really enjoyed the pools! There is a huge, elaborate pool complex which is basically made up of 3 levels. The top level, which has 3 pools and a kiddie pool. The middle pool is one large pool that the resorts splits in half-- one side is family friendly and the other is adult only. Finally, you have the bottom level with the water slide pool and the fantastic Mother of Pearl Pool which is all tile with the Phoenician logo in the middle, which was our favorite. The kids loved the slide which was wild at the end and gave everyone a few injuries. We especially enjoyed George Alexander the slide attendant! Now the pool situation can be a bit frustrating. Half of the chairs are in the shade, which is a problem for people like us who want the sun. However, there is one catch to the pool situation which was annoying, and would bring the hotel's rating down. Large businesses rent out parts of the pool complex so the guests can't get near the lawn with their event. During our stay, they rented out 3 of the pools including the Mother of Pearl Pool! Now this really ticked me off. Why would a hotel let a business rent out a pool and block it off from their guests who rightfully paid for it!!!?? That is just wrong-- the guests should be the priority, not the businesses! But in the end, this is a management problem, and the staff can't do anything about it-- this is the manager and owner's fault. On the other hand, all the staff we encountered did put the guests first. EVERYONE was so kind and helpful! Everyone always asked how our stay was and what they could do to make it better! I should've told them that they should open up the pools that they closed for the businesses! Overall, the hotel and grounds are gorgeous and staff is very helpful as well. The view looking back towards Camelback Mountain is breathtaking! I'm sure I left plenty out but I tried to cover a lot. I do definitely recommend Scottsdale Fashion Square for shopping (it's a mile down the road). It was also worth the drive to the Kierland Commons up north. Additionally, we took a drive to Sedona and it was so worth it! It is a must do if you've never done it before!

tripadvisor · 2013-10-27 · 3/5view source

Older facility meant for the golf crowd Without doubt the views from the property are amazing and amenities were most likely top notch 'in the day'. This property looks and feels as if it was once an gem and has been holding onto a heyday long gone. It truly has the makings of a gorgeous hotel however the cream marble and brass fixtures mixed with some of the newer pieces, accentuate even further what is out of date. Handrails throughout the property were wet with paint during our visit, so obviously the 40th coat when replacing them would provide an aesthetic upgrade and tactile confirmation. Upon arriving our room was changed from the first floor (where there was loud construction) to the third floor. After a walk down a very long hallway, that had no lights and still surrounded by machine noise, we arrived to a half update room. Request a room closer to the elevator. Apparently, the third floor had been used for a convention/meeting rooms recently and they were putting furniture back together and cleaning up wet carpets. Perhaps this is why things didn't match in our room - three different eras of lamps and incongruous art? Car service and valet were stellar. They were prompt and helpful with information about the area and able to give us an idea how long to get where we were going each time. Bell service was confused with our room change and I ended up going back to get my luggage to bring to the room myself. Housekeeping began knocking at 8 a.m. and came back every 20 minutes - even after asking that they come in the afternoon. Several items in our mini bar were stale and out of date - a bummer when you are hungry for a snack and have acquiesced to mini bar rates for convenience. The golf courses looked pristine and the hotel guests seemed to be mostly older folks and families. The children's pool was busy while the adult pool was moderately populated with Ricky Martin on the radio and men drinking cans of beer in the pool playing water basketball. A trip to the spa was telltale that this is not the touted 5 diamond resort & spa that it once was even though the pricing (which is elevated on the weekends regardless of being a hotel guest). Manicure pedicure services are in the hair salon while the 2nd floor of the spa is reached by an industrial "wood" formica elevator. Not a recommendation. We booked elsewhere after canceling our appointments. The gym was clean and the equipment looked new and well kept; floor to ceiling glass made the small space seem airy and inviting. The food was excellent at JG Steakhouse and the bar and live entertainment excellent. I would definitely recommend the restaurant, bar and the ability to sit outside next to the fire pits with a cocktail. Service at JG was top notch - attentive and personable without being intrusive. Not a bad hotel - just not as fabulous as the website leads you to believe.

tripadvisor · 2013-10-25 · 4/5view source

Loved it! This is my second time to Scottsdale and first time at The Phoenician. Overall my boyfriend and I really, really liked the property and our stay. The space itself is beautiful and Camelback provides a great view. We received an upgraded room prior to checking in and also received some coupons for breakfasts and dinner upon check-in, which was great. (This may be through a Starwood frequent member type program, I'm not sure.) We had a corner room that was a two-room suite, which was really spacious and included two bathrooms. The only negative was that it was a bit far from the pool and restaurants. The bed and turn-down service was great though! The pool area was great and included 8 pools with one adult relaxation pool. My only suggestion would be to have more adult pools and just a few reserved for kids. The adult pool was shaded most of the day so it was mostly families instead of some quiet that we were hoping for. There was no wait for chairs and the staff brought out a pitcher of water right away and kept it filled all day, which was great. The waitstaff was really friendly, but a few more servers probably would have been helpful as there was a bit of a wait for food/drinks. We ate lunch by the pool each day and the menu and food was good. I wasn't as huge a fan of the dinner options at the restaurants on-premise, but I did enjoy the live music by the lounge/bar at night. We headed into Scottsdale for dinner two nights and had really blah meals at two places that had great reviews, which was surprising. The cabs seemed really pricey for the distance ($29 for a ride that was maybe three miles?!) and the places were really not worth it. (We went to Wildfish and Roka Akor.) The spa treatments were overall really good, though not cheap. The spa itself was pretty nice, but lacked much outside of the treatments itself. There is a meditation room, which is basically an outdoor quiet area with nice chairs. There was also a steam room and jacuzzi, but it left a little to be desired. I had an excellent treatment with Sara and highly recommend her. Overall a great stay and just what I was looking for - R&R. We're already planning to come back next fall.

tripadvisor · 2013-10-14 · 4/5view source

A lovely desert oasis...perfect for a long weekend We booked a 4-night stay for the two of us before my husband had to stay for the following week for a business meeting. The hotel is only 15-20min away from the airport, and is close enough to Old Town that you have plenty of restaurants and activities from which to choose. Hotel Overview: The lobby is spacious and grand, with a beautiful fountain as the centerpiece. A grand piano serves as the focus of some light evening entertainment, with the Thirsty Camel bar overlooking the grounds. Check in was smooth and easy and we got into our room shortly. It is a large property overall, so be prepared for a lot of walking in between your room and the other areas of the property. Some stairs as well, so maybe not as convenient for those with mobility issues. Room: The rooms are a nice size with a king bed and sitting area (sofa, chair, coffee table) plus a desk. The balcony was a comfortable size as well with two chairs and a padded chaise lounge. We overlooked the pool and cities of Phoenix/Tempe in the distance. There is ample space for clothes with TWO full size closets (very nice to be able to separate clothes) and a large bureau with several drawers. Bathroom is very large with a deep soaking tub, double sinks and a walk-in shower. ONLY complaint (and it is a small one) is that the shower head is low-flow (I'm sure for conservations reasons...being in the desert and all) and it took awhile for the water to get hot. Very small complaints, but it was something I noticed. Pools: There are many different pools on different tiers of the property. There were always plenty of padded loungers available in the morning, but they would fill up pretty quickly in the afternoon. Attendants would bring extra towels and a pitcher of ice water with cups. This was a wonderful touch that I honestly have not experienced anywhere else, even at the top beach resorts we have visited. Hope they don't stop doing this! There are plenty of shade options, including umbrellas. Attendants stroll through if you want to order a drink or food. The lowest tier pool has a slide attached, so that is where most of the kids are...if you want a quieter experience, go to the "adult's only" pool by the cocktail bar. Restaurants: We ate at J&G Steakhouse our first night and really enjoyed it. We ordered salads, filets and a side of potato gratin and it was all amazing. Nice ambiance and the servers are well trained. Would recommend, even if you are planning to eat some meals off property as well. We ate breakfast each morning at Il Terrazzo and it was always an enjoyable experience. Definitely get the "Il Terrazzo benedict" poached eggs with spinach and tomatoes on top of foccacia bread- delish! Spa: Had two treatments at their "Centre for Well-Being" and they were both nice. The spa itself is actually pretty small, so don't expect a large property. There is a small jacuzzi, a steam room and a sauna...plus a co-ed area with zero-gravity chairs to relax in before your treatments. I had an 80min massage and 80min facial, and they were both pretty average, but nonetheless relaxing and enjoyable.

Fabulous This hotel is fabulous. The rooms are really large and spacious with gorgeous views and a lovely balcony. The staff is welcoming and helpful. Everyone couldn’t have been more helpful. There is a bar with an outdoor area and fireplaces! Such a great ambience. Hotel parking costs $29 per day, so not inexpensive but it is a city. The food in all of the restaurants was very good. I highly recommend staying here for any reason. You will love it!

tripadvisor · 2013-09-29 · 5/5view source

Exceptional Anniversary Trip!! This was our first trip to the Phoenician and we were extremely happy with everything!! I surprised my husband with a trip here for our 20th wedding anniversary and couldn’t have picked a better place to stay! After about a 20-25 minute ride from the Phoenix airport we arrived around 3:00 pm and were greeted by the very friendly and professional Kaitlin at the front desk. She congratulated us on our anniversary, informed me that we were upgraded to a 1 bedroom casita and made sure she added my Starwood number to our reservation. She went over everything with me, pulled out a map of the property and showed me exactly where our casita was and that we could park right in front of the room. I took the keys and we were on the way! We stayed in Building “F” and were able to park directly in front of our door. The casitas are 2 stories and do not have an elevator so we were quite happy that we were on the ground floor. Our room was one of the most luxurious rooms we’ve stayed in. (It’s right up there with the Ritz, Peninsula or Four Seasons in Chicago and Boston). We had 2 full bathrooms, a very large living room with a fireplace, dining room table with 6 chairs, work center (fax, printer, internet connections) desk and a very large bedroom. The bedroom also had a large desk/chair, 2 side chairs and table, 2 nightstands and a foot-bench at the bottom of the king size bed. The mini-bar/fridge was fully stocked with everything you could need and the master bathroom was almost the size of the living room! The bed was incredibly comfortable, the towels were very soft and absorbent and the toiletries smelled fresh and exhilarating. We had 3 sets of sliding glass doors that allowed you to walk out onto the 2 different patios. There were more than enough chairs/lounges on the patios that you have several couples over for cocktails. You could walk out the patio, across the lawn and a bridge and you were at the “lower” pool. We spent all of our time at this pool and on our patios. This was an excellent building to be in because in the afternoon the patio stays in the shade and when the sun is BLAZING out there you can sit on the patio, stay cool and enjoy the views. Service at the pool was excellent. Every lounge chair had its own towel already on it waiting for you to sit down. As soon as you did, one of the servers came by with an ice cold pitcher of water and 2 cups. With the heat index it was 100 degrees when we were there so the water was refreshing and welcome. Rich was our server and it was incredibly helpful without being over-attentive. Because it was so warm we ate lightly and had the tuna salad sandwiches. They were delicious and had a very nice spinach salad as a side. We couldn’t have asked for a better trip. The Phoenician was wonderful and made our anniversary even more special. We will definitely go back for a visit and are already taking about spending our 25th anniversary there!! Thank you so much to the entire staff who made us feel so special during our visit and we will continue to tell all of our friends about out tript!!!

Very Happy Big room, very well appointed, quiet and overlooking the pool. Staff were all friendly and helpful. Great pools and we had a fabulous meal in J&G steakhouse, Whilst we didn't use any sport facility they all looked fabulous. If we visit Scottsdale again The Phoenician will definitely be our first choice place to stay. We were staying over Labor Day weekend and the hotel planned many extra entertainment events, we really enjoyed the bird display. tripadvisor · 2013-09-18 · 5/5view source

A week in paradise at an amazing luxury resort My wife and I just returned from a fabulous 8 night stay at The Phoenician. Our stay at the resort was truly exceptional, which is what prompted me to join TA and write my first ever review. We were celebrating my wife's 50th b-day and wanted a week of complete rest, relaxation and to spoil ourselves - and that is exactly what we got. My wife and I can be very critical when it is justified, so we feel it is only fair to also be complimentary when it is well-deserved. We stayed in a 1 BR Casita Suite which was very spacious, had luxurious furnishings, and was most comfortable.The mattress, duvet, sheets & pillows were perfect (wish we could take the set home with us). The room was immaculately clean upon arrival and kept as such throughout our stay, with turn down service each evening. We had complete quiet/privacy, while at the same time being at close proximity to the Spa, the Golf Clubhouse, and the 'Mother of Pearl' pool. Shortly after checking in, the hotel was kind enough to surprise us with a bottle of champagne in honor of my wife's 50th birthday - very thoughtful and appreciated. After our daily early morning walk, we had breakfast most mornings at Il Terrazzo, and I have to say that we were pleasantly surprised by the quality & selection of the breakfast menu and the world class service of the wait staff. After the first day, the hostesses greeted us by name upon our arrival, and we were seated at the same table (per our request). The manager (Marc) and our waiter most days (Paul) and the rest of the staff went out of their way to ensure we had a great start to the day. I highly recommend the Yogurt Parfait, the omelets, and the 'everything' bagel with smoked salmon. We spent time relaxing at all the pools, and were very pleased with the various amenities such as the plush new towels, the comfy cushions on the loungers, the many umbrellas available (as we mostly like to be in the shade). In addition, the pool attendants bring the guests a pitcher of ice water which is a nice touch, though there is also a great assortment of food & beverage offerings at a reasonable cost considering it is a 5 Diamond resort. We had lunch by the pools several times, with the Turkey Burger and Chicken Wrap being our favorite choices. We wanted to highlight one pool attendant in particular - Benjamin B. - who provided outstanding service. For dinner on our last evening we were fortunate to receive the assistance of Eric at the concierge desk who was able to get us a reservation (a prime table at peak dinner hour on a Saturday night) at Mastro's City Hall Steakhouse (5 minutes from the resort) - without Eric's help we would not have been able to get a table as Mastro's was completely full all night. I played a few rounds of golf, and although there are three 9 hole courses, I suggest the Desert & Canyon courses which are the most picturesque and challenging. The staff in the pro shop and the starter were quite friendly and helpful. We each had 2 treatments at the spa (Centre for Well Being) as well as using the steam room & meditation lounge on most days. The facilities are wonderful and the experienced therapists gave absolutely great massages. After every visit we felt refreshed & rejuvenated. After our first visit to the spa, we were also greeted by name on each subsequent visit by Phillip at the spa reception counter. The grounds throughout the resort are nothing short of spectacular. From the time you turn off Camelback Road and drive up to the main building, the majestic palm trees and flora greet you to make a memorable first impression. We loved strolling through the cactus garden, watching & listening to the numerous fountains, discovering the native artwork throughout the property, and watching the koi fish in the lagoon, etc.... The main lobby & bar is also quite impressive and a great place to have a cocktail and listen to the evening entertainment either inside or on the patio overlooking the resort. We've stayed at other resorts in Scottsdale (Westin Kierland, Fairmont Princess, Hilton Tapatio), and we've traveled extensively across the USA, Europe and Asia; and I have no qualms in saying our stay at The Phoenician was the best overall experience we've had - by far. Any discerning traveler would undoubtedly appreciate the heightened level of customer service and attention to detail by the staff as well as the deluxe accommodations, dining options, activities, etc... We will absolutely return to this spectacular resort again next year.

tripadvisor · 2013-09-15 · 4/5view source

Grounds & view lived up to "Luxury Collection" branding, rooms not so much Husband and I celebrated our anniversary here over Labor Day Weekend. Stayed 1 night - the Saturday of Labor Day Weekend. Consistent with other reviews, I'd say the rooms were my least favorite part of the hotel. They were better than average and spacious, but definitely felt more dated than luxurious. At check-in, I believe the front desk confirmed I had a Platinum upgrade....Ground floor at the end of the wing. We had no noise issues which was nice, but again, there was nothing special about our view. Service was ok. Again, not spectacular. Waited a while to check in on Saturday around 5:30pm. Someone at the front desk finally gave me the "we'll be with you in a moment" when she must've seen my irritated face when when another guest approached and looked like he wanted to cut in front of me and not wait his turn. We made it in time for last call at the Relish bar for happy hour. Initial service was nice as they put in our order at 5:58pm so we could get the specials before they ended at 6pm. After that, it felt like decades before we were checked on again. The resort had a nice outdoor concert and 2 food trucks on the lawn by the pools Saturday night for Labor Day. That was a nice surprise. Interesting that some reviews mentioned there being an "Adult Only" pool at the resort. I didn't see any note of that during our stay but would've definitely liked that if they had offered and enforced that. All in all, I'd say our stay was ok. I wouldn't go out of my way to plan a trip to Scottsdale and stay here, but I would recommend this resort (with my words of caution above) to anyone who will be traveling to Scottsdale. Don't expect uber-luxury and you should have a fine stay. We stayed at the Westin Kierland the next night and it had its pros and cons too. If pool time/relaxation is what your looking for, you will probably have a better chance of achieving this at the Phoenician.

View is the best part, rest is okay Having grown up near this resort but never having stayed here I was curious to stay here on a visit back to Scottsdale. I am a frequent guest at the other top resorts around Camelback so I wanted a change of pace. tripadvisor · 2013-09-14 · 5/5view source

World's best Babymoon!! After visiting the Phoenician last week for our "Babymoon", I am not surprised to learn the resort is the #1 rated Luxury Collection hotel in the Starwood chain!! Wow! What an experience! My husband and I both work stressful jobs and we desperately needed some R&R before our baby makes her debut. I read way too many hotel and resort reviews before finally settling on the Phoenician. I was initially concerned about staying at the resort during Scottsdale's "off" season and worried the weather would be too hot for a 7 month preggo to enjoy the pool and sun. However, after spending four days there, I quickly realized that off season is OUR season. Because the resort wasn't at 100% capacity, we felt like we were given a lot of special attention (and maybe they make everyone feel that way all throughout the year). From the moment we checked in, every single person at the resort made sure our stay was exceptional. The ladies at the front desk were so kind and offered restaurant advice and appropriately commented on the nature of our trip. They even gave me a gift-- a Starwood Kate Spade golf bag! The bellman, the servers... Even housekeeping made our stay phenomenal. We all know you can stay in a beautiful building with the nicest amenities... But if your room isn't clean then your view of the hotel is diminished. The housekeeping staff at the Phoenician are some of the best in the country. We always had plenty of fresh towels, always replenished soaps and coffees, and the little extra touches like chocolate on our pillow and slippers by our bed at night was so appreciated. If you stay at the resort, I highly recommend participating in the resort events and activities. As a non-yoga person, yoga was surprisingly one of the highlights of my stay. Susanna, the yoga instructor is amazing and truly teaches on every level--including altering her class so that I could participate (full belly and all). My husband enjoyed the cocktail lesson and we loved the live music at the Thirsty Camel at night (see my separate review on Yelp). The bottom line of my review: Would we go back? Absolutely!!!

tripadvisor · 2013-09-11 · 3/5view source

I am saddened that she is not as I remember her. It is with sadness that I have to write a review like this, but I think it is necessary for other travelers who are coming here looking for a quiet and serene oasis. I have been coming to the Phoenician for over 20 years in which I have many wonderful memories. During the years it has changed hands many times. It was at one time the premiere resort in Arizona. After my last visit, I still believe it to be a gem in the desert, but until I feel I have a need or longing to come back, I will gladly choose the Four Seasons and here’s why. The Phoenician is a massively large resort requiring a tremendous amount of upkeep and maintenance. While they have done an okay job considering it is a resort encompassing over 600 rooms and suites, she is wearing down, and fast. Nothing has been done to really overhaul any of the standard rooms (besides suites) in the past 25 years. Carpets are dingy, floorboards and bases are dirty with old dust in crevices…it just looks old. The resort as a whole needs repairs to really look clean again. I would have thought within the past few years they would have attempted to update/renovate some of the standard rooms, but they have not. I knew the resort was looking a bit dated , but I kept coming back because it was still a quiet oasis to me with great service and it was still an impressive property. It was like coming home whenever we would visit Arizona. We were on a short vacation with my parents in which we were arriving later than them. My father informed me the front desk kept them waiting 3 hours to check into their room. The woman at the desk told them it wouldn’t be long, so they went down to the pool bar to grab something to eat. Over 2 hours later they were still waiting which resulted in a wasted day. If the front desk had just told them after many inquiries about the room that it might be a while, they could have changed into their swim suits and enjoyed a pool day. However by the time it had been 2 hours it was too late for that. Come to find out they kept them waiting while housekeeping shampooed the carpet. It was still damp when they finally entered the room. It was around the time of my parents’ anniversary so I had decided to send them three different gifts purchased off of the amenities section of the Phoenician’s website. I was very clear that I wanted one item to be delivered each night at 6:30pm over the 3 consecutive nights that we would be there. I even designated which item should be delivered on what date. I was disappointed to find that this instruction was completely ignored when the first night TWO of the gifts I had ordered arrived 1.5 hours before the designated time. Because we were still outside enjoying the pool, the chocolate covered strawberries were left out in the room to sweat and become warm (and undesirable to eat) and one of the other surprises I had ordered was ruined due to its early delivery. I called the front desk to express my displeasure and they referred me to in room dining who only apologized for the mistake without replacing the undesirable strawberries. I knew they screwed up, but they only went so far as to say they had sent an EXTRA of the fondue, rather than admit they made a mistake altogether without intention of sending my third surprise on the correct night. I told them it was fine when they said it would still arrive on the third night, although it really wasn’t because the surprise had been ruined. It would have been nice had they owned up to their mistake and offered to make up for it with something else, not just send a second of something they already got. My parents finished the second dessert the next night and left the tray of dirty dishes on the bench at the end of the bed for housekeeping to take. They did not want to put it outside their door because they feel dirty dishes outside hotel room doors just isn’t nice to look at. They left it in a spot that was more than visible for housekeeping to take. However, whoever turned down the bed that night not only neglected to inform the correct party to remove the dirty dishes (or take them themselves), they proceeded to knock over the martini glass full of chocolate onto the fabric bench, leaving a huge stain. Whoever the offender was attempted to wipe it up, although making it worse and even getting it onto the white sheets. They then PROCEEDED TO LEAVE THE DIRTY DISHES and the offending stains! Seriously? My parents had to go down to the front desk to inform them of the mishap so as not to be charged for something they didn’t do. This blatant lack of attention is not what I would consider 5 star or 5 diamond service. If you are looking for an escape from the craziness of daily life, DO NOT come here over a holiday weekend. It’s almost as if the Phoenician forgets their original vision…it was not at all quiet, serene, or an oasis. Loud obnoxious drunk people crowded the Mother of Pearl pool and restaurants, and after speaking with fellow guests, found there was some less than desirable activity of a sexual nature going on at the pool bar the Saturday night we were there. If the Phoenician has changed their vision, in which it appears they are marketing themselves as a family resort, is this something you’d want your children to witness? From what I have heard nothing was done to quell this disturbing display. I know the Phoenician may respond and try to defend the resort by stating they can’t control the activity within the resort walls, but they absolutely can. Slashing rates to almost $100 a night will cause this type of behavior to come trickling in. Considering I have never experienced this here before, I was appalled and disappointed with what I saw, and we always traveled here in the low season so that had nothing to do with it. It was a combination of slashing rates and heavy promoting of the Labor Day activities that caused the activities we saw. I can’t fault the wait staff at the Mother of Pearl pool; Rich taking care of the cabanas was as great as he’s been in the past, but I did see some cabana guests bringing in their own alcohol which is unacceptable and according to hotel policies, not allowed. However nothing was done to remove the offending alcohol from the premises. I was also under the impression that the pool just before the steps leading down to the Mother of Pearl pool is supposed to be an adult pool, although every time I went by there were children in that pool. Once again, the Phoenician failed to enforce their own policies. (Note: I am aware the Mother of Pearl pool is NOT adult only, although some guests believed it was supposed to be. The Phoenician needs to do a better job of informing guests of this, although I agree with other guests that it should be adult only.) The Phoenician also needs to put a limit on the amount of people occupying one cabana. We counted 12 people in the one next to us which was just overwhelmingly too many and invaded into the space we rightfully paid for. If I come back, I know not to come back over a holiday weekend. We stayed at the Four Seasons Labor Day Weekend in 2011 and it was nothing like what we saw at the Phoenician. Everywhere we went we could not get away from loud, obnoxious people. We visited in July 2012 and had a wonderful, quiet meal at J&G. This time we were accompanied by the same VERY LOUD drunk people that were by the pool every day. While the food was still good, the ambiance was less than pleasant and I had to shout just for my husband sitting next to me to hear what I was saying. We did not ask to be moved in fear they would stick us into some back room that wasn’t encompassing of the restaurant’s beautiful décor. All in all I will visit again if I know I can get back the experience that the Phoenician was once known for. For now, I prefer to remember her as she was in her yesteryear as she is not what she used to be.

tripadvisor · 2013-09-07 · 5/5view source

What a lovely experience! My husband and I are just wrapping up our six night stay at the Phoenician. I have always wanted to stay at this lovely, expansive hotel and I was not disappointed. This is our second trip to Scottsdale to play golf in the last three years and our trip did not disappoint. We checked in for six nights the day before Labor Day. Things were a little crazy Sunday, but everyone cleared out on Monday, so we basically had the place to ourselves for the week. The staff is lovely! So kind and helpful. The decor is nice and despite its age (the Phoenician is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year), it is extremely well maintained. All in all. . .I loved the place and was not disappointed after wanting to come visit for so long. The hotel is huge. If you are looking for a private, boutique experience, this is not your place. If you're looking instead for a property that offers everything you could possibly need. . . golf, spa, pool, restaurants, in an elegant atmosphere, this is it. We took advantage of all of that and were not disappointed. The room was large. I believe we had a Grand Deluxe room, which i understand is "grand" because of the view over the pool. It was lovely with a king size bed, a good size balcony, a sitting area inside the room with a desk, sofa, coffee table, armchair . . a huge bathroom with a large sunken tub, marble shower, separate water closet, two sinks. The room did not disappoint. The first night we dined at Il Terrazzo, a restaurant in the bottom level of the hotel which offers three meals a day. We took advantage of a three course, prix fixe menu with wine pairings for an additional nominal charge. I believe the charge for dinner was $29 each plus $10 or $15 for wine pairings with every course. It was a good value. . . the food was fine. . . nothing to rave about, but very solid. We enjoyed Il Terrazzo for breakfast almost every morning and was also not disappointed. ITs a beautiful restaurant with a lovely outdoor area if you're willing to brave the elements. The pool at the Phoenician is what I would call a Vegas-style pool in that it is huge and diverse with a bar and a restaurant in the middle, like an island. There are fountains and water features. . .an impressive slide for the kids that will land them in a separate pool off to the side. The place is huge with three or so different levels of pools. . . private cabanas are available for rent for $150/day. We originally rented one only to realize that the hotel cleared out after Labor Day and we pretty much had the entire three-levels to ourselves. We enjoyed the pool, the bar/restaurant. . . Steve was wonderful in taking care of us several afternoons. We enjoyed this part of our trip very much. Another highlight was the spa. Do not miss this! I enjoyed a massage and a facial while my husband also had a massage. What I thought was exceptional about this spa was Luanne, who provided a facial for me and shared her knowledge from 22 years at the spa at the Phoenician. She herself has beautiful skin that I attribute to her practicing what she preaches. I emerged myself with gorgeous skin that I have kept up with the help of some of the products I purchased at the spa and plan to continue using when I return home. The spa will ship for no charge. . . Golf was another lovely offering at the hotel. It was day 3 for us, so the heat had caught up. We didn't play our best game, but we enjoyed the course. We also played Troon North, Grayhawk and We Ko Pa on this trip, but the Phoenician maintains a beautiful 27 holes. I am still learning the game after picking it up five years ago, but I enjoyed the course. All in all, it was a lovely stay. I was honestly worried when I booked a six night stay that my husband and I would be climbing the walls after day four or five, but everything the hotel had to offer really made for a lovely, entertaining yet extremely relaxing stay.

tripadvisor · 2013-09-04 · 4/5view source

An Ordinary Stay The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Hotel in the Starwood family, is somewhat oddly located in the Scottsdale area. Fairly close to Old Town Scottsdale and the Scottsdale Fashion Square. The Phoenician is away from many other resorts in Scottsdale, but does have a great location in that it hugs the south side of Camelback Mountain. As you enter the property, you will encounter a guard gate. You will merely be asked if you are checking into the hotel, there for dinner, to play golf, etc. and pointed towards the appropriate parking area. The Phoenician offers valet parking, of course, or complimentary covered self-parking. If entering through the self-parking garage, you will take the elevator or escalator to the third floor in order to check-in. Check-in was smooth, and all SPG Gold amenities were explained. Since there is a resort fee of $29 per day, which includes internet, I chose the extra 250 points as my amenity. Although the hotel was probably not more than 30% occupied, I did not get an upgrade. I was able to book my room by finding a Better Rate Guarantee, which netted me an extra 2,000 Starpoints so all was not lost. Rooms at The Phoenician are fairly large by most standards, measuring approximately 600 square feet. The Grand Deluxe King Room overlooks the pool areas. There is a balcony with patio furniture, but when its nearly 110 degrees sitting outside doesn’t sound like an appealing proposition. Upon entering the room, there is a small bar area with a Keurig coffee maker to the right. The bathroom is located to the left, and is very spacious. There is a large soaking tub, shower and separate toilet. There are double sinks with ample counter space, however three large vases take up some valuable counter space, although it is located over the tub. There are Laboratoire Remede branded bath amenities which have a menthol/minty scent. The bedroom is very spacious with ample room to roam around without running into furniture. The bed is very comfortable, with super soft pillows. There is a bed bench at the foot of the bed. There is a large sofa and lounge chair with coffee table in which to unwind, relax and watch TV or have a conversation. The desk area although fairly large, was lacking in outlets that were convenient to plug in your computer or to charge your phone or gadgets. The Phoenician boasts 9 swimming pools, 27 holes of golf and tennis courts, in addition to a somewhat small gym and full spa. Although a Five Diamond AAA hotel, service was professional but somewhat impersonal. All employees were polite but not overly friendly. The hotel also boasts J&G Steakhouse, a Jean George Vongerichten restaurant. Although I did not get a chance to eat here on this visit, it is definitely on my list. If anything close to my past visit at Prime at the Bellagio this is a sure hit. The property is also starting to show its age, and could use an update in the near future. I would definitely stay here again if I can find a good rate, otherwise there are other properties in the Scottsdale area worth checking out.

tripadvisor · 2013-08-29 · 5/5view source

The Phoenician saved our holiday We were actually booked into another nearby hotel (supposedly 5*) but when we arrived and saw the tiny pool with no free sunloungers at 10am in the morning we called the Phoenician and luckily they had rooms free, so we hopped back in the taxi and fled! 30 minutes later we were happily perched at the Oasis pool bar with plenty of space and room to actually swim in the pool, rather than just stand at the edge squashed in with other guests. We had previously stayed at The Phoenician in 2012 for a week so we knew we'd be happy there and it didn't disappoint. We had a spacious room on the 4th floor overlooking the pools - the room was spotless every day and the turndown service was always appreciated, although times were very variable. The property is large, you can take a spin round it on the complimentary bikes. With the many pools, well equipped gym, cactus garden, trails up the mountain and 27-holes of golf there's plenty to do on site but we also made a couple of trips to the shops and hired a car for the day to go up to Sedona which is about a 2 hour drive. We ate in J&G Steakhouse twice - great meals with really good service on both occasions. Breakfast in the restaurant is quite expensive, but you can pick up pastries / croissants in the ice cream parlour which was more reasonable. I've only ever been during the hot summer months when the hotel (and indeed the whole area) is quite quiet - I couldn't comment on what it's like at peak times but given what I've seen I imagine the staff are more than capable of providing consistently good service. I can't find fault with The Phoenician, and I suspect it won't be long before we return.

tripadvisor · 2013-07-21 · 5/5view source

Amazing Luxury Oasis in the Desert The Phoenician is one of the nicest, friendliest resorts that I have ever had the opportunity to visit. The first part of my visit was for business. The resort handled all aspects of the conference without a hitch. The conference rooms were always the perfect temperature, the technical needs almost perfect and the food was top notch - yes, buffet food, top notch. The 2nd part of my visit was personal. I flew my young son out to spend the weekend with me, and we had the best time ever. The hotel grounds are simply spectacular. The facility backs right up to Camelback Mountain, and to see this beautiful landmark from all areas of the resort was simply amazing. The Cactus Garden is gorgeous - an amazing place to visit. The buildings are well maintained and absolutely stunning. The room I stayed in was in one of the casitas - plenty of space. The hotel housekeeping staff made up the sleeper sofa for my son after his arrival. He was so impressed that the staff would make up a bed for him AND call him 'Master'. He thought he was quite hot stuff. The amenities in the room were the best. The bed was soooo comfortable; rarely have I slept any better in a hotel. The bathroom was huuuge complete with big fluffy robes and an awesome soaker tub. Bliss! The first day of my son's visit, I had a 1/2 day of work to finish up so I signed him up to experience the Funicians Kids Club. He had a blast feeding the fish in the Koi pond, riding on golf carts over to the Kids Explorers game room and then hanging out in the Funicians Fun Room playing xBox and Monopoly. Oh, and he got to choose his lunch AND he got a cool back pack and stuffed desert bunny for the day. He loved it!! Laura and her staff took such good care of my son that he wanted to go back the next day!! The Funicians Kids Club is a bit pricey at $65 for a half day and $85 for a full day, but it does include lunch and the kids get to experience quite a few areas of the resort. I highly recommend the program - it was perfect for my child. The pool area was also just "the best". We spent an entire day lounging around the pool. My son enjoyed the "lily pads" in the pool and the slide. We also enjoyed beverages and lunch. Megan took good care of both of us...we never had to go after any type of refreshments. During our "pool day", my son had the chance to participate in the Rubber Duck Races and the Frozen T-Shirt contest. He had the best time competing with the other kids and even won the Frozen T-Shirt contest. The prize? Free ice cream! That night we were supposed to have a dive-in movie, but unfortunately inclement weather forced a cancellation. My son was sooo sad as this was our last "Momma-Son" activity together, but Laura saved the day. She graciously allowed us to check out the movie and we returned it the next day to the front desk. She has no idea how special our little movie night was in our room. We ordered in Room Service and snuggled in to watch the movie complete with Mountain Dew and Chicken Tenders. What could've been a bummer turned out to be a huge blessing. My kiddo was literally smiling in his sleep. In addition to the big activities, we enjoyed playing pool, foosball and Wii at the Explorers Club as well as a round of Monopoly. We also enjoyed an amazing lunch at Relish complete with a Smores dessert finale. If you go to Relish, be SURE to save room for dessert, and order the s'mores!! They bring out a little adobe fire pit that sits on the table and we roasted marshmallows assembled our s'mores AT THE TABLE!! Overall this hotel is truly one of the best I've ever had the opportunity to visit. I was kind of concerned about a business meeting and attempting a vacation in Phoenix in the summer (hot!), but the hotel really made the heat pretty much a non-issue. It was simply amazing for both business and pleasure. If you are on business and are thinking about bringing out the family, just go ahead and do it! Or, definitely visit it even if just for pleasure. If I lived closer, this would be my go-to stay cation resort. The kids will have a blast and you will too. The staff is just the best, the facility is phenomenal and I can't wait to go back at any time of year!

Relaxation has been found!! I had read quite a few reviews prior to selecting this resort for a quick weekend of relaxation. Something must have been wrong with the first person's reservation, bc it took a good 15 minutes for me to finally get helped. The staff was very apologetic though and seemed to sense it was taking longer than it should have. The other times I was in the lobby, there always seemed to be a line at the front desk. On Sunday when I went to leave the hotel at 12:30 there was a considerable line of people waiting around and again only 2 people to help this time. I was glad I didn't need to check out at the desk, or I would have certainly been late for my flight. So, it may have been a busier weekend in off season and they just weren't staffed for it, or their computers could have been slow, as the computer did seem to be slow during my check in. So, just leave yourself extra time when needing to do something at the front desk. It certainly didn't ruin my trip at all, but might have been frustrating if my kids had been with me! I had a room in the main building and was upgraded from a deluxe room to a grand deluxe room by calling prior to my arrival and asking for a room that had a pool view! This was very much appreciated and I would certainly recommend booking the grand deluxe room if you are traveling during high season unless you absolutely don't care about your view. Some things in my room were a little dated or in need of repair, but I had read this in previous reviews and knew what to expect. The carpet had a few stains on it places and my patio table had some holes in it, but I have read that they are remodeling the rooms shortly, so I'm sure these things will be replaced then. Again, did not take away from my trip at all! Others have complained about outdated electronics, but my room had a great flat screen TV, iPod docking clock with radio and wireless telephone and keurig coffee machine (loved it!) , so I didn't see that as an issue. When the remodel does occur, a ceiling fan in the rooms would make a great addition. The room thermostat was an older model, but it functioned great when I turned the air conditioning up at night and then down during the day! The bed in my room was amazing, just as I would expect at any 5 star resort! There were also lots of little things in the room that I really appreciated and that stood out. There were 4 magazines on the table in the sitting room when I arrived, a copy of Kiplingers and Tennis among them, when I arrived! I hadn't bought any magazines prior to my trip, so this was a great little touch! The full chaise lounger on the deck was also fabulous. The first morning I didn't feel like getting organized to go down to the pool, so I just laid on my deck for the morning! Yes, it was pretty hot in June, but that is what I was there for!! I used the refrigerator for some snacks I brought back to my room and wasn't charged for anything from the minibar, but you do need the key for the minibar in order to use the refrigerator. I was glad I had taken the key to the minibar when asked if I wanted it upon check in! The pools were laid out differently than I might have expected, but by the second day I found the perfect place to sit in my opinion! The first day I sat up on the top pool west side and that pool had a little action at times bc the volleyball net was there and then was quiet at other times. The food and drink service was excellent here and I believe that Jeremy was my server that afternoon! He was wonderful! It was actually really nice that they didn't try to scoop my food away right when I stopped to take a break from eating! I was enjoying some chips and salsa for a couple of hours and most places I would have had to tell them 6 times that I was still nibbling on them! The drinks here were amazing as they came from the main pool bar. I found over the next couple of days, that the drinks that came from the main pool bar were the best. The next two days I sat down by the mother of pearl pool and the drinks down there were not quite as good, but I needed to stretch my legs at one point and walked up and got one from the main bar and that again was much better. I found it wonderful to sit on the chairs facing the lake and fountains and then when I got hot I turned around and went for a dip in the mother of pearl pool with the cabanas and mountains in the background! This gave you 2 different views and I felt like I had more space then had I been squished in the chairs next to the pool. I used the fitness center one night and your room key lets you in at any hour. It was great and had better fitness equipment than my gym membership I pay $100 a month for! Couldn't ask for anything else at a hotel fitness center. They had cool towels in the lobby with a citrus spa scent! If you get hot at the pool, walk over and grab a couple of those towels! Extremely refreshing! They also had 2 mini fridges packed with water bottles and a basket of apples and oranges! I grabbed an apple and had one for breakfast the next day and one by the pool! The final thing I really enjoyed were the walking paths and all the different things to explore right on property. I wish I would have made it out to the activities center, but ran out of time. You had lots of room for walking at night and exploring the gardens by day. At the pools there were games you could borrow like scrabble or cards. There were also all the kids water activities like the water slide and floating lilly pads to run across! I would certainly bring my family also! This is an amazing resort that delivered all I needed in my weekend away for some relaxation. There were lots of people that lived locally that had just come for a couple nights away and I wish we had resorts like this in my hometown!! Great idea for the 100 degree weather! But also a wonderful place to come from far away! Being in the travel industry, I've visited a lot of resorts,but this one is amazing, so feel free to message me if you have any questions. It is certainly the little things that add up to make a property like this a shining star in my book!

tripadvisor · 2013-06-12 · 4/5view source

Loved The Phoencian Visited the Phoenician for one week as part vacation part business trip. Check in process was efficient, polite and informative. Our room had a view of Camelback Mountain and the cactus garden. Found the room to be spacious, clean and comfortable. The grounds were kept in fine form as cleaning was done constantly. We visited the gym which was not huge but had all of the usual equipment you would expect to find. The spa was inviting and full service staffed with those who were interested in making sure that you left feeling relaxed. After donning a robe, you may wait for your masseuse to come and get you as you sip any number of naturally flavored water available. You may wish to wait and relax in the meditation room. Had the Swedish massage which was fantastic. Had my nails done which began with a neck massage followed by a hot pack placed on my shoulders. Visited the salon just for an up-do. Enjoyed both my stylist and my hair style. Dined in all of the restaurants. Truly enjoyed the ambiance of JG Steakhouse. Eat out on the patio as there are open flame fire pits which set a beautiful scene. Started with oysters and my main was the Dover sole - delectable. Relish is the burger place which is located by the golf course. Visited for lunch twice. I ordered the same burger on both occasions - True Blue. Prepared to my liking both times. At the Camelback lounge we were able to order food from the II Terazzo menu. Would seem to have been a bit scaled down from the normal restaurant menu as we were eating in the lounge but was tasty nonetheless. There is a cafe that also serves breakfast, specialty coffees. I particularily enjoyed the smoked salmon which I had on a couple of occasions. Nothing special or unique in presentation, I just would have never thought that they would have offered this item on a limited menu and I appreciated its presence. We rented a car for our week stay and made a trip to Sedona to the the must-see red rocks. Michelle - one of the 2 concierge named Michelle was helpful and informative with directions. She gave us a wonderful lunch selection - the Enchantment Resort. Taking her advice we ate on the patio at Tii Gavo in full intimate view of a red rock mountain as our backdrop while dining. I especially enjoyed the sangria of which there was the choice of red and white. I chose the red = delish. Returning to the Phoenician was convenient for those who have rented a car as you have the choice of valet or self parking. The self parking is great as it is located underground. Ample parking available. I definitely recommend checking out the Phoenician should you be considering a trip to AZ. You will not be disappointed!

Great Desert Getaway My husband just took me here to celebrate my birthday. He had informed them of my birthday and I was greeted with a happy birthday by everyone, and with a smile also. Thanks, Phoenician, it was a great time!!!

Wow, The Phoenician!!! We had a wonderful experience at the Phoenician. Extremely upscale resort. Phoenix is hot, but not humid, no uncomforable sticky feeling. Love the Southwest US. This is truly a great area. Our room overlooked the back, beautiful cactus garden. Try breakfast on the balcony overlooking this rock/cactus garden. Trails allow walking through this and other garden areas. The property, while large is easy to navigate. Breezeways are open, airy and offer great views. Loved the large pool and cabanas. Exceptional hotel and pool staff are ready for any request. The hotel offers a great spa, tennis, golfing, and other outdoor activities can be easily arranged. There is a great patio for dining, cocktails, and dinner overlooking perfectly manicured lawns. Whatever you want,The Phoenician can do it! We can't wait to return for more fun, hiking, horseback riding, cabanas and romance in the sun!

Great stay at the Phoenician This is our third year staying at the Phoenician for our family reunion. The place was really incredible. Even better than a couple years ago! We had another visit to the Phoenician over Memorial Day, multiple families and rooms. If anything I think they have raised their game! With only one exception (a cranky waitress at the pool side cafe), everyone, and I mean every single person who worked there was fantastic. From the moment you arrive at the front door all the way through the visit, the staff is friendly, attentive, patient. At meals we had to settle bills on multiple rooms from at least 2 tables, and the staff just handled it with grace and expertise. Except for the one cranky blond waitress at the cafe, wish I remembered her name. All she could commit to was 'doing the best she could'. Get the everything omelet at the buffet (killer!), and have Jose be your waiter. Breakfast couldn't be better. Get a pool chair under a shade tree. Don't sit right next to the DJ if you want to talk. tripadvisor · 2013-05-27 · 5/5view source

Seamless luxury in downtown Scottsdale We chose The Phoenician over the other top competing 5-star resorts (The Boulders and the Four Seasons) based on its convenient location (the others are north of Scottsdale on the border of Carefree). If you want the natural ambience of the Sonoran desert and mountains and a less urbane resort atmosphere, then the others are probably a better choice, but for convenience and saving 30 minutes to downtown Scottsdale or Phoenix (each way!) the Phoenician is unbeatable. Gratis self parking is convenient, and underground (important on hot days) located in the basement of the hotel building. Lobby check-in was prompt and efficient. No bell captain was available at check-in, but the head of housekeeping insisted on taking our luggage to the room and would not accept a tip. During our stay, there were other special items we asked for, and they were promptly and unobtrusively provided. We were offered the opportunity to waive daily housekeeping service "for reduced environmental impact" which we politely refused. The lobby still reflects the 1980's/90's Charles Keating era of over-the-top decadence with giant chandeliers and marble floors; I'm not particularly a fan of this, but it did not distract from an excellent stay. The $25 million artwork scattered around the grounds, primarily from the Native American sculptor Allan Houser is another story: that is absolutely stunning and spectacular. Make sure to pay homage to the life-size bronze statue of the Chief offering the Peace Pipe near the front of the spa; it is the same piece that also fronts the United Nations building in New York City. The hotel is laid out in two separate curved terraced buildings separated by a driveway. Our first room was in the upper terrace with a view of the city (and rooftop of the first building) that we were not happy with, but they moved us the following day to the lower terrace with a view of the gardens and golf course and we were much happier with that. This was also more convenient each day as the parking lot is underneath the first building and uses the same elevator. Rooms are laid out with calming beiges and botanical prints; are spacious and were absolutely and impeccably spotless. Unlike many other 5-star resorts nowadays, the Phoenician still provides full nightly turn-down service automatically, tidying up the room and providing bottled water and chocolates. I was charged $29/day "resort fee", and did not use any of it, except the internet service. I was not given an option to waive it, but did not ask if I could either. The highlight for us was eating outdoors on the terrace of their main restaurant Il Terrazzo. Each day, it included a simple but good quality breakfast buffet, and a huge staff that obviously enjoys their jobs and keeping the clientele happy. Please note the aggressive wild birds that are on a constant look-out for an ignored plate of food or pitcher of cream, and KEEP DISHES COVERED if you visit the buffet...even if others are sitting at your table. Definitely a place for stresses and worries to seem far away. I will certainly be staying here again.

Beautiful Property in Scottsdale I recently stayed here for two nights while attending a business conference. Although I did not have time to check out all of the facilities this property offers, I have to say the areas I did get to are beautiful and well maintained. Expect to do plenty of walking if you stay here as the property is very spread out. My room in the north wing seemed a little out of the way at first, but I found shortcuts to get from there to the main building and ballroom area where our conference activities were taking place. Although huge, comfortable and clean with a private balcony, my room did not have a view, as the balcony was surrounded by tall, thick shrubs. Great for privacy, but disappointing as I'd have loved to view the area and Camelback Mt. My favorite spot was the cactus garden, to which I had easy access from the north wing. All in all a nice property, but expensive - even with a convention rate discount. Oh, and I have to agree with a previous reviewer - the coffee served at breakfast could have been much better!
