A room with a view was expected You would rightfully expect the best out of such a prestigious and expensive hotel. The kind of place where you would not expect rooms overlooking another building separated by a roof top. We had a very small balcony with no sunshine at all. We would have appreciated to be able to enjoy some privacy on our balcony since the pools were over crowded with children, hard to find lounge chairs in April (probably a remainder of spring break). We did not expect families, once again considering that this is a pricey hotel. The spa services were again overpriced for the quality of treatments, the restaurants on site were also average. We travel a lot and we have to admit that we were disappointed. According to our experience, this hotel is over rated.

tripadvisor · 2013-05-13 · 5/5view source

Great experience during recent conference Recently stayed at the Phoenician for a business conference and had a tremendous experience. Beautifully crafted hotel, rich, opulent and luxurious. Amenities are fantastic: golf, cactus garden, tennis, fitness center, spa, 9 pools, art tour, restaurants, live lounge music and shops. It is conveniently located not too far a drive from Phoenix main airport. Valet of $29/night definitiely high, but can opt for self-parking your vehicle. Hotel has a desert, beige, neutral tone throughout that fits the locale very well. They have a $25 million dollar art collection on premise, including 7 million year old fossils, and fantanstic Native American statues throughout the grounds. Room was great, with a generous patio with lounger, table and chairs, nice big TV, desk, sofa, great in-room bar and snacks. Bathroom was superb, with rainshower shower, enclosed toilet area, soaking tub, huge mirror and dual sinks - marble everywhere. Had one of the best burgers of my life at Il Terazzo restaurant on premise - Kobe beef, boston lettuce, avocado and aioli on a butter toasted bun - a must for lunch if you go. Front desk and car service were a little robotic or workmanlike, but friendly. Requests for ice were handled immediately. Tiered pool area during the day and outdoor fireplace at night were spectacular. Being a luxury property, this does not come cheap, but if willing or able to pay, it is a tremendous property.

tripadvisor · 2013-05-02 · 4/5view source

Nice place, lots of pool areas, nice grounds, restaurants OK, very isolated location My husband and I stayed at this resort for a conference last month, we spent 4 nights here, it was our first time in Scottsdale. Giving the Phoenician a 4 is pushing it, I was debating between a 3 or 4. Although this is a 5* diamond rated place..... I did not get that vibe. However, it was a very nice property with nice staff. I had a few good experiences which I highlighted below. 1) Pools- I think the staff in yellow did a great job replenishing our waters, clearing out towels, providing towels when needed. What I did not like was that there was no great adult area. I believe one pool was the Casbah pool which was only for above 18. However, that pool was in between the two other large pools, not an ideal place for an adult only area as it gets loud with traffic. Also, it felt a little congested in terms of the layout/tree coverage. 2) Oasis pool bar/grill- Blair and Gabe were great the two times I dined poolside, the Mediterranean wrap was excellent. One thing I noticed not just at this restaurant, but all restuarants in Scottsdale is that the establishments are very understaffed. I'm not sure why that is. Although we had to had to wait quite a while before we placed our order, got our bill, etc. the waitstaff was superb and pleasant. 3) Il Terazzo- dined here twice for breakfast. The first day I was NOT impressed with the hostess and our waitress. I thought they were cold and a bit snooty. The menu was very overpriced, typical for a resort I guess. The yogurt and granola parfait was excellent. Jocelin our host the next day, and Jose our waiter, were both excellent and reflective of what the restaurant should be for a fine dining place. Also the first day we dined on the patio which was great, however, there were crows EVERYWHERE. They would fly in constantly and feast on the plates that were not yet taken away. The staff should do a more speedy job of clearing out tables after guests leave to help prevent this. It was a bit of an annoyance and also not sanitary to have birds all over chairs/tables 4) Thirsty Camel- loved the piano and live singing, I think her name was Tanya. Added a nice feel to the evening if you want a relaxing evening outdoors, watching the sunset. The food was not impressive, did not like the Tiramisu, it was 80% cream which made me nauseus 5) Cactus Garden- Beautiful and different! I was so happy we were able to go on the cactus tour with Naoiti, who was a great guide. 6) Camelback hike with Grayson- great experience! he was a great guide, he was a little too fast for my husband and I to keep up with comfortably though. Can be done without the guide, hike costs $20 per person w/o resort fee. However, I liked having the guide as he explained the sights and nature during our trek. 7) Meditation course with Cindy- atrium is beautiful and relaxting in the center for wellbeing. The meditation course was a very interesting experience, happy I was able to try it. Phillip in the Center was very helpful in making the appointment. 8) Rooms/hotel- spacious, clean, housekeeping did a great job, nice spacious bathroom, bit outdated colors. The carpets are definitely in need of replacement, the large floral prints look very 80s-ish. The lobby is spacious with ample seating 9) Front desk was very helpful and friendly throughout our stay, check-in and check-out Overall I'm glad I tried this place, haven't stayed in a resort like this before. One downside is it is a drive from Scottsdale downtown, old town, the mall, etc. The cab ride is around $8-9 so not bad, we did that twice because we were getting tired of the limited options for dining at the hotel as many of the restaurants and room service have similiar menu items. There were a lot of families there, it wasn't overcrowded with kids, but definitely noisey at times. Would have liked more areas for adults only.

tripadvisor · 2013-04-23 · 5/5view source

Wonderful Stay with Kids @ The Phoenician We stayed at The Phoenician 4/17 for four nights with our two children, ages 12 & 10. With a very early flight from the Midwest, we arrived at the hotel @ 8:00 a.m. We were not expecting a room to be ready, but to our surprise, we were upgraded to a Casita room that was available at no extra charge. There is free parking right outside of your casita which saved us the $29 valet charge per day. Our casita was an end unit in the N Building and very convenient to the lobby & pool. It was very cozy with plenty of room for the 4 of us. Sliding glass door overlooking the lake and the kids could go out and play on the lawn. Very large marble bathroom with large bathtub & separate room for toilet & a bidet. Two sinks on opposite sides were a plus for my husband & I. Large stone shower with seating area, rainfall shower head & glass door. The largest bathroom at any resort I've ever stayed. The mattress & bedding was incredibly comfortable. We all slept like rocks for 4 nights! On the way to our casita, we walked over several footbridges over the lake at the resort & came upon the Kids Camp director feeding the koi & ducks with several other children. She was kind enough to invite my children to feed them as well (even they they weren't enrolled in the camp)and gave them handfuls of fish food. There were dozens of koi that literally swim right up to you for food, as well as a mother duck and her brood of babies. My kids enjoyed that very much! We also saw a turtle & there are tons of little bunnies roaming around the property. If you have children, make sure to stop by the Kids Camp before 4 p.m. and they will get a free plush bunny as a souvenier. Very cool.. as we've never stayed at a resort that ever gave such nice free gifts to the kids. The grounds are very expansive. It took us about a day to get acclimated. There are beautiful stone walkways winding around the resort with lush landscaping & flowers everywhere. A private gazebo and patio in the shade with tables & chairs to read a book. Waterfalls, flowering trees, cactus & a beautiful backdrop of Camelback Mt. The resort is beautiful at night, too, with the resort lights glowing and the firepits and swimming pools lit up. THE POOL: There are 3 levels of pools. The first pool is at ground level and overlooks both the pool & lake. Saw mostly adults at this pool & we never stayed at this one. Go up the stairs and you come to the Adults Only pool & bar. Again, didn't stay at this one, but looked like fun. Go up another level and you will come to the largest pool which is divided into three separate pools by walkways. The one in the center is the largest & has a basketball net, as well as a volleyball net. This is where we spent most of our time. There is also a waterslide for the kids. Plenty of padded chaise lounges with umbrellas. Extra long towels provided so cover the entire chaise. Excellent food & beverage service out by the pool. They also bring you pitchers of ice water & refill as soon as you're low. All the food we had was excellent, especially the homed guacamole & salsa. If you want several chairs out by ANY of these pools, I suggest you get out there no later than 9:00 a.m to get your chairs. I went out @ 10:00 a.m. the first morning & had a hard time finding 4 seats together. Most of the chairs were taken by families or had the good ol' towel & personal item on them to be "saved". The pool staff really needs to keep an eye on this sort of "chair saving" practice because it is very annoying to the other guests who are actually ready to sit out by the pool & cannot find a chair. I had two chairs next to me "saved" and no one showed up for 4 hours. Some people even took up a whole chair just to lay there bags & clothing on. The pools are heated so the water is not freezing. Large hot tub was very nice. Ducks occasionally fly in & out of the pool. Great view of Camelback Mt. from the pool. Great gold course although my husband did not play during our stay. Il Terrazzo was pricey and the food was good. Nothing to write home about as far as Italian food, but it was good. We had breakfast off property most days since The Phoenician did not have a breakfast buffet except on Sundays during our stay. We drove over to Talking Stick Resort and enjoyed the breakfast buffet for $10.95 per adult. Very good & very good value. We also enjoyed breakfast at the 5 & Diner and Butterfield's (both off-site). There is an ice-cream parlor/coffee shop on-site which was a nice treat. The only THREE negatives we encountered were the following: 1. There was a private function in one of the restaurants one evening during our stay. We had to walk by the front entrance to the function to get to our restaurant we were eating at that evening. There was a man "guarding" the entrance to the private function like he was the Gestapo and practically charged my kids saying "No, no" at them like they were trying to get in. He told us we could not walk through since there was a private function, so we had to walk back to the elevators, go to the 2nd floor, go around & catch the escalator & go back down to the first floor and walk to the restaurant. I did not like the feeling like we were outsiders when we were paying good money to stay at this resort. If a guest is holding a private function, please consider having it in a private function room, not one of the main restaurants where paying guests have to be guarded off & re-routed to get to their own dining location. 2. My husband ate out on the lobby patio one evening with our kids and ordered them a side of fruit from the kids menu ($5 each). When the bill came, I saw that the waitrees charged us a total of $26 for both fruit plates. When I brought this to her attention, she had somewhat of an attitude and explained that they ordered the adult fruit plates @ $13.00 a piece. Why would we do that?! I reiterated that we asked for the children's fruit plate & she took the bill and checked it with her manager. When she returned (again with a noticeable attitude & no apology) she explained that her manager took off one of the fruit plates off the bill. So I was still overcharged, but just paid the bill and left. 3. We stopped by the front desk & asked the gentleman if we could get 4 foam pillows. He asked for our name & room number and let us know they would be delivered shortly. After waiting for nearly an hour and it was getting late, I called the front desk and they said they had no request written up for the pillows?? She apologized and pillows were brought to our room shortly thereafter. Those were our only problems. Other than that, we loved this resort, had a great mini-vacation & would highly recommend staying here!

tripadvisor · 2013-04-22 · 4/5view source

Nice Place for a Staycation We won our 2-night stay at The Phoenician at a charity auction, which included dinner and brunch at the resort's Il Terrazzo restaurant, and even though we live in Phoenix it seemed worlds away from home. We requested a pool view at check-in and the only room available had two beds. Not a problem, we thought, until we saw that they are full-size and not queen. Oh well, our romantic weekend was just that much, um, closer. The room was large and the balcony relaxing. Nothing super special but well appointed and comfortable. They hadn't given us a key to the mini-bar so we had to call for one, then we couldn't find an ice machine so we had to call for ice. Both were delivered promptly and with a smile. Later we had great cocktails (try the $20 Manhattan - it's worth it) and smiley service at the Thirsty Camel, outside at sunset - very romantic. The live music in the lobby was awesome and we felt like we were truly on vacation. We had no problem finding a spot at the pool on Saturday, at about 10:30am. We even snagged an umbrella but there were other people who had problems finding loungers and umbrellas later, when it started getting warmer. One couple, next to us, ordered lunch from the gluten-free menu and told us all about the resort's separate "allergy-free" kitchen. I had no idea that the restaurants could accommodate just about any food request or allergy. Nice touch. In fact, they said it is why they prefer the Phoenician to other luxury resorts in the area. All in all it was just a nice, relaxing atmosphere. Everyone was super nice and I never detected an attitude among the staff, no matter where we were on the property, or what we asked for. Refreshing. They also didn't nickel and dime us to death like some other resorts. We may have felt this way because we self-parked and since we are Starwood Gold members they waived the resort fees and gave us a free drink. At checkout we told the front desk clerk that they needed to clean the bathroom door in our room - it was black with grimy fingerprints when we checked in). She was very apologetic and seemed genuinely interested in making sure it was noted. That's all we ask for, what we expect and what we found at The Phoenician - an effort at sincere customer service.

tripadvisor · 2013-04-21 · 5/5view source

Perfect Combination of Activities and Relaxation The physical infrastructure of the resort was what you would expect from such a highly rated facilitated. The service set it apart for a North American hotel - every Phoenician employee I interacted with was professional, courteous, and trying to go above and beyond. I was fortunate with the weather (70s and 40s) so outdoor activities (great trail within a mile walk from the hotel) were possible. The fitness center, spa and pools were great. Specifically regarding the fitness center - clean, good choice of equipment, etc. It is a tad small for a resort this large. I recommend, weather permitting, to do your cardio outside of the gym and use the gym strictly for resistance training. Final comment - food and drink prices are Mandarin, Ritz, Four Seasons like. I expected higher than average, but not that high.

tripadvisor · 2013-04-16 · 5/5view source

Attention to Detail A wonderful place to stay with friends especially if someone in your group has food allergies. This property boasts a dedicated allergen-free kitchen where dishes from all food service outlets can be made and then served. The options for gluten-free are plentiful and pretty much limitless. If it's not on the menu, just ask. The servers throughout the food outlets are knwoledgeable and attentive. Sometimes to a fault, they tend to enjoy your company a little too much and don't want to bring you the check to leave, but alas, there could be worse things. The rooms are spacious and feature a his & hers closet as well as double sinks in the bathroom. If at anytime your remote control stops functioning, simply drop it on the floor and it will resume operations (not sure why this method is so effective). The beds are also extremely comfortable. However, there are few poweroutlets by the nightstands making it rather challenging to charge anything than an iPhone for which the alarm clock has an adapter for. They claim to have 9 pools, but I'd say it was closer to 7 as 3 of them are actually just one pool with some land bridges. Just saying. The hot tub tends to be really hot during the day, but I'm sure its more than enjoyable at night. I was slightly disappointed with the lack of swim-up bar, but the lounge chairs service more than made up for it. Also if you plan on outdoor dining off of the lobby at the firepits, claim your spot early as they fill up and folks are reluctant to leave. Moreover, the hotel does NOT provide s'more kits, so bring your own. It's not condoned, but allowed. There are also 27 holes of golf as well as putting green and a driving range. The driving range prices are extremely affordable considering everything else on property. Sadly, I did not make it to the gym, but the cactus walk was a nice touch. Finally, don't get roped into the $29/day valet parking when the self-parking option is free and easily accessible from the elevators in the lobby.

tripadvisor · 2013-04-08 · 5/5view source

This is the place to stay! A warning, my spelling stinks but it's a very knowledge review, I promise, so read on! My husband and I were just there this past weekend to celebrate our 11th anniversary. All cards on the table, we did meet at the Phoenician and then got married there as well so it will always have a soft spot for us. But here is why you cannot go wrong staying here: The resort is beyond incredible looking. Make sure to bring your camera, you'll want to take a LOT of photos. The rooms have anything you could ever need. Check that, they could use some black tea, all it had was decaf but I'm nitpicking. They even provide complimentary slippers and turndown service. And they sent a lovely champagne split for our anniversary, so sweet. Our room overlooked the pool and were three balconies to the right from the thirsty camel lounge so in the evening we sat outside with a glass of wine and listed to the entertainment (a wonderful singer) without having to go to the bar. There are sooooo many options for dining. We ate lunch at RELISH and I had the amazing Blu Burger. The tater tots are excellent as well. We stopped at the Ice Cream Parlor for some of their signature Phoenician Crunch ice cream. It's some of the best ice cream I've ever had, don't miss it! We had dinner at II Terazzo. We had the appitizer special, a mushroom rosotto filled fried balls (looked like meatballs) in a WONDERFUL red sauce. I then had the petite filet with a perfect bernaise and a side of sweet potoatoes, all excellent. HOWEVER, my husband had the other steak and found it was not trimmed properly which dampened his enjoyment. The staff quickly offered us complimentary desserts to make up for it but we didn't have the room. Breakfast was the buffet back at II Terazzo. It was excellent, highly recommended. Don't miss the crossanuts (sp) both regular and chocolate and you can build your own bagel and lox complete with red onion and capers, yum! Re entertainment we played tennis twice. The courts were in excellent condition, and they provide towels and water, and if you need, raquetts and balls. The kids club is also right there, hummmm, maybe drop off the kiddos and play a couple of sets? We also tourned the catus garden which is at the base of Camelback mountain, lovely. The pool was quite crowded. We sat at the upper pool and were lucky to get two chairs together. Admittedly, we didn't arrive at the pool till about 1 in the afternoon. I'd recommend going earlier to stake out a good spot. It also did take awhile for the attendent to come by to take our drink order (I had a very potent rum and ginger based drink listed in their menu that was well worth the $9 price). But the pools are fantastic, perfect tempature and so beautiful. There are many other things to do but as this was just a one night stay we didn't get to the spa, gym or golf. Will we go back again? Just try to stop us!

tripadvisor · 2013-04-02 · 4/5view source

Lovely but not special The Phoenician is a lovely and the service is great, from the waitstaff at Relish Burger to the staff in the fitness center. The problem is that during spring break the pools are absolutely packed. There are days we would be at the pool by 9:15 and there were no available pool chairs. The pool staff will try to locate chairs (old vinyl lounge chairs) and set them up for you but that might be in the lawn area, outside of the pool, with not a bit of shade. The days that we were able to get pool chairs, the chairs were literally lined up in 4 rows, with about an inch of space between them. This was a major negative for us, as we were looking to go do some sightseeing in the morning, before the heat of the day, and come back to the hotel to enjoy the pool. It was so stressful to think that we wouldn't be able to sit at the pool if we didn't get there immediately after breakfast. The space around one pool is taken primarily by cabanas ($275 per weekday, $375 per weekend day). There are ducks on property that hang out in the pool. On top of that, guests were tossing chips into the pool to feed the ducks and no one who worked at the hotel was asking them to stop. This seemed kind of gross and not what we expected at this level of hotel. There was not much to do at night with kids, even during spring break. They had movies at the pool two nights. We tried to take them to the ice cream parlor that has been mentioned in previous reviews. It was closed by 8:00 on a Friday night, which seemed unusually early. Our room was not ready until 5:30 on the day of check-in. Maybe this is the norm but we hadn't experienced this in many years of traveling. The good: No complaints about service. Staff worked hard to keep pool area clean and bring water pitchers around. The concierge was extremely helpful in giving restaurant recommendations/reservations, hike suggestions, etc. She encouraged us to stop back before we left for a hike to pick up cold bottled water. She also told us that Il Terrazzo provides a complimentary coffee station in the mornings which would have been nice to know when we checked in, since we had been purchasing coffee elsewhere. A yoga class was very enjoyable - nice bright fitness room and the instructor was helpful. Our room (deluxe room in casitas) was spacious, with a large patio and very quiet. We didn't really hear anyone from within our room. All in all, there were no major complaints. It might be better to be there during off-peak season. But there was nothing about the grounds or facility that really "wowed" us. We would not be interested in returning.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-29 · 5/5view source

Magnificent property Traveled to AZ for business so the hotel was chosen for me. However, the hotel is beautiful, from the lobby to the pool, the spa, the restaurants and the hotel shops, we were impressed at every turn. The rooms themselves are very spacious, huge bathroom with Jacuzzi tubs with every amenity you can think of (lip balm, nail file, cotton pads for makeup remover, slippers, robe, ipod dock/radio,small in-room safe) with turn down service nightly. I was very happy this is where I was booked to stay! Staff was wonderful across the board. Helpful and pleasant. Ate in all of the restaurants, food was good, no complaints. (try the tater tots at Relish!) Spa was enormous, very clean, with many treatment rooms and a meditation room to relax before/after treatments. A bit tricky to find the spa (its down a flight of stairs beneath the hair salon) but well worth the walk across the grounds. I had a massage with Cher, one of the best I've had, I highly recommend! Pools were very crowded so be sure to head out early to secure a prime spot (and plan to stay there) The hotel discourages "saving" lounge chairs and has several signs posted stating they will remove unattended property after 9am, which I think is a great idea. Overall we had a great stay and I would return to this property if I'm ever in the area again.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-15 · 4/5view source

Convention Hotel and Spa I'd always wanted to try the Phoenician - as a spa destination. I was surprised when my company named it as our incentive trip. The grounds are beautiful and perfectly manicured. I didn't golf but those who did said it was wonderful. Our room was in the casita. Easily accessible and had a lovely view of the fountains in the lake. Food was decent. (We were eating in mass scale, not the restaurants). Service was good from front desk, lounge and lobby bar. Housekeeping didn't show until after 2:30 one day and we'd already been out and come back. There was a layer of dust in several areas of the bathroom. Everything in the room was in good working order except the vanity makeup mirror in the bathroom, which should have lit up but wouldn't. I guess the bulb was blown. It remained that way so I guess housekeeping never checked it. The pools are delightful. The staff is extremely attentive - if you ask where something is, they don't tell you, they take you....Signature 5 star service. If I was a spa guest, seeking a retreat, I'd not have been happy with the corporate crowd overtaking the lobby bar. But there were other lounge areas in more quiet places and my little group managed to escape to the steakhouse lounge, which was incredibly beautiful and on the top floor with a deck with firepits overlooking the pools and gold course. Very tranquil. It's a stunning place and I'd consider it a "must see" for any true traveler. I'd stay in the casitas again. There are parking spaces just outside the doors to the rear of the casitas - perfect if you have a vehicle. On another note, when we checked in, we were told that in order to have our reserved room (a king) we'd need to take a an accessible room (handicapped, For the politically incorrect) or a double in the casitas. The casitas sounded better and people in the main hotel said they though the casitas were the superior option, but when I reserve a king at a 5 star resort, I expect to get what I reserved.....Not a compromise that I need to negotiate at check in. I get sick of hotels making me negotiate my room at check in. The double was a mistake. When you are used to a king, you need to sleep in a king, IMO. . At minimum, I'd like what I reserved. Also, don't go without a fat wallet ( not that you would anyway). Cocktails were $20 each. Each time the two of us sat at the bar, it was $100 with tip. Be ready for that. The drinks are well made and they are generous with pours. I was drinking French Martinis - very well done. Overall, is return, stay in the casitas (in a king!) and spend more time in the spa. I also thought the spa was small and I would have expected more quiet areas/hydro retreat...maybe a plunge pool and some aromatherapy....a place to escape and relax before or after a treatment.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-14 · 2/5view source

Please, 5-star? Who are you kidding? The Phoenician is a lovely property, but take a bundle of cash for ANY extra charge you can imagine and be prepared for surprises. A regular cup of carry-out coffee is more than $4.00, oatmeal is $9, you are charged for "porterage" even if you never see a porter and wheel in your own bag, and despite the high-end rack rate, you are charged on top of that for housekeeping, which, for us, one day did not happen at all and another day we had to request it since past 2 PM, it did not look like it was going to happen for the second day in a row. Then to add to our comedy of errors, we received three phone calls over the course of two nights AFTER we had gone to sleep, all between midnight and 2:30 AM with no one on the other end of the line, just music. I feel badly I had to explain my disappointment to such a nice young lady at the desk, but though this place is indeed beautiful, it needs a lot of work behind the scenes.

Can't Beat This Palace Great ambiance. Superior accommodations. Excellent food and beverage service. Perfect locale for large group event as well as small group. Convenient to airport. Very friendly staff. Easy drive to Tucson, Sedona or Flagstaff.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-06 · 5/5view source

Great resort to visit while in Scottsdale Have visited before for business so decided it would be good for a quick trip to AZ. We had some Starwood points to use so decided on this location compared to a couple of other locations we have stayed at in the area over the years. We had 5th floor room with a garden view of the mountain and catus garden which is always nice and peaceful. Staff are always great no matter who you are dealing with in the hotel. Turn down service that includes chocolate and waters. Rooms are large with large baths and showers, and ours had a good size balcony. My wife tried out the spa and said it was great. It is a nice complex to walk around as a true resort property should be. We were there on a Sun and Mon in Feb so it was a little slow which is great to get seating for great views around the patio lounge areas. Their bar snacks and drinks are always good. We even had a chance to visit the Relish Burger Bistro one night for a good dinner and sunset views. Do wish the little stores stayed open later but probably do in summer. Be sure to take a walk around the place because you will find a lot of unique areas. The resort is convient to most of the Phoenix area and it is very easy to get back to the airport. Will probably stay there again when we are in the area. Valet parking is a little high in my opinion since you are already paying a resort fee.

tripadvisor · 2013-03-04 · 5/5view source

Service Perfection The Hotel is spectacular and well situated to drive to the airport or to activities in and around Phoenix. Unfortunately, I didn't get to try the golf course or spa but everything about the hotel is 1st class. The most impressive thing about it is the service. Their hiring and training practices must be perfect as every encounter with staff from the front desk to the restaurant was enjoyable. tripadvisor · 2013-03-04 · 5/5view source

Top of The Line In Scottsdale My first stay at this grand hotel and you just couldn't go wrong here. It has a defined style and opulence that is reminiscent of the resorts of yesteryear, with the exception that this has been modernized. From your initial drive up the property to being escorted to the main lobby, this hotel will, and does, make you feel special. I had a room with balcony overlooking the pool complex. The room was well decorated, very nicely equipped bathroom and everything was just top notch down to the caliber of the wait staff, bartenders - everyone polite and well polished. The outdoor lounge in the evening is a great place to enjoy drinks (they have an extensive beverage selection). You pretty much know going in that your credit card is going to get a work out - bar tab for 2 people for a few hours almost 150.00 - if you use the spa there are packages easily exceeding 500. a treatment. So, you are either used to paying for amenities or if you want to give yourself a real treat just accept that you'll pay - but unlike other places that may just be expensive - this place actually makes you feel good about being here and spending your money! Very novel, yes? If you enjoy soft feathery pillows on your bed (and I do!) this is the hotel for you!

tripadvisor · 2013-02-15 · 4/5view source

We love this place My husband and I come here at least once a year and have yet to be disappointed. This is our second time to stay in the one bedroom Casitas and they are wonderful. There are two full baths and a formal dining table, not to mention the nice cozy furniture placed around the fireplace. We were only the lower of 2 floors, which I usually request to be on the top floor, however, this was perfect. Our bedroom had a patio with 2 loungers and the living room patio had a table for four as well as a lounger. The grounds are so well maintained, that sitting outside listening to the fountain and watching the family of bunnies and and smelling the fragrant trees and shrubs was just lovely. The rooms furnishings are still a little dated, but they still feel look much better than average hotel furniture. The golf course is perfect and there are at least twelve tennis courts. The first hour was free if you paid a daily resort fee. The parking at the hotel, I believe is $26.00. It's free at the Casitas. They have a very nice and busy Wellness Spa and the pools are heated. Be sure and book ahead,if you want to get into the spa. We found a great little find last year at the golf course. Relish, a restaurant and bar. If you go between 4:00-6:00? they have a half price menu for several appetizers and drinks. Try the BBQ Nachos, yummy. The ll Terrazzo is a nice place for dinner and breakfast. There breakfast Buffett is the normal Buffett, but good. We ordered room service for dinner one night and was told it would be 30 minutes. It was exactly 30 minutes. They came in set the table and asked when we would like for them to return. We said,"we would call them" they were there within five minutes after we called for them to pick up our dishes. The service is perfect through out the hotel, except for breakfast, it seemed a little slower. They also have a little wine cellar, which you can go in and sample wine and cheese. They have two wines that they donate part of the proceeds to certain organizations. One was breast cancer. The nice thing is, you can stay right there and choose a wine you like without ever having to leave the hotel. We did have rainy weather one day, so we just laid around, read our books, ordered dinner in and sat by the fire place with our glass of wine. Could it get any better? I love this location. Why? Because it isn't in the middle of town, but it is, just two miles from old town and the Fashion Mall. Old town is great to walk around and there are some great restaurants and neat little art galleries. Make sure you do the Breakfast Club for breakfast. Be prepared to wait in line, but you won't mind once you eat there. The Fashion Mall is also right by old town. I am a shopper so getting to shop a mall with high end stores is a plus. I'm from Oklahoma City so our shopping is minimal. This resort has good food, nice rooms, great golfing,tennis,pools and spa. The service is almost perfect. We will always make this a yearly trip. It reminds me of the Four Seasons in Dallas, but I think the food and resort activities are much better.

Incredible landmark Scottsdale resort This is one of the most impressive resorts in Scottsdale with a great central location and all the facilities and activities you could hope for. christmas trip vaction this was a new adventure for our family to be gone over christmas- the property and staff all gave a wonderful impression- the good was very over priced- we did enjoy the lunch and happy hour at the restaurant in the golf area- it has a smaller warm feel- rooms comfy- the spa services lovely but I think it needs an update in the locker rooms-we also enjoyed the classes offered- a bottle of champagne was left in our room for our daughters 22 birthday- very thoughtful-

Great stay, will be back. Stayed in November with the whole family- booked a casita, which was quite spectacular in appointments, decor and size. great location and quite built up. We were here from 27th to after new years eve. Clearly very high season for this resort. Despite that, we didn't feel crowded in. Only time I regretted having a full resort was one evening when my family wanted to stay outside near the outdoor firepit. There are four large outside and they were all full. We settled for a room with a fabulous view, lobby live music seating instead. Not a bad compromise but nevertheless we would've preferred the former. The resort is beautifully kept with clean pool, freshly stocked towels, large koi pond with hundred of fish that you can feed. My daughter thoroughly enjoyed doing this. there is a hiking trail about a mile and half from the property that is quite challenging but beautiful. My only regret is that food prices are astronomical. Thankfully we rented a car and drove out for breakfast, lunch and dinner but usually we prefer to eat in the resort since we had little kids with us. The spa and gym are also nicely appointed. If you have kids keep in mind the resort is quite spread out so be prepared to walk a lot from one part to another. For instance, Relish a restaurant that is open for lunch is clear on the other side of the resort, whilst our room near the cactus garden were one small lake, three pools, one elevator ride and a short hike away. whew. I really felt those distances when my daughter forgot her swimming goggles or something she really needed.

tripadvisor · 2013-01-01 · 5/5view source

Beautiful property We've been dying to try this place for awhile and it was worth the wait. We had 4th floor rooms in the main building overlooking the pools. (Note - I paid extra to guarantee connecting rooms, which I've never been charged for before, but did not have connecting rooms when we arrived. My kids are older so this wasn't a big deal, but would have been with small children. The check in agent did remove the charge and was very apologetic.) The room seemed recently renovated, was ample sized with a spacious balcony. The property was tastefully decorated for Christmas providing some lovely photo ops. The pool area is beautiful with a restaurant/bar smack in the middle. Drinks and food at the Oasis were delicious. We utilized the gym, which was clean and had ample equipment, although the temperature was kept way too warm for a gym. The spa had plenty of room to relax before/after services, spa, sauna, and I had a great massage from Steve. The main dining room was very nice, food was very good, but one of my pet peeves is when a dining room is empty and the hostess tells you that she can seat you in a half hour because they are full. That happened twice. The lounge off the lobby had a great drink and appetizer offering and live music at night - Tony was a great bartender. Waitress service in the lobby lounge was very slow. The hotel was at capacity for football bowl games/New Years so I think they were slightly understaffed. The waitress recognized this and sent a complimentary round of drinks - kudos for recovery. There were lots of holiday activities going on and the activity director took us on a tour of the Cactus Garden, which was quite informative, and beautiful at night. Concierges were spot on with their activity recommendations. Would absolutely recommend this property and am certain the hiccups were related to the time of year.

tripadvisor · 2013-01-01 · 4/5view source

Beautiful grounds, I can't wait to go back for a longer stay I had a one night stay here to celebrate my anniversary and really enjoyed it. This would have been a 5* review but there were a few small issues which dropped it down to 4*. We used a suite night upgrade and were upgraded to a beutiful deluxe suite with an eastward view over the valley. The room was a huge two room suite with two full bathrooms and two large patios with nice chairs, loungers, and table. Some of the prior reviews complained about dated rooms, but ours was very nicely furnished. We were on the 5th floor so the view was nice. I would strongly reccommend asking to stay on a higher floor because the lower floor rooms on our side were right on the roof line and their view would have been obscured by air conditioning vents, etc. We loved the free self parking and I would highly reccommend that to anyone. You can even drive your luggage up to the front and then go park the car. Unless you love valet, there really is no reason to use it here. The hotel was pretty busy and we never had to park further than a 1-2 minute walk from the elevators in a covered parking garage. On the downside, checkin took 15-20 minutes becuase there were only 2 front desk agents and one of them was occupied with an angry guest for the entire time we were there. I must commend the front desk agent for being so cordial. The complaints we overheard were silly, but the front desk agent and the manager that eventually came over were very friendly the entire time. That said, they should have called over another agent because there were several guests waiting to checkin. We also chose the two continental breakfast vouchers as our platinum amenity which are good for Il Terrazo, but when we went down around 9:30 there was a 30 minute wait for breakfast. We were in a hurry so we had to skip, but it would have been appreciated if the front desk agent had warned us about how busy breakfast was so we could have made reservations. Usually hotel breakfasts are never crowded, but this was crazy. If you're staying in high season, definitely make reservations if you plan on eating breakfast and don't want to wait. All in all, we had a good stay and I would definitely come back. The grounds were very well maintained and we loved the room decor. Hopefully we can stay longer next time to spend more time at the pools, etc.

Just Go Here! OK, this resort is an absolute must. If you are looking for elegance and relaxation-this is the place for you. They have a gorgeous golf course that my husband and his friend played and loved. They also have a large amount of professional tennis courts, that I wish I knew about. I would have brought my gear. They do rent everything, but it gets expensive to go that route. They have I believe, 9 gorgeous pools. We were lucky to have fantastic sunny weather for the first week of November. The service at the pool is incredible. I love that the staff gets along so well and helps each other out at every turn. The staff at the pool I would like to acknowledge: Hope, Blair, Brittany, Megan and Marcel. All were very efficient and helpful to each other. We were always able to get what we wanted at the pool. Get the nachos and guacamole, it is to die for!! One thing I would recommend to the hotel, get some music at the pool. Doesn't have to be loud and annoying-but something would be great. We heard many people say this. We had breakfast at the Il Terrazzo every morning. Now here is where my most Fav employee comes in--Aleksander. We LOVED him!! Our first day there, we knew he was going to be our guy everyday. He is just that ray of sunshine you need in the morning! He has the absolute best sense of humor and is perfect for his job. He went the extra nine yards to accommodate my annoying gluten and dairy intolerance and my love of grape jelly which is not normally there but was for me! Oh, by the way-it is HUGE to me that I could have gluten free toast, or a bagel or a sandwich at this resort!!!! BIG PLUS!! Food in this restaurant is fantastic. We also had a dinner there and we all unanimously agreed it was top notch. The atmosphere was lovely too. I love dim lights, table cloths and candles. It makes for a romantic evening. I thought this restaurant was absolutely superior in the quality of food to the "famous" steakhouse also in the resort. Our room was very spacious and lovely. We were checked in by Kelly, who was very sweet and made sure we got the best room we could based on availability. We were very satisfied with our accommodations. Loved the bath soaps and lotions. Very spa-like! Loved the evening turn down service with the chocolates, music and bottled water. We had drinks a few nights in the lobby at the Thirsty camel. We were kind of turned off the first 2 times by blonde server we had. She did not have a good attitude, and I felt like we were bothering her just being there. I will say we went back a third time and had Ashley, who works there part time. She was the best! We received wonderful, fast and pleasant service from her. She is really in her element in this type of work! She is Very much a people person. My friend and I signed up for a Pilate's class at the fitness center. We really liked it. The class was taught by Grayson, who clearly is passionate about what she does. She led the class and was very informative. She made sure that we were using good form and understood what it was that we were doing. Was worth going to! There is a package you can purchase that is relatively inexpensive in which you can get all aspects of the fitness center and tennis courts daily. We weren't going to do this everyday so we did ours ala carte. If you are a fitness buff, I would definitely buy the package. Lastly, I want to mention that this is a great place to walk around and look at. The grounds are so well kept and esthetically pleasing. I would go back here in a heartbeat! Please note that this is not a party place! It is an upscale place to hang out and relax. That is what we went for and that is what we got! We will definitely be back to this great resort!

A Desert Oasis Everything about this resort proves to earn it's 5 star rating. The grounds are breathtaking and so well kept. I enjoyed waking up and watching the sunrise from our balcony overlooking the many pools with the mountains in the background. Excellence in every way I can't say enough about this property. Again, I get really scrambled and can babble on tangents forever if I don't make a list. Positive- 1. Honestly I wondered if they secretly have a cleaning crew following guests around with a mop and broom, because the whole place is spotless- even around the pools and outdoor areas. 3. The room - Is huge. It's larger than my room in my house, and quiet a bit cleaner haha. The bathroom had a separate soaking tub and shower with an enclosed room for the toilet. A younger valet agent got snippy with my boyfriend and then apologized profusely for it and asking if we'd like an amenity sent to our room because he was confused (apparently our car didn't receive a valet parking paper upon entering the resort). While walking around the resort we were greeted multiple times by staff and some asked if we needed any assistance. Everyone had a smile on their face and were VERY FRIENDLY. A ++++ Negatives - 1. Valet price - I can't really complain about this because it's not expensive compared to other cities (NYC $75 p/n) and really this is mine/my traveling companion's own fault. We didnt even check our valet ticket (which has the valet rate on it, $29 per night), we just went to our room and crashed since it was late. Anyhow, valet can get pricey pretty fast but they were excellent gentlemen. If you decide to self park it might seem like the garage is forever away but its right under the lobby area or close to it, so it's not bad! If you can afford the valet for your stay- I'd recommend it, if not no sweat! Really would recommend this resort to anyone. It's fabulous, and we will definitely be back in the future.

Just Perfect My wife and I stayed at the Phoenician from Oct. 28 to the 31st and we must say that this is one of the most luxurious resorts in the Phoenix area. Service was top notch throughout the entire stay. The golf course was amazing and the pool area(s) were awesome. Our room was very large with an oversized bathroom and a good sized balcony. tripadvisor · 2012-09-05 · 5/5view source

Quite frankly, it doesn't get better than this My wife and I took a long overdue extended weekend during the Labor Day holiday to do nothing but relax. We decided to spend our time at the Phoenician, which neither of us had been to, but had been aware of, having spent previous years vacations in Phoenix at other properties. I'm always interested in how I am treated as a customer, whether at a restaurant or staying at a hotel, and I am someone who goes in with the glass half full, and not with the glass half empty. I've left my cynicism behind years ago, and understand that my experience is mine to make or break. I go in positively expecting the best, yet reserve what I consider to be a healthy dose of critical thinking that is willing to spot inconsistency, and then share it in a positive way. Bottom line, the Phoenician now can count on me as one of their fans. I was impressed with the attentive customer service that I received from each and every individual staff member whom I encountered, no matter what position they were in. Our days were spent by the lower pool, going from lounge chair to water and back and forth from 9am to 5pm. We were told that for this holiday weekend, there would be no exclusive adult pool and, gracefully, there were no particularly rowdy kids. It all worked. The chairs were comfortable, the towels were huge, and the water was the perfect temperature for floating around on a styrofoam noodle, which there were plenty of. This is a high end resort, and you will pay for it. I would say that it was well worth the price. We had a package that gave us the 4th night free, as well as a $65 breakfast credit. We stayed in a superior deluxe casita, which has the larger bathrooms and a beautiful view of the lagoon, the casita grounds, and the lower pool and cabana area. The resort is so well appointed, inside and out, the Il Terrazzo restaurant (the only one we went to) so excellent, that we would have been satisfied not to leave the grounds, even though we did leave to seek out other restaurants. There is obviously a very good customer service training program going on, and I would say that it is working. I appreciated the attention paid to the guest children, with activites planned around the pool for them and, at night, an outdoor movie by the pool. Even though the place was quite crowded over this past weekend, I never felt crowded and I always was attended to as if there were far fewer people around. So as not to write the kind of glowing review that looks like I work for the place, I will say that I noticed little bits of wear and tear, such as the bussing station in Il Terrazzo that should be refinished or replaced, some chips and gouges in the concrete around the pool area, and less than perfect clean up of various areas (such as finding a half eaten french fry on our balcony when we checked in - it was gone the next morning). These to me are minor and did not detract from the comfortable ambience of this resort. My impression is that if I had called about the french fry they would have come running. Attention to customer service is always number one in my book, and, I gather, in the Phoenician management's book, also. I would stay here again and again, and am planning to so next year. I would say that if this place does not meet someone's high standards, perhaps nothing ever will. Excellent job, Phoenician!

Very pleasant stay! We stayed here on a combination business/pleasure trip, as I was attending a conference at the resort. Our room was clean and comfortable. The housekeeping staff came twice a day (morning and then evening for a turndown service), and they never once came while we were in the room, which was impressive. There were two things about the bathroom that were a little disappointing: no air vent or fan to help dissipate heat/humidity, and the stand up shower is a bit small especially compared to the very large size of the bathroom. For the resort as a whole, the property is very beautiful and sits at the edge of Camelback Mountain. We did take advantage of the pools a couple nights. However, we were disappointed to find out that on weeknights, the pool bar and grill close at 5 pm! Hoping to have a relaxing dinner by the pool, we instead were able to get some dishes and drinks "to go" from the Italian restaurant, with help from the friendly bartender at the adjacent lounge. The couple meals we did eat at the hotel were very good, but quite expensive. We often drove into nearby Scottsdale to eat and enjoy the many delicious restaurants there.

tripadvisor · 2012-07-30 · 4/5view source

Very Good, but not a 5 Star Experience I would rank our stay at The Phoenician between 3.5 and 4 Stars... Let me start by saying that I had every intention of staying at the Hyatt Gainey Ranch for this trip, because I am a Gold member and had points to spend. However, this summer, the Hyatt was renovating their entire pool complex and that was not just not an option for my family. I thought that The Phoenician would be a similar stay in that both properties had the same kinds of amenities and the Casita option. Thus, my family reserved two Grand Deluxe Casitas on the first floor. I really enjoyed the patio and since we had our dog, the ground floor was very convenient for potty breaks. The grounds of this resort are extremely vast and beautiful. Between the Koi ponds and the Orchid gardens, and the backdrop of Camelback mountain, you are literally looking at beautiful views all day long. What I really liked about my stay: - The check-in process was easy - Excellent grounds and fitness facility - Casita parking right outside the building - Thirsty Camel Lounge and Patio - Relish Burger Bistro - Complimentary pitchers of ice water at the pools - The Cactus Garden - Turn-down service (but housekeeping sometimes arrived too early in the a.m.) - Complimentary late check out Why I was disappointed: And, let me just say, that when I stay at a 5 star property, I expect near perfection- - The Food was ridiculously expensive. We were lucky because we had a car and could go off the property. The resort will not let you deliver ANY food in. I am also sick of 5 star properties saying that they are in line with other 5 star properties in regards to their food cost! Instead of following along, Be innovative and offer a more economical option. It should not cost $7 for a bagel! - I really disliked the location of our casitas. We were traveling as a family, but not with young children. Our back patios were literally at the base of the children's waterslide. This was not peaceful or relaxing and with our dog, it was very stressful at times. It was not the kind of trip we were anticipating. When I expressed my concerns about the location, I ran into an employee at the front desk who was not helpful and seemed to care less. I was not offered a change of location or venue. - Finally, my family was visiting partly to reunite with some family in the Phoenix are and partly to celebrate my parents 37th wedding anniversary. Reservations was aware of this fact. Sadly, during our entire stay, nobody wished them a "Happy Anniversay", offered a complimentary drink, or meal or a even a special gesture...at all. I was VERY surprised that we were not offered a complimentary upgrade at check-in, considering that the property was only at 1/3 capacity ( we learned this from an employee). It saddened me to read a recent review concerning a family's stay at the Four Seasons Troon North and ALL of the complimentary, special things the resort did for this man's wife's birthday. We were not acknowledged at all. We didn't feel special at all, and honestly the stay was just not that memorable. I know what that feeling is like, when you feel like you are the only guest because of how well you are treated and taken care of. I have stayed at these resorts before. However, I did not feel this way at The Phoenician. For those visiting, I would suggest at some point staying in Sedona, because it is so unique and the shopping, spas and tours (to me) are way more special than plain-old Scottsdale. Then, I would suggest, that if you are looking for that 5 star treatment, either splurge and stay at The Canyon Suites, or stay at The Four Seasons Troon North. This is what I plan on doing next time. There must be reasons why a 5 star property like The Phoenician is only #12 on Trip Advisor, and I think those extra above and beyond moments that were lacking during my trip are the reasons why.

Beautiful resort A group of us stayed in casitas at this beautiful resort. The rooms were lovely and the bathrooms were spacious. There was a large walk-in closet. Unfortunately, in my room, it was in the corner by one of the very comfortable beds and it was difficult to get into it. In other rooms, the closet is inside the bathroom. There was even live music because of the holiday weekend. The grounds are gorgeous and the way the hotel is situated against Camelback Mountain is impressive. tripadvisor · 2012-06-24 · 5/5view source

Stunning resort with the highest standard of service I have been visiting the Phoenician for more than a decade, whenever I visited the area. This is one of the most stunning resorts in the world. The grounds are immaculately landscaped and cared for. There is not a weed in sight. The resort sits at the base of Camelback Mountain in Scottsdale, Arizona, a resort city adjoining Phoenix, Arizona, that has more than 30 four and five star resorts. Anyone can build a luxury hotel, but the thing that makes this resort stand out is that the impeccable service is consistent. No matter when you visit, whether high season or low, whether you arrive draped in fur or in shorts and sneakers, the staff will treat you as if you are a VIP. On one occasion, my husband and I brought my mother and father and on the second day my mother was not feeling well. She had caught the flu or a cold on the flight in. When my father showed up in the dining room for breakfast alone, the waiter asked if his wife would be joining him. He explained that she wasn't feeling well. A short while later, while he was still eating breakfast, room service arrived with complimentary home made chicken soup, a pot of tea and biscuits, and bottled water (with a rose in a vase) for my mother. Rooms: In the main building, rooms are quite large (around 600 s.f.) and look out over the expansive grounds, including world famous golf course and a huge pool area. Standard rooms look at the mountain, but are otherwise the same. The mountain views can also be stunning. Camelback mountain is covered with saguaro cacti and at night spotlights illuminate the mountain and the scenery is breathtaking. Bathrooms are large with oversized tubs (some have jacuzzis), showers, marble floors and vanities, and are stocked with more than the usual amount of amenties. Towels are large and fluffy. Rooms include luxurious bathrobes. There are flat screen televisions and a sitting area alongside the bed and on the patio/balconies. The Canyon Suites are a separate all suite resort within a resort area east of the main building. They have their own drive up area, concierge, and pool area similar to the signature swan pool on the main grounds. The Phoenician Residences are two and three bedroom villas, some with their own swimming pools, garages and golf carts. Dining: Food is outstanding but expensive. Il Terrazo serves Italian American fare. World famous chef Jean George Vongerichten's J & G Steakhouse sits at the top of the resorts' main building overlooking the grounds. Room service food appears to be the same as what can be ordered at Il Terrazo, but note that there is an automatic delivery fee that is more than 20%. Relish Burger Bistro is available at the clubhouse and food can be ordered while in the spa and served in their juice bar area. Perhaps the best traditional afternoon tea in the area is served in the afternoons until 3pm. Reservations are highly recommended as this sells out. It is a very formal affair though most people dining wear resort casual dress (dress code applies in the building so no bathing suits). Private dining is available in the Praying Monk, an area that looks like a medieval wine cellar. I've never eaten there but the atmosphere is amazing. Limited seating (its a very tiny space). There is also an old fashioned ice cream parlor with indoor and outdoor seating on the grounds. Pools: Multiple pool areas including large upper area pools, lower area childrens pools include a 165 foot waterslide and the resort's signature pool, crafted of mother of pearl tile (an adult only area) surrounded by luxurious cabanas like you've never seen before: ceiling fans, tables, chairs, television, computer hook ups and wifi access, robes, fruit basket, and poolside dining. Sports: Championship golf course, tennis, hiking, tours, 20,000 s.f. spa (The Center for Well Being). Other activities: Cactus Garden, nearby dining and shopping at Fashion Square (a five minute drive east of the resort), and a world famous art collection worth more than $25 million dollars. Shops on the grounds include gift shops, jewelry store, women's clothing, and resort wear for both men and women. Note: There is a fee for valet parking and currently a resort fee of $29 per night that includes access to the fitness facilities and a number of other amenities. There is a kids club on the grounds with many activities and I can attest to the fact that this place is special. When my daughter was given a choice between going to an amusement park or the Funicians kids club for her birthday, she chose Funicians. Half days are around $45 and full days with lunch $75. The experience at the Phoenician is outstanding but their peak season room pricing is extremely high. If possible try to come in the off season, when temperatures rise beginning in May and the prices drop from 50-75%.

tripadvisor · 2012-06-18 · 5/5view source

Unaldulterated Luxury in the Arizona Sunshine We spent a marvellous ten days in this luxurious resort and can't recommend it too highly. A spectacular setting immediately below Camel Back Mountain reveals a substantial property with large, comfortable rooms, good wines, beers and good food. Nine swimming pools to laze in, and as many sunbeds as you could possibly want. You'll get first class service in the restaurants and by the pool(s). The hotel and the grounds are immaculate and the rooms are spotlessly clean - good facilities and powerful showers. Scottsdale Old Town is only five minutes drive from the resort and there are plenty of shops and eateries all around. If you can't be bothered leaving the hotel, spend a couple of hours in J G's Steakhouse on Thursday evenings for excellent Jazz and tasty bites, or - seven days a week - call in at the the Golf Clubhouse for burgers and beers with Happy Hour prices from until 6.00 pm. Or simply laze on the terrace with a glass of chilled Pinot Grigio or a Pacifico beer to hand in the warmth of the setting sun and watch as a myriad of planes land into Phoenix Sky Harbor. Don't miss out on this amazing resort - this is our fourth visit and we'll be back next year.

A four star The Phoenician was not a five star, okay maybe it was ten - fifteen years ago but not anymore. The bedroom location was a trek - down a lobby, up an escalator, through an outside area back through another lobby. The room was standard for a four star. There was a spider on the headboard (Im not one for spiders but I can forgive them for this since the outdoor terrace was practically built into camelback mountain). However the carpet wasn't vaccumed or it was superficially. Down beside the bedside locker there was a lot of lint and fluff and general dirt. The outside bar was vey badly lit, we had to use the light from our phones to read the menu. On the first proper day here, we went down to the pool but it was full to capacity! There was staff on hand, helping people to set up sunlounger but they didnt come near us. They were pretenting to be busy. We had to lift our own sunloungers off a stack of extras that they had set up, We could see everyone had towels but again that was another trek back in through the pool area to get these. Great Resort We loved the Phoenician. The resort was lovely and the staff was superb. The concierge desk helped us make some great dinner reservations. Excellent suggestions and so very friendly. Matt, the manager of the lounge off the lobby was so friendly and also had an excellent and friendly staff. The ice cream shoppe (which was so much more. Oh, and my husband enjoyed the golf as well which was great as this was one of the main points of the trip. He liked the golf course at the Phoenician and also enjoyed the other golf courses he played in the area (suggestions by the concierge). Excellent service, great room My husband and I chose The Phoenician based on a great online deal and weren't disappointed. tripadvisor · 2012-05-23 · 5/5view source

It Doesn't Get Any Better Than This! This was my husband’s and my 4th stay at the Phoenician Resort, Scottsdale, AZ and this time we brought 3 friends with us. Each time we visit, it is more amazing than the last. Staff is incredibly friendly and knowledgeable. Just about the entire staff remembers and calls you by name. Sometimes, I have a hard time remembering my own! To be greeted at breakfast with “Good Morning, Mr.& Mrs.____“ before we even reach the hostess station makes us feel so special. It is like they really appreciate our business and want us there. Our room was more than lovely. Large, and immaculate. The huge bathroom was spotless. Night service would remove any used towels, turn down your bed, put soft music on, fill the ice bucket, leave chocolates and the luxury of all, place a white cloth on the floor on the sides of the bed so that when you got up in the middle of the night your feet were not on the rug but on the foot cloth. That, I had never experienced at any other hotel. The grounds did not have a blade of grass out of place and the landscaping was beautifully done with waterfalls, pools, flowers, trees and ponds. One day while pointing out the Desert Walk on the property, a bell boy, Manuel, saw us and asked us to get into the golf cart and took us on a tour of the entire grounds. He had worked there for 16 years and was a wealth of information. The concierge staff was more than helpful, knowledgeable and very accommodating. Would arrange any activity you desired. House keeping would come back after they cleaned the room and ask if everything was Ok. If not, they would fix it. The pools were warm and clean and the pool staff very attentive. This time we witnessed the pool staff in action..... 9 baby ducks followed Mommy Duck into the pool. Unfortunately, the babies did not know how to swim yet. Babies were stuck in the pool when Mom flew out. 4 or 5 pool staff worked about 45 minutes to get the ducks out. Mommy would not let them near the babies. Finally, after getting them into a box, the staff said they would bring the ducks to the pond, just a few feet away. Mommy would know where to find them. Well, Mommy didn’t know and was quite upset. We finally had to leave and go back to our room, however, shortly after returning there, we received a call from the pool staff saying the ducks were united with their mother. The staff knew how concerned we were and wanted to put our mind at ease that all was well. I cannot imagine any other resort having as much concern for the ducks or their guests. They certainly went above and beyond. The Phoenician has a great location with lots to do in the Phoenix, Scottsdale and Tempe area. Sedona less than 2 hours away. This is truly a First Class, 5 Star Resort, one you have to experience just once, but you’ll go back!

tripadvisor · 2012-05-15 · 5/5view source

Classically Extravigant There are a lot of excellent options for full service resorts in the Phoenix area. But The Phoenician stands out for its central location, lavish appointments and excellent service. The property is a symbol of 1980's excess with an amazing, world-class build. If you want to feel like a million bucks and want a property a little more formal than other comparable options then the Phoenician may be a good choice for you. Great for couples, golfers and jet setters... not as ideal for families or younger travelers seeking nightlife or a 'scene'. Also consider Royal Palms and Arizona Biltmore. Location: The Phoenician is located on the Phoenix-Scottsdale border near downtown Scottsdale and minutes from the Biltmore area and PHX. The property is set on the SE side of Camelback Mountain, affording excellent views of the city. (Something most competing properties cannot offer.) While you are close to many things you can walk to nothing. If you want to get off property then either rent a car or be prepared to use the resort's town car service. (Taxi cabs are NOT allowed to pick up guests on property.) Dining/Amenities: We did not try the full service restaurant but did enjoy excellent room service at breakfast. The food quality was superb and the service was unusually outstanding. The new-ish J&G Steakhouse has best on property views of the city, very good craft cocktails and good (but perhaps not notably so) cuisine. Try the cocktail lounge before dinner. The Phoenician offers a full spa, golf and tennis. The pools look especially nice. Rooms: We stayed in the casitas below the main building. The room was spacious and offered an incredible view of Camelback Mountain. Everything about the appointments was first class from the linens to the technology. Marble, gold plate and berber everywhere. While a refresh has updated the color palate the rooms retain their 1980's opulence. It's a better thing than you might expect. On the down side the room was not as clean as you might expect for the price range and the patios are less than private. Overall my wife and I quickly felt at home and in love with the place. Service: People are helpful and usually crisp. Something about our interactions (other than room service) left something to be desired. I'm nitpicking but at this price point you deserve to know that service is arguably more intuitive at the smaller, boutique Royal Palms but it still top notch here. Perhaps just not world class. Other: Self-Park is available and convenient. This is a Starwood Property that participates in SPG. Very good wi-fi. The $29 resort fee is pushing it and is higher than some competing properties. Bottom Line: The Phoenician is incredibly unique and perhaps unexpected in Phoenix. You will pay 5 star prices. Value will be there if the property fits your traveling needs and you will have a memorable experience.

It is, however, well maintained. 3) Can be pretty expensive - but I was able to snag a discounted rate!

tripadvisor · 2012-02-15 · 3/5view source

Mixed Comments Visited The Phoenician last week for a combo business/pleasure trip. Overall thoughts are positive, but not without some reservations. Checked in late afternoon after a brief wait. Our room was way, way on the far end of the resort property, about as far away as it could be. Someone’s got to have the room that’s farthest away, and my wife and I are both able-bodied, so it wasn’t a huge deal. The employee that checked us in did mention how long the walk was, but said it was an oversized room and hoped we would find it comfortable. As it turns out, the room’s size was very generous, very spacious. And we had a nice deck with two chaise lounges, two regular chairs and a little table – all facing the setting sun. The hallway to our room was dark (not W Hotel-like “chic dark”, but just dark and depressing) and in need of refurbishment. The carpeted areas leading up to the internal doors that separated the inside hallway to the outside hallway were a bit soiled and frayed, probably from years of roller bags and luggage carts banging across the threshold. The room itself was okay. The furniture was decent, the flat screen TV was decent, the bed and bedding was excellent (one of the best hotel beds I’ve slept on in a while), the bathroom was okay. The only significant issue with the room was the shower. If my wife and I took back to back showers, the water would begin to back up. This was particularly noticeable to me, because I was almost always the second person to shower, and my wife takes long showers. By the end of my relatively short shower, I would have water at about ankle height. I thought about reporting it to the front desk, but didn’t because I knew that the shower had to run for 15 minutes or more before it happened, so the maintenance guy would probably show up, turn on the water, see it drain okay and then think we were crazy. I probably should’ve reported it anyway, but didn’t. The other comment on the room was about the little wet bar area, where the coffee maker was, etc. The caulk between the counter and backsplash around the three sides of the wet bar area was very old – a bit discolored with some gaping holes where the caulk had cracked. I commented to my wife “you know, it wouldn’t cost anything to have someone take the old caulk out and put fresh caulk in and this would look so much better….”. Service throughout the resort was spotty. Spotty might not be the right word, because it was more typically good/great than disappointing, but, as is typically the case, the disappointments stand out more than the good interactions. On the good/great side, we were looking for the sundry shop one evening after dinner, probably around 9 p.m. We inquired at the front desk, and the young man said “The Pinata Shop is already closed, but I can find someone to open it up for you”. We said “that’s not necessary”, but he insisted. And he then personally escorted us from the front desk to the sundry shop, opened it up, let us shop for our soda and snack and then charged it to our room. That was excellent service. The concierges were excellent in our few brief encounters. The bellmen were excellent. The business center staff was very helpful. On to the disappointing….the service at the pool, while polite, was inconsistent. Example: we sit down next to a colleague/friend and a waitress swings by and asks if we would like menus. My wife and I say yes, our friend says yes, so two menus are handed out. 45 minutes later (and I’m not exaggerating) we hadn’t seen hide nor hair of the waitress. One would think that if you ask if someone wants a menu and they readily say yes, it’s because they’re hungry and want to order some food. I finally had to flag a towel boy and ask him to find the waitress so we could order lunch. She comes over, takes our order and then begins to walk away, and we say “miss, I think our friend here wants to place an order, too!”. The next day we waited forever to get the check at the pool, and when we finally flagged down our server (a man, this time), he kept flipping through the checks and couldn’t find our check. He was a good guy, but he finally, said “I’m sorry, I can’t find it, I’m going to have to go print it out again”. Which could happen, I know, but since we had already waited so long, we said “just add the automatic gratuity, we’re going to head to our room”. The biggest service lapse related to housekeeping. I was in my room on Saturday morning watching my alma mater play a bball game on ESPN. The doorbell rings about 10:30 a.m. (the game started at 10 a.m. local time) and it’s housekeeping. The first words out of her mouth were “Do you want your room serviced today?” I was really, really surprised that she would ask that question at a place like The Phoenician. It’s not as if it was 5 p.m. and we had had the Do Not Disturb sign on the door all day. I said “yes, we would but would you mind coming back in about an hour and a half”. The lady says ok. An hour and a half later (I’m being generous, it might have been a little less than 90 minutes, but let’s say 90 minutes), the game is still on and the doorbell rings again. It’s the same lady, and I say “I’m sorry! Would you mind coming back in 30 minutes?” She hesitated, paused, and had this look of irritation on her face that really threw me for a loop. She hemmed and hawed a bit, before finally saying “yes, okay”. Maybe I was really screwing their schedule up, but it was only noon, on a Saturday (when I’ve got to think that people are, generally, leaving their rooms later than they are during the week). Her irritated look irritated me, so I said, trying to make a point, “are you sure that’s okay?”, to which she replied “yes, that’s fine”. I don’t know, maybe I’m at fault and readers of this review will tell me that I am. One final comment regarding housekeeping. At some point on Saturday, between the time we left for the pool and returned from the pool, someone dropped off a tray of candies, with a postcard from the resort manager thanking us for our stay (we were leaving the next day). We left the tray, uneaten, on the wet bar counter and headed off to dinner. When we returned, the housekeeping staff had been in the room for the turndown service, and we noticed that one of the candies had been eaten! It was completely not a big deal, because we weren’t going to eat them all anyway, but it was still a bit weird. Knowing I was probably going to post a review on Trip Advisor, I asked my wife twice “are you sure you didn’t eat one of these??” She let me know, in no uncertain terms, that she hadn’t. Let me close with a couple of positives. The food was great. We had lunch at Il Terrazzo on day of arrival – great (and great service, too). We had a group dinner at Il Terrazzo on evening two and the food was outstanding. The lunches we had poolside were very good. We will definitely return (partly due to business commitments, but for pleasure, too), but the service lapses are, at best, interesting.
