My new favorite hotel Leveraging our points, we stayed at the Phoenician for 5 nights in mid-January. Overall we were extremely pleased with the experience. It may be one of my favorite hotels in the world. Pros: all the stuff that comes with the resort fee such as the bikes, lounge at the spa, great fitness center, etc.; huge rooms; tons of little amenities and great yoga classes taught by Meta. Cons: expensive if you don't have points, a bit of a walk (but very doable) at night (they will loan you a bike during the day) to get anywhere "off-campus" if you choose not to rent a car. Mini-gripe: They charge $20 ($10 if you pay the resort fee) for a "120 min" guided hike that is "an intense cardio workout". Obviously these are very subjective terms, and from my perspective, a huge exaggeration. They really should change the description to read: "a hike up to Post 18 on Camelback mountain which is less than half way to the summit, but still an athletic experience for those who aren't well conditioned. Note that most of the allocated time will be on the road getting to and from the trailhead." Though they did refund my $10 after I alerted the front desk to this minor grievance. I wrote an extensive blog article about the Phoenician, Camelback Mountain and nearby parts of Scottsdale with tons of pictures and tricks such as where to get a free healthy breakfast. Check it out at: http://freetravelgenius.com/phoenician/ Do note that we were there from Jan 12 to Jan 18th. The place pretty much looked like a ghost town during this period. I think it may have had to do with being a less busy time of year, or maybe the place is just so big, you can't see anyone else. Anyway, it worked out great for us, but it is possible my thoughts would be different if there were big crowds.

Staff Took Great Care of Me With My Broken Foot OVERVIEW OF BRAND Starwood Hotels & Resorts established the Luxury Collection after it acquired Sheraton (Sheraton had bought the properties from an Italian group and branded these unique hotels as Sheraton Luxury Hotels). These hotels are intended to reflect each area’s unique culture or the historic building it is in (e.g., if it used to be a royal palace) as opposed to mirroring the look of other hotels within the brand. Luxury Collection Hotels used to have a uniform logo (with four horses) but each hotel was allowed to design it’s own logo beginning in 2009, which may confuse some customers. THE PHOENICIAN This hotel opened in 1988, and it is located approximately 12 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX). An affordable way to get here is to take SuperShuttle for about $16.00 each way (if reserved online) plus tax. The grounds consist of a massive golf course, tennis courts, a cactus garden, a spa and fitness center (in the Centre for Well-Being), a salon, and a barbershop. There is a mini-mall called “the Shops at the Phoenician,” which includes a coffee shop, ice cream parlor, cyber café, wine and spirits shop, a fashion store, small art gallery, and a gift shop. Self-parking is free while valet costs $29.00 per day. The in-room guest services guide states that there is a resort dress code with jeans only allowed during the day: “Appropriate evening wear is resort casual. Slacks, button-down or polo shirts, skirts, pants and dresses are acceptable.” I’d only brought jeans so I hid in my room the first night. However, when I asked the front desk about this on my second day, the staff informed me that the rules have become more relaxed except for the J&G Steakhouse. Several staff members stated that the slow periods at the resort (i.e., when you may get better deals and more attention) is in-between Thanksgiving and Christmas and during the hot summer months. THE ROOM This is my first stay at the Phoenician (over Thanksgiving Weekend), and I was assigned a “Deluxe Room” on the first floor of the Main Building (B Wing); my view consisted of a green lawn (on which people played badminton) and a large concrete slab. In this type of room, you should find a 42” LG flat-screen (720p) LCD TV; a “mini bar” and fridge with soft drinks, wine, beer, and spirits (price range = $1.50 [small bag of chips] to $55.00 [champagne]); a pull-out couch; coffee table; desk; an iron and ironing board; a wall safe; and a Sony CD clock radio (ICF–CD–7000) with an iPod jack. There is no coffee maker in the room. The bathroom has a hairdryer, dual sinks, a cushion seat, and Remede bath products. There is a patio with a round table, two chairs, and a lounge chair (for sun tanning). There is WiFi and Ethernet; prices are about $13.00–20.00 depending on the amount of bandwidth that you want. FOOD There are 11 restaurants and eateries on the grounds. I only ate food from two of them: The Thirsty Camel and Il Terrazzo, which both seemed to have the same menu. Room service is available 24-hours with breakfast items ranging $7.00 (cereals) to $22.00 (Crab Benedict Plate); lunch/dinner ranging $8.00 (soups and salads) to $34.00 (steak and fries); and a limited after-hours menu ranging from $7.00 (desserts) to $17.00 (pizza). There is an afternoon teatime (2:00–3:00PM) in the main lobby. The resort does have the Kids Pass Program, which is an “all-inclusive dining program” for children 12 and younger. Visit the SPG site for more details (www.spgpromos.com/kidspass/). GYM AND POOL The fitness center is located at the Centre for Well-Being, and it looked like a well-equipped hotel gym. There are numerous pools and cabanas on the property, including one pool designated for adults only. There are exercise classes that you can sign up for (for a fee) and a daily guided-hike up the mountain. SPG SPECIFIC There is no Club Lounge for the regular hotel; however, I think there is one at the Canyon Suites (an exclusive area of the resort). Otherwise, there are no free food/drink perks for Gold/Platinum-Preferred Guests. Platinum members do get 500 Starpoints, free Internet (regardless of what bandwidth you choose), and the resort fee ($29.00) is waived. There is no “Green Choice” Program (where you waive housekeeping for points or credit) at this hotel. I requested late checkout and was given 2:00PM (versus the 4:00PM typical for Platinum). I’m not sure why as there was a mass exodus in the morning given it was the Sunday of a holiday weekend…and the beginning of their “slow season” in between Thanksgiving and Christmas. Nevertheless, I know that SPG resorts don’t have to give late checkout (Sheraton–Carlsbad being the absolute worst about this), and I appreciated the 2:00PM offer. OVERALL RATING The Phoenician is a beautiful desert resort, though it may be uncomfortable for people not wanting a very upscale place with a rather homogenous crowd. Yet, the staff is extremely friendly (esp., Bernie, a bartender; and Connie, a housekeeper) and they offer many interesting activities if you don’t care to golf, play tennis, or hangout by the pool. For instance, I signed up for the “Adult Cocktail Making Class,” in which Kira taught us to make a pumpkin martini for the holidays, gave us generous samples of an Amaretto-infused warm-cider, and samples of wine—a nice free treat given the lack of free drinks for Platinum guests typical of most other properties. I am also very appreciative of the chef who prepared me a special Thanksgiving meal for my room (which was not on the room-service menu) given that I was somewhat immobile because I recently broke my foot. Overall, the Phoenician is a very nice retreat to come to, even as a “staycation” for the locals.

tripadvisor · 2011-12-11 · 4/5view source

Great Resort, But Losing Its 5-Star Touch A Bit I stayed at the Phoenician for 2 nights in August with my family, and although we had a great stay and enjoyed the hotel, I think it may be resting on its laurels a bit. I had heard of the Phoenician many times before coming to Scottsdale. It had really been hyped up as the most gorgeous 5-star resort one could want. However, I noticed some areas that could use improvement, just in terms of renovations and service. I think one contributing factor to being less ‘wowed’ than I expected was the fact that we had just finished 2 nights at the beautiful Ritz-Carlton outside of Tucson. Having that as a comparator, I still loved the Phoenician, but didn’t see it as quite the same level of service. The Phoenician is a large, beautiful resort, nestled right at the foot of Camelback Mountain. Considering that it’s in the desert, it’s really great how lush and green everything is. It’s like a beautiful island oasis, so they definitely put a ton of effort and money into creating this feel in the desert. That impressed me. The grounds are large, with lots of waterfalls, koi ponds, and palm trees. It’s nice to walk around the resort, and in keeping with its desert location, there is a cactus garden on the Camelback side of the hotel. I guess it would also be really easy to do some hiking on Camelback from the resort. The location was really great for touring the area. It’s only a 5-10 minute drive from Old Town Scottsdale and all of its shopping, art galleries, and many restaurants. We took advantage of that area for dinner each night. It was also convenient to some of the attractions we wanted to see in Phoenix (the hotel is essentially right on the border of greater Phoenix and Scottsdale). It was also a very easy 20-minute drive back to the airport at the end of our stay. I loved being right in the middle of things, yet have the secluded resort feel when we were there. We chose a grand deluxe room in the casitas. I definitely recommend both this room type and the casitas in general. I was very confused when booking a room online before the trip, so it was good to figure out what the different room types are. Essentially, you have a choice between 2 locations and 3 views. The price only seems to differ by view, not location. The 2 locations are the main building and the casitas (there are many more rooms available in the main buildings). The main building rooms are in the 2 large horseshoe-shaped buildings on the side of the resort by Camelback. This is where the lobby, restaurants, and conference facilities are located. The other option is the casitas. These are also arranged in a horseshoe shape, but they are a grouping of several small two-story buildings across the resort by the golf club. The rooms here all have exterior entrances and parking right by the buildings. We chose a casita room just to try something different, plus it sounded very convenient for parking and access to the pool, which it was! Even if you’re in the casitas, it’s only about a 5-minute walk up to the main buildings, which requires walking up past the 3 levels of pools. I actually thought it was a really pleasant walk at night. I looked at the aerial view of the resort on Google Maps to get a good feel for how it’s set up before we arrived. In terms of the views, superior is the most basic view. In the main buildings, this means looking across at other rooms and the hotel driveway. The way these buildings are built, one is built directly behind the other, so that rooms on one side of each look right into those in the other building. In the casitas, a superior view would get you a view of parking lots. Deluxe is the next view upgrade. Deluxe is a view of Camelback Mountain and the cactus garden in the main buildings, but a view of the golf course and gardens in the casitas. The best view is Grand Deluxe. We went for this view and loved it. Regardless of which building you choose, this is a view of the pools and beautiful grounds/gardens in the middle of the resort. You’ll just be looking at different pools depending on which building you select. Our room itself was great, and very spacious. We were on the second floor of the casita and loved the view. The casitas do not have elevators if you’re on the second floor, but that wasn’t a problem at all. It was so convenient to be able to park our car in the small lot right outside our casita, and just walk up the stairs and into our room. Our room had windows on 3 sides, which is unusual for a basic hotel room. The balcony was huge, and so nice to sit out on. The balcony was completely covered, which was perfect in the August heat, and had a chaise lounge, as well as a table with 2 chairs. We had a great view of the mother-of-pearl pool from our balcony. The room itself was a great size, and decorated just as the pictures show. The rooms are pretty neutral with a botanical sort of style. It definitely wasn’t just redone, but it was still nice. I think the rooms will need to be renovated soon to look fresher. However, everything was in great condition and perfectly clean. The bathroom was great. We had a huge bathroom, much larger than what I’ve seen in other pictures posted. It had a tub, 2 separate vanities, a walk-in-closet, and huge shower that could easily hold several people. The toilet is in a separate room with a bidet. The bathroom definitely shows the age of the rooms. The bathroom is very nice with marble everywhere, just doesn’t look like it’s ever been updated. We really enjoyed time at the pool. There are several pools on different levels, each with lounge chairs and lots of noodles in the pools (some of which definitely needed to be replaced-they're cheap enough!). The top level has multiple pools closest to the main buildings. The middle level is the adults-only pool with a swim-up pool bar. The lowest level is the signature mother-of-pearl pool, which is the one we chose to use, since it was closest to our room. There is also a very fun pool slide by the lowest level pool. I recommend guests of all ages try the slide. It wasn’t too crowded at the resort when we were there on a weekend in August, so we didn’t have trouble getting lounge chairs ever, but I can see that it might be an issue other times of year. A lot of the chairs are reserved for those who purchase cabanas for the day. Maybe it was because we were in a casita, and would come and go from there, but we didn’t encounter much of the staff. The only staff I interacted with was the pool attendants, who actually left a bad taste in my mouth. They essentially keep all of the towels in their cabana, and are responsible for bringing each guest a towel when they arrive at the pool, along with a complimentary pitcher of ice water. They also serve drinks and food. The first day I was at the pool, the staff must have looked at me and decided that I wasn’t going to be purchasing any food or drinks, and basically ignored me. It took almost half an hour for someone to even come over with a towel and water pitcher. In the meantime, the same few guests were being waited on over and over again. Once someone finally did come over to me, there was no apology. The attendant acted as if I had refused a towel previously and was bringing it over “just in case you need one”. I don’t have a problem getting my own towel, and I honestly wish towels would just be out to pick up yourself. However, if a resort sets up the pool like this, with attendants guarding the towels, I expect that everyone will at least be given a towel promptly. I will say, the second and third days at the pool, the service was better. All in all though, we really did enjoy our stay here. The grounds are lovely, and the room was really comfortable and nice. Time at the pool was so relaxing. Looking at the lobby and some things about the rooms, though, I will say that the hotel seems like it’s seen better days. It’s a bit over the top with marble for my taste. It looks like it was built to be really flashy in the 1990s, but that’s just not the style that new resorts have today. My parents were really impressed by the marble and crystal chandeliers everywhere in the lobby, but my brother and I thought it was a little over-the-top and outdated. The rooms, while nice, were also not recently redone, and the bathroom definitely showed its age. Is it beautiful? Yes. Is it a great resort? Yes. Does it live up to its hype? Not quite as much as I expected. I think it’s seen slightly better days, and service needs to get better (at least at the pool) to stay a truly 5-star property. There is stiff competition for resorts in this area. I recommend the resort highly, but I wasn’t quite impressed enough to say it’s the only place to go in Scottsdale.

tripadvisor · 2011-11-25 · 3/5view source

Storied property is run down--needs major interior renovation The Desert Southwest was arguably hit as hard as any region of the United States as a result of the Great Financial Crisis of 2007-2008. The ensuing economic downturn has led to cascading real-estate prices and diminished economic activity throughout the Valley of the Sun. This is all too apparent at the Phoenician, the once famous luxury resort located in Scottsdale, AZ. We traveled and met a group of friends in the spring of 2011 for a long weekend. It should be noted that the grounds and landscaping at the Phoenician are still immaculate... We went with the three day tennis package and stayed in a standard king room. The room itself was large enough to be comfortable and had a small patio overlooking the main entrance to the resort. The interior of the room was worn and looked about five years overdue for an upgrade. The same story was true with the bathroom--everything was worn and needed to be redone. This is not the trait of a five star resort. The pool was nice and we rented a cabana for one of the days of our stay. The same theme prevailed with the cabana as it wasn't that clean and seemed rather worn. The service at the pool and cabana was average but friendly. The tennis facility was first class but the service there was a little behind the quality of the facility itself. It is highly recommended otherwise. This resort has seemingly unlimited potential and it's a bit surprising that it's in the shape it is in considering it is a Starwood property. In the meantime the best options remain the Royal Palms or Four Seasons?

Great weekend experience We spent 4 nights at the Phoenician in October of this year and had the most amazing time. We were upgraded to a deluxe room with a spectacular view of the grounds facing south. We did not want to leave the room or balcony view. The bathroom products are incredible! However the pools are so tempting we had to experience all of them (There are 7) - and they were incredible! The pool staff is professional and the pool side menu is very reasonable for a property of this caliber. We did our best to experience all of the restaurants on site. We dined at the Il Terrazzo restaurant for our anniversary dinner and for breakfast. The service and atmosphere was outstanding! We highly recommend dining there - the food is delicious and very well presented. They have an extensive wine list for all tastes and budgets. Coffee at the Ice Cream Parlour / cafe was a bit pricey @ $5 a cup but not unexpected at a property like this. If you so choose, the tennis facility is immaculate and the golf course looks great - lots to do without ever leaving the property! We can hardly wait to bring our family back in the spring to enjoy this property again! As a SPG Platinum member, we have experienced many great Starwood Properties and the Phoenician has become a new favorite!

tripadvisor · 2011-10-26 · 5/5view source

Friendliest staff anywhere We were here for 4.5 days in October, to see Jimmy Buffett on Thursday night and the Steelers on Sunday. Despite the fact that Scottsdale is on the other side of Phoenix from these venues, we picked the Phoenician. Much has been written thus far about the opulence of this resort, and most of it is true. Golf, biking, hiking, tennis, swimming are all available without leaving the resort. The equipment is all new-ish and up to date, and the rec area featuring the clubhouse and tennis garden are an easy walk from the main building. There are several bars/lounges in the resort, but as a warning, they are all very low-key. If you're looking for nightlife, you're going to have to leave the Phoenician. In fact, the only live entertainment while we were there was a guitarist that can only be described as "coma-inducing" playing in the main lobby off of the Thirsty Camel bar. This was really the only drawback to the entire resort. The staff though, is what makes this place. From the valet to the front desk to housekeeping to the bartenders, tennis staff, pool staff and grounds crew, everyone was on top of their game. You never passed a staff member in a hallway without being greeted, and on more than one occasion, they even asked out of the blue how our stay was and if there was anything that they could do for us. There are several pools, including one that is "adult-only". Getting chairs was not a problem, as the pool staff continuously monitored unused chairs and replaced old towels with new, and moved belongings to a common area where they could be picked up by their owners. Great idea to keep people from "reserving" chairs at 9:00 AM only to not return until 2:00 PM. We've all seen that at every resort. If you're looking for a relaxing place to get away from it all, The Phoenician in Scottsdale is an excellent choice.

tripadvisor · 2011-06-13 · 4/5view source

Great Bed! I visited The Phoenician in May 2011 traveling by myself. I had always heard about the legendary Phoenician and was anxious to stay there. The grounds are incredible and have all the beauty that a mature garden offers. I had the distinct impression I was traveling back in time to the 60s-70s as I drove up the road to the hotel. But that was OK. The exterior of the hotel buildings themselves are a little disappointing. Lobby is nice-- rooms not so nice. I can't imagine that I could have gotten a worse located room. No view at all. But I booked at the last minute-- what do you expect. The room smelled musty which is odd considering this is the desert-- a smell more associated with wet climates. The bed was heavenly which is exactly what I needed. Shower incredible. Bath large but dated. The shampoo, bath wash etc were very nice. I loved the idea of the outdoor terrace bar but the food, service and ambiance were less than wonderful. A lot of the problem were the kids ( which is not the responsibility of the hotel) but it is after all a bar. And where I come from, children aren't allowed in bars by law. And certainly not allowed to run, play and scream. The food was bar grub and expensive and wholly underwhelming. The J&G steakhouse was wonderful. And one of the reasons I stayed there. Service and food quality were on par with what I get in New York and San Francisco. The next morning the breakfast was just plain odd. There are 2 locations for breakfast that I could find-- one that is a ice cream shop and the other on the first floor. There were many very unhappy people at the restaurant downstairs-- Il Terrasse? may be I don't recall the name. But you were greated at 9 in the morning with "do you have a reservation?" Duh... no... is that what it takes to get some coffee? There were no fewer than 4 groups who were unhappy when I get there-- unhappy due to seating location, time taken to seat and selection on the menu. The restaurant was empty pretty much and it took 15 minutes to get a table. Once you got in, no one explained the menu or how it worked. There was some sort of convoluted buffet vs brunch that I never figured out. I just told the wait staff what I wanted to eat and let them point out which way to go. There were omlet makers ( good) who had only 3 pans ( bad) with which to cook. A gigantic hotel that offers custom omelets while you wait has only 3 omelet pans? And the chefs are struggling to clean them in front of you while you wait. Pools were beautiful. I could have lived there. Lots of choices and since I swim early or late I missed any kid traffic. The business center was a terrific asset to have-- print your boarding pass etc. I also loved the underground self park. It was very convenient. I don't know if I would return since there are so many 5 star choices in Scottsdale. But overall, I was glad I went and will seek out other hotels in this chain for the beds alone.

I can't imagine visiting Phoenix without staying at the Phoenician! Great service throughout the entire hotel, unbelievable golf, great amenities, well managed, nice bar atmosphere and close to shopping. Just do it!

Fantastic AZ Destination I was fortunate enough to stay at the Phoenician in Scottsdale for a work function and was there for 4 days. The property was fantastic and the service was great. The resort offers so many activites from golf, volleyball, pool, spa, etc. It's really a great resort if you plan on spending multiple days in one location. My massage was wonderful and I'd recommend the spa to anyone who visits the Phoenician. The only thing that disappointed me was the value of the experience. Great venue, but very pricey. For example, I ordered coffee, oatmeal, fruit plate, and orange juice for room service for breakfast and the total came to $52.00. tripadvisor · 2011-03-23 · 5/5view source

Impeccable Service! I spent four nights at this wonderful place with an intent to enjoy some sun, spa treatments and a three day conference. The service was impeccable. I arrived late am to the hotel and was allowed to check in early to a very nice grand deluxe room. The receptionist was so nice and throughout my stay I was always greeted with a smile and a hello. Twice when I was walking the grounds (which were beautiful) the front gatesman offered and gave me bottles of water. The staff also brought pitchers of ice water to the lounge chairs at the pool (it just would appear as I had my eyes closed just relaxing in the wonderful sun). As you can tell I live where we haven't seen the sun since October. I ordered room service twice and it was in my room within 30 minutes and the food was fantastic. I also ate at the Il Terrazzo for breakfast and the Oasis for lunch (3X). I found the food to be very good (loved the strawberry and spinach salad and again the staff/service was great. tripadvisor · 2011-03-14 · 4/5view source

Very Nice, Obscenely Expensive Resort First of all, everyone knows that The Phoenician is hideously expensive. If you go to a resort like this and agonize over the price and the hundreds of ways they scheme to separate you from your money, you're going to ruin your vacation. If you can afford to stay at a resort like The Phoenician, just enjoy yourself and pay the bill when it comes due. That said, it should be recognized that this resort is not just hideously expensive, it is obscenely expensive (example, three soft drinks from the on-course bevarge cart will run you $18. A hamburger at Relish, the clubhouse grill is $16). We traveled with a couple who were attending a medical convention, so received a favorable room rate. We stayed in the casitas and I can highly recommend them. While they are removed from the hotel itself (a short walk), they are immediately adjacent to the golf clubhouse and spa. The rooms were very nice and surprisingly quiet. The beds were very comfortable and the shower pressure was amazing. I don't understand how they can get away with that kind of water usage in the desert, but I promise you, you could fill a swimming pool with the water that shower put out in five minutes. No complaints whatsoever concerning the accomodations. In addition, the surrounding grounds are beautiful and impeccably maintained. My wife utilized the spa and was very happy with the treatments and the service she received there. We did not experience the pools, but they were lovely and I'm sure very servicable. The golf course sports three nine hole tracts and we played the Desert/Canyon nines. Simply put, this is not an impressive golf experience. First, it was VERY crowded and pace of play was a problem. The length of the round exceeded five hours and that is unacceptable. The course is also VERY short, measuring only 6,000 yards from the tips. While it is only a par 70, most championship courses measure closer to 7,000 yards. As a result of its lack of length, many of the holes are "tricked up" and poorly designed. For example, a 303 yard par 4 with a pond in front of the green, requiring a mid iron off the tee and a sand wedge approach; a 97 yard, sharply downhill par 3 that you could throw a ball to; and numerous par 5s reachable with short iron second shots. It could be fun under some circumstances, and the conditioning of the course was not bad, but there are dozens of better golf options within a 30 minute drive. The practice area is marginal at best and the range was actually out of golf balls. We did have one particularly bad experience upon completing our round. As we finished very near dark, one of our travel companions neglected to remove his $400 range finder from the cart. The cart was taken directly to the cart barn to be serviced for the next day's play. Without question, the range finder was discovered in the process of cleaning the cart, but was not turned in to lost and found. This has happened to a group of mine on two other occasions (once involving a watch). In those two instances, after being initially told that the property had not been located, the head pro ultimately went to the service area, read the Riot Act, and returned with the property. For two days, Phoenician staff showed little or no interest in recovering my friend's range finder. Finally, they offered him a cheaper model that someone else had lost and never recovered. I suspect if he keeps his eye on e-Bay, he may recognize his rangefinder for sale by someone with a Phoenix/Scottsdale address. We had lunch at Relish and the pricey burgers were very tasty. We dined at J&G Steakhouse with a fantastic view of the valley and the food there was excellent as well. The Sunday brunch was only average at best, with not nearly enough food available at the buffet, sending long lines snaking through the restaurant. Bottom line, this is a sumptious, beautiful, full service resort that has fantastic accomodations, a very nice spa and an average golf course. It is convenient to the airport and sports very nice restaurants and service. It is also obscenely expensive, so don't sweat the small stuff or you'll ruin your vacation.

Looks nicer than it is First off, beautiful grounds, views etc. I disagree with most of the complaints as far as the bars, restaurants go. I thought they were generally fine. The food and atmosphere was very good. My problem was with the service and the value. First day there we had to wait almost 30 minutes to get menus at pool bar. Lunch (salad and fish tacos w 2 drinks) was $68, ouch. Second day the concierge seemed annoyed we were asking for some recommendations. Add that to the fact that they wanted $19.95 a day for WiFi and $10 day for the fitness center!! Transportation to town (2 miles) was $13, would have expected a complementary shuttle from such a high end property. I wasn't in a cheap room either, I was paying for an Executive Suite!! tripadvisor · 2011-01-29 · 5/5view source

Renew your body and mind for a low nightly rate in the summer! Check out their summer rates! You can book rooms at more than half off their normal rates when you book during July - August! I had first visited this hotel on my honeymoon 10 years ago. My husband and I had visited ever summer for the following four years (then children came along)! I returned recently as a "girls getaway". It was just as amazing as I remembered. Luxurious, spotlessly clean, spacious rooms. Complimentary fluffy robes for the length of your stay. Scheduled turn downs, soft mat placed at your bedside for comfy tootsies from the moment you wake up! I love the multiple pools option. Feeling like a good splash or a just want a relaxing moment poolside? The option is yours. Dining facilities are worth the visit. A little expensive, but the food, atmosphere, view and service is well worth it. The Wellness Centre is just that, a place to make you feel good. Meditate or have a spa treatment. There are many to choose from. (The Bindi Treatment is my favorite). Complimentary robes, flip flops and lockers are offered to you at sign in at the Wellness Centre. I am not a golfer, however, my husband is. I volunteer to drive the golf cart so that I can enjoy the beautiful scenery and read a book for a relaxing morning. Scottsdale has a lot to offer people traveling alone and with families. Upscale neighborhoods, shopping, dining, etc.

What happened to the Beautiful Meditation Atrium? I have been bringing my family to the Phoenician for the Holidays nearly every year for the past decade. Impeccable service The staff were so friendly, it almost seemed surreal how genuine their smile and hospitality were. We had lunch outside at Il Terrazzo and inside for dinner. The Sunday buffet was well worth the food, service and ambiance overlooking all of the pools, yes, all (there are 9). tripadvisor · 2010-08-18 · 4/5view source

Gorgeous property in the desert but no refrigerated AC! We checked in at The Phoenician on July 30-Aug 2, 2010 for a weekend of golf. Booked two rooms - One King and one Double. Originally booked a superior room but was "supposedly" upgraded to a King Casita (7153 connecting). I would have preferably remained in the superior room as I will describe. The property is gorgeous and well-manicured at all times. Several pools around the property - considering the size, it is very quiet. Room service is prompt but expensive. Ordered 2 onion soups to our "casita" for $42 which included all the extra fees they added. The price on the menu was $9.00 each. Our room was conveniently located right across the golf clubhouse which allowed easy access without driving around. The golf course was under some sort of maintenance therefore my husband did not enjoy it as much. He considers the Biltmore and Gainey Ranch to be the best so far. Each room has a plasma screen tv, two phones, large bathroom with tubs ,safe, iron and table, robes and slippers. Minibar - expensive. Our room had a Dream Machine CD/Radio, the other room had a Bose. Don't know why. Internet for a fee is available in the rooms. Each room had a private balcony with lounge chairs and a table. Our room balconies faced Camelback Mountain for a nice view. Had breakfast at the Il Terrazo - good but pricey. A-la-carte - The Steal-Cut oatmeal is to die for! Buffet is about $25pp. Excellent service. Later discovered the cafe in the hotel shoppes which serves the same items but at a much lower price. Dined on July 31 at Il Terrazo - excellent food and service but again very very pricey. I ordered the Filet Mignon with 6 shrimp that was excellent - better that Ruth Chris! The Pina Colada arrived quite watered down. The server quickly replaced it with a Lemon Drop Martini. The restaurant had only about 6 tables occupied (two were ours) on a Saturday night. Overall the staff is very courteous and professional at all times. PROBLEMS: 1.) Room had a leak by the sliding glass door. Water leaked in during a rainstorm. Maintenance came to evaluate problem but blamed it on the rain. They said it was coming from the balcony on top. Did nothing else but offered to vacuum up the water from the carpet. That was never done 2.) None of the rooms on this property have refrigerated A/C but a water coil cooling system that dumps 100% humidity into the rooms. It was the most uncomfortable condition. Sheets were moist; carpet is icky; cannot do your hair with humidity and the awful humid smell. Contacted maintenance again when on the second day we realized that something was wrong with the temperature of the room. We felt ill with the dampness. The tech came and explained that this was a cooling system and that in the summer the humidity was felt higher. Living in New Mexico, we are very familiar with evaporative cooling systems, aka "Swamp Coolers," and are not very fond of. In our home, we have refrigerated air (we are original Floridians - so we know what we are talking about.) They offered to move us to another room that may be a little cooler without as much humidity but we declined as it was our last night and did not want to move. We were completely disappointed with the tempertature condition of this property. A 5 star property with a mediocre cooling system! As my husband prefers Arizona to play golf, we frequently visit Scottsdale and Phoenix but have never experienced this problem in any of the many hotels 3-5 stars tht we have stayed. Tthe front desk staff was made aware of the discomfort we experienced and compensated us however, The Phoenician is definitely not on our return list until the cooling systems is upgraded.

Great hotel and resort.. they have it all I have stayed at the Phoenician many times. They have everything there. tripadvisor · 2010-07-13 · 5/5view source

A wonderful experience in the Arizona desert From the entrance to the resort, the drive up to the lobby, we thought WOW, and we were not disapponted. The Phoenician is in a wonderful location, set within the backdrop of Camelback Mountain. The Lobby and lobby bar, The Thirsty Camel give you an idea of what is to be a perfect relaxing location. Upon check in, we were allocated a stunning deluxe room overlooking the lawns and pool areas. One slight negative here, was the check in clerk seemed more keen on me signing up to a Starwood loyalty card. I will summarise the different facilities on the resort site to give an overview of each; Pool area - nice ambience with first class facilities. Usually very attentive poolhosts and hostesses, plus waitress facilities at pool side. Pool Bar - Centre of lunchtime activity. Good drinks menu, and basic but fair snack menu. Great service from Steve and Juliane. New TV installed allowing a drink with the days sport on. Il Terrazzo - Breakfast menu was fair. Had eveining meal (Italian fare) which was very good. The terrace area was lovely (watch for the friendly but hungry birds). J&G Steakhouse _ Located on the 6th floor, very good food, ate there twice, 1st time was better, as waiter on 2nd visit seemed slightly uninterested, but nice place with stunning views of Scottsdale and Phoenix in the distance. Returned for 2nd visit after 4 day trip in San Diego. Arrived 3rd July, so for a day or two the occupancy was near 100% for Indepedence Day. Given a deluxe room with extended balcony with views of golf course, Cactus garden and the grounds. Beautiful balcony to watch the Arizona sun go down over Camelback. In summary a great place to stay, yes some things are quite expensive. $6.50 for large Latte $6.00 for bottle of beer. $120.00 for meal and drinks for two. However the overall impression was a great big PLUS, and we will deifnately return.

tripadvisor · 2010-07-12 · 4/5view source

Feeling super-relaxed after a weekend stay. I just returned from a weekend at the Phoenician and it was great! Because it was 112 degrees the rates were very reasonable. The a/c kept the indoors cool but not too cold and the pool was glorious! Pros: 1. The room was clean, spacious, with a nice view of the cactus garden out back. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was great! We were upgraded when we checked in so I'm not sure what style room we had. Given some negative reviews on the quality of the rooms, perhaps they've remodeled/updated recently? 2. The service was consistently helpful and friendly. 3. Fiesta Fridays at Relish (the Golf Club burger bar): The margaritas were tasty and only $5. They had a good band and there was dancing. 4.The pools are amazing! We swam laps, shot some hoops and went down the water slide. Because it was offseason, it was not at all crowded. There was plenty of lounge chairs in the shade and they supply oversized, thick beach towels. 5. The spa was expensive but very nice. We took advantage of the summer time discount of a 2nd service for 50% off. 6. Free, underground parking. 7. Generally beautiful views from every part of the property. Cons: 1. The food is very expensive. Breakfast costs about $50 for two people. That's not too bad for the Sunday buffet but otherwise it feels like extortion. $10 for oatmeal... really? 2. No coffee maker in the room. We like to bring our own tea and instant oatmeal along when we travel. It just makes for a healthier way to travel. You can get a coffee machine delivered to your room but it costs $38 for the duration of your stay. 3. No recycling or evidence of water conservation. 4. No free wifi. It costs $6 for 15 minutes online in their 'internet cafe'. I don't think I would go here during the 'high season' but I would definitely go back in the off season to take advantage of the discounts and combine a little bit of luxury and a visit with friends who live in Phoenix.

tripadvisor · 2010-05-01 · 4/5view source

Relaxing stay with excellent service I booked a long weekend Sat- Mon, at the Phoenician using 12,000 Starwood points per night in April when the weather is absolutely perfect! It was just after the Spring Break crowds had left and it was pure heaven. You can valet park or self park for free. Check-In The check-in was speedy and I love Daniela Ilieva at the Front Desk. As a Platinum member I was upgraded to a very large Grand Deluxe room (4196) with a huge balcony. The Main Building has 6 floors and the rooms at the far end are bigger have the large balconies. The Platinum Thank You amenity (chips, salsa and bottle water) was quickly brought to my room, as was the luggage. The mini refrigerator was already in the room, as I had requested it ahead of time. The service at this resort is excellent. Complimentary shoe shine, if you want. Note: bottle water is not provided free in the room, but you can get it, no charge, from the concierge or down in the Fitness Center ( they have fruit there too). I love, James, the resort ambassador who greets you at the door. There is also free coffee in the morning until 9 am at Il Terrazzo Di Luce. I was surprised and disappointed that the water and coffee was not in the room as it is in most domestic Starwood hotels (one reason it did not get Excellent rating from me). Room The room was huge with king bed, gigantic flat panel TV, sofa + 2 chairs, desk and balcony with lounge and table + 2 chairs. I was told the bed was a Westin Heavenly bed ( very comfy) and the bath towels were so plush! Two closets, mini bar and large bathroom with Remede toiletries...really in heaven now ( valued at $40.)! I love that the room had a bathroom scale, but unfortunately, this one wasn't working. Magazines in the room to read or take to the pool. Turn down service between 6-9 pm with chocolates. I asked for a DVD player and at first they said it was for a fee, then the next thing I know, they brought one up and installed for free! Also, since there was no coffee maker, I asked for some hot water to make tea and they delivered with a nice cup/saucer, cloth napkin and spoon at no charge. Everyone is so friendly and wanting to help make your stay enjoyable. Amenities There is a Business Center/Cyber Cafe with one free computer near the lobby and fax/copier. There are other shops here, (florist, women's fashion, general store, wine/beer, souvenir) but were all closed when I walked by. Disappointing was the Centre for Well Being spa...it looked dated and in need of remodel (also why it didn't get Excellent rating). The free Fitness Center appeared to be well equipped (has a scale) and there was a room for classes. Two acre Cactus Garden is along the north edge of resort grounds and is very interesting to stroll through. Restaurants I did not eat at any of the restaurants, but the Il Terrazzo patio is beautiful this time of year and they have a Sunday Brunch from 10 - 2:30 pm at three courses for $35. and $10 more for traditional American breakfast buffet. Afternoon tea in the lobby appears to be very popular, open daily at 2 pm. The highlight of the resort is world renown Jean-George Vongerichten's J & G Steakhouse. Pool The Oasis pool is the main pool with a children's pool and whirlpool. There is a 165 foot water slide for kids and young at heart. Mother of Peal pool for adults overlook the Necklace Lake filled with beautiful koi, ducks and one turtle. Cabanas are available for rent. The one turnoff was there was alot of bird dropping on the lounge chairs and weren't cleaned off daily. I got home and bird dropping on my clothes, etc...gross. Needs to be some improvement in this area (definitely not getting an Excellent rating for this)! Activities Funician Kids Club is supervised program for ages 5-12. Family Activity Center with movie theater, video game room, air hockey, foosball and board games. 27 hole golf course and 11 court tennis complex. Nearby is the Fashion Square mall with many of my favorite stores, such as Antropologie, Macy's and upscale designer store, such as, Jimmy Choo, Louis Vuitton, Gucci and Barneys New York. There are many restaurants and my favorite Paradise Bakery, love the spicy Southwest Chicken Caesar salad! Also a movie complex. Overall, this resort is very nice with excellent service and good location ( love Fashion Square). It is very relaxing and I would return again, but there are alot of other great places in Scottsdale, like the Westin Kierland (I like the Kierland Commons next door) and Fairmont Scottsdale Princess (best spa experience yet). Check out the photos from my stay: http://www.facebook.com/album.php?aid=120446&id=1539673139&l=07b2ad012e

tripadvisor · 2009-12-14 · 5/5view source

A lot depends on the room you get ..... I like The Phoenician. I stay in Scottsdale fairly regularly and I rank it my No.2 hotel there, beaten only by the Royal Palms, the quiet intimacy of which I really love. The Phoenician is much larger and hosts a lot of conventions which inevitably changes the atmosphere somewhat (noisy groups roaming the premises, no room in any of the bars etc.) But the service is still pretty good and the rooms, bathrooms and common areas are all elegantly decorated so if the rates are reasonable, I'll very happily stay there. The numerous, large pools make it particularly attractive if pool time or sunbathing is high on your agenda. I recommend the Grand Deluxe rooms which are a bit larger than the basic ones and some of which have a beautiful view of the pool area and valley beyond. But some have better views than others, and for me, a lot of the wow factor depends on that view, so I've been disappointed by my room in the past. And if there's a big convention on, and you've just booked the one room, your requests for a better one probably won't work. But this time I got a great room, close to the centre of the building and with a great view. Food and drink prices are very high, but probably no higher than other local hotels. I wish the bathtubs were deeper, but that's really my only complaint.

Good Family Friendly Resort. My husband and son stayed here on a weekend trip. We found this property very nicely kept, grand, beautiful decor and comfortable. tripadvisor · 2009-10-10 · 4/5view source

Definitely worth to be part of The Luxury Collection! Wow. This is how I have to start this review. The Phoenician is one of those hotels that you plan on returning to the next time you are in town. Several room amenities that we experienced include: turn down service with chocolates, the wait staff offered to get us fresh ice with our room service meal, and soothing music playing in your room with fresh ice each night. These little bits are small, but quickly add up as you realize that importance of knowing that the hotel cares for your business by providing these little things that you will remember and makes The Phoenician different than other hotels. The room was clean and very nice. I thought the room reminded me of a room in a french mansion with nice white walls, white moulding, and golden carpet in our room. The patio was definitely a nice way to relax and sunbathe. We opted for a entry level executive suite and were moved to a larger suite when I pointed out that the square footage of the suite we reserved was more than the suite we received. I did not know that there are suite categories so technically they were the same class. Nonetheless the manager on duty moved us to a larger suite as the check in person did not explain this. I was wowed with the hotel making sure I was happy. The location is pretty close to anything you wanted like the Kierland Commons and Old Scottsdale, both for shopping. The grounds are breath taking with the Camelback Mountain on one side and lush green golf courses on the other side. With a gated in fence we felt safe 100% of the way during our stay. Would I return, yes. The Centre for Well Being Spa and golf courses are top notch and I enjoyed these portions of our stay. What is nice is a full cactus garden you can walk through on the resort grounds. Very informative and fun at the same time. More pictures and information is available at my personal travel experience site: http://www.jetsetlife.us/resorts/luxurycollection/phoenician/phoenician.html

tripadvisor · 2009-10-05 · 3/5view source

Would not want to pay top dollar for this place We stayed for ten nights at the beginning of September, it was very hot but we got a great rate :) Negatives The hotel rooms were a dissapointment - we booked a deluxe room which is one up from the entry level room. tripadvisor · 2009-08-05 · 5/5view source

The Phoenician is Where It's At Recently stayed at the Phoenician over a July weekend and really do not have a bad word to say about it. Many good ones though. Let's see: Rooms: Upon check-in we were upgraded to a Casita Suite probably b/c the hotel was at 40% occupancy. I mean, who trips to Phoenix in July? The Living Room of the Casita Suite was a bit outdated with the furniture but very spacious and had a very large patio that looked out onto the golf course. The bedroom was nicely updated with all the amenities that one would expect to find at a resort of this caliber. The bed was large and very comfortable and the TV was updated and large as well. The patio of the bedroom was again a good size and provided many seating options. Bathroom: Very nice sized bathroom with separate tub and glass shower. The shower was very large and provided a bench and an amazing shower head that provided a very nice flow of water. Pool: The pool(s) are the best thing about the resort. We spent both days on the top level at the activities pool and enjoyed basketball and volleyball and music, both live and radio, all while being waited on by very attentive pool attendants providing complimentary water and beverage service (not complimentary). The water slide was great and the kids that were out at the resort seemed to really enjoy that as well. There is a pool for everyone depending on what you are in the mood for. If you would like to hang out at the pool without all the activities then the serenity pool on the lower level is probably for you. Grounds: The grounds around the hotel are simply beautiful. It's a good walk from the Casita Suites to the main hotel but the grounds are so beautiful that it's not a big deal at all. If, not for the heat you would forget that you are in Scottsdale. Food: Did not eat at the resort so I have no comment. Service: In addition to the upgrade of the room and the service at the pool the overall hospitality and striving to make our stay perfect was definitely noticed. We called the front desk around 12:30am the first night that we were there b/c a glass of wine had been spilled on the bed. Housekeeping was at the room and had the bed lines all changed withing 5-10 minutes (they got a nice tip for that one). I made several requests upon check-in, none of them unreasonable, and they were all taken care of in a very timely manner without the hint of a complaint. $: Yes, it's expensive but you get what you pay for. Parking charges were avoided because of staying in the Casitas but there is free self parking that is not too far away from the main lobby. Drinks are a bit on the high side but you should know what to expect going into a experience like this. Do your research and then you are not surprised. Overall, I would definitely recommend the Phoenician to friends and family and to people looking for a great getaway in the middle of the dessert.

tripadvisor · 2009-06-02 · 3/5view source

The bloom has fallen off the rose.... I really should have listened to the negative comments on this site about The Phoenician. The grounds of the hotel are amazingly well cared for, standing in stark contrast to the guest rooms. The guest rooms were spacious, however, they were in need of a serious renovation. The carpets had stains on them and were generally on the thread bare side. The bed was large and nice, however, the sheets had a few small holes in them. The crown modeling and the walls looked slightly worn. The bathroom was large, but needed an overhaul. Everything needed updating/replacing. You could tell that perhaps ten or fifteen years ago this resort was beautiful, but they had done very little, if anything, to upgrade and modernize the facility. The first room I was assigned was at the end of a hallway in the main building that smelled like feet. There was a large pile of trash in front of the door of an adjacent room that sat there for hours before it was removed. The room itself was dark and the patio doors opened to a patio that was almost completely blocked by a wall and shrubbery. Only a sliver of light reached the inside of the room, making it feel cave like (or jail like) and confining. I promptly asked for another room and was assigned a casita near the spa. This room was equally as worn, however, it had a lovely view of the koi fish pond and the pool. The pools are plentiful (nine of them, to be exact) and nice, however, they seem to have a duck problem. Flocks of ducks swim in both the koi pond and the pools themselves, leaving duck poop around the entrances to the pool. On one occasion, a duck had left a gift right at the entryway to the pool, and when one of the cabana boys was alerted to its presence by one of the guests, he said he would "tell his manager" and did absolutely nothing about it. Neither he or manager did anything about that poop pile or any of other poop piles left by the duck during my four day stay. Safety might be an issue at this hotel as well. While I was sitting in my room, a gentleman opened my door with a keycard that the front desk had given him. I think we scared the living daylights out of one another. He told me that he had been assigned the room I was in, and I told him there must be some mistake. After he left, someone from the front desk called, not to apologize, but to ask me what I was doing in the room because according to the hotel's records, I was supposed to transfer rooms again on that very day. I informed her that I had no desire to move and if I had to move again it would be to another room at another hotel. The resort food is expensive, however, that wasn't my biggest problem with it. The resort has a problem with ever aggressive birds that swoop down and grab the very expensive food straight from the plates of the patrons. As people would leave their tables to retrieve food from the breakfast buffet ($25 + tip), the birds would swoop in and take a nip from people's water and juice glasses. If someone left the table with food on it, forget about it. The crow-like birds would carry everything off in an instant. The operated in packs. At one point during breakfast on Saturday, a bird flew down and pecked a woman eating breakfast. She wasn't hurt, and the restaurant staff was extremely apologetic, but they could do nothing to abate the chronic bird situation. The resort was particularly boring as well. No real activities to speak of and the pool bars, which were hopping during the day, closed at 6pm sharp, leaving most folks looking for things to do off of the resort property during the evening. Good thing self-parking was plentiful, because you could come and go as you pleased in order to find entertainment off property. The spa is sufficient, however, it's ridiculous that the only way you can use the only gym in the resort without paying an additional daily fee, is to purchase a spa treatment. If you purchase a spa treatment, access to the smallish gym is complimentary for the day of your spa treatment, however, if you don't, you have to pay $20 a day to use the gym. Final note: If you go to this resort, make sure you have mapquest directions or a GPS before you come to Phoenix. On three different occasions, I called the resort for directions and got different and wrong directions every single time. What should have taken about twenty minutes to get to the resort from the airport, ended up taking me more than an hour. I eventually just ran across it with absolutely no help from the resort staff. p.s. -- On my last morning at the resort, I made my way to one of the pools and guess what saw on the lawn? I pair of dirty mens underwear. Lovely.

tripadvisor · 2009-04-24 · 3/5view source

Weird 80s Concept Hotel Yes, it's 5 star. Yes, it's in Scottsdale. But who really wants to stay in a kitsch 80s boutique whose main building looks suspiciously like a GEICO regional office and with an interior straight from The Donald's tower in NYC. Worst of all though is the acres of lawn and water features. Here in the desert. It just all seems so out-of-step and inappropriate now. Maybe creating these "oases" was all the range 25 years ago but today it just seems wasteful in terms of water resources. The trouble is that management probably hasn't realised how amusing this place is - or rather would be if the issue of water conservation in the south-west were not so serious. Slopping millions of gallons of water on manicured lawns and sub-tropical plants while the Colorado River dries up to a trickle is not just non-PC, it's downright unethical. There are plenty of great hotels around that make the most of the gorgeous desert landscape and vegetation (like the Hyatt in Palm Springs). They really should take a look around at the competition across AZ, CA and NM. Be warned too that this is firmly a 'family hotel', at least it was a Easter Spring Break. Zillions of kids everywhere - especially in the 'Relaxation Pool' (what's that about?). Between the ever present, over-loud poolside rock music from the speakers and the little angels you won't find much peace unless you sneak off to the golf club house and eat and drink there (the main restaurant was closed for a refurb when we were there). The Spa was dated too. Cheap tile on the floors and walls rather than natural materials. And maybe i'm out of touch but $150 for a 50 min Swedish massage? I can't vouch for how good it might have been as I swallowed my tongue when I saw the price list and had to be escorted to the relaxation area for a long lie down and a cold flannel. Value-wise we paid little for our room (which was very good - large and with a generous terrace). But they'll nail you on the food and drinks. We're used to Four Seasons prices but given the kitschness of the hotel we were expecting to pay 80s food prices too. Well, not really but we didn't expect a $19 burger at the pool. My girl and I are small eaters but even the simplest lunch (appetizer, small salad, 2 glasses of wine) worked out somewhere noth of $60. Finally, before choosing this hotel you have to ask yourself if you want to stay in a sort of ersatz palace styled on a 5,000 year old civilisation from the eastern Meditteranean but stuck in a suburb of Pheonix. I wish I had. We'd have stayed at the Marriott or Four Seasons instead. Oh yeah - and as for paying $15 or $20 a day for wifi when the rest of the world gives it for free these days - get real! The business centre was helpful though and I (and a few other starry-eyed men) filed our tax returns from there. I suppose apart from the horrendous extras bill and the lack of peacefulness it was quite an amusing choice for Easter!

Spacious room, great amenities My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend in January at the end of a conference he attended at the resort. We booked massages at the spa, dined at Windows on the Green, sat by the pool. Our favorite activity was sitting outdoors with drinks by the fire pit at the Thirsty Camel Lounge. tripadvisor · 2008-10-14 · 4/5view source

Pleasantly surprised Stayed 3 nights here. Had heard that it was slightly "stuffy" but we didn't find this at all. The room was lovely - tranquil colours - and the marble bathroom was beautiful. One of my bugbears is always the lack of clothes hangers in hotels - not in this case! The mother-of-pearl pool was a peaceful place to relax and the water was warm. Staff were attentive and friendly, particularly in the bakery, where they insisted that we take a free cookie or brownie for our journey home. Lots of activities, great location and best of all, following disappointing experiences at a couple of other Scottsdale hotels, where we were unceremoniously displaced without notice from hotel bars and pool areas to make way for conference functions, the conferences & functions at The Phoenician seem to be contained in their own areas of the hotel. There were several taking place while we were there and not once did we feel like we were at a hotel which gave preference to conference guests. (The conference areas looked very nice, so don't be put off if you are going there for a conference!). The bad points: it isn't made particularly clear when you arrive that you will be charged $26 per night for valet parking - this is just printed faintly on the valet receipt. We retrieved our car after we checked in and parked it in the closest self parking area - there is a lift up to the lobby from there. Disappointed that there is a $20 charge if you want to use the gym before 3pm and $10 for after 3pm. Inconvenient that the only printer in the cyberspace area was out of order when we wanted to check in for our flight online. Also, there is an hourly charge for using the internet in the cyberspace room. The restaurants were empty while we were there, which was a shame, but the bar area was nice and the food from the bar was delicious, particularly the cioccolato dessert! It takes a little while to find your way around the resort, even with the map you are given, but once you have the hang of it, its a beautiful place. We would definitely go back, as we left feeling refreshed and relaxed, and feel that this resort compared favourably in terms of character and customer service with eg. the Fairmont & the Hyatt Regency, where we have stayed previously.

tripadvisor · 2008-10-01 · 5/5view source

Amazing resort and spa! This was for a business retreat for my husband, so everything was taken care of for us. We were upgraded to a casita, which was lovely and very large, but unfortunately it had a view of the parking structure and we could hear cars and see headlights if we kept the door or curtains open. This initially upset me, I even called to change rooms, but they were full. It's hard to complain when someone is picking up the tab and it was very clear that other rooms had amazing views and non-handicapped bathrooms so we let it go.
