Nice but not Fabulous The hotel was plush but not worth the $600 a night the desk clerk quoted. The biggest issue is that I expected a true spa. The hotel bills itself as a wellness center - world class spa. I expected middle of desert with incredible spa & lots of health oriented activities, In fact, its in the middle of a suburb with an average gym/spa. The waiting area for spa services is coed and small - it was very crowded and uncomfortable sitting there in a robe across from men who were more than uncomfortable. If you book a day package - they bring you lunch and expect you to eat it on your lap. Going to get a manicure...you have to leave the spa building in your robe and walk outside to another building. The treatment rooms were a bit dingy. My day spa package cost over $500 and I felt a bit ripped off. The rooms were very clean and the beds very comfortable. The staff was incredibly nice and helpful. Food was good. The hotel is very convenient to downtown Scottsdale. It was a nice stay - just wasnt wowed for the money.

tripadvisor · 2006-11-07 · 5/5view source

Phoenician: A gem in the Valley, luxury across the board. I've enjoyed two stays at the Phoenician, once in a casita and once in the main building. On many other visits to the area I have enjoyed meals or golf at the Phoenician while staying with familiy in the area. One will be hard-pressed to find a better resort in the Valley. I can think of only a few that are its peers. I preferred the Casita, those nearest the pools are best. Farther away and you will be too close to some of the access roads and the comings and goings will affect the soltiude of your visit. However, if one gets the right Casita, it is substantially better than the main building. If you're relegated to the main buildings do try and score a room up against Camelback mountain. The standard rooms are nice, if a bit tired in places. Fairly spacious, decent terrace, fine furnishings. The room is on par with some of the other Starwood Luxury collections I have enjoyed. Pool area: massive, loads to do, plenty of options. I don't like the water, so I am not the best person to judge, but their is a lot of space, although during peak periods, it will get crowded. Golf: is prettty good, it's basic "resort golf". The 3 nine-hole courses are fine. I would try and play Canyon and Oasis as part of an 18-hole loop. The desert course is goofy golf in my opinon. Overall,the golf operation is seriously top-notch, from the outside service to the golf pro shop. There are many other activity options, the place goes all out to have options for the guests. Hiking is a good idea, if it's not 118 outside. Try and see the cactus garden, I like it and I could not care less about gardening. Dining: The 19th hole area at the golf center is a good choice for an al fresco lunch. Windows on the Green is a fine restaurant, I've had some excellent meals there. Room service is first-rate, some staff do better than others, but overall it is quite good. Try a few cocktails in the main building's two bars. The house drink: "Camelback Cooler" (?) was a favorite. Service: Luxury Collection standard, indeed. These people are trained well and provide very fine service. Hard to find much fault with any staff. A modicum of trouble once with front desk personnel, but that's life. Overall, service is what makes the Phoenician a great property. If you stay at The Phoenician in Feb-April or late Fall you will think Phoenix is the best place to live. Arrive in July or August and you wonder what you did in a past life to deserve this fate. Still, it is a dry heat and staying at The Phoenciain will mitigate the scorching oven that is the Valley. I truly enjoy staying at The Phoenician, you will too.

tripadvisor · 2006-09-29 · 5/5view source

Exquisite! Beautiful grounds, exceptional staff, great restaurants, gorgeous and very clean rooms with the most comfortable beds ever! It is rather removed from other things around the city which gives the property a peaceful and relaxed atmosphere. Car rental is available on-site, or town-car service to almost any destination. There were family activities, spa services and beautiful pools. I would definitely stay here again. I have stayed at other nice hotels in the area, but the Phoenecian is my favorite.

tripadvisor · 2006-09-05 · 5/5view source

Fantastic resort As a local, I often stay at the resorts in Scottsdale, and the Phoenician does not disappoint. I would have to say this is among one of the top 5 resorts in Scottsdale in terms of service, rooms, pool, and dining. As a Starwood member, upgrades are a plus. I recommend getting a city view, and the deluxe rooms on the west side of the building have spacious balconies with nice views of Papago Mountain. The remote control retractable awning is a nice feature, and we loved dining out there at night! (be sure to request this, as not all rooms with balconies have it) We dined outside in the middle of August, so it was rather hot. We called and requested a fan, and they brought us one in minutes. The bath products come directly from the spa at the Center for Well-Being, and I always like that I have extra to take home. : ) As for the bed and linens, they are to die for. The pillows are the best. For 5 star dining, Mary Elaine's is quite an unforgettable experience. It boasts one of the top chefs in the Southwest, and the service is unparalleled. Count on having at least 3 to 4 servers throughout your meal, all of whom will address you personally by your name. The view is quite lovely with large windows overlooking the city. It's very romantic, and the menu offers everything from a caviar tasting menu that runs around $500 to the most delicious mushroom risotto I have ever had. Ladies, you even get a little stool for your purse! I highly recommend the brunch here as well. We went on New Year's Day, and it had an amazing array of food. The desserts are wonderful. For cocktails and live music, there is the Terrace. If you just want to hang out and watch the sunset after a round of golf, this is a great place to unwind. In the winter they light the fire pits, so it's a nice place to have drinks. Also, in the evening, be sure to visit the giant telescope for a view of the moon. It's quite amazing, and the nice man (who is extremely knowledgeable) will tell you whatever you want to know about the solar system. My husband loves this guy. We have also seen a celebrity or famous athlete a time or two there, so it is always a fun place to go. They also serve tea by the lobby, and I have always had a lovely experience with girlfriends there. It's a delightful place to do a baby shower or ladies' get-together. The finger sandwiches, the wide selection of teas, and desserts are all top notch! There is usually a live piano player playing right by the lobby too. It creates a nice ambiance along with the gorgeous fountain they have flowing in the center. The spa is nice, but not my favorite in all of Scottsdale. There are places that are newer and better, but it has some nice features. The meditation room is pretty, very relaxing. However, I have had some services that I found to be rather mediocre. This resort is also in a great location. Not only is it nestled right in the heart of Camelback Mountain, but it's minutes away from Scottsdale Fashion Square. This is a really nice mall, and you will also find many great restaurants right at your fingertips. All in all, you will not go wrong with the Phoenician. I have stayed there 3 times and will keep going back!

tripadvisor · 2006-08-17 · 5/5view source

Great Place to Stay at Off-Season Rates! My girlfriends and I booked a 3 night stay in late July at the Phoenician and it did not dissapoint. We chose the Phoenician b/c I got a great rate ($169) and an upgrade by being a Starwood Preferred member, and this was a slightly cheaper rate than the Camelback Inn and the Four Seasons, the other two properties we were looking at. The resort was gorgeous, the views were great, and our upgrade did not dissapoint! I found the bathrooms to be very large and have great amenities, and the bedding was great. Our room had a huge balcony with 2 chaise lounges and a table and two chairs for dining outside. We also each booked spa appointments and the spa was wonderful. I especially enjoyed the meditation room and the tea room, where you have your choice of hot and cold teas and even a complimentary martini glass with fruit salad. I can see how some fixtures in the bathroom (such as the faucets and bidets, etc.) could appear a little dated, but the furniture, bedding, carpet and marble in the bathroom all had a great luxury hotel feel. In addition, the full sized bottles of toiletries and the soft mattress/pillows on the lounge chairs at the pools really were great touches. My only complaint was the price of food. While I would expect dinner or even lunch at the pool to be slightly inflated and didn't mind, I would recommend against eating breakfast in the coffee shop. A bagel and cream cheese (with nothing else) was $5.25 and a bowl of oatmeal was $7.00... the bowl came with nothing but raisins and brown sugar.... But the food all tasted great, I guess it's just the price you pay and we didn't mind since we got a great off-season rate. Would I stay here for $500 a night in the winter? Probably not, since there are great hotels in Mexico and the Caribbean with an ocean for $350-$400 a night... But if you can get a good rate on a shoulder season, it truly is a hotel up there with some great luxury hotels.

tripadvisor · 2006-08-15 · 3/5view source

A Step Above Average We booked a room through American Express Platinum Travel Services the same afternoon we were to check-in and was able to secure a rate of $230USD for a standard room. We arrived at The Phoenician around check-in time and overall check-in was smooth. The public areas of the hotels are immaculately maintained for the time-being but need to be refurbished. Valet was a hit or miss, I always saw two or three of them chatting it up at their valet stand. Some would come over to help you and others you had to be firm to get their attention. When I checked in, the Front Desk agent graciously upgraded me to a premier category room (I was told it was substantially bigger and included a huge patio and overlooked the golf course). When I spoke to Guest Reservations I was told the standard room I booked and the room I was upgraded too goes for in excess of $400 and $700 during HIGH season. Our room was at the end of the hallway in another wing of the hotel (the wing directly across from the valet station). The walk to my room reminded me of a Vegas hotel—long, never ending hallways and it seemed dimly lit. Some of the corner rooms surrounding my room had burnt out light bulbs. The supposedly upgraded room was really bland in its offerings (aesthetic wise, everything looked dated except maybe the TV which isn’t a flat screen) and it seemed the fourth floor where we were staying was a smoking floor?—or at least it reeked of smoke as we were walking in the dimly lit hallway. The room in fact was big: it looked as if you could put two king beds without any problems. I never found anything on TV because their choices in channels are REALLY limited. No MTV, E, etc., but there was HBO. The lighting was horrible; the room relied heavily on table and floor lights. Except in the foyer, there was no ceiling lighting. There was your overpriced minibar as well. There were few “laundry bags” to put your soiled clothes in. The bathroom was acceptable: separate shower/bathtub but again the design was tacky. Not enough bath towels and water pressure in the shower was not that strong. There was a huge blandly furnished patio. It was furnished with those “cheap” plastic/rubberish lounge chairs. It was not inviting to say the least and there was a water build up on the edge of the patio. From what I gather there was not even a light switch for the patio. You had a nice view of the “golf course” if you leaned up against the ledge and turned your head sharply right. Otherwise, we looked at a street leading up to the mountain or something. On a happy note, their beds are really comfortable and in a higher up position instead of being so low. Because we didn’t have a car, we relied heavily on taxis and the sort and when I inquired about the resort having a house car to shuttle us around, I was incorrectly told there was a complimentary house car to shuttle us around Scottsdale. As it turns out the Mercedes R350 “house” cars only shuttle guests around the resort ONLY. As a driver was taking us to the Fashion Square Mall (it was <2 miles), it was while he was driving did I find out that what I thought was a complimentary service in another sedan was in fact a hired driver, needless to say I was ---. It costs $12 (exclusive of gratuities) from the resort to the Fashion Square Mall. It costs $37 from the resort to the Phoenix airport and the ride was like 10-15 minutes. I highly recommend someone in your party being able to rent a car of having access to a car if you decide to come to Phoenix or Scottsdale, etc. because otherwise, the taxi rides will be very expensive. You have to be at least 21 years old to rent a car in the area. The other resort we were previously staying at said that the city’s public transportation is really bad—think: nonexistent. I am not a food connoisseur by any stretch of the imagination, although I don’t mind paying for “haute” cuisine. We decided against dinner at The Terrace (a AAA Four-Diamond rated establishment) instead choosing something from The Ice Cream Parlor—I personally liked this place: basically a deli with ice cream and other desserts (the prices were reasonable compared against where we were staying: $14.95 for a deli sandwich as opposed to $38 for a dinner entrée at The Terrace. I loved the Butter-Pecan ice-cream—couldn’t get enough of it. Breakfast Buffet at The Terrace was $22.95/person and service was just average, and food was average, nothing special. During the entire duration of my meal the potatoes were never replenished. The bacon was sitting in the warmer on a piece of toast and seems to get staler as time passed. If you want to eat “fresh” scrambled eggs, get them through the omelet station. A bottle of wine (small one, mind you) at the mini-bar costs $49. There were other dining establishments on site but I didn’t check them out. The restaurants generally closed after lunch to set up for dinner, so if you need an in between meal, your dining options are very limited. If you want to order something through in-room dining, there is an automatic 22% service charge, plus taxes, and a $4 delivery fee slapped on the entire order which is obscenely expensive but should be expected at a place like this. I didn’t utilize much of the resorts facilities; however, there are “nine” pools at this resort and there is a water slide. I personally wouldn’t pay money to use the cabanas I saw; however, it does offer a shred of privacy. I didn’t see a lot of pool attendants out at 9AM as I would have expected to cater to the needs of the guests. But then again, there were an abundance of chairs, etc; thereby illustrating the resort was not running at capacity; hence, less pool staff were needed. Spa/Fitness facilities—didn’t see them, so I can’t comment. As this is a AAA Five-Diamond rate property, you should, keyword: expect superlative service which is sometimes not on par with other five-diamond properties. It took two hours to deliver a welcome note after speaking to someone from the front-desk. There are only two concierge desks with two people supposedly serving at capacity 600+ rooms. Concierge was unable to get information about cost of a taxi to the airport as opposed to taking the sedans at the hotel ($37 to the airport). While the resorted noted we were celebrating an anniversary, nothing came to us, no amenity. If you are there for a special occasion and nothing comes, call and ASK for it because you deserve it. We called and ½ a bottle of champagne and cookies were sent to our room. Having things sent to your room takes a LONG time. Housekeeping kept knocking at our door despite a DNB sign. As we were departing our room, housekeeping came in and asked us how long we were going to be until we left, we said ten minutes, and ten minutes later as we left the room, the housekeeper was waiting outside and jumped right in to clean our room—it was a really rushed feeling. Check-out was very smooth and efficient. All in all, if you could secure a very good deal during low season, the location is excellent because you are in closer proximity of select attractions. This resort is big so I am sure one could keep themselves occupied if they choose not to leave the resort. The resort is definitely due for a renovation if they want to charge anything in excess of $400+. I didn’t mind paying $230ish but if I paid anything close to $700+ for the room I was staying in, I would be absolutely livid. If the property did an absolute makeover of guest rooms, tasteful at that, then it may warrant paying such rates—which I don’t mind paying if it is consistent with its offerings.

tripadvisor · 2006-07-06 · 5/5view source

Relaxation and Utter Indulgence at the Phoenician My husband and I spent six relaxing days at the Phoenician this June. He was there for business, I for pleasure, and both of us to celebrate our wedding anniversary. I emailed the resort to tell them it was our anniversary, ask for a room upgrade, and make dinner reservations. When we arrived at the resort we had been upgraded to a Junior Suite in the Canyon Building. The Canyon Building is above the center of the resort and very private. We never ventured to any of the other pools or buildings, other than for dinner at Windows on the Green. Staying there was the way to go for a couple looking for relaxation and quiet. Our suite was spacious, bright, and airy. There is an honor bar and fridge which we promptly filled with our own beer, water, and snacks from a local Safeway. The price of the food and drink in the honor bar was outrageous. We’re talking a $14 bottle of airplane sized vodka. Really. The bathroom was beautiful and the bed was like a dream. I can see where the dated comments regarding the furnishings come from. It wasn’t obvious until you looked a little closer, but there were some nicks in the wood and scratches on the glass. It wasn’t a big concern to me, but if I had paid the peak season price of $2500 a night for one of these suites I would have wanted absolute perfection. It wouldn’t take much to update and I’m sure it’s in the future of the resort. The Canyon pool was the absolute best. No kids. On weekdays, at its most crowded, there were maybe 10 of us there. It was wonderfully relaxing and the pitchers of ice water were a very necessary nice touch. I was hot like I’ve never been hot before in my life! Spending the days on the padded loungers reading the USA Today delivered to my room each morning was as close to perfection as it gets. I ate lunch by the pool most days. Everything was overpriced, but fine. Nothing spectacular, but it required no effort on my part, so it worked for me. Being tucked down in the valley of Camelback Mountain provided absolutely amazing scenery. The pools are all open 24 hours a day and a night swim was the ideal way to unwind before bed. Unfortunately, we were unaware there was a spa just a few steps away from the Canyon pool. It’s in a pretty little spot nestled in the desert. The room was replenished each day and the turn down service was lovely to come home in the evening to. Every employee we came in contact with greeted us with a smile and a kind word. A great majority of them seemed to be college kids. The food and service at Windows on the Green was top notch. We received a complimentary toast and dessert for our anniversary. We ordered room service at 2:00 a.m. and they were the most expensive and delicious cheese burgers I’ve ever had! We had the Canyon building’s concierge call us cars any time we needed to get somewhere and rides ranged from $12 - $40. Into Old Town was $12, out to the airport was $40, and the in between. We had an amazing time. It was about nothing more than relaxation and indulgence. I would lay by the pool all day, go to the room and take a bubble bath in the marble Jacuzzi tub, and nap in a giant fluffy bed…I was so spoiled. It’s tough to be back in the real world again. I would stay at the Phoenician again in the off-season. The lower rates make it well worth it. I’d think twice about in-season rates because it costs money just to breathe there. If you’re in the mood to treat yourself, I’m sure you’ll be spoiled by the Phoenician, too!

Nice resort Our first impression of the hotel was that our room was huge. I think it must have been oversized, because it was closer to 800 sq feet and then a 300 ft patio/balcony with a retractable awning! We were quite impressed. I was very impressed by the service at this spa. The golf course is amazing. It's just beautiful, as it winds around the mt. The only complaint I had was about the pool decks. There was simply not enough room to accomodate the guests poolside. With the 3 pool decks, we should not have had to walk around 3 times at 2pm to find two chairs. tripadvisor · 2006-04-21 · 2/5view source

Catch a Falling Star! Here's the summary in a nutshell. If you are from the Phoenix area, and you want to spend time at a hotel that will completely make you forget you are in Arizona, the Phoenician is your dream come true. Landscaped gardens, massive swimming pools, soaring palm trees and more green grass than you can shake a stick it. Just don't shake a rain stick, because anything else remotely native Arizonan is relegated to a minor role at this property that is more suited to the beaches of Maui than to the Arizona desert. If you're coming to Arizona on vacation, and want to actually feel like you're in the desert, and enjoy some desert culture, run like the wind to another property. Don't get me wrong. Many folks will probably love the Phoenician. It has a commanding location at the base of Camelback Mountain. It has a spa, golf courses and fine restaurants (more on that later). If you like shopping, Scottsdale is just down the street. If you like to see and be seen, look no further. Cash in your Starpoints now. Want some peace and quiet? Steer clear of the lobby. The fountains are so loud you'll have a tough time hearing the cover band, much less getting the attention of a cocktail waitress. Want to take a quiet, peaceful late night stroll on the grounds? Hope you like the Rippingtons. Want to sleep in on easter sunday morning? The Phoenician has a very unique wakeup call. It's called gardeners with leaf-blowers. Yes, on easter sunday morning at 9 am. It took three calls to the service desk to get them to leave 90-minutes later, and not before they had blown dust over every car parked near the casitas. I guess having clean grounds is more important than having the guests have clean cars. (see photo). That's probably the part that really eats me about the Phoenician. It has so many things going for it, but to truly be a first-class five-star resort, the can-do, guest-first attitude has to permeate to every employee on the property. It means nothing to have a doorman great every guest in the lobby when you have irresponsible gardeners and stuffy cocktail waitresses. And then there is the front desk staff. If you take the room you are assigned, they will be the most pleasant folks you've ever met. Just don't try to make any changes. Since we were staying at the hotel for five nights, and we were Starwood Platinum Members, we wanted to ensure a comfortable room for five days. Being our 10th anniversary, I requested a room with a king bed. Instead I got a casita with two double beds. When I requested to change to a king bed, I was relegated to a ground level casita with a breathtaking view of a brick wall. The dark stuffy room wasn't going to work for five days, so I returned to the front desk and requested to see a room that actually had a view and perhaps was in sight of a cactus. The room was a major downgrade, and I would've taken it if it wasn't for the fact that someone had smoked in it. When I asked if they could ionize the room, I was told it would take 90 minutes (fair enough), and so I inquired about if they could transfer my luggage from my original room to the new one when it was ready. You would've thought I asked the front desk staff to club a baby seal on the head with a big mallet. After a minute of blank stares and raised eyebrows, they finally demured and graciously, well, not so graciously, offered to have someone deliver my bags to the new room. If this is how they treat the hotel chain's best guests, I shutter at how they would sneer at a someone with mere mortal hotel status. The casitas are a slight improvement over your typical apartment complex. If you can overlook the fact that the rooms are pushing 30 years old, they are, as other reviewers have written, tired. The carpeting is worn and stained in areas. There is not a single comfortable chair in the room. No sofa, no leather chair or ottoman. Just two desk chairs and your beds. The beds are extremely comfortable, the best part of the stay. The marble bathrooms are nice. Marble never gets worn and tired. There are no in-room coffee makers, but room service will gladly set one up for you for a daily fee. If you want a room with a cactus view, you'll have to settle for the main tower facing the back side of the hotel, where there is a cactus garden at the base of Camelback Mountain. The Easter Brunch was delicious and the presentation was masterful. The chefs should be applauded on their creativity and culinary skills. The food was superb, as was my bill. Easter Brunch for two was a world-record $217 including tax and mandatory tip. It wasn't the food that dissapointed, it was the service. Twice I had to ask the wait staff to clear my plate when I returned from the buffet, and more than twice I had to ask for my beverage to be refilled. Once again, the wait staff seemed more interested in checking out how much of a tip the table behind us left, then they were in making sure our coffee was warm. For $217 you'd think that they would brew the coffee right there at the table. In fact, for $217, I'd expect Juan Valdez himself to walk by with his donkey and pour my coffee personally. I don't eat much, and frankly I didn't expect much, but I figure each strawberry I ate cost about $4, so the least they could do is pick up my plate on their way to deposit their tips at the bank. I'm being a little tongue in cheek here but only slightly. Honestly I was hoping to rave about the Phoenician. I talked about it for weeks before I left. I was heading to Arizona to unwind on a spa vacation. Now I'm still talking about it. Maybe if you went with low expectations you'd be more pleased. I remember Starwood telling me that the Phoenician is their best resort in Arizona. I'd really beg to differ. On so many different levels, the other properties are executing world-class service while many at the Phoenician seems content to rest on their laurels. Speaking of resting on laurels, watch where you step at the spa. After our leaf-blowing wake up call and $5 raspberries, we decided to check out the spa, the other reason that we came to the legendary Phoenician. I thought for sure the spa would blow my mind and make all the other experiences uneventful. The spa did blow my mind, but not in the way you might expect. I was expecting world class. We walked into the main spa lobby to inquire about using the facilities for the day and booking some appointments. There were four people in line in front of us, and the desk was being run by a young lady probably twenty years old. She was stressed out because the kind people at the front of the line were taking quite a while to decide what type of services to book, while the line was growing longer and longer behind them. Her stress level was so high that it just permeated the room. Not the way you want to kick off your $200 Reiki Chakra Balancing. Undeterred, we waited. She eventually summonsed some help, and the line started moving, but the entrance had the peaceful mystique of a bus station. The facilities were underwhelming to say the least. The spa is truly tired. The tile floors were dingy, if not dirty. The jacuzzi in the men's lounge was directly between the locker area and the toilets, right in the main thoroughfare. It was so crowded, with lots of little kids too, I can't imagine how anyone could find the spa and steam room facilities relaxing. There is a decent meditation room and the fitness center is modern. For the prices they charge, you think they could invest a fraction of it into keeping the facilities clean, peaceful and up to date. Nearly every review I googled on the spa mentions that it is tired, and it truly is. If they are not willing to invest in improving the spa while charging top dollar for services, I suggest you invest elsewhere as well. They may have the best spa staff in the world, but it'd be like getting a world-class massage at a 24-Hour Fitness. I've seen YMCA's with nicer locker room facilities honestly. Now again I know, some folks will find the spa inviting. This review isn't for you. This is for the Starwood people who have been around the world and seen truly world-class spas at the St Regis in Dana Point, at the former Orchid on the Big Island, even at the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass in nearby Chandler who's spa makes the Phoenician's look like a condo-complex recreation room. I must credit the hotel on a few items. First, they did offer to have a bellman come to our room and take our car for a complimentary carwash. Granted that was after three calls and more than a few other rooms complaining about the blowing dirt, and at the end of the day, I didn't want to trust my new sedan to a hotel that didn't have enough respect for me not to blow dirt on my car in the first place. And second, they were kind enough to let us check out early without a fee for doing so, probably because they realized that this review would've been twice as long had we stayed! Obviously from the reviews, there are many people who loved this resort. There are some tremendous things about it. It's just that if you don't get the basics right, if you don't excel at the little things, than the bigger things become less meaningful. You're only as good as your weakest links, and if you brag about your 5-Diamond Service on your website, you need to back it up. As we drove down the long boulevard from the hotel, with the sun setting on Camelback Mountain and the dirt billowing off our windshield as we passed the beautiful fountains, we made tracks for the brand new Sheraton Wild Horse Pass instead. And how did we, the cynical, difficult, frustrated hotel guests fare down there? You'll just have to click over there to find out. But I'll give you a hint. If there is any justice in the world, the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass will pick up one of the Phoenician's famous five stars in the coming year.

Horrible Spa Experience My mother in law loves the Phoenician and gave me a b'day gift certificate to the Spa. Having recently moved to AZ from California I was excited to try a decadent treatment but proceeded to get lost on the drive over. The Map quest directions were wrong and about 20 minutes before the appt. I called for directions and found out that I was on the right track and 10 minutes away. I checked in over the phone to save time and was told that I would receive the full treatment time of 90 minutes. I was understandbly rushed into the changing area. However no one did a client in-take in regard to contraindications, medications or health concerns etc. I received a frown when I asked to use the bathroom. Then I was led to my spa room and as the esthetician began the treatment. She chided me for having on makeup (I hadn't come from home.) After removing it and begining the treatment she tells me that she will have to take 20 minutes off of my treatment time and that I would be charged for the full amount. Which I didn't understand as I wasn't 20 minutes late. Cleansing is included in any treatment time and there should be two cleansings one to remove makeup and one to clean your skin. She then said that perhaps I should just reschedule and got me off the table and led me in my bathrobe to the front desk where other clothed guests were checking in. There I was told that I would be accessed a charge for not giving a 24 hour cancellation notice! I think that it was 20%. The surly upfront girl of about 17 then offered me appointments that were in the evening during the weekday and the soonest was more than a week away. Finally it was determined that I should just choose a 60 minute spa service and I was trotted back to the spa room where I received a decent but not fabulous facial treatment. Afterward I used jacuzzi and the Scotchhose in the shower room and found the shower tiles cracked and fallen out. I thought the spa looked old and rather dated but somewhat charming. Not $200 treatment charming however. I filled out the customer service card and never heard from anyone. I will never go back to the spa at the Phoenician again. I have however gone there for lunch. The hostess was friendly and talkative and commented to us that management made many demands of them. The waitress looked a bit harried and over-worked and brought the wrong food over. Best hotel in the area Went to Phoenix and Scottsdale for a 4 day quick trip. Stayed at a private home, but spent two days touring all the hotels in both Phoenix and Scottsdale. Result: #1 place to stay - Phoenician - beautiful resort hotel. Had lunch here and service was exactly like Four Seasons. Asked our name when we arrived and then addressed us by our name throughout the meal even after knowing we weren't staying at the resort. This may be important to some people, but this is the only resort that has grass and flowers. Phoenix and Scottsdale (other than golf courses) are flat, dusty, and the color brown. If you like shades of brown with no color than Arizona is your kind of place. So it was nice to enter a resort that actually had color in both grass and flowers. Pool area luxurious. #2 place to stay - Hyatt Regency at Gainey Ranch - for a large hotel, felt "homey". Pool area had double cushion lounge chairs for couples. Grounds very pretty - not as nice as the Phoenician, but still very nice. Would not recommend The Boulders. Too far from anything and frankly - just blah. Small pool. Liked the big boulders to look at, but after an hour we'd had enough. Spa at the entrance of a gated area - not with the hotel. Would not recommend JW Marriott Camelback Inn. Outdated and just bland. JW Marriott Desert Ridge is definitely a corporate hotel. Large, plain, lobby nice, that is about it..nothing special...but for a free stay on the company dime...not too shabby. If your not with a business group, you will be disappointed. Overall, unless you golf or love art, I'd skip Phoenix/Scottsdale all together. Nothing to do, will be bored. For the money, go to Cabo, Santa Barbara, Las Vegas, etc.

Great spot for hiking and pool lounging. Just back from a weekend at the phoenician. We stayed in a suite near the 'sunset spa' and had the hot tub and the pool to ourselves all weekend. I am not a resort person but this is a great place to relax by the pool and have rum drinks and good food delivered to your chaise lounge. We enjoyed hiking to the top of Camelback mountain (map is in your room). My husband thought it would be some sort of paved trail for old folks but it was indeed a really challenging climb. There are all sorts of tubs and showers to relax in after a massage or hike, too. Worth every penny. Also: the staff was over-the-top professional, down to the lawn crew. Great resort to relax in My husband and I stayed there for my birthday. We used our starwood points to get 50% off rack rate so it was a good deal. Service was wonderful. Great escape from Florida's hurricane My husband and I had an upgrade from a standard no view room to a quiet casita overlooking mountain, pool, and laguna. We did not have a car and so stayed on the resort for our entire 3days stay. We played tennis, laid by the pool, and hiked up Camel Back mountain. With the resort being so large, you can always find something new to see or do. The mountain hike is within walking distance from the hotel and it was a beautiful but yet challenging hike to the top. Though dining is 30-40% more than what we would pay at off-site restaurants, the food was great. No complaints about the food quality at the Terrace, the pool Oasis, or the Windows on the Green. One night, we ordered a delicious oven-roasted pizza to share and the room service guy set up a romantic table-clothed dinner for us on our patio (including a red rose). tripadvisor · 2005-08-29 · 4/5view source

Worth almost every penny! My husband and I were forced to make an emergency stopover in Phoenix due to unexpected illness after a trip to Mexico. I asked the cabbie to take us to the closest 5 star. He recommended the Four Seasons above the Phoenician but it was too far away. As we pulled into the Phoenician’s grounds after a 15 minute ride, even my husband who was extremely ill commented that he was happy with the choice. The Lobby doubles as a restaurant with view and has a large lit fountain at night with a sole pianist which lends great ambiance to the place. Check-in was effortless and quick, and we were presented with a number of room choices. I chose the golf view with King bed, which was the priciest. It was on the second of four floors, and was actually more of a croquet/pool view. We were pleasantly surprised with the room quality as we entered. Two adequate closets flank a more than adequate mini bar, which contained a multitude of drinks and snacks, tanning essentials and a souvenir or two. They do not have ice machines in plain view so you have to call concierge for that, but they are relatively prompt. The marble bathrooms are quite spectacular- very spacious with two sinks and a large soaker tub, larger than average toiletries from the spa, and enough towels. My husband commented that he liked the shower gels and shampoo and he normally couldn’t care less about that stuff. There is also a marble shower with excellent water pressure for a very relaxing shower. The toilet is separate, and the entire bathroom was immaculately clean. The bed and pillows were extremely soft and comfortable and there were a variety of pillows available. The adjacent couch, coffee table and desk were well appointed. There were four great magazines for us- Travel and Leisure was among them. There was above average quality stationary along with an internet connection for laptops. We paid 19.99 for 24 hours of internet usage and it was well worth it, since my husband was laid up in bed- we could book our plane tickets home without having to leave our room. The TV was a newer and larger version than what we you’d normally see at a hotel. The dresser could have held more clothing than anyone could bring. The patio was large and had a table and chairs and a lawn chair for tanning. The room was great. It wasn’t the best we’ve been in but it wasn’t far behind. The best part of this hotel is the service. The concierge did everything they could to make our stay enjoyable and comfortable, and the front desk graciously extended our check out till 5 pm for a hundred dollar charge- it should have been 250.00, as it’s normally 50 dollars per hour after 12 pm. The staff were all extremely accommodating (at about midnight we were able to have someone from housekeeping come and change our bedding because my husband had finished sweating out his fever.) The following day I went to the salon with a special request and they were great about meeting it. We prearranged our bell service and airport transportation and it was carried off with zero glitches. The pools are on a series of different levels, they’re all great, but a little overcrowded- there are enough padded chaise lounges and to accommodate the crowds however, and enough umbrellas that each couple can share one. There are about 3 large hot tubs and lots of cabanas. Attendants lay out towels for the guests, and menus for the poolside café are on about every third chair. There are a lot of little kids, but they’re not half as bothersome as the many college kids. The clientele had to be the one of the cons to this hotel. Lots of pretentious women walking around the poolside in high heels. The food wasn’t notable either. We paid 40 bucks for room service to bring us pancakes and a bowl of cereal, and they got the order wrong. The hotel has a little shopping corridor near the lobby that is quite impressive. From souvenirs, books and cards to sundries, men’s and women’s casual and more formal wear, sleepwear and swimwear, floral and gifts, they’ve got it all in one of about ten shops. There is even a little café there where you can have coffee and lighter fare, although the service there is mediocre compared to the rest of the hotel. We didn’t get a chance to use the spa or golf centre since we were only there for about 24 hours. We are definitely planning to go back though…unless we go to the Four Seasons instead!

Phenomenal Phoenician This is absolutely the best hotel we have been to in a long time. In short, i have not found a better hotel looking at the value for money you get from The Phoenician. tripadvisor · 2005-06-18 · 5/5view source

Lived up to expectations We spent a week at the Phonecian and left without any major complaints. The hotel is expensive if you pay rack rate but who pays rack rate when good deals are so easy to get. The setting is excellent - we loved the cactus garden. It is not the ideal hotel for those who want to sit by the pool all day and order a cheap pizza in the evening. The extra do add up (no more than in any other five star hotel), but with a bit of thought you can keep them to a reasonable level. For instance valet parking is expensive ($25?) but why not self park in the underground car park for free ? The hotel lacks an every-day dining option, on the other hand the food in the Terrace restaurant was very good, both for evening meal and breakfast. Not cheap, but good quality - and there are plenty of good restaurants in Scottsdale. The room was in excellent decorative order, and everything worked as it should. Housekeeping was polite, efficient and attentive. The rooms are large, and suitable for comfortable long stays. The pools can fill up a little , especially when the hotel is full, and, yes, they do allow children to swim in them ! The pool staff do not clear towels away, and on busy days all the loungers were 'reserved' before 9am. Don't come here just for the pool, but do come if you want an excellent hotel with a good pool. I suspect some of the negative reviews come from conference goers who need to keep the extras down and would not have chosen this type of hotel for their own holiday. If you are paying your own way the good news is that the hotel is big enough to absorb conferences without making any facilities in to no-go areas for regular guests. We would return, and rank it in our top 10.

The meditation room was comfortable but not great. (i recently went to the Boca Raton Hotel spa - now that is a nice spa!) The grounds at the Phoenician were perfect - flowers of all colors, bunnies hopping around the landscape, fountains and big lawns,. The food is pricely but pretty good. Rooms are a nice size. Bathrooms are very big - but the "two person soaking tub" is not for 2 people! Maybe 2 children. Oh the "9" pools at the Phoenician - that includes a few small kiddie pools. All pools had more kids than adults in them. THey were heated though! The big jacuzzi had so many children in it that we couldnt get into it. We went during teh Easter holiday so maybe that is why there were so many children. Got to the pool on Sat at 11.30 am and could not get a lounge chair. The hotel started to put chairs in the lawn away form the pool, so i was lucky enough to get one. On thur and Fri - the pool was quieter and much more appealing. Service by the pool was great, except for Sat. People waited an hour for their food. Ask for a room facing the pool area for the best views. We faced the mountain - so close to the mountain, that the room was dark. Housekeeping was very good. Our refrigerator was broken but it was stocked with many many things. Restaurant at the golf course was good. The main dining room - Terrace - wasnt as good. But everyone who worked at the hotel was soooooo extremely friendly. I will go back - one day when i have a family. If you go with kids, bring balls, frisbees, etc, b/c there are many big lawns to run around in. The hotel provideds balls too. There is a volleyball court and bball net in the pool.

tripadvisor · 2004-09-18 · 5/5view source

A Fine Resort I enjoyed a long weekend at the Phoenician Resort and was most impressed with the lovely surroundings and fine service. I was situated in the Canyon Building-- a hotel within the hotel with its own spererate lobby and concierge staff. The pool was quiet and relaxing, with classical music playing in the background. Unlike the rest of the resort which can feel crowded and noisy, this wing was a most welcomed escape of tranquility. Service at the resort was superb with good name recognition and the valet would have my car brought to the drive faster than I could get from my room to the lobby. Be prepared to pay extra for everything--from the gym to parking--but the experience was excellent and I would gladly return.

tripadvisor · 2004-09-07 · 3/5view source

Good but not great We stayed for 7 days at the Phoenician during the last week of August. Positives: -Rooms are big, well appointed and clean. Ask for a 1 bedroom casita type room. They are over 600 sqft and include huge bathrooms and terraces as well as dsl, 32" tvs and other great features. -Staff is very professional, friendly and for the most part go out of their way to please. Everyone from the pool crew to the cleaning crew were superb. - Parking was free when you stay in a casita type room as you can park right under it. -Offseason rates (july-aug) are hard to beat. -Location is very convenient to the best shopping and dining in Phoenix. Negatives: -Resort is very big. It either feels empty and depressing or crowded and hectic depending on whether its empty of pretty booked. -Tel calls from room (which we never make except for this once) include an initial $24 charge! -Gym has a $20 per day fee though most of the time we got in for free. -The restaurants serve decent food though none have any local cuisine or uniqueness to them. -The resort feels very tired and very 80s which might not be of your liking. -Lobby and main building areas feel like you are in Las Vegas. -Pools are not salt water. -Can get very noisey at times between the kids, the music which is constantly blaring out from pool-side speakers (you can turn the music down/off by turning button) and the constant grounds crew sawing and cutting. Conclusion: If you are less than 40 stay at the Four Seasons in Troon North. If you are over 40 or have more than one child, stay here.

tripadvisor · 2004-05-26 · 5/5view source

My best stay, ever Absolute opulence. Amazing room with outstanding amenities. I had torn my pants. At the concierge's urging, I left them on the bed, and ran to my meeting. When I returned two hours later, the pair of pants was on a hanger in my room, pressed and mended. No charge. MaryElaine's is a very classy atmosphere. 5* experience throughout. Great golf as well.

tripadvisor · 2004-04-14 · 3/5view source

Wake up early to get a place to sit at the pool Spent Easter weekend here (4 nights) in Room 3123, the cheapest level room at US$395 per night. It overlooked the entry garden which was fine but was near an exhaust that nearly knocked me out with a gas smell each time I used the terrace. I was honestly nervous to spend much time outside on the terrace. Good room in size and furnishings, staff did well, a bit stressed at the restaurant, great concierge, outrageous US$26 per day to park and the only place I paid to park in all of the trip. Nice pool grounds but very poor system. Signage says the pool service is open at 9 a.m. I believed them and relaxed my first morning and had breakfast and headed to the pool just prior to 9 a.m. Too late, no chairs left - it looked like a factory with rows and rows of chairs at all pools, even extending on the lawn outside of the pool fence. Not very nice for the price. System is first come, first served and I suggest you get there by 7:15 a.m. when I found the pickings acceptable the next day (amazing - no one sleeps late at this hotel but newspaper comes late). You must return before 10 a.m. or you lose your chair but I noted hotel staff were shy to do this when people left personal items (paperback book, suntan lotion) on the chair and ignored the rule and wandering guests in search of chairs. It is quite amusing to watch the high paying guests who return after 10 a.m. find their chairs are taken by other high paying guests. Pool staff feign ignorance and the guests argue and nearly get into fist fights. A bit of action at a seemingly tranquil spot. There is a Tranquility pool where no music, sports or cell phones are allowed, but the hotel hired a cheesy wedding band to play above the pool and I could not hear the conversation of my partner in the next chair without shouting. Another kind guests gave the band US$300 to stop playing for a couple of hours. Hotel is close to shopping. I liked it, food good and staff try but for their prices, there are no excuses. I would consider returning but would likely prefer to try someplace else that may pay more attention to service and details. Lovely grounds, great spa, service that tries hard but cannot always win due to understaffing, tacky pool chair procedure, need to tip everyone everywhere to get any service. Good to consider, worth visiting the grounds, but think two and three times before booking. Also, I wondered how the people whose terraces overlooked the always busy motor entry felt - no privacy and noise, lights and busy activities at all hours - I felt lucky that I could close my terrace door and ignore the gas fumes.

tripadvisor · 2004-01-20 · 5/5view source

Terrific place to relax! Just returned from a 4 day holiday weekend at the Phoenician. We stayed in the Canyon Building in suite 8221..the ground floor. This is our favorite buidling to stay in at this resort since we love the lobby with its fireplace and view of the magnificient waterfall outside the doors. The Canyon building has its own pool area with a wonderful large, scenic and private hot tub and the best cabannas on the property. The staff was unceasingly friendly and helpful whereever we went on the resort grounds. The Center For Well Being was used extensively by us and we enjoyed the massages, facials and time to relax in the meditation room with the wonderful waterful and lounge chairs. The only spa service not up to par was the spa pedicure which had me sitting in a chair with my feet in a bowl of water. A massage chair with bubbling foot area is the more luxurious and usual setup for an $80 treatment of this sort. Other than that, we loved the workout room...the grounds were glorious with all the flowering plants and cactus gardens...the food both at the pools and the restaurants was outstanding. The most relaxing aspect of walking around and enjoying the resort were the many waterfalls they had everywhere... For children, they have a childrens program 7 days a week, several kiddie pools and a slide that all would enjoy. All in all...a wonderful vacation.

tripadvisor · 2004-01-06 · 4/5view source

Beautiful, but service needs help We stayed at the Phoenician for 2 days over the New Years. We have seen some of the other resorts in Scottsdale and felt that the scenery and layout is much more appealing than the others. However, service was not, in our opinion, up to par for a luxury resort. The front desk staff seemed clueless. They struggled with check in, never did call us, as promised, once our room was ready, never let baggage valet know to have our luggage brought up, struggled with check out, etc. We had to constantly call for requests that we shouldn't have had to make. On the other hand, The Oasis restaurant staff was very friendly, we loved the Thirsty Camel lounge with its indoor and outdoor setting and enjoyed the Center for Wellness spa.

(4/5) · I'm receiving an important award soon and to thank the wonderful people who supported my nomination and helped me to get selected, I wanted to do something nice for the elders in my life. My culture teaches about respecting my elders, so organizing an afternoon tea here for them as a token of my gratitude felt like the right thing to do. Afternoon tea seating is from 2-3pm. A pianist is scheduled between 3-5pm. Some of us arrived around 2:40pm for a 3pm reservation and pianist was already playing. The lobby of The Phoenician is beautiful and classy. I'd definitely come back again and have a drink at the bar, enjoy the ambiance and people watch. To the right of the lobby, that is where you check in with the hostess. We had a party of 12 (I reserved for 11), and the hostess's response to me wasn't the response I was expecting honestly. She said let me check if we can accommodate your one extra person. I was thinking to myself, "you gonna turn away a party of 12 because of one extra person?" You're gonna lose out on a decent amount of business, but ok, up to you. She was able to accommodate our one extra person in and led us to our table. To be honest. I didnt quite like that two seats were placed on the two ends of the table, felt a bit cramped. I've only seen one seat usually at each end of a long table. The afternoon tea area also felt a bit cramped, but the views were lovely of the balcony and outside. There's a summer special for afternoon tea, so it brought the cost down to a little under $100/person before taxes and gratuity. Also note they have very strict no show policy. If people in your party don't show, it's a $35 fee/person. You can choose from a variety of teas and I got the coconut one, which was lovely. I enjoyed it! I love anything with coconut! Then the finger sandwiches kept coming, first a few showed up in the first course and then more! Then, there were scones and the Devonshire cream was lovely. Last course was an assortment of small, cute and delicious desserts on a plate. The food and tea were delicious and everyone seemed to enjoy and many of us were so stuffed we needed to take home the tray of small desserts. I guess my only suggestion to the hotel would be to have all the options plated on a tiered tray where people could choose from any of the above options all together vs being served in courses. Service was attentive and friendly. Definitely would be a spot I would come back to for a special occasion!

She then received a phone call that she took and spoke for 15 minutes next to the pool with her back turned to the chair. At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. When she turned back around and realized her things were gone she immediately alerted the staff including waitresses and the towel clerk who had been working the area. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, "I am sorry maam, there is nothing we can do." Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items. We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $2K+ at Neiman Marcus just down the street, so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. There was one gentleman that worked the hotel security, I believe his name was Thomas, and he was the only one that took any ownership of the issue and showed an ounce of empathy towards our predicament. The extent of effort from the rest of management at the Phoenician was to blink, stand still and continue to say "I am sorry, there is nothing we can do." One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, "Things get stolen here all the time" as if they had as much control over this as the weather. Further, if that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority. Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant ($500+) but not catastrophic. I can hear the critics whispering, "first world problems." The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can't list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property. We were waived through, never asked for a name or room number. If I was a thief I couldn't ask for a more vulnerable environment. Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? Less than five we thought. We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, "I am sorry, we can't track that." How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff "If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately." With today's tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests. We were routed to some off-sight Marriott risk assessor that did not respond to us for three weeks only to tell us "our investigation results in no compensation to the guest." I can only imagine the depths they went into that investigation. Moral of the Story: Don't take anything valuable to the pool Second Moral of the Story: Don't rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do.

Violet D. (5/5) · Where do I even begin. We stayed for the 4th of July weekend in this gorgeous resort and had the time of our lives. We stayed at the Canyon Suites and had a beautiful balcony facing the resort entrance and in the back was the most glorious cactus garden I have ever seen. Not to mention we were right next to the Camelback mountain. Just WOW! Breakfast is served from 6:30 am which is wonderful as most places start much later than that. We would start off our days downstairs eating some yummy food, then we would head to the pool area or shall I say "pools" there were so many different pools at the resort it was almost like being in a candy store. We hopped from one to the other. Also they have a fun waterslide which made us feel like kids again and a fun bar for the 21+ folks by the adult pools. In the evenings we enjoyed a glass of wine in their bubbly hot tub ( sooo relaxing). We really wanted to make the most of our time at the resort and booked spa sessions & nails (our masseuses and nail technicians were perfectionists and made us feel like gold after our treatments), tennis court time (which should be booked in advance) and golfed in their drop dead gorgeous golf corse. Everything was unbelievable, the service and care we received made us feel on top of the world. This place is worth every dime. Also we had talented musicians performing by the Thirsty Camel bar in the lobby area where we danced the night away, they have awesome cheese and meat plates, the gin fizz was perfect and so refreshing. If you go to this resort make sure to take full advantage of all the things it has to offer. The location is amazing and so close to old Scottsdale which is full of old fashioned bars and restaurants. Really takes you back in time! Thank you to the Phoenician and their staff for being so wonderful to us! You can really feel the dedication and job each one of you has in being a part of peoples' time spent in the resort. The Phoenician must be one of the nicest hotels in town. We used Starwood points to book our room (The Phoenician is in the Luxury Collection) and thought this hotel offered excellent value. We stayed two nights in a beautiful room with a comfortable bed and an attractive bathroom. We hung by the pool, drank at the hotel bar, and had an all-around lovely resort experience. The pool was nice, nothing elaborate but very pretty, and I was impressed with the food and service we got from the comfort of our lounge chairs. I had a salad with spice-encrusted ahi tuna, watermelon, jicama, navel orange, cucumber, and baby field greens in a sweet chili vinaigrette--like a legitimate quality restaurant salad. My husband's cheeseburger was also tasty. We also had good drinking, both at the pool and the bar, where we were able to use drink tickets that came complimentary with our Starwood reservation. We had Four Peaks pale ale and a solid Bloody Mary at the pool, and nice cocktails inside. I enjoyed a Prickly-Peño Margarita with tequila, lime juice, Cointreau, orange juice, and a jalapeño-prickly pear syrup. The Single-Barrel Mojito and the Lychee-Jito were also great. Parking was free and easy, and service was pleasant all around. I only wish we'd had more time to hang out. Two days was just not enough time to do all the relaxing we wanted at The Phoenician. We'll have to come back again next year.

Chris C. (5/5) · I've stayed at several Starwood properties in the greater Phoenix area (Westin Kierland Villas, W Scottsdale, Four Points Tempe) and the overall experience at the Phoenician tops them all. The service was top notch, breakfasts on site were great, and we had a blast at the pools. The overall décor seemed a bit dated (or at least not my stle), but that didn't distract from the overall experience. LOCATION: Located less than 10 minutes from Old Town Scottsdale and Scottsdale Fashion Square (shopping, eating, and drinking), the Phoenician is a great home base for a trip to the desert. If you're in town for Spring Training, the Phoenician offers free shuttle service to the Giants games with Salt River Fields (D'Backs and Rockies) less than 20 minutes away and a host of other teams within a reasonable drive. ROOM: We stayed in Casita "A" in Room 7103 for three nights. We were on the ground floor and our sliding glass doors opened up onto a patio overlooking the large lawn and the Necklace Lake. We had a king bed and a rollaway bed for aC. The bathroom was spacious with a separate shower and tub. There was a small nook in the hall area with a coffee maker, waters, etc. Even with the addition of the rollaway bed, there was plenty of space for two adults and child to move around, hang out, and not feel cramped. It was a great setup for a family as aC could walk right out to play on the lawn and we were a very short walk from the various pools. If you have kids, I'd opt for a ground floor Casita room rather than an upstairs unit. Parking was available right outside the Casita, which made getting around a breeze. I didn't feel like we missed out on anything by not being in the main building. RESORT: First of all, the service from the front desk to the pool to the restaurant was fantastic every step of the way. Everyone was friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome. This is the kind of service every hotel should have. We spent a lot of time at the gorgeous pools and on the waterslide, and aC joined the other kids on the property running back and forth trying not to fall off the floating mats (which I like to think of as "Wipeout Jr."). The Surge splash area hadn't yet opened, but we could tell that it would've been a great hangout for little kids. The only possible thing that was missing was a lazy river (like at the Westin Kierland) but there was still plenty to do at the pools here. Finding chairs to lounge in was not an issue. While we never dropped aC off the Funician Kids Club, we did take her to Hoppy Hour where she was able to pick up a stuffed animal bunny, which is a great souvenir and reminder of our time at the Phoenician. SPG PLATINUM: This was my 50th stay (not nights but stays) at a Starwood property, and we were welcomed to our room by a cheese plate, bottles of Voss water, a Phoenician beach/pool bag, pool toys, and goggles. Given that this was a family trip, they couldn't have chosen a better way to greet us and aC was very excited about all the "presents." We didn't have to pay a resort fee or for anything other than the drinks we ordered at the pool. We had the full run of the breakfast buffet (pastries, fruit, meats, smoothies, omelet bar, etc.) every morning and we were never once charged (contrast with some Starwoods where you only get a continental breakfast).

Veronica P. (4/5) · The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Hotel in the Starwood family, is somewhat oddly located in the Scottsdale area. Fairly close to Old Town Scottsdale and the Scottsdale Fashion Square. The Phoenician is away from many other resorts in Scottsdale, but does have a great location in that it hugs the south side of Camelback Mountain. As you enter the property, you will encounter a guard gate. You will merely be asked if you are checking into the hotel, there for dinner, to play golf, etc. and pointed towards the appropriate parking area. The Phoenician offers valet parking, of course, or complimentary covered self-parking. If entering through the self-parking garage, you will take the elevator or escalator to the third floor in order to check-in. Check-in was smooth, and all SPG Gold amenities were explained. Since there is a resort fee of $29 per day, which includes internet, I chose the extra 250 points as my amenity. Although the hotel was probably not more than 30% occupied, I did not get an upgrade. I was able to book my room by finding a Better Rate Guarantee, which netted me an extra 2,000 Starpoints so all was not lost. Rooms at The Phoenician are fairly large by most standards, measuring approximately 600 square feet. The Grand Deluxe King Room overlooks the pool areas. There is a balcony with patio furniture, but when its nearly 110 degrees sitting outside doesn't sound like an appealing proposition. Upon entering the room, there is a small bar area with a Keurig coffee maker to the right. The bathroom is located to the left, and is very spacious. There is a large soaking tub, shower and separate toilet. There are double sinks with ample counter space, however three large vases take up some valuable counter space, although it is located over the tub. There are Laboratoire Remede branded bath amenities which have a menthol/minty scent. The bedroom is very spacious with ample room to roam around without running into furniture. The bed is very comfortable, with super soft pillows. There is a bed bench at the foot of the bed. There is a large sofa and lounge chair with coffee table in which to unwind, relax and watch TV or have a conversation. The desk area although fairly large, was lacking in outlets that were convenient to plug in your computer or to charge your phone or gadgets. The Phoenician boasts 9 swimming pools, 27 holes of golf and tennis courts, in addition to a somewhat small gym and full spa. Although a Five Diamond AAA hotel, service was professional but somewhat impersonal. All employees were polite but not overly friendly. The hotel also boasts J&G Steakhouse, a Jean George Vongerichten restaurant. Although I did not get a chance to eat here on this visit, it is definitely on my list. If anything close to my past visit at Prime at the Bellagio this is a sure hit. The property is also starting to show its age, and could use an update in the near future. I would definitely stay here again if I can find a good rate, otherwise there are other properties in the Scottsdale area worth checking out.

Originally you could find fine art hanging on the walls, European decor and the fine bone china used for afternoon tea was the same pattern Princess Diana had in her collection. When you walk in the lobby from the valet, stop in front of the fountain where the star-shaped pattern is on the marble lobby floor. Have a cocktail at the Thirsty Camel and sit outside on the balcony. In the evenings they have a piano player so you can listen to live music while you take in the panoramic views of the city. They have fire pits outside and plenty of seating. If you walk down the stairs off the lobby you'll see a wooden door with a stained glass window. That's a private room called the Praying Monk, its a wine cellar that's used for private parties-less than 20 people, it's really cool so check it out on the way to the pool. If you can stay for lunch go to the Terrace and sit on the patio. Order the Prickly Pear Ice-Tea. I also recommend Afternoon Tea served in the lobby. It was a fabulous experience-it's now a steak house so I can only say that the location of the restaurant is on the top level so at night views are amazing. Guests in the Presidential Suite ranged from Michael Jackson, Stevie Nicks and Bon Jovi to a Saudi Prince who one night requested Maine Lobster to be flown in from...wait for it...you guessed it! Maine. Having worked in a 5-Star first class hotel, you learn very quickly what true 5-star standards are, so when you travel you're pretty good at deciphering what meets true hospitality standards and the Phoenician still has it all!

Gina T. (4/5) · ** This review is for the spa and pool area only ** I went with a couple of girlfriends on a Saturday to The Phoenician to take advantage of a deal we picked up for a massage, glass of champagne and access to the pool and spa amenities for the day. Overall, the experience was very pleasant. I arrived early for our massage check-in time, since I wanted to try out their gym and steam room. I had no problem with check-in at the spa -- Emily, the girl at the front desk, was very polite and took the time to show me where everything was since I hadn't been there before. The ladies' locker room is nice and very clean -- they do provide you with rubber "slippers" and very heavy white robes to wear for lounging. The gym is not extremely big, but it's a good size compared to other resort gyms I've used and has a number of treadmills, elliptical machines and bikes, along with machines and free weights. After working out, I hit the steam room. The room itself seems a little old and tired, with some grout "issues" and rusty sprinkler heads in the ceiling (however, I didn't find it gross or dirty). It smelled *heavenly,* like eucalyptus. After a steam for about 10 minutes (the steam room wasn't overly hot, which was nice since I could actually relax), I took a shower to get cleaned up for my massage. Their showers are big, with a separate little "staging area" inside them where you can change, dry off, hang your towel/robe and leave your slippers. They do provide you with shampoo, conditioner and body wash, which was high quality and smelled great. My friends and I met up in the waiting area, which is behind the reception desk. Their "water bar" is a nice touch, with several different fruit-flavor-infused waters and hot tea. We waited for maybe 10 minutes or so before our therapists arrived and introduced themselves, leading us back to our separate treatment rooms. My therapist was Mandy and she was fantastic. I am not always a fan of massages because your level of enjoyment can depend on the skill and... shall I say, "chattiness" of the therapist. Mandy was lovely -- she was very sweet and gave a great Swedish-style massage. I am all about NOT TALKING when I get a massage, since I find it much more relaxing to just let my mind shut down and enjoy the pampering. Mandy asked me a couple of questions during the massage (i.e., making sure the pressure was OK and if the room temperature was comfortable) and that was it. I would highly recommend her -- she knows what she's doing and was very professional. I nearly fell asleep a couple of times and I NEVER do that! After we were done, Mandy led me back to the waiting area where I met my friends and we compared notes. Both friends enjoyed their massages, but one did say that her therapist talked the ENTIRE time. We went up to the pool area after freshening up and changing -- the pool area is above the spa, so you walk out the front doors, and then turn around and go the opposite direction. Being a Saturday, the pools were pretty busy, so it took us a little time to find three lounges together. A server found us fairly quickly, and he almost immediately brought us a pitcher of ice water, cups and a menu. The service in the pool area was great -- they were busy, but our server didn't forget about us and was very friendly. I tried their chips, salsa, guacamole and their chicken wrap, which was REALLY good. I really had only two concerns: they were doing some remodeling on one of the pool areas just below us and the fumes were horrible. As in, the fumes gave all three of us headaches and at one point, we were breathing through towels. We mentioned it to our server, who said they were aware of the smell... but there wasn't anything that could be done about it. Had we been able to move to a different location at the pool, we would have -- it was pretty disconcerting. Too bad they were working on it during the middle of a busy Saturday. The other thing was that they had a guy who played steel drums at the pool area. Loudly. All day. Really, I don't mind steel drums. The fellow was talented and having a great time. But for the love of all that's holy, it wasn't fun or relaxing to shout to talk over a guy playing "Billie Jean" on his steel drums... and he was ALL the way on the OTHER SIDE of the pool from us. Had he turned it down a few notches, it would have been fine. Once he wrapped it up for the day, we were able to hear the waterfall, the birds chirping... and not have to yell at each other. No issues with splitting our check for the food and drinks at the pool, either, which was nice. Around 5, we went back to the spa for a quick whirlpool, shower and... we were done! I really enjoyed my time at The Phoenician. Other than the pool remodeling fumes and the excessively loud steel drums, I had a wonderful day and will certainly be back (particularly once the pool remodeling is over!).

Georgeann G. (5/5) · Honestly, if I were to have paid for this room I might have only given it 4 stars. But, I happen to have a friend who travels to resorts around the country for work, and when he told me he would be staying at the Phoenician and invited me to be his guest for the weekend, I was pretty much all about it. He worked about 12 hours a day while I lounged around the pool, took bubble baths in the huge hotel bathroom, and drank wine in bed while waiting for him to get off so I could show him around Scottsdale. It was like "Pretty Woman" except instead of sexual favors, I paid for my stay with extensive local knowledge and amusing witty banter. We were in the main building, where the rooms are very decently sized, and the bathrooms are pretty damn huge. The grounds are gorgeous, and the close-but-not-too-close to Old Town Scottsdale location makes it ideal for having a night out without worrying about a $40 cab ride to get back to your secluded resort hotel. There were a couple things I would change about the room. For one thing, I wasn't a huge fan of the beds. For what I imagine would normally be a $250+/night stay, I've had better. It was a nice bed, for sure, but not as opulently luxurious as an Arizona Biltmore or Royal Palms, in my opinion. Also, the bathroom had a lighted magnifying cosmetic mirror, which is awesome, but it protruded from the wall at exactly 5'5" from the ground, and wasn't adjustable. So, it would be perfect for A. 5'5" women and B. Pete Wentz. But if you're 5'2" like me, it was pretty useless. The pool was actually really relaxing. No DJ and drunk partiers were at a minimum as well. I also appreciate that they bring out pitchers of water to everyone without the stupid "bottle or tap" question (which obviously comes with the obligatory eye roll when you're fine with not paying $12 for something that comes out of a toilet for free) . The service was a little spotty. We called it "leisurely" but some might call it slow. Plus, somehow my card got charged twice, once for my real amount and once for a completely different amount, which probably means the server accidentally ran my card for somebody else's tab, so hopefully that falls off my bank account before posting. At $7/beer, I can't really afford to pay for anyone's drinks but my own. All in all, I would give it 4.5 stars, but I had a great weekend with great company and the fact that I didn't have to go the Vivian Ward route to get it (though I still got the bubble bath) made it even better, so I'm rounding up to 5.
